Experts Love These 3 Seahawks-Cardinals Bets in Week 9
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals and Seattle Seahawks meet once again for Week 9 NFL action at Lumen Field.
The Cardinals move into today looking to stop a ten-game losing skid to the Seahawks, and after their Week 2 lopsided loss to Seattle, Arizona is hoping the second time will be the charm for first-year head coach Mike LaFleur.
Both teams feature backup quarterbacks this week, as Drew Lock inherits the starting job from an injured Sam Darnold while the Cardinals made the switch from Jacoby Brissett to Gardner Minshew moving forward.
It's an interesting week of football in the NFC West — here's the three of the top bets we could find for this afternoon:
Robert Criscola, Covers.com : "Tyler Allgeier broke out in the win over the Cowboys, rushing for a season-high 147 yards on just 11 carries. It can't be overstated how much better the ground game, and Allgeier, looked with Minshew under center.
"During his time on the field, Allgeier managed three runs of 10+ yards, more than 25% of the 11 that the entire offense had made all season up until that point. With Jeremiyah Love now on IR, a lot of carries open up for Allgeier."
Will Hill, FOX : "'Minshew Magic' helped propel the Cardinals to a comeback win last week in Dallas, but there’s a reason Gardner Minshew has spent much of his career as a backup. I’ll bet on him throwing one to the other team this week, as he draws a tough road matchup against the tenacious Seahawks defense.
Mo Moton, Bleacher Report : The Arizona Cardinals have covered in two of their previous three games, with road wins over the Los Angeles Rams and Dallas Cowboys. So, they should've earned a little more respect than a double-digit line even before the Seahawks ruled out Sam Darnold with a quad injury.
However, the Cardinals will play this game with second-string quarterback Gardner Minshew II and without running back Jeremiyah Love and possibly backup Bam Knight. Arizona's wide receiver corps is also decimated by injuries. Michael Wilson is dealing with broken ribs. Kendrick Bourne and Jalen Brooks are on injured reserve.
Laying double digits is risky given Arizona's recent results, but the Seahawks blew out the Cardinals 31-7 in Arizona in mid-September with backup quarterback Drew Lock, and they can do it again at home.
Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change.

title: Cardinals Activate Starter From Injured Reserve vs Seahawks
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are activating offensive guard Isaiah Adams off injured reserve just in time for their Week 9 road test against the Seattle Seahawks.
Adams, who had his 21-day practice window opened this week, returns just in time to a Cardinals offensive line that has struggled with health in recent weeks. He hasn't played since Week 4 after suffering an ankle injury and is expected to start at right guard in Seattle.
The Cardinals also elevated TE Shawn Bowman and RB Jerome Ford to the active roster from the practice squad for Week 9. Bowman will operate as Arizona's TE4 while Ford will backup Tyler Allgeier and Evan Hull in the RB room.
With left tackle Jayden Williams out and quarterback Gardner Minshew now starting, the Cardinals are hoping to get their offense back on rhythm with different moving pieces on their side of the ball.
“Just go play each play," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said this week.
"Let’s prepare just like we would any other week. We have a great opponent and let’s have a great Wednesday and be where our feet are. If we look too far ahead, which looking too far ahead for me is Sunday, we know what kind of challenge this is going to be. We’re going into a hostile environment against arguably the best defense in football and an offense that we know firsthand can score points, but right now we’re just focused on our prep.”
It's been an unfortunate game of musical chairs up front with the Cardinals' offensive line, as injuries have hindered their starting unit practically every week.
Adams hasn't been overly impressive when playing, though especially with Jon Gaines II out this week, Arizona does get a boost to their interior with Adams' arrival from injured reserve.
The Cardinals haven't defeated the Seahawks in their last ten tries, and Seattle's 31-7 victory over Arizona back in Week 2 still looms large.
"They're great. I've played against (Seahawks Head Coach) Mike (Macdonald) a few times, even going back (to back) in the day," Minshew said this week.
"Always a challenge. They have a lot they can throw at you. They've been very good. They've been great this year. It'll be a great challenge and one that we're fired up for."
The Cardinals could very well have their trade deadline impacted by their result in Seattle. You can learn more about that here .

title: Updated List of Cardinals 2027 Draft Picks After Jacoby Brissett Trade
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals ' trade with the Baltimore Ravens became official today, as the organization dealt starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick.
The Cardinals continue adding to their pile of 2027 draft picks, which first began with trading Marvin Harrison Jr. weeks ago.
As of today, Arizona's sitting strong with their future draft ammo, ranking sixth in Tankathon's draft capital power rankings .
All eight of the Cardinals' picks they currently own, and their projected placement:
*The exact pick numbers will fluctuate on a weekly basis until the season is officially over. These projections are from Tankathon*
The Cardinals own their original draft pick in the first round. According to ESPN's projections, Arizona has a 62% chance to finish with a top ten pick and an 18% chance to earn a top-five pick.
The Cardinals currently have two second-round picks thanks to their prior trade with the Houston Texans involving Harrison. In that deal, Arizona sent back a 2027 seventh-round pick.
As of now, both of these picks sit in the top ten of the second round.
Arizona owns their original draft pick in this round. This is currently the 13th pick in the third round,
This is where the Cardinals' trade for Brissett comes into play, as Arizona now owns two fourth-round picks thanks to the deal. With both of these close in proximity, it wouldn't be a surprise to see the Cardinals try to package them together in a move up at the end of Day 2.
Arizona's original fifth-round pick was sent to the Ravens as part of the Brissett deal. For those curious, this is overall pick No. 150, which is the eleventh in the round.
Also, the Ravens now have three fifth-round picks — though two of them are compensatory picks and wouldn't have been allowed to be traded for Brissett. Those won't be officially awarded to Baltimore until March.
The Cardinals sent their sixth-round pick in the trade involving Harrison.
The Cardinals have two picks in the final round of the draft, one belonging to them (234) and the other (252) originally belongs to the San Francisco 49ers, which was acquired by Houston in August and was packaged in the trade for Harrison.

title: Cardinals' Surprising Success Doesn't Hide Monti Ossenfort's Biggest Mistakes
full_text:
Before Week 9 kicks off in Seattle against the Seahawks, Arizona Cardinals fans are coming off a very exciting win in Dallas against the Cowboys. Arizona's 33-30 win against Dallas featured some of the best highlights of the Cardinals' season.
That said, the win also masked several issues that Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort have made.
When the Cardinals selected Notre Dame running back Jeremiyah Love with the third overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, many thought Arizona reached. Not only because running backs are less valuable in the NFL than they were in prior decades, but also because the Cardinals recently signed Tyler Allgeier in free agency.
During his four seasons on the Falcons, Allgeier totaled 2,876 rushing yards and an silently efficient 4.2 yards per carry. Drafting Love, at least that high in the draft, made little sense for Ossenfort and crew.
On Sunday, Allgeier had an amazing game against Dallas' defense. He ran 147 yards and averaged 13.4 yards per carry. Allgeier's longest run of the day was a 63-yard touchdown run, a big play that helped Arizona get back in the game.
Allgeier put up a game to remember while Love is sidelined with his third ankle injury of the season. When Love did play. the rookie runner averaged just 2.6 yards per carry and struggled to put it in the end zone.
I'm not saying Love is going to be a bust. However, it's becoming clear that the Cardinals could have went other directions with their third overall pick. They could have drafted a player like edge/linebacker Arvell Reese to help the defense or wideout Carnell Tate to better help the offense.
Speaking of the Vikings, after Arizona cut ties with quarterback Kyler Murray, who then signed with Minnesota in March, the question was who would be the Cardinals' next signal caller? Jacoby Brissett was coming off of a very okay season at best where he wasn't terrible, but he also was not great either.
Out of quarterbacks who played at least double-digit games in 2025, Brissett ranked 14th in quarterback rating and touchdown passes.  After last season, Brissett wanted a pay raise for the final year of his contract. He skipped voluntary OTAs and mandatory minicamp. Instead of letting Jacoby go and going with veteran Gardner Minshew as the starter, the Cardinals and Brissett agreed to a restructured deal.
Brissett eventually got benched in the third quarter last week. Minshew came in and orchestrated a comeback victory for the Cardinals. In just two quarters, Minshew looked much better than Brissett has in any full game this season. If Minshew had started the whole season, the Cardinals might have won one of the close games they lost, such as the New York Giants contest.
Ultimately, some may say this doesn't matter, as the Cardinals are in a competitive NFC West division. Many expected the Cardinals to be in a year of developing and building future talent, so getting an extra win or two in the season to go from three wins to five wins isn't a big deal.
However, little mistakes do add up. Ossenfort's tenure with the Cardinals has typically been one step forward, two steps back. He has made some solid decisions, but it always seems like there's a costly move afterward.
Arizona will likely have a high pick in what looks like a loaded draft class next year. If owner Michael Bidwill sees Ossenfort's mistakes pile up, he could look to get a new general manager.
Overall, the Cardinals front office still has a lot of question marks despite the starting win against Dallas. Arizona ownership will have to do a lot of research to determine the next best step for the franchise.

title: Injury Report: Several Big Names Officially Ruled Out for Cardinals-Seahawks Clash
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals and Seattle Seahawks are ruling a total of ten players out for Sunday's Week 9 battle at Lumen Field.
The Cardinals are going to be without Jon Gaines II (ankle), Bam Knight (concussion) and Jayden Williams (knee) for their road test in Seattle.
Questionable for Arizona is Isaiah Adams (ankle), Max Melton (knee) and Walter Nolen III (ankle).
The Seahawks have a much lengthier list of players out this week:
Charles Cross (ankle), Sam Darnold (quad/ribs), Brandon Pili (back), Rashid Shaheed (knee), Leonard Williams (stinger), Quenton Nelson (knee), Uchenna Nwosu (ankle)
Connor O'Toole (foot) is questionable for Seattle.
The two teams can make up to two standard practice squad elevations this weekend, and with the amount of injuries on both sides, it wouldn't at all be surprising to see the Cardinals and Seahawks utilize both spots.
Pay special attention to who gets elevated, as this could be telling on who each team believes will be healthy (Cross in Seattle, Nolen in Arizona) entering Sunday.
The NFL mandates teams reveal final inactives 90 minutes before game time. For Sunday's 2:25 pm MST kickoff, that would be 12:55 pm.
After trading Jacoby Brissett , the Cardinals are rolling with Gardner Minshew as their new starting quarterback — who spoke with reporters about the difficulty of staying focused on his role.
“Yeah naturally. I think over time that’s one of the things (I've) learned to handle better. I think everybody at this stage was the best wherever they came from," he said this week.
"I was used to that growing up and it is a different circumstance and everybody wants to be the guy out there, but you only have so much control over that. Focusing on the things that you can’t control is always a challenge and I feel like I’m proud of the way I did that this year.”
Drew Lock, meanwhile, will get the start for Darnold this week. Lock was under center against the Cardinals in Week 2, which was a blowout win for Seattle.
"You can see the stuff he liked and what they had success with," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said of prepping for Lock.
"Obviously, a lot has changed since Week 2. The first week is what it is. Week 2, you’re still kind of trying to find yourself and you’re not really even settled in yet as a team by any means. But yes, we can use that as a benefit for sure.”

title: Cardinals GM Reveals What Led to Jacoby Brissett Trade
full_text:
ARIZONA — What a difference a week makes.
Just seven days ago, Jacoby Brissett was the lead quarterback of the Arizona Cardinals entering Week 8's matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.
At halftime, Brissett was benched for Gardner Minshew. When the team boarded their plane for a victory flight home to the desert, the Cardinals (reportedly) were already making trade calls on their quarterback.
Monday saw Brissett demoted to third-team duties behind Minshew and Carson Beck , and Wednesday prompted a trade to the Baltimore Ravens that was just finalized today.
It's been a whirlwind seven days for everyone involved, and reporters got a pleasant surprise press conference from general manager Monti Ossenfort on Friday to break things down:
"I think it was a little bit of a perfect storm of a lot of things there," said Ossenfort.
"Obviously, our game played out the way it did on Sunday, and then post-game, our discussions on how we were going to operate moving forward, and that continued into Monday morning. And then, Mike [LaFleur] informed you guys there that the roles in that room were obviously going to switch, and Jacoby was going to assume the third spot on the depth chart. While at the same time, I would say, along with this, Baltimore was dealing with their own set of injury issues that happened with them on Sunday, and so then discussion started there, and then continued over the next couple days.
"And I think, as always with trades, it takes two parties that have to come to an agreement, and [we] came to an agreement that worked for both of us. It was the right thing to do for us, and obviously the right thing to do for Baltimore, and so that's kind of how it all shook out."
Brissett successfully secured a reworked contract where he was given $15 million in guaranteed salary for the 2026 season. After replacing Kyler Murray in Week 5 of last season, Brissett earned starting quarterback duties and was reportedly told he would be Arizona's starter in the offseason.
Now, he's sent packing to Baltimore in a trade that nets the Cardinals a fourth-round pick this year and a 2028 seventh-round pick.
"I have the utmost respect for Jacoby Brissett. Going back to last year, what he did to stabilize a position that was in flux last year, and the toughness and the leadership that he brought to that position, the professionalism, the way that he went about his job every day, took a lot of shots, kept getting up, a lot of respect for Jacoby," Ossenfort said.
"Part of this too is like, hey, they [Baltimore] have an opportunity for Jacoby that we couldn't provide. And so he's going to have an opportunity to go there and play. We'll see how it shakes out for them. I can't answer that, but just a lot of respect and a lot of appreciation for what Jacoby meant to our team, both last year and this year."
The Cardinals now move forward with Minshew and Beck as their top two quarterbacks.
What gave Ossenfort confidence in his quarterback room to pull such a trade off?
"I think really it's how we were going to operate moving forward. Mike and I, we spoke, and Mike determined that was going to be the order of the quarterback room, and so now, as the team is built where Jacoby's in that third role, an opportunity came to trade him for some value," said Ossenfort.
"And so if Baltimore or whatever team, if that opportunity doesn't come, then we're probably moving forward just the way that we were built, and Jacoby would have been in that third role.
"So I think with anything, it's an opportunity that came up, and it just worked out for both parties."

title: Cardinals Rule Out 3 Key Players vs Seahawks
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have ruled out three players on Friday, ahead of Week 9's clash in Seattle.
Head coach Mike LaFleur says all of running back Bam Knight (concussion), tackle Jayden Williams (knee) and guard Jon Gaines (ankle) will be out for their road test against the Seahawks.
None of the three players practiced on Wednesday or Thursday this week, casting serious doubt around their status before LaFleur made things known on Friday morning to reporters.
The Cardinals will release their official injury report later today after practice.
The 3-5 Cardinals have battled some serious injuries this season across the board.
Tyler Allgeier will be Arizona's lead back for another week after shouldering the load in Dallas last week thanks to injuries to Knight and Jeremiyah Love — who is on injured reserve.
Josh Fryar likely gets the nod at left tackle with Williams gone another week, though LaFleur called Fryar a "steady" presence in a game that was anything but for Arizona due to injuries.
"Steady. I thought he stepped in [well], and it [circumstances] doesn't matter. The situation, just like Gardner [Minshew] wasn't playing in the the first half. Jayden, his last play was that long run, and he was hurt before that," said LaFleur.
"So I think that tells you a lot about Jayden. I think you guys really got a good glimpse of the the men in that locker room from this last game. ... Fryar stepped in, and I don't think I knew that until like four plays after he was in there because we had enough stuff we were trying to figure out."
As for Gaines missing another week, the Cardinals are potentially getting back starting right guard Isaiah Adams — who recently had his return window opened from injured reserve. He's been limited in both practices with his ankle injury.
Arizona moves into the weekend with a laundry list of injuries to keep an eye on, including Walter Nolen, Max Melton and Michael Wilson among others.
The Seahawks themselves are quite beat up, losing starting quarterback Sam Darnold for the week and propping Drew Lock up to start vs. Arizona for a second time this season. In their Week 2 win, Lock guided Seattle's offense to a 31-point performance over the Cardinals' defense.
Arizona being down three key players entering the weekend — with more on the way — isn't ideal.

title: Details of Cardinals-Ravens Trade for Jacoby Brissett Revealed
full_text:
ARIZONA — Details of the Arizona Cardinals' trade with the Baltimore Ravens for quarterback Jacoby Brissett have been revealed.
The deal itself was officially announced today by the two sides, though the Cardinals unveiled a short and sweet press release with no picks revealed.
"The Arizona Cardinals Football Club today announced it has traded quarterback Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore for undisclosed draft compensation," it read.
However, NFL insider Ian Rapoport revealed (through his sources) the final package that got the job done: Baltimore is sending a 2027 fourth and 2028 seventh-round pick while the Ravens got Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick.
Final terms for the now-official Jacoby Brissett trade to the #Ravens , per sources: – Baltimore gets Brissett and a 2027 5th rounder. – #AZCardinals get a 4th rounder in 2027 and 7th rounder in 2028. pic.twitter.com/dlRQFZadY7
The Cardinals continue their trade deadline activity after acquiring a second-round pick for Marvin Harrison Jr., and the organization might not be done ahead of the league's Nov. 10 deadline.
Brissett's benching last Sunday propelled trade discussions, and after Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur revealed Gardner Minshew would be the team's starter moving forward (with Carson Beck as QB2, pushing Brissett down to emergency QB status) the Ravens reportedly ramped up their interest in Brissett.
The veteran quarterback now lands on a Ravens team hoping to turn a lost season around. After dropping to 4-5 following their loss on Thursday Night Football and no Lamar Jackson/Tyler Huntley the rest of the way, Baltimore feels as if they needed a fresh presence in the team's quarterback room.
Brissett, a cheap veteran on an expiring contract, was an ideal candidate for the Ravens thanks to the relatively low cost and prior working experience with Baltimore quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork, who sat in the same seat for Arizona last season when Brissett took over.
The Cardinals did decide to increase their load in terms of salary eaten, which likely pushed the trade compensation higher in their favor.
Now, Arizona opens the path for Minshew and Beck to start the rest of the 2026 season, which has already surpassed expectations with a 3-5 record.

title: Cardinals' Road Trip to Seattle Could Change Everything Before Trade Deadline
full_text:
ARIZONA — Rarely does a single regular season game create a monstrous domino effect, though that's exactly what's at stake for the Arizona Cardinals this weekend.
The NFL's trade deadline (Tuesday, Nov. 10) looms large for the organization. With one completed trade (Marvin Harrison Jr.) and another on the way ( Jacoby Brissett ), the Cardinals have already been quite active.
Sitting at a 3-5 record, their outcome against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 9 just might have massive influence over how the Cardinals operate in the following days.
Arizona has a few potential trade deadline candidates ranging from Budda Baker to Josh Sweat among others . The Cardinals don't sound exactly eager to deal either player, though there's expected trade interest around both.
A win against the Seahawks would push them to a 4-5 record — which isn't exactly enough to plan a Super Bowl parade, though it's far beyond where many projected the Cardinals to be entering the second half of the season.
Pending results of Sunday, the Cardinals could exit this weekend tied for second place in the NFC West with wins against the Seahawks and Rams in their pocket. It's unlikely anybody in the NFC West is catching the 6-1 San Francisco 49ers, though crazier things have happened.
As of now, Arizona's just two games out of the final NFC wildcard spot. It's far too early to start doing playoff math, though a win would very much keep them in the mix and at minimum preserve meaningful football for the month of November.
Hope would be enough reason to keep some of their biggest names around until the end of the season, especially for a general manager who could cement his job status for another season with a 2026 campaign that finishes well above expectations.
According to Tankathon , the Cardinals' remaining strength of schedule (.463) is seventh-easiest among NFL teams, which will only weaken more after consecutive matchups against the Seahawks and Rams.
Yet for as much as a win could lead Arizona to believe they should stand pat, a loss to Seattle could also have the opposite effect.
In that scenario, the Cardinals drop to 3-6 — still above expectations but tough to justify keeping around big names who might not fit the future of the organization, especially if trade offers strengthen in the ensuing hours after.
Arizona already has an extra second-round pick thanks to their trade with Houston for Harrison, and it's likely deals involving Baker or Sweat would net more Day 2 selections in a draft class that could springboard the Cardinals' rebuild.
Currently, Arizona sits just outside of the top ten in draft order at No. 11. More losses down the stretch of the season would heighten their chances of landing a top ten pick. ESPN's football power index has them at a 62% chance to finish in the top ten of the 2027 draft order while a top-five finish has an 18% chance for Arizona.
While teams don't tank, losses down the final eight-game stretch are more likely without two of Arizona's biggest names on the defensive side of the ball. That would place the Cardinals in a prime spot to take a top position of need, or perhaps even in reach of a blockbuster trade-up for a quarterback — if they so desire.
Wins and losses will continue to pile after Sunday, though 60 minutes in Seattle could very well determine the road Arizona travels in the coming months.

title: Mystery Piece Could Complete Cardinals-Ravens Jacoby Brissett Trade
full_text:
ARIZONA — Chatter around the Arizona Cardinals and Baltimore Ravens' trade for Jacoby Brissett only heightens after Thursday Night Football, where the Jacksonville Jaguars handled Baltimore with ease.
The Cardinals and Ravens reportedly agreed to terms earlier in the week on a deal that would send Brissett to Baltimore, though compensation for the veteran quarterback has yet to be revealed as the two sides are waiting until this weekend to finalize a move.
Arizona, at this time, doesn't have a third quarterback in the building with Brissett reportedly in Baltimore. Gardner Minshew is taking over starting duties while Carson Beck awaits as QB2.
A potential component of a trade could be a familiar face to round out their quarterback room.
Slovis played for the Cardinals this preseason but was released ahead of final roster cuts, as Arizona planned to roster three quarterbacks (making one inactive).
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur was asked this week if the organization had plans to find a third quarterback for the remaining stretch of season.
Slovis spent an entire offseason learning LaFleur's system and is familiar with Arizona after signing with them in 2025.
When evaluating the most important traits of a QB3, oftentimes the simple ability to correctly run and operate an offense ranks near the top of the list. Slovis has that, specifically in his recent experience with LaFleur.
While Slovis isn't exactly valuable to most of the league, his value is higher in relation to Arizona and their potential search for a new quarterback to fill Brissett's slot.
That's what made Slovis' arrival to Baltimore earlier this week a bit more interesting. Brissett and the Ravens have been connected in trade chatter for several days now thanks to injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley.
Reports indicate the Ravens reached out to Arizona about a potential trade after LaFleur officially announced the Cardinals would be benching Brissett.
The Ravens signed Slovis from the Green Bay Packers' practice squad to their active roster on Tuesday, after Arizona and Baltimore reportedly began discussing a deal centered around Brissett.
Coincidence? Perhaps. The Cardinals could have easily signed Slovis off Green Bay's practice squad themselves, and for what it's worth, current Ravens QB coach Israel Woolfork was Slovis' position coach in Arizona last season.
However, it wouldn't be at all surprising to see Slovis included in a potential deal.

title: Jeff Ulbrich: Falcons Defense ‘Not Even Close’ to Potential Ahead of Bengals
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons defense has shown flashes of its potential throughout the 2026 season, but defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich believes his unit has yet to put everything together.
With a difficult matchup against Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals approaching, Atlanta has an opportunity to demonstrate just how good its defense can become.
"We have not played up to our potential, in my opinion. Not even close," Ulbrich said. "I'm excited for these guys to start putting that on the table."
Through eight games, the Falcons rank 18th in total defense, allowing 341.6 yards per game, and 17th in scoring defense, surrendering 23.6 points per contest. Atlanta has also allowed 118.3 rushing yards per game, an area that became a major concern following its recent loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Despite those numbers, Ulbrich remains confident in the personnel and believes the defense has considerably more potential than it has demonstrated.
One of the biggest reasons for Ulbrich's confidence is the mentality within the defensive locker room.
"There's not one person that I could point to that operates in any way other than what's best for the defense, what's best for the team, what's best for the group, as opposed to what's best for the individual," Ulbrich said.
Ulbrich also credited the group's preparation and commitment to improving throughout the season. Schematically, Atlanta is continuing to identify its strengths and weaknesses while finding ways to maximize its personnel.
However, the Falcons have some immediate issues to address, particularly against the run.
Atlanta allowed Tampa Bay to dictate the game with its rushing attack, something Ulbrich acknowledged.
"Whenever you give up that many rush yards, that is a failure by everyone in a lot of ways," Ulbrich said.
He also took responsibility for not making additional adjustments, including using more six-man fronts and different safety rotations.
The challenge gets even tougher against Cincinnati. Burrow has thrown for 2,115 yards and 20 touchdowns with six interceptions through seven games. He also has two dangerous receiving options in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
Higgins has recorded 726 receiving yards and four touchdowns, while Chase has added 492 yards and six scores. Together, they give Cincinnati the ability to exploit defenses that devote too much attention to one side of the field.
Ulbrich understands that Atlanta cannot eliminate every offensive threat and will need its defenders to win individual matchups.
The Falcons do have an encouraging strength entering the matchup. Atlanta has generated pressure on 40% of opposing dropbacks this season, the sixth-highest rate in the NFL, despite blitzing on just 24.8% of dropbacks.
That ability to pressure Burrow without consistently sending extra defenders could be critical.
For Ulbrich, the objective is getting his defense to play closer to the standard he believes it can reach. Sunday's matchup in Madrid provides another opportunity to prove that potential is more than just talk.

title: Falcons Hope Nick Folk Can End Frustrating History at Kicker
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have spent the better part of the last two seasons searching for stability at kicker, cycling through multiple options while struggling to find a dependable answer in critical moments.
After going through a lot of kickers in recent years, Atlanta believed it had finally found that consistency by bringing in veteran Nick Folk. However, even with his impressive track record, the Falcons are experiencing some familiar problems.
Folk’s recent struggles have brought renewed attention to the position, making special teams coordinator Craig Aukerman’s confidence in the veteran especially important as the season progresses.
Through eight games, Folk has converted 12 of his 16 field goal attempts and missed an extra point, snapping a streak of 67 consecutive successful extra-point attempts. That is a significant departure from his previous three seasons, when he missed just one field goal in each campaign and consistently ranked among the NFL’s most accurate kickers.
The Falcons’ problems at kicker extend beyond Folk’s current season.
Atlanta went through three different kickers in 2025, with Younghoe Koo, John Parker Romo and Zane Gonzalez all getting opportunities. The trio combined to make 32 of 39 field goal attempts, an 82% conversion rate that ranked among the league’s worst.
There were several costly moments along the way, including Koo’s missed potential game-tying field goal against Tampa Bay in Week 1 and Romo’s missed extra point in a one-point loss to New England.
Those struggles ultimately contributed to Atlanta making a change in the offseason, bringing in Folk and Aukerman in hopes of establishing a more reliable special teams unit.
Folk appeared to be the right answer. Before joining Atlanta, he had led the NFL in field goal percentage in each of the previous three seasons, including a 96.6% mark with the New York Jets in 2025.
Now, the Falcons need that same consistency to return.
Despite the recent misses, Aukerman continues to stand behind his veteran kicker. Speaking to reporters in Madrid ahead of Sunday’s international matchup, Aukerman explained that much of his responsibility involves maintaining Folk’s confidence rather than overcorrecting his technique.
“It’s a little bit of the rain, it’s a little bit of distance, it’s the weather — it’s all these different types of things,” Aukerman said when discussing Folk’s missed 53-yard attempt against Tampa Bay. “And Nick will tell you the first thing, it’s no excuse. Same thing with me. But it just went over to the left a little bit and it’s unfortunate the rain started coming down really hard at that time. But it is what it is.”
Aukerman also emphasized the importance of moving forward instead of allowing one missed opportunity to affect the next.
“My biggest thing is I just want to support him, make sure that he knows that I’m there,” Aukerman said during an earlier press conference. “If he does miss a kick, I know the next one, we have all the confidence in the world with him.”
That relationship could become one of Atlanta’s biggest advantages moving forward. Aukerman previously worked with Folk in Tennessee in 2023, when the veteran enjoyed one of the best stretches of his career. Their familiarity gives the Falcons an established working relationship rather than forcing a kicker and coach to build trust from scratch.
Atlanta has already experienced what happens when consistency is missing at the position. The organization made a significant investment in Folk because of his experience and production, and abandoning that approach after a difficult stretch would be premature.
With Aukerman continuing to offer his support, Atlanta hopes its latest kicking solution can finally end a frustrating stretch at one of football’s most important positions.

title: Falcons Place RB on Injured Reserve, Sign Replacement Among Other Moves
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are making another significant change to their running back room ahead of Sunday’s matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals, placing Brian Robinson Jr. on Injured Reserve with a hamstring injury.
Atlanta announced the move Saturday, ending Robinson’s availability for at least the next four games as he works toward recovering from the injury. Robinson had already been ruled out for Sunday’s game after missing the previous two contests with the same hamstring issue.
Robinson was limited in practice throughout the week in Madrid, but his inability to get back on the field has forced the Falcons to make a roster move. To fill his spot, Atlanta is signing running back Khalil Herbert to the active roster.
Herbert has already stepped into Robinson’s role over the past two weeks, providing additional depth behind Bijan Robinson in the backfield. The veteran running back has appeared in two games for Atlanta this season, recording six carries for 21 yards while adding two receptions for 22 yards.
Herbert’s opportunities have been limited, but he has experience handling a larger workload. During his time with the Chicago Bears, he recorded 731 rushing yards and four touchdowns in 2022, followed by 611 rushing yards and two touchdowns in 2023.
Robinson, meanwhile, finishes his current stretch with 211 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 53 carries through six games. He also contributed five receptions for 30 yards. His four rushing touchdowns were tied for the team lead among running backs.
His absence creates another challenge for an Atlanta offense that has relied on having multiple options in the backfield. Bijan Robinson remains the primary option after rushing for 780 yards and four touchdowns on 150 carries this season. However, Herbert’s ability to provide a complementary presence will be important with Brian Robinson unavailable.
The Falcons also made several other roster moves ahead of Sunday’s international matchup.
Atlanta activated linebacker Yasir Abdullah and wide receiver Beaux Collins from Injured Reserve, giving both players an opportunity to contribute after working through their respective injuries. Defensive end Drake Jackson was also elevated to the active roster for Sunday’s game.
Defensive end James Pearce Jr. has officially been activated following his eight-game suspension but remains questionable for the matchup because of a back injury.
Meanwhile, offensive tackle Cameron Williams has been downgraded to out, creating another personnel concern for Atlanta heading into Sunday.
With Robinson heading to Injured Reserve and several other players returning or dealing with injuries, the Falcons will have to manage their roster carefully. Herbert now has an opportunity to establish himself as the team’s primary backup running back while Atlanta looks to maintain its rushing attack against Cincinnati.

title: 3 Keys to Victory for Atlanta Falcons vs. Cincinnati Bengals
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have an important opportunity to get their season back on track when they face the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain. With the two teams meeting on an international stage, Atlanta will look to put together a complete performance against a Cincinnati offense capable of creating problems for opposing defenses.
The Falcons have struggled to find consistency throughout the season, and injuries have also begun to catch up with the roster. However, a matchup against the Bengals presents an opportunity to turn things around.
Here are three keys to victory for the Falcons against the Bengals.
If the Falcons want to pull off the upset, their best opportunity could come on the ground. Bijan Robinson has been one of Atlanta’s most productive players this season, and getting him involved early will be important against a Cincinnati defense that has struggled to stop the run.
Robinson enters the matchup with 780 rushing yards on 150 carries, averaging 5.2 yards per attempt. He also has 203 receiving yards, giving the Falcons another way to get the football into his hands.
Cincinnati has allowed 4.8 yards per carry this season, creating an opportunity for Atlanta to take advantage of a weakness in the Bengals’ defense. The Falcons cannot afford to become one-dimensional, particularly with Michael Penix Jr. coming off a difficult performance against Tampa Bay.
Robinson needs to be a focal point of the offense, helping Atlanta control the clock, create manageable third downs and keep Burrow off the field.
There might not be a more important matchup on Sunday than Atlanta’s defensive front against Burrow and the Cincinnati passing attack.
The Bengals quarterback has been playing at an elite level, throwing for 2,115 yards and 20 touchdowns with six interceptions through seven games. Cincinnati is averaging 29.4 points per game and ranks among the league leaders in passing offense.
Burrow also has plenty of weapons around him. Ja’Marr Chase has recorded 492 receiving yards and six touchdowns, while Tee Higgins has added 726 yards and four touchdowns.
Atlanta’s defense will need to generate pressure without consistently sending extra defenders. Defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich has emphasized the challenge of defending Burrow’s ability to recognize coverages and deliver accurate passes.
The potential return of James Pearce Jr. could provide a boost to the pass rush, although his availability remains uncertain because of a back issue. Regardless, Atlanta needs its defensive line to make Burrow uncomfortable and force him into difficult decisions.
Atlanta’s margin for error is extremely small against an offense as explosive as Cincinnati’s. That makes protecting the football one of the biggest keys to Sunday’s matchup.
The Falcons are coming off a 16-0 shutout loss to Tampa Bay in which they committed four turnovers. Penix threw a career-high four interceptions, and Atlanta managed just 224 total yards.
Those mistakes cannot happen again against Cincinnati. The Bengals have scored at least 30 points in each of their last three games, making turnovers particularly costly.
There is also some historical motivation for Atlanta. Cincinnati leads the all-time series 10-5 and has won the last three meetings, including a 35-17 victory in 2022. The Falcons have not beaten the Bengals since 2010.
A clean performance, particularly from Penix, would give Atlanta a much better chance of ending that losing streak.
Atlanta will have its hands full in Madrid, but the formula for an upset is straightforward. If the Falcons can establish Robinson, disrupt Burrow and avoid costly mistakes, they will give themselves an opportunity to leave Spain with a much-needed victory.

title: The Time is Now for Atlanta Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr.
full_text:
Michael Penix Jr. has an opportunity to put his worst performance of the season behind him when the Atlanta Falcons face the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain, on Sunday.
The Atlanta Falcons quarterback is coming off a disastrous outing against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, completing just 8 of 24 passes for 125 yards with no touchdowns and four interceptions in a 16-0 shutout loss. Penix finished with a 12.0 passer rating, the lowest mark of his NFL career.
It was a difficult afternoon for the second-year quarterback , who struggled to find consistency in the passing game.
"It was hard to watch it, but at the same time, that's what comes with it," Penix said Thursday. "You still got to look at it, even though games like that you don't really want to watch it, but you got to correct some things that need to be corrected.
"So, spent that next day doing our correcting and then after that, it was, 'We're moving onto Cincy.'"
Moving on to Cincinnati could present an ideal opportunity for Penix to regain his confidence. Through six games this season, he has completed 104 of 168 passes for 1,282 yards, nine touchdowns, and five interceptions. He is completing 61.9% of his passes while averaging 213.7 passing yards per game.
While his latest performance was a significant setback, Penix has already demonstrated what he can accomplish when he finds his rhythm. Now, he will face a Cincinnati defense that has struggled to consistently slow down opposing passing attacks.
The Bengals enter Sunday's matchup allowing 383.3 total yards per game, ranking 27th in the NFL. Their biggest vulnerability has come through the air, where Cincinnati is surrendering 261 passing yards per game, also ranking 27th.
Opposing quarterbacks have completed 63.6% of their passes against Cincinnati while averaging 7.6 yards per attempt. The Bengals have allowed eight passing touchdowns through seven games.
Cincinnati has also struggled to get opposing offenses off the field on third down. Opponents are converting 47.3% of their third down opportunities, ranking the Bengals 29th in the league.
Those numbers should provide some encouragement for Penix and the Falcons' passing attack.
Offensive coordinator Tommy Rees knows the season will come with highs and lows, but emphasized that the Falcons cannot afford to let one performance carry into the next week.
"It's week to week. You have the highs, San Francisco, and then you've just got to refocus after last week," Rees said. "Mike's pretty even-keeled, we all know that, but it's part of our job to always motivate, always reassure."
Rees also made it clear that the coaching staff is not using the weather as an excuse for what happened against New England. Instead, the focus has been on the mistakes Atlanta can control.
"Last week, yes, you can point to the weather all you want, but that's not what we're falling on. They played in the same weather we did, and our job as coaches, our job as players, is playing football," Rees said.
The message from Rees has been centered on execution, decision-making, and improving the details that ultimately determine whether a team wins or loses.
With receivers such as Drake London, Kyle Pitts Sr., and Jahan Dotson available, Atlanta has the personnel to take advantage of Cincinnati's struggles in coverage. Dotson has been particularly productive, recording 14 receptions for 337 yards and two touchdowns this season.
However, the Bengals are not without defensive strengths. Cincinnati has already recorded 23 sacks through seven games, ranking fourth in the league in that category. The defense has also forced 11 turnovers, including four interceptions.
That creates an important challenge for Penix. Cincinnati has allowed plenty of passing production, but its ability to pressure quarterbacks could create problems if Atlanta's offensive line struggles to protect him.
The Falcons will need to give Penix time to work through his progressions and find opportunities downfield without forcing throws into coverage.
Despite the difficult performance against Tampa Bay, Penix continues to have the support of his teammates.
Wide receiver Jahan Dotson believes the quarterback's mentality will allow him to put the performance behind him and respond against Cincinnati.
"He's super even-keeled. I have no doubt in my mind that he'll bounce back. That's just the kind of guy he is and the way he goes about his business," Dotson said.
Dotson also acknowledged the difficult weather conditions Penix faced against New England, recognizing how challenging it can be for a quarterback to operate when dealing with rain.
"I can't imagine being a quarterback and trying to throw a pass in the rain like that," Dotson said. "But he's looking to bounce back this week, and so are we as a football team."
Penix does not need to do everything himself. He needs to make smart decisions, take what the defense gives him, and allow Atlanta's offensive weapons to make plays.
After the worst performance of his season, Penix will have a chance to make Sunday's game a turning point.

title: FalconsSI Staff Predictions are Split on Falcons vs. Bengals in Spain
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are in Madrid, Spain, for an international Week 9 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday. Atlanta is looking to get back into the win column against a Cincinnati team that has won three consecutive games.
The Bengals present a difficult challenge for Atlanta, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. Joe Burrow leads one of the NFL’s most productive offenses, featuring star wide receivers Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. With injuries beginning to catch up with the Falcons , slowing down Cincinnati’s passing attack could be a major challenge.
Atlanta’s offense will also need to deliver a strong performance against a Bengals defense that has struggled at times this season. Michael Penix Jr. and Bijan Robinson will be important pieces as the Falcons attempt to keep pace with Burrow and company in what could be a high-scoring international matchup.
Here are the Falcons On SI staff’s predictions for Sunday’s Week 9 matchup.
The Falcons will have a difficult test on Sunday with the high-flying Bengals offense. They will score plenty of points in this one, and it will be on Michael Penix Jr. to match that production. Working in their favor is the fact that the Bengals are not an elite pressure team, so if they can keep the quarterback clean, then the Falcons could keep up.
Atlanta usually wins one of these games they aren’t supposed to every year, and I think Atlanta can find a way to get to Joe Burrow a few times.
It’ll be a high-scoring game, and the Falcons’ season survives one more week with a 34-30 win.
Prediction: Falcons 34, Bengals 30
Welcome to another week of the most unpredictable team in football. This game has all the makings of one the Falcons play up for. International game, and the Bengals have been rolling with three-straight wins. This game could make for fireworks.
Cincy is pretty much the middle of the pack defensively, but has one of the top offenses in the league. So the Falcons will have opportunities to put points on the board too. But can their secondary keep up with the likes of Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins? We have to wait and see if they prove it. Expect a high-scoring affair in Madrid, with the Bengals coming out victorious.
Prediction: Bengals 38, Falcons 34
After picking the Falcons to win each of the last three games, I’m finally going against Atlanta this week. I believed the Falcons had opportunities to pick up wins in two of those matchups, but unfortunately, I was wrong.
Heading into Sunday’s matchup against the Bengals, I think Joe Burrow and Cincinnati’s offense will be too much to handle, especially with Atlanta’s injuries beginning to catch up with them. I expect the Falcons to keep it close, but ultimately, I’m taking the Bengals to win 27-24.
Prediction: Bengals 27, Falcons 24
As inconsistent as the Falcons are, they’ve consistently shown us that they will beat teams they have no business beating and lose to teams they have no business losing to. That makes this a great week to be playing one of the better teams in the league.
Pattern recognition aside, there are several aspects of this matchup that make me hopeful. The obvious key to this game will be whether the Falcons can stop Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins. But the Falcons have been one of the better pass defenses in the league; they now have a fully healthy secondary, and their best pass rusher is back from suspension, although he is questionable for Sunday.
The offense will need a big bounce-back to pull off the upset. Michael Penix Jr. will try to rebound after his best Desmond Ridder impression last week. But I think the Falcons’ o-line will be just as inspired to have a great showing after getting dominated by the Buccaneers’ d-line last week.
Ultimately, I have the Falcons pulling off the upset behind an inspired run game and some big plays from Jeff Ulbrich and his defense when it matters.
Prediction: Falcons 33, Bengals 30
I've said for years that trying to predict what the Atlanta Falcons are going to do is a good way to look like an idiot. General manager Ian Cunningham has helped fix that off the field by dutifully addressing needs in free agency and matching premium positions of need with his top draft picks.
However, all is not fixed in less than a year. The team on the field remains maddeningly inconsistent because of talent and depth problems inherited by Cunningham and head coach Kevin Stefanski.
The Falcons have the same record that I do when trying to predict the outcome of their games: 3-5. In each of their three wins, I've picked them to lose.
So naturally, being an underdog in a foreign country is the type of game that makes the Falcons dangerous for Cincinnati. That said, I'm a creature of logic, and logic tells me the cracks in Atlanta's defense will be too much for the offense to overcome.
Prediction: Bengals 30, Falcons 20

title: Why the Falcons’ Maddening Trend Could Spell Trouble for Bengals in Madrid
full_text:
Those familiar with the Atlanta Falcons know that this is a roller coaster of a franchise.
Taking it back to just last year, think about how they beat Super Bowl contenders like the Minnesota Vikings, Buffalo Bills, and Los Angeles Rams.
But suffered blowout losses to the Miami Dolphins and Carolina Panthers en route to finishing 8-9 and missing the NFL Playoffs for the eighth straight year.
Dr, Jekyll? Mr. Hyde? The play-up, play-down thrill ride continues.
After going down to the wire with the Chicago Bears and then defeating the San Francisco 49ers , Atlanta took an immediate step back.
Last Sunday, Nov. 1, Atlanta was shut out 16-0 by Tampa Bay Buccaneers as it rained buckets at Raymond James Stadium.
“It’s ebbs and flows of the NFL,” said Jessie Bates III, Falcons safety. “Nobody cares what you did last week. You’re going to get your best from everybody week in and week out. Just got to bounce back.”
Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. tossed the rain-soaked football for four interceptions , ending his hot streak where he had been named the NFC Offensive Player of the Week days before kickoff. He vowed to “shake back” and “put my head down and keep working.”
“We have a chance to redeem ourselves as a football team,” Falcons wide receiver Jahan Dotson added. “Being in the circumstances that we had last Sunday, you kind of want to put it behind you as quickly as possible.”
The chance to regain respect comes this Sunday in a Week 9 international matchup. The Falcons (3-5) face the Cincinnati Bengals (5-2) in the second-ever NFL game in Madrid, Spain.
If history’s an indicator, the Bengals’ three-game winning streak points to the Falcons getting up for the NFC-AFC battle.
“It is what it is. You’ve got to move on to this week,” Xavier Watts , Atlanta’s safety. “It’s a chip on our shoulder. Coming back this week and proving that we’re better and going to improve from last week’s game.”
Atlanta has flashed. Their wins over the Green Bay Packers, New Orleans Saints, and 49ers had fans and experts alike thinking it was a top NFL team.
And at times, the light has been dim – very dim. Beyond the quarterback purgatory of the first two weeks, the team shrank in overtime against the Baltimore Ravens, struggled in the first three quarters against the Bears, and was bad all around at Tampa.
“There’s still a lot of stuff to clean up,” Bates said. “But there are also great things you want to continue to build on.”
It's never really over in the crazy NFC South. If only one of the four teams wins on Sunday, that team, including the New Orleans Saints at 3-5, will be in first place. The Falcons could be in first place at 4-5 if they win and the Panthers (3-4) and Buccaneers (3-5) both lose. They could be in last place if they lose and the Saints and Bucs win.

title: James Pearce Jr.'s Long-Awaited Return Could Be Longer: Falcons Injury Report
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons received some encouraging injury news ahead of their Week 9 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals , but there are still several question marks surrounding the team’s availability for Sunday’s international game in Madrid, Spain.
Atlanta officially cleared defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. to play, while linebacker Divine Deablo is questionable. Edge rusher James Pearce Jr. is also questionable after experiencing a setback with his back. Brian Robinson Jr. and Zachariah Branch have been ruled out with hamstring injuries.
The biggest uncertainty, however, could be Pearce.
After completing his eight-game suspension, the former first-round pick was expected to make his season debut against Cincinnati. Defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich previously indicated that Atlanta planned to use Pearce primarily as a pass rusher while monitoring his workload.
However, head coach Kevin Stefanski revealed Friday that Pearce experienced a “flare up” in his back injury. The Falcons will monitor how he progresses over the next two days before making a final decision on his availability.
Pearce is officially listed as questionable, creating some uncertainty around his anticipated return. His potential availability would be important for an Atlanta pass rush looking for additional production against Burrow.
Fellow edge rusher Samson Ebukam went to Injured Reserve this week, leaving the Falcons short-handed at the position.  Charles Snowden could see more time at edge, and Za'Darius Smith could increase his workload after battling an injury the last several weeks. Another option is inside linebacker Harold Perkins creeping up to an edge spot in pass-rushing situations.
Cameron Thomas saw extensive action last week in Tampa with 47 snaps. Snowden was next at edge with just 26.
Bowman is one of the biggest positive developments for the Falcons heading into the weekend. The rookie defensive back has been working through a hamstring injury that forced him to miss the previous two games. However, he returned to full participation earlier in the week and maintained that status throughout the Falcons’ practices in Spain.
His return should provide a boost to Atlanta’s secondary, particularly against a Cincinnati offense led by quarterback Joe Burrow. Bowman has an opportunity to help strengthen a defense that needs to perform better after its struggles against Tampa Bay.
Meanwhile, Deablo remains questionable as he attempts to return.
Deablo has been dealing with a forearm injury and was limited earlier in the week before returning as a full participant Friday. His progression is an encouraging sign for Atlanta, which has been without the linebacker over the previous two weeks.
Robinson, who is recovering from a hamstring injury, remains out for his third straight game. The running back has also missed the last two games. Khalil Herbert will most likely be called to back up Robinson again this week.
The Falcons have some encouraging developments heading into their international matchup, particularly with Bowman’s return and Deablo’s progress. However, Pearce’s setback adds another layer of uncertainty to Atlanta’s defensive plans, especially with Samson Ebukam heading to Injurred Reserve.
With several players still awaiting final clearance, the next two days will be important as Atlanta prepares for its Week 9 showdown against Cincinnati.
Darius has a Master's in Communications from Georgia State and has previous experience covering the Atlanta Falcons with 3 Point Conversion and covering the NFL with On SI.

title: Falcons Get Major Defensive Boost Ahead of Joe Burrow, Bengals Showdown
full_text:
MADRID – Atlanta Falcons edge rusher James Pearce Jr. is finally set to make his season debut, and the timing couldn't be more important for a defense searching for answers.
One week after being gashed on the ground by the Buccaneers’ rushing attack, the Falcons will face a fundamentally different challenge with Joe Burrow and the Bengals. This unit tops the NFL in passing offense and boasts one of the league's most dangerous receiving duos in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
Slowing Cincinnati's passing attack will require pressure on Burrow, making Pearce's return especially important. The Falcons have already been busy making space for their star pass rusher, and Samson Ebukam's hamstring injury has created an immediate need for snaps.
What that impact could look like remains a lingering question.
Pearce has been around the team for the past month but was only cleared to practice earlier this week. He's spent most of his time in the weight room and meeting rooms, raising questions about how much he can handle in his first game back. Stefanski said the coaching staff has a good idea of Pearce's capabilities but declined to disclose his expected snap count.
“He’s been working his butt off, and he’s super excited to get out there and help contribute,” Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich said Thursday. “I think initially, he’ll probably be more in a pass-rush capacity, whether that be second-and-longs, third downs. But we’ll see. A lot of his conditioning and ability to play more will be dependent upon what he shows us as the game goes along. Thinking as we go in with a pitch count, but you can obviously change that thinking really quickly based on how it plays.”
Pearce led the Falcons with 10.5 sacks last season, marking the first time that the franchise had a player hit double digits since 2016, and he was an instrumental piece in this unit’s franchise-record 57-sack season.
Without him, the Falcons have leaned on a four-man front to generate pressure. The unit has been effective (No. 6 in pressure rate, 40.0%) but has been less consistent at getting the quarterback on the ground (No. 14 in sacks, 18).
The pass rush has spread the wealth, with 12 players having recorded a half-sack or more this season. Veteran Za’Darius Smith (4.5) has led this group, but Pearce’s return would be an adrenaline shot.
He was expected to build on his rookie on-field performance, but an offseason incident marred the first half of his sophomore season. Pearce was arrested in February on allegations of domestic violence, but a pre-trial agreement helped him avoid possible jail time . The league later suspended him for eight games.
Since rejoining the team, Pearce has had an opportunity to rebuild trust within the organization. Ulbrich believes the young pass rusher has shown meaningful personal growth during that process. The two have been meeting once a week, and the Falcons defensive coordinator called those interactions “eye-opening.”
“I think I’ve just gained appreciation for him as a man,” Ulbrich said. “I see a guy that’s really – he’s working his butt off to right some wrongs, and he’s working his butt off to become a better version of himself. I have deep appreciation for that because that’s not easy. And not everybody has the humility and the wisdom to do that. I feel like he’s made a real concerted effort to become the best version of James.
“I’m just super hopeful that that translates to success because we all know that just that would bring that idea that I’m on the right track, and I’ve got to keep going on the right track.”
Pearce's return is unlikely to immediately solve all of Atlanta's defensive problems, particularly against a Bengals offense that can attack defenses in multiple ways, but his ability to generate pressure could give the Falcons a much-needed boost. After leading the team in sacks a year ago, Pearce will have his first opportunity to show what he can contribute to this defense in 2026.
How quickly he can make an impact remains to be seen.

Garrett Chapman is a sports broadcaster, writer, and content creator based in Atlanta. He has several years of experience covering the Atlanta sports scene, college football, Georgia high school football, recruiting for 24/7 Sports, and the NFL. You can also hear him on Sports Radio 92.9 The Game.

title: One Ravens Player Who Should Surprisingly Be Traded Before the Deadline
full_text:
There is no ideal time to get out of the Trey Hendrickson contract. Only a half season into what amounts to a two-year, $60M deal it looks pretty disastrous.
And, like oh so many of the contracts executed by failing general manager Eric Decosta , it carries nasty cap and cash ramifications for a team in salary-cap hell because of terrible contract situations with Mark Andrews, Marlon Humphrey, Roquan Smith, John Simpson and others. All the while Tyler Linderbaum and Isaiah Likely and Charlie Kolar and Pat Ricard left as free agents.
That’s bad business. And worse football.
Oh, and unlike every other NFL team with an elite quarterback, they can never get Lamar Jackson extended when they should when the market resets, so his $84M cap hit in 2027 hangs over everything ( he controls their offseason ) while their season spirals to the abyss. This is a mess. It runs years deep into the future and every effort should and must be made to start getting out of it (the entire league sees this for what it is ). And, believe it or not, there is also a case to be made that moving on from Hendrickson – one of the more consequential signings in recent franchise history.
This season is over – not even the Ravens themselves can seriously believe Jackson is going to swoop into this tragedy in all three phases of football and bail them out against all odds in December – and, this I can tell you without a doubt, the conversations about their horrific cash/cap outlays in future are well underway. No one could dare sugarcoat that (especially with Jackson having all contract leverage with the no-trade and no-tag provisions).
Given all of that, here’s why I’d advise getting out of Hendrickson now by any means necessary.
This was really a play for 2026, trying to win right away despite the most inexperienced (and as we’ve come to find out, naive, coaching staff in the NFL (even Miami’s head coach had been a college head coach before, and this staff has more in common with Miami’s than any in the NFL ). Hendrickson was their parachute when the front office had second thoughts about trading two first-round picks for Maxx Crosby (turns out he was worth it) to address years of a suspect pass rush.
Hendrickson was lingering on the market because he was 32, he can’t play the run and that will only get much worse at that age. He has been injury prone lately and he spent a lot of time finding reasons not to play for the Bengals in recent years. His financial ask was seen as to steep according to execs from multiple teams who were exploring pass-rush options, and when DeCosta pounced executives around the league began calling this out. DeCosta, meantime, tried to sell his fans on a master plan to and Crosby and Hendrickson .
Hendrickson looked like a $30M a year guy in Week 1 against the hapless Colts, hurt his finger and has not shown up in the fourth quarter all season. Hailed as a closer, undrafted special teams rookie Ethan Burke has more sacks than him in the fourth quarter. He isn’t even in the top two on the team in sacks and this pass rush is impotent (3.5 sacks leads them). His 12% pressure rate in the fourth quarter is a try-hard guy, not a game-wrecker and 2027 it a retool year no matter how they try to spin it.
“This isn’t going to age well,” said one longtime NFL personnel executive who has watched Hendrickson closely. “You make a move like that, something they never do (big free-agent signing), Year One, he’s supposed to pop.
“Come in, take the game over, make the young guys better.  You see the same thing I do ... They talked him up like the guy who changes your defense when he walks in the locker room and they still blow a lead every time they get it with this guy  … This is worse than (former defensive coordinator Zach) Orr’s tape, and they stuck him with (aging quasi-pass rusher Kyle) Van Noy.
“This is a disaster, man. Don’t let anybody tell you anything different. I watched his tape. It gets worse every week … They have the hand bandaged up like an amputee. The guys (broadcasting the games) in the booth can’t miss it. That’s all you’re going to hear about now.”
Indeed, overmatched rookie head coach Jesse Minter, when asked about mustering two sacks in the last three games while allowing 33 points or more in all of them, immediately brought up Hendrickson’s finger procedure from early in the season. They had seven total pressures as a team with their season on the line against Jacksonville at home, mind you, and THE CLOSER had none.
“We have one guy really kind of playing through having one free hand,” he said. So all the more reason to sit him – better yet: man up and trade him – and play the kids after four straight horrific losses with Hendrickson doing nothing to help the NFL’s worst second-half defense (while leading the league in choking).
Mike Green is one of few ascending young defensive players on this roster, he should be playing more and while he isn’t special against the run he is a helluva lot better than Hendrickson (especially playing with one hand). They both primarily want to line up over the left tackle. One is young and cheap and the other makes $29M more next year.
Does having Hendrickson coming off a washout first season here set to be the second-highest paid player on the team next year make sense when you know Steve Bisciotti is going to want to cut payroll after DeCosta lit $370M on fire this year and couldn’t keep them truly in the hunt past Halloween? Does having him blocking guys like Tavius Robinson (on IR for weeks and still more sacks than Hendrickson) in 2027 make sense? And what about the growth of DeCosta’s latest day-two pass rush reach (my does the epic list of failures here run long ) Zion Young, and Green, too?
And if you are scoring at home, the Ravens are getting real low on draft capital after panic moves for Cam Jurgens (we told you that was an all-time laugher in real-time ) and Jacoby Brissett. They need picks, badly. And with DeCosta’s draft record so poor, they really need all the picks they can get. And with so many bad contracts they don't have many they can get anything back for.
As one GM said: "(Hendrickson contract) looks terrible now, and it was questionable when they did it, especially after the Crosby thing ... Could (Hendrickson) get one, year, $30M, fully guaranteed, right now, coming off this, if he was a UFA (unrestricted free agent)?"
Yeah, trading him now will only save $2M against the cap next year, but every penny helps especially if they have to carry Jackson into the league year at $84M. This team is stuck with basically $100M in cap/dead cap tied up in Andrews, Humphrey, Simpson, Smith, Ronnie Stanley, Derrick Henry, Rashod Bateman no matter what they do (designating two as post-June 1 cuts would help some, but not all that much).
If they wait to make a move on Hendrickson until 2027, you are looking at a $25M cap hit and if they deal him now and admit defeat, that number would be $16M for 2027. He hasn’t been the kind of guy who can put together a full season to be worth $30M a year for a while now, and even these masters of gaslighting till have a hard time pretending they have a Lombardi roster next year.
Is that a risk the Ravens should be willing to take again in 2027 with that $29M fully guaranteed? I sure wouldn't.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: What We're Hearing About the Ravens Ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Ravens are a team many opposing front offices are enjoying watch squirm, with their reputation for hubris and stubbornness – much like the Orioles – catching up to them.
And with the franchise carrying one of the least enviable payroll, roster and contractual situations into the trade deadline next week, they are going to get solicited for select veterans. Whether they think its beneath them or not.
At 4-5, in a four-game losing, allowing 33 points or more in three straight games with one of the worst defenses on the planet and going four in a row failing to score even 14 points for the first time in franchise history with a rookie coordinator they called a genius all summer, they are going nowhere. Two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson has them completely by the throat with how his contract is structured ($84M cap hit next season with a no-trade and no-tag provision) and they not only have the worst salary cap situation in the NFL right now, they have by far the worst projected cap in 2027.
And there are no easy solutions until or unless they get Jackson extended, and even a trade before June 1 would wreck their cap ($74M cap hit), and a trade after June 1 means they are carrying him into the League Year in March counting $84M against the cap and giving them scant chance to build a roster. NFL GMs are baffled by their trade for Cam Jurgens as we reported on in real-time , and two who have looked at their cap situation believe they are essentially handcuffed in 2027 no matter what they do at this deadline.
“It’s not the worst I’ve ever seen,” one GM said, “but the quarterback (Lamar Jackson) makes it unique. They are at his mercy, really ... They have a bunch of really bad contracts they’re going to have a hard time getting out of. They’re pretty screwed. It’s really bad.”
Our friend Mark Levin, who helped Jackson negotiate his contract extension (and explained the uniqueness of that process on the “The Daily Flock” in May ) while running the salary cap and administration department of the NFL Players Association, is studying the situation for us as well. Levin oversaw the cap for the Washington Commanders prior to that and is a unique expert on these matters and went over every key Ravens contract with us this week.
“It’s definitely a mess,” he said when asked him for some historical perspective on how the Ravens cap currently looks for 2027 and 2028. “I don’t think that I could say I’ve never seen anything like it … But this is not going to be an easy fix. They're in a really tough spot.”
The Ravens can’t restructure their way out of it, the voidable years bills are coming due whether they cut their legion of bad players on bloated contracts or trade what they can, and the league is watching closely while the coaches they fired are exceeding expectations with the Giants and Browns. So what do other execs think that means for the deadline?
The general consensus is that, given general manager Eric DeCosta’s track record and how they are trying to sell this season as not the disaster that it is, and the fact they have some injuries to hide behind, it’s viewed as unlikely they sell close to as aggressively as probably warranted. Owner Steve Bisciotti would have to be fully on board, and DeCosta has already made desperate moves, giving away fourth-round value just Friday to complete a trade for benched journeyman QB Jacoby Brissett.
“DeCosta won’t sell,” said a high-ranking official from a team that has faced the Ravens this season and does not think highly of their talent or contract situation whatsoever. “To him that’s a sign of weakness … He started making panic moves in October. Those guys are completely full of (garbage).”
The GM said: “What do I think he’s going do? He just added Brissett. That’s telling you, isn’t it? … Nobody he thinks he’ll really be a seller. I don’t see it.”
As to who the industry believes the Ravens should move – Derrick Henry top the list . After 17 carries for 57 yards Thursday; right at the abysmal 3.4 yards/carry he has averaged the last four weeks behind a broken offensive line while leading the NFL in carries at age 32, this is over. Multiple execs told me the Ravens could get a fourth-round pick for him, most likely, perhaps with contingencies for more based on his production with the new team.
“It’s not going to work for him there without Lamar,” the exec noted. “They can’t win up front.”
Henry would still count $15M in dead cap next year even if dealt.
The contract makes this complicated – DeCosta really did a number here. Stanley is struggling with penalties and he doesn’t seem comfortable in this new offense and has played unsure. But left tackles with his pedigree aren’t everywhere and there are plenty of contenders who could find a spot for him and maybe some even wondering how he might fare on the right side if need be. Without having to worry about protecting Jackson’s blindside anymore now would be a great time to find out what young tackle Carson Vinson could do.
Our pal Marty Hurney, longtime NFL GM, who joined us on “The Daily Flock” this week, believes the Ravens could get a fourth-round pick for Stanley (assuming teams are okay with medicals; a big issue for him in the past).  Other execs have implied the same, but this is another player the GM has made a favorite over the years, so there is skepticism he’d do what needs to be done. Like the rest of this, we only saw this coming back in the spring ( as explained on April 13) .
Oh, and Stanley will count $28M in deal cap in 2027 if dealt, so there’s that.
He was a bottom 10 starting corner in the NFL last year by any measure and rather than pay him $4M to leave DeCosta paid him $19.3M to obliterate the locker room and secondary yet again. Pays to be a made man! Spoke to a member of the Jaguars organization a little but before Thursday’s game. Here’s what he said:
“We are coming right after 44 (Humphrey). (Head coach) Liam (Coen) is going to attack him. He has a target on his back every week … Everybody threw on him and the other guy (Nate Wiggins) all last year. What are they doing over there?”
Humphrey was beat for 50 yards by a blocking tight end off the jump. Nobody is paying him $7.5M for the rest of the season. I suggested a total salary dump in exchange for reserve QB Joe Milton before the season – that’s how devalued this player is everywhere except in Owings Mills (Jerry Jones might have taken on the salary). And he’ll count $12M against the cap in 2027 even when he’s gone as a free agent (good luck with the comp pick there).
Maybe he wants to stay on this sinking ship in what the 40-year-old said was almost certainly his final NFL season. He is incredibly close with defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver, and loved his first sting in Baltimore, but brings elite leadership and is a world-class teammate and on a functional defense as part of a decent rotation, he can provide value.
“Who wouldn’t want Calais on their football team,” the exec said, noting the return would be minimal.
Campbell would not count against next year’s cap if traded.
The GM said: “He doesn’t do much for me. They like him a lot more than we ever did … I guess you could something for him.” Hurney told us on “The Daily Flock ” this week getting anything for Bateman would be addition by subtraction. A real front office would explore it vigorously and maybe let fourth-round pick Elijah Sarratt actually be active for some of this embarrassing defeats.
Bateman would count $8M in dead cap next year is dealt.
The Ravens are stuck with Mark Andrews ( he can't even handle a direct snap now ) and will have to pay him $5M guaranteed next year no matter what and eat $16M in dead cap to cut him. DeCosta giving him Isaiah Likely's money really blew up in his face.
