title: Ex-Ravens DC Zach Orr Was Flogged Then Fired After 2 Seasons. Jesse Minter's Defense Is Significantly Worse
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens gushed about what a remarkable defensive mind Jesse Minter was when they hired him at age 42, with just two years of experience as an NFL defensive coordinator, to replace John Harbaugh, who is building a credible case for the Hall of Fame and might be the NFL Coach of the Year this season.
They hailed him as a genius of sorts and leaned into to any and all comparisons to true unicorn Mike Macdonald, former Ravens coordinator who went 10-7 as a rookie head coach in Seattle and won the Super Bowl last season. They hailed the fact Minter had Ravens roots – serving as a young assistant in Baltimore before – and therefore was an extension of their culture and winning formula and understood all the vast intricacies of what made them such a first-rate organization.
You see, what owner Steve Bisciotti and team president Sashi Brown and general manager Eric DeCosta were pushing out highly accomplished veteran coaches to hire young, cheap and malleable replacements, the implication was they had all the answers within their front office; these bright young minds coupled with DeCosta’s Lombardi-worthy roster would immediately put them over the top.
“Exciting time for us,” Brown said when introducing Minter as head coach. “Thirty years in the books of Ravens football history here in Baltimore, and we're at an important time for our locker room. We know we have the talent to go out and pursue championships now. When we set out to find our new coach, we wanted to make sure that we were very serious about bringing a great leader, but also a great person to this organization, to our locker room, and we found that in Jesse Minter.”
And indeed, Minter has made a remarkable and indelible imprint in his first nine games on the job  - the season is effectively over in November after four straight ugly defeats, and this product is less professional-grade than before (three QBs hurt on about 12 snaps has to be a record). Minter actually increased the franchise’s already record rate for blowing double-digit, second-half leads to lose. Minter, unquestionably, has made the defense - his calling card and the one thing his very presence was supposed to make demonstrably better – a failure in ways beyond what his predecessor, Zach Orr, dragged for two years by critics before getting fired, could muster.
Minter to this point has been unfit to perform either duty he was hired for, things are only getting worse, and everything about his messaging and lack of accountability and pathetic lowering of standards from week to week to try to obfuscate from just what an abomination this is should be beneath this once-proud franchise. Instead it captures exactly what DeCosta and Brown have constructed – with the worst cap situation in the NFL for years to come it will get worse . And if the Ravens allow him to keep wearing both hats, and if they abstain from gutting this roster at the trade deadline like any competent staff would spend every waking hour trying to do , it will only reveal even further how detached from reality they are.
“I believe in our guys,“ Minter said when asked about the trade deadline Thursday. “I think that there's a lot of things that we need to look at and improve on, but I do think that we have a team ... In really all three phases, there's spurts of good enough football. There is a real inconsistency, I would say, at all three levels, all three phases. And again, some of that is due to whatever, but that is what it is … I do think there's a good opportunity for this team."
SPURTS OF GOOD ENOUGH FOOTBALL IS THE NEW “PLAY LIKE A RAVEN.”
That’s the best they can offer. Lamar Jackson props them all up, or they fail. Will they allow Minter to be unmasked at two jobs instead of one and will they keep this Frankenstein roster through the deadline and run it back in 2027?
Minter’s defense is quite likely going to get worse, given it already has shown strong quitting tendencies (as former Ravens luminaries have pointed out on social media and as former coordinator Wink Martindale made very clear on “The Daily Flock Show” ). Minter got exposed by Trevor Lawrence on throws of 10 yards or more (8/10 for 193 yards and TD) and passes to the middle of the field (12/14 for 154 yds and TD).
Minter had no solutions; nothing even remotely close (it’s the roster and the culture).
He can’t get $19M corner Marlon Humphrey to cover a glorified tackle eligible 50 yards downfield or a first-round safety, Maliki Starks, who he was supposed to turn into a star in Year Two, to ever make a play on the ball or be the last line of defense when desperately needed. They jumped offside to give Jacksonville a critical fourth-down conversion before falling apart to give the game away in the first half (the penalties are shameful and they lead the league pre-snap – no surprise to regular readers . Their $60M fully guaranteed “closer” Trey Hendrickson was held without a pressure, hurry or hit, let alone a sack, and he can’t play the run and will be 33 next season.
Well, at least he had that revenge game against the Bengals! (If the Raiders keep Maxx Crosby, and Lamar decides to stay in Baltimore, best not dress him for that game with Vegas. Mad Maxx has every reason to hold a grudge against this front office).
And Orr didn’t have a $150M defensive roster and an alleged All-Pro edge rusher; he had Kyle Van Noy and Dre’Mont Jones past their prime. Let’s compare the 2025 and 2026 defenses (and, again, these numbers will get worse this season):
Points/Drive Allowed: 2.20                 2.31
TD% Allowed: 23%                 24%
Opposer Pass Rating: 89.6                 96.1
Pass Plays 25+ (thru 9 G): 17                    18
Yards/Attempt: 7.0                   7.6
INT% : 1.8%                1.4%
Sack %: 4.8%                5.9%
Pressure Rate: 31.7%              35%
Hold up, Orr gets killed for having to blitz to generate any pretend pass rush at all with a decidedly cheaper and lesser roster and he has to survive virtually all of last season without Nnamdi Madubuike after the September injury, and he still outclasses his successor? How's that happen?
Minter is scared to call a game like a big boy and bring any heat, he has Hendrickson and Madubuike and Mike Green in Year Two (another alleged breakout) and Calais Campbell is back and instead of fixing their massive hole at hole in the second round DeCosta give Minter another edge presence, Zion Young, who they called a pass rusher and we told you he was not. (Then DeCosta trades a potential top 40 pick in 2028 for whatever is left of Cam Jurgens, while concussed, right before the Eagles were benching him ).
But this is a first-rate operation. Surely not just an attempt to stay in power.
And Minter barely has a better sack rate or pressure rate than Orr despite all of that, and he wants to play dime all the time and zone it up because he is prettified of allowing big plays … and he has arguably the worst second-half big play defense in the NFL despite all those 10-point leads and has allowed more passes of 25 yards or more at this stage of the season than Orr despite not playing a playoff team schedule like Orr did and getting mostly garbage QBs so far.
This is a complete and total disaster, folks, and he is trying to push some narrative about SPURTS OF GOOD ENOUGH FOOTBALL. (Am I the only one who immediately flashes to Richard Hell And The Voidoids ? Probably)
When are these spurts and how long do they last? How do we make the more consistent?
They never seem to occur when ish gets real. Not for his garbage defense. Not nearly enough.
Zach Orr wasn’t the problem, just like Chuck Pagano and Dean Pees, brought in to help him, weren’t the problem. And Minter, with a staff that includes his dad but no former NFL head coaches ( by design ) ain’t fixing it, either. title: Ravens Coach Jesse Minter Must Cede Play Calling Duties: And 3 Other Takeaways From Thursday's Debacle
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will need a full reboot on defense for 2027, and they have truly needed one since losing the AFC Championship Game in 2023, and Thursday night’s shameful display should provide all the data points any reasonable front office would need to start dismembering this roster ahead of next week’s trade deadline.
The defense is a joke, allowing over eight yards per play in the first half and free runners all over the middle of the field and no semblance of a pass rush. Rookie head coach Jesse Minter looks like a foil for a power-hungry front office, and pushing out John Harbaugh to hire someone failing miserably as a head coach and a defensive coordinator is quite a trick. Baltimore lost for the fourth straight game, with undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano pretending to play quarterback this time; they head to Week 10 with two AFC victories all season (horrible Colts and Titans) and they have become an utterly noncompetitive football entity.
Losing Lamar Jackson for the season (he isn’t coming back to play meaningless games after going to IR with a thumb injury) isn’t the problem The defense that is stocked with bad football players (far too many either overpaid by failed GM Eric DeCosta or over-drafted by him or both). Minter has made them worse than they were under scapegoat coordinator Zach Orr the last two years and there is no reason for hope.
Malaki Starks, a supposed difference maker, got destroyed when he actually had to show up in coverage, on a 50-yard TD pass to Parker Washington that made it 17-3 at the end of the first half and effective ended this game. The final was 33-10 at M&T Bank Stadium, Baltimore (4-5) has now won three times in its last 12 home games and is 6-9 since last Thanksgiving and has been utterly noncompetitive against winning teams for years.
“Obviously, the results are not acceptable,” Minter said amid many rambling answers in which if he wasn’t excusing a lot of this garbage he was coming closer to it than he should.
Here’s what we learned from this slopfest, in which Kyle Hamilton left and did not return (Minter said he didn't have an update):
Derrick Henry running the Wild Cat is cute, but Jacoby Brissett, who just lost his job to Gardner Minshew and couldn’t function against the woeful Cowboys defense is fixing nothing. The Ravens have a lot of time between now and Tuesday afternoon’s deadline to make the decisions that need to be made.
Henry has to go . Ronnie Stanley, a middling left tackle nearing the end of his career, should go if at all possible . Calais Campbell, 40, is wasting the final year of his career here. Rashod Bateman should have been gone years ago. DeCosta having the guts to lecture the media and fans on how Marlon Humphrey (he is getting clowned by former Ravens players and coaches all over the country) was a $19M corner was something. Humphrey got picked on immediately in this game and has to be benched for TJ Tampa ( no one is trading for Humphrey , who got beat by a blocking TE for a 50 yard gain to open the game, seriously).
This is an unserious franchise that seems to take its fans for fools. I expect zero accountability from the failed GM or his boss, the billionaire owner who couldn't be bothered to do much during the coaching search. But if they don’t starting trying to reposition this franchise before they host the Chargers on Monday Night Football, it’s a new low.
Minter delivered a dissertation about this team not being as awful as it clearly is when asked about direction at the deadline, which sums up their general MO when it comes to what they sell in Owings Mills, and reality.
If your players are going to quiet quit from week to week, and the Ravens won’t admit defeat that they put together a cheap and naïve coaching staff (only the Ravens and Dolphins had no former NFL head coaches employed ) and they won’t bring in former head coaches to help Minter, then it's time to let defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver do the job and call the defense.
Minter has been a barely-functional head coach. He needs to learn how to have a spine and hold players accountable and establish protocols and standards in practices and games. He can’t be trying to fix a defense he keeps breaking at the same time. Pick a lane, but Minter has been an unquestioned disaster to this point.
They gave up 223 yards in the first half in the rain, at home, and had an 11% pressure rate (impossible, right?) with their alleged “closer,” $30M a year pass rusher Trey Hendrickson made no impact, again. This after having Josh Allen and Joe Burrow have perfect passer ratings in the second half against them the previous two weeks, and Deshaun Watson overcoming a 10-point lead in the second half to blow that game.
DeCosta wanted a novice after winning the power struggle with Harbaugh after last year’s pathetic season. He got it. The middle of the field was open the entire game and the defense has no soul.
Part of the reason Minter looks out of his depth is because he can’t command a presence from this team and get them to focus and show attention to detail. Not with this crew.
They had a silly penalty on a return on special teams to back up Fagnano way deeper than he needed to be. They jumped offsides on a fourth-and-short when this was still a football game to give Jacksonville a big first down. They had false starts on successive plays in the first half, with veteran tight end Mark Andrews ( a colossal DeCosta mistake who did nothing of note again and botched a direct snap) committing the second one – he leads all tight ends in that category and in drop percentage.
In a desperate spot to start the second half … we got yet another brutal false start to further compromise a QB who was not ready for this assignment. But when your most overpaid players are also your worst players, and they are never held to account, then why wouldn’t these issues permeate the entire roster ? A fumble on a kickoff return was a nice touch, too.
"It's ownership of players and coaches that keep happening … the pre-snap penalties are unnaceptable," Minter offered. Funny thing is they are acceptable but the biggest culprits - Andrews and Stanley - are made men from the GM and beyond reproach, apparently.
After the rookie offensive coordinator badly embarrassed himself and the entire organization with ridiculous play calling Sunday in playing a key role in his quarterback room getting decimated, Doyle finally grasped the severity of the situation Thursday.
He was committed to Wild Cat and gimmick plays and throws behind the line of scrimmage. He leaned heavily into tackle eligible and 13 personnel (three tight ends), trying to bleed the clock and keep this game as close as he could for as long as he could. Made sense, especially with Fagnano’s right ankle heavily taped in the rain.
Still wasn’t nearly enough, but at least he tried this time. Once the Jaguars opened up a 14-point lead Fagnano had to drop back (he threw one pass beyond the line of scrimmage in the first quarter) and he was under constant duress and it just got uglier from there.
Fagnano is incredibly raw and limited and even with a rudimentary game plan and all that scheming, in a short week he had no chance against this defense. Fagnano was quite poor in the second half. Brissett will start in primetime for this fallen franchise next.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Four Ways Ravens Offense Needs To Adjust Without A Mobile Quarterback Moving Forward
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will be without the greatest dual-threat quarterback in NFL history for the foreseeable future and potentially the remainder of the 2026 season. On their first offensive play in a Week 8 road loss to the Buffalo Bills , two-time league MVP Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that will require surgery.
This setback officially landed him, as well as his primary backup, Tyler Huntley, who suffered a significant turf toe injury in the same game, on injured reserve on Thursday . Both signal callers will require surgery to address their respective physical ailments.
While the Ravens are slated to start undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football on a short week, they are reportedly finalizing a trade to acquire journeyman veteran Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals.
Bringing in the well-traveled career backup and occasional spot-starter gives the Ravens a proven commodity under center with ties to the coaching staff, as he played under current quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork last year in Arizona. What it doesn't provide is a player at the position who is anywhere near a threat in the run game, like Jackson or even Huntley.
This means that the Ravens and first-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle will need to adapt their plan of attack moving forward to better suit the strengths of their current quarterback room with Brissett and Fagnano, who is also more of a traditional pocket passer. Here are four key adjustments they need to make to give the offense its best chance to thrive without the greatest force multiplier in the game for the time being, and possibly the rest of the season.
The Ravens' rushing attack has struggled mightily to run the ball with any consistency and gain consistent traction on the ground over the past three weeks after posting a season-high 208 rushing yards in their first game without Jackson, following his high ankle sprain. They've averaged just 82 rushing yards during their three-game losing streak and will need to make five-time Pro Bowl running back Derrick Henry even more of a focal point of their offensive approach moving forward. The future Hall of Famer has been the subject of several trade rumors since Jackson's injury, but with him gone, Henry is the last star left standing in the Ravens' backfield.
No matter who is under center for this team for the rest of the season, Henry should be carrying the ball early and often, especially now that the offensive line is getting healthier and building more cohesion, with first-round rookie Vega Ioane slated to return from a one-week absence and two-time Pro Bowl center Cam Jurgens getting more acclimated since being acquired via trade.
Despite not having Jackson's electric mobility at their disposal, they still have several playmakers on that side of the ball who can make explosive plays in space with the ball in their hands. At the top of that list is two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers, who, even after being held without a catch for the first time in his four-year career last week, still ranks eighth in the league in receiving yards. Since losing veteran blocking specialist tight end Durham Smythe to a season-ending torn Achilles, trying to run the ball or just simply operate out of multiple tight end sets, especially out of condensed formations, has been inefficient and downright futile far too often.
The Ravens should still keep the under center element in their offense to preserve and amplify the threat of play-action, but as far as personnel packages go, they should look to spread their formations out with multiple receiver sets. It'll force opposing defenses to have more ground to cover, lighten the boxes Henry has to run into at the line of scrimmage, and get more explosive wideouts such as veteran Rashod Bateman, rookie Ja'Kobi Lane and third-year pro Devontez Walker the ball more.
After having three quarterbacks go down in one game due to poor pass protection just four days ago, including the face of the franchise, the Ravens' offensive line can't be trusted to hold up for deep dropbacks or handle basic stunts, twists and blitzes until they prove otherwise. Doyle should be dialing up quick-developing plays and overemphasizing the necessity for his quarterbacks to not hold onto the ball too long after seeing two of them get strip-sacked this past Sunday. His screen designs and sequencing have been one of the most impressive aspects of his new offense this year. Leaning more into getting his dynamic receivers, running backs and tight ends in space with convoys in front of them should increase even more.
While the soon-to-be 34-year-old Brissett isn't nearly as fleet of foot as the Ravens' injured first and second-string quarterbacks, he is among the best in the league at using his legs to pick up first downs on sneaks. Baltimore's struggles to convert on third and fourth and short are a major reason why they've struggled to sustain drives and finish them in the end zone without Jackson under center, dating back to last year.
Brissett leads the NFL with 17 quarterback sneaks, four more than the Bills' Josh Allen, and is responsible for picking up 16 first downs and scoring a touchdown rushing through eight games. Having him lined up behind Jurgens, who successfully ran the famous 'Tush Push' play with Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia Eagles, should be the Ravens' go-to play anytime they find themselves needing two or fewer yards to move the chains. Against the Jaguars this week, with Fagnano on a bad ankle, the Ravens should line up one of their tight ends under center in those situations.

title: One Move The Ravens Can't Afford To Get Wrong At The NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Ravens can be myopic and simplistic and sophomoric, and that's been their brand the further removed they are from their heyday under legendary general manager Ozzie Newsome.
They can keep pretending that people like Eric DeCosta, who made a career getting promotions by leveraging Newsome’s accomplishments , have this team on the cusp of a Super Bowl or get real about an aging and bloated payroll, the worst salary cap situation in the NFL for 2027 ( it’s not even close ) and another showdown looming with two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson, whose contract talks they have butchered since the became eligible for his first extension back in 2020, and who can decide whatever he wants in 2027 by virtue of some of the more unique contract language in the NFL ( as explained thoroughly here) .
They can come to grips with the fact they enter Thursday night’s home game against Jacksonville as 10-point dogs for a reason, and that blowing 17 double-digit leads in the second half to lose since DeCosta took over for Newsome is not some fluke. They should get real about the fact that come midnight, they’ll likely be 3-9 in their last 12 games at M&T Bank Stadium and 6-9 since last Thanksgiving. As it stands now, they are 3-7 in their last 10 against winning teams and win 33% of their games during Jackson’s tenure when he doesn’t start and he’s not throwing another pass this season with the way to rest of this will play out.
So the biggest mistake for them to avoid is simple.
It’s the same mistake they keep making when the owner fired a Hall of Fame coach to replace him with a total start-up to produce the worst second-half football in the NFL, but implied it’s a Super Bowl roster and called DeCosta the best GM in the league and said he “bats .800” in his personnel transactions so who cares about the whiffs. The team president said Minter had the immediate pedigree to keep them on their Lombardi path and DeCosta thumped his chest about his offensive line and ability to get Jackson signed and how Marlon Humphrey was worth $19M when he spoke before the season began.
The biggest mistake they can’t make is to continue to believe their own self-aggrandizing and self-mythologizing and do something about embracing change and fixing their cultural disease for once. The biggest mistake they can’t make is try to continue gaslighting and obfuscating the fans and taking them for fools, rather than actually start repositioning the team for the future.
It will be next to impossible, mind you, given the abysmal way they structure contracts and how DeCosta plays favorites with who he overpays. They are going to stink for years to come no matter what they do now. But if things are ever going to change here – they won’t, by the way, with these people in charge (it’s tragically similar to the Orioles across the board) – waiting til the offseason serves no one . For a multitude of reasons.
This ain’t much, especially consider this is a $370M payroll that, according to Bisciotti, is the envy of football with a true mastermind managing it. The Ravens are remarkably screwed this offseason, and punting all of this til January because of optics and trying to protect their alleged reputation (many in the NFL believed DeCosta is vastly over his skis before he took the reigns) strains their covenant with the people who make all of this possible.
And, yeah, this sell-off should include Bisciotti selling the team, cashing his chips, and finding a motivated and hungry and focused and sharp new steward of the franchise, like he used to be. But that was a long time ago, now. Start with moving Derrick Henry and do whatever you can to get something for Ronnie Stanley, too.
It’s imperative there is a runway to finding out if Trenton Simpson or Teddye Buchanan can wear the green dot and replace Roquan Smith who hasn’t been an impact football player since DeCosta vastly overpaid him. This is a blight and embarrassment either way, but we knew they are too prideful to bench him, and no one wants anything to do with this contract. They can spite themselves and their future by playing silly games. We’ll see how it plays out.
Same needs to start happening with tackle Carson Vinson and tight end Matthew Hibner and receiver Elijah Sarratt (going to make your fourth-round pick inactive on a terrible offense every week in a seven-win-at-best season?). It needs to happen for young vets like corner TJ Tampa, and receiver Devontez Walker with a long runway as a starter.
You know how you start to clean up a culture of entitlement and quitting in the second half and showing no pride at home and empowering losing football players who seem to enjoy trolling Ravens fans more than actually doing their jobs (Humphrey) – you admit it is your brand and you hold people accountable. I know it’s tough when the head coach comes off as a puppet (well) and the offensive coordinator also seems horribly out of his depth , but if you don’t want the locker room walking all over them forever, you do something now.
Call out the player stupidity and lack of effort at times, and get a former NFL head coach here to start coaching up your coaches on how to lead and message properly. Bench people immediately, in game (I know DeCosta must be an annoyance on the sidelines, but he can’t stop you from doing the right thing in-game). The longer you continue this charade – and keeping all of your biggest mistakes past the deadline would be the most pathetic thing possible – the worse it will only become.

title: Ravens Week 8 Rookie Report: Undrafted QB Sees First Regular Season Action Under Dire Circumstances
full_text:
Several members of the Baltimore Ravens' 2026 rookie class saw extended action in Sunday's 36-10 road loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 8. They are in an AFC North division in which every other team has a record above .500, and after falling to 4-4, they deservedly sit at the bottom of the standings heading into next week.
Drafted and undrafted first-year players saw extensive playing time in all three phases. First-round stud interior offensive lineman Olaivavega Ioane missed his first game with an MCL sprain. The only rookies who were healthy scratches were fourth-round wide receiver Elijah Sarratt and fifth-round cornerback Chandler Rivers. Fifth-round running back Adam Randall wasn't activated from short-term injured reserve in his fourth week of eligibility and seventh-round defensive tackle Rayshaun Benny is on the practice squad and has yet to be elevated.
Here’s an overview of how these rookies performed in their late taste of NFL regular-season action.
While the undrafted rookie had dressed for each of the Ravens' first seven games, it was as the emergency No. 3 quarterback, and in this game, it didn't even take a full half for his services to be needed after both of the team's veterans got hurt . Fagnano checked into the game for the offense's second drive of the second quarter and had an exciting start with back-to-back completions of 10-plus yards and then it kind of went downhill from there, largely due to poor pass protection.
Nonetheless, the preseason darling who earned his way onto the roster showed a lot of grit and toughness as he eventually got banged up with an ankle injury before this one was over, getting sacked three times. Fagnano finished 10-of-21 for 91 passing yards and an ill-advised interception off a tipped pass while he was staring down his intended target. The most impressive throw of his regular-season debut performance was a 22-yard completion to wide receiver Rashod Bateman on a key third down in the third quarter that he threw with anticipation and had 15 yards tacked onto the chunk play after he got taken out by the knees by Bills defensive tackle Ed Oliver.
Joe Fagnano with a very nice anticipation throw outside the numbers here. If he can make this throw, he can make all the throws. Give him protection and he'll be just fine. pic.twitter.com/CuEoaASCbq
The second-rounder saw the sharp uptick in playing time on defense that many expected after the Ravens lost sack leader and stout run-defending fourth-year pro Tavius Robinson to a season-ending pectoral injury. Young's 35 defensive snaps set a new career high and accounted for 42.7% of the team total, and he played a key role in limiting the Bills' rushing attack to just 3.7 yards per rush with how well he set the edge and forced runs back inside. He finished with an assisted tackle on Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen on a quarterback sneak for no gain on third and short. Young was the Ravens' highest-graded rookie defender and second-highest overall, according to Pro Football Focus , with a grade of 71.8.
Decade long starter in the NFL pic.twitter.com/Kje0Z148Lh
With all the turnover at the quarterback position, the third-rounder didn't get many chances to make many plays in the passing game. He hauled in his lone target for 13 yards and a first down before getting pushed after moving the ball deep into the red zone to the Buffalo seven-yard line.
The fourth-rounder played the second-fewest offensive snaps of the season in his second week back from a hand injury. Hibner was targeted as a pass-catcher for the first time in his last three appearances but didn't record a catch. He had an up-and-down performance as a blocker in the running game, helping spring Derrick Henry for the Ravens' only touchdown of the game and struggling to execute other insert blocks fully.
Nice cleanup block by Matt Hibner, giving Derrick Henry room to cut back for the TD. pic.twitter.com/fdrWadzTxp
The fifth-rounder played his fewest offensive snaps since Week 2 for the second week in a row with 13, and once again, that didn't stop him from making his presence felt as he recorded at least one catch in his fourth straight game. He reeled in one of his two targets for 15 yards on a diving catch for Fagnano's first completion. Cuevas was overthrown by primary backup quarterback Tyler Huntley on his first target and finished as the Ravens' highest-graded rookie and overall offensive player per PFF, with an overall grade of 84.7.
The sixth-round specialist had a strong outing with five punts for 249 yards, including a season-high average of 49.8 yards per punt and a long of 62, tying for his longest of the season. Eckley didn't have any touchbacks and was able to pin the Bills back inside their own 20-yard line twice.
You have to look pretty hard for a silver lining with the Ravens right now. But I’ve found one. With Lamar Jackson out, we’re likely to punt more. That’ll give Ryan Eckley the reps he needs to settle in and find the consistency his game needs to truly succeed at the NFL level! pic.twitter.com/V4pcUK5ZZT
The undrafted free agent saw double his previous career-high in defensive snaps played with 34, which accounted for 41.5% of the team's total, and his 22 snaps on special teams ranked first among all rookies and was the second-most on the team. He has upside.

title: The Ravens Anointed Trey Hendrickson As A $30M/Year Closer. Turns Out He's An Opener
full_text:
When the Ravens got embarrassed by the Bills on Sunday, their second-half defense, worst in the NFL, up to its usual antics, coaches and execs around the league took note.
The Ravens lack of pass protection and competent play calling had a role in three quarterbacks getting injured in about a 12-play span – highly unusual stuff – and once again they had been unable to stop an opponent from marching all over the field on them after halftime, the same collapsing, listless unit that has been torpedoing this franchise for years. All of that was supposed to change, of course, after firing a legion of respected coaches, hiring young defensive wizard Jesse Minter as head coach/defensive play caller and, after raising the ire of folks around the NFL with the shady way they withdrew from a blockbuster trade for Maxx Crosby then giving Trey Hendrickson $60M for two years to attack the quarterback.
Minter immediately coronated the 32-year-old his “closer” with a checkered recent injury history and an ugly end to his esteemed Bengals career with holdouts and hold-ins and not a lot of impact football lately. There were plenty of reasons Hendrickson’s market was soft, allowing Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta’s stunt withdraw from the trade over alleged health concerns, and then having the audacity to claim to his fans that he had plans to land both payers.
On Sunday night, after that 36-10 defeat with the Bills averaging 7.5 yards/play in the second half and with Josh Allen under no duress like so many opposing QBs before him, one NFL GM noted the Ravens might be getting what was coming to them. “Karma,” he noted from how they handled Crosby. A longtime NFL head coach who was watching, used the same word: “Karma is real,” he noted.
Whether karma or not, Year 1 with Hendrickson has been a disaster.
He has been a no-show in the fourth quarter all season, and by Week 9, that season is effectively over. Whatever he does from here on out – extended garbage time – is tainted. Rather than put games away, the Ravens have extended their pathetic run of getting DeCosta-ed – blowing double-digit leads in the second half to lose. Hendrickson has been the antithesis of an opener; like his rookie head coach he has been a no-show when it matters most.
The Raiders have to pry Crosby off the field; Hendrickson got hurt in his first game for Baltimore, his production tailed, he missed time with a surgical procedure, and he has as many sacks as Roquan Smith (two). He hasn’t has an impact moment, he was absolutely shutdown and invisible in his big “revenge’ game with the Bengals, and the Ravens better hope he isn’t aging fast, and has a resurgence next year, because, again, 2026 is a wrap (and DeCosta should he trading veterans).
We’ve been suggesting for weeks on “The Daily Flock Show” how the Ravens should handle this. Maybe they’ll start to adjust. You’d think allowing the most points of any team in the second half, and the second-highest passer rating, and second most big plays and ranking 30th in yards per play might prompt somebody there to try something else.
Here’s what they need to do:
Hendrickson is generating a pass-rush rate near 21% in the first half of games. In the fourth quarter, he has just five pressures on 43 pass rush reps, a woeful 12%. The Ravens have three fourth-quarter sacks as a team (Ethan Burke, undrafted free agent, safety Malaki Starks and Tavius Ronbinson, on IR but still leading the team in sacks.
It’s not like Hendrickson is taking games over early, but he is definitely effective. The injury is probably a big deal, so then get him on more of a pitch count, and be willing to blitz more to keep him fresh. His age was a serious concern for teams in free agency. He isn’t getting home late in games, and he isn’t opening things up for others; the Ravens rank 27th in pressure rate as a team in the fourth quarter.
They need to ration his pass-rushh reps better and accept that he'd probably a designated pass rusher, no matter how much they paid him.
DeCosta made a big reach in the second round for edge run-defender, Zion Young, rather than address his massive center need (he could have had his pick). He needs to have the guts to pay him on run downs or just early downs in general, and stop pretending Hendrickson is something he’s not. He’s never been good against the run.
Longtime Ravens defensive coordinator Wink Martindale – very familiar with Hendrickson and the person who created the defense Minter is running, cut to the quick with what he sees on the film:
“Going against him when he was with the Bengals I think he is a very good pass rusher, and that's it,” Martindale told me on the show . “That's what he is. I think he's a third down, second-and-long type guy because he wants to get to the quarterback. The problem is, when they're playing in these games, especially with (backup) Snoop (Huntley) at quarterback, they've got the whole playbook that they're facing.
“They're not getting leads where people have to throw the ball to get back in the game. And when you get selfish, and you're rushing a passer on a run play, it exposes players. And that's what I'm seeing. That's what I'm seeing with him.”
Teams are going to start road grading the Ravens more and the Ravens aren’t going to win many games, so that closer stuff is basically out the door, anyway. They aren’t getting $10M out of Hendrickson this year, let alone $30M, and they are stuck with it all over again next season. Better find a way to make this age gracefully, while Crosby remains one of the unique every-down edge defenders in the NFL, and incredibly durable at that.
Turns out the Ravens started getting De Costa-ed even before the season began.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Bills' Final Week 9 Injury Report: DJ Moore Cleared, Two OL Starters Questionable
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills ' official injury report took up an entire page with 19 active players listed in Week 9 .
While wide receiver Josh Palmer, who pulled his hamstring last time out, has been ruled out for the November 9 primetime visit to the Minnesota Vikings, three others carry a questionable tag heading into Monday Night Football.
In addition to rotational defensive tackle Greg Gaines, who injured his calf in practice more than one week ago, the left side of the Bills' offensive line is questionable to play.
Starting left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson are fighting through injuries that occurred against the Baltimore Ravens on November 1.
As a result, neither hog molly recorded a full practice this past week, and the Bills could be missing one, if not both, against a Vikings' pass rush that gets home more frequently than any other unit in the NFL. Minnesota records a sack on 12.32 percent of all pass attempts.
Surprisingly, Dawkins was absent from practice again on Saturday after back-to-back misses on Thursday and Friday. Three consecutive missed practices usually lead to being scratched on game day, although Dawkins is listed as questionable to play.
With Dawkins sounding slightly optimistic while addressing reporters on Friday, it seemed as if the blindside protector would finally practice in a some capacity as he fights through a ribs injury. Therefore, Saturday's practice status is cause for concern when it comes to his Week 9 availability.
"I feel good," said Dawkins after Friday's practice. "I've been winning my battles off of the field to try my best to be available on Monday."
There is a reality where all parties feel comfortable with Dawkins, who has missed only two careers starts due to injury, playing despite zero practice reps. If he physically capable, head coach Joe Brady isn't concerned about the bookend's lack of reps during the week.
"Some of these guys have played so much football, I have a trust that they know what their assignment is and that they can handle it," said Brady on Saturday. "Had a conversation with Dion earlier in the week, and was like 'hey, let's do what we gotta do to be able to get to the game.' We'll continue to evaluate and play on Monday."
Upgraded to limited participation on Saturday, Anderson also carries a questionable tag heading into game day.
The starting left guard injured his ankle on the opening drive against the Ravens in Week 8. He exited following a pass to Khalil Shakir, giving way to veteran Austin Corbett to finish off the touchdown drive.
Anderson, who visited the blue evaluation tent, received clearance to return after missing only two snaps. He finished the game, but reporters apparently spotted the lineman wearing a walking boot on his right foot while leaving the locker room.
The severity of his sprained ankle, which is unknown, will obviously go a long way in determining if Anderson can go on Monday night.
Earlier in the week, there appeared to be a possibility where the Bills were down three starting offensive linemen for their Monday Night Football matchup.
Starting right tackle Spencer Brown, who missed the Week 8 game due to a back flare-up, was still limited in practice. On Saturday, however, Brown improved to full participation.
Brown, who initially suffered the injury on October 12 , has been cleared for Monday night.
With Brown now set to start, backup Tylan Grable will prepare to potentially replace Dawkins at left tackle.
When the practice week kicked off , wide receiver DJ Moore, tight end Dalton Kincaid and wide receiver Keon Coleman were all donning red non-contact jerseys as they fight the effects of upper-body injuries.
Moore is in the late stages of recovery from his shoulder issue that dates back to Week 2 . He also appear to avoid a potential knee injury in the fourth quarter against the Ravens. Moore visited the blue tent following his final catch, but was cleared shortly thereafter.
Kincaid, who finally ditched the red jersey on Friday, is dealing with a ribs/chest injury that emerged during the third quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders on October 18.
Coleman is a new addition this week with a shoulder issue.
All three players don't carry game designations and have been cleared for Week 9.

title: Bills' Kelvin Benjamin Trade Lands Among NFL's Worst Deadline Mistakes
full_text:
With the 2026 NFL trade deadline approaching, Buffalo Bills fans are desperate for their team to make a move. The Bills are 6-1 and currently hold the No. 1 seed in the AFC, but they do have a major weakness that needs to be addressed.
Their pass defense is suspect, at best, and they can use help at safety and cornerback. The good news is that general manager Brandon Beane is reportedly open to making a move, but that doesn't guarantee whatever trade gets done works out.
There's no shortage of deadline deal moves that don't pan out, and Beane was on the wrong side of one of the worst over the past decade. During his first season as the GM in Buffalo, Beane sent a 2018 third-round pick as well as a 2018 seventh-round pick to the Carolina Panthers for wide receiver Kelvin Benjamin. That trade ended up being a bust and Brent Sobleski of Bleacher Report named it among the ten worst deadline deals over the past decade.
As Sobleski writeds, Benjamin showed promise early in his career and seemed to be a perfect ft for the Buffalo offense. Unfortunately, he hardly made an impact and played just 16 games for the Bills.
"Kelvin Benjamin was 26 at the time of the trade. He posted 1,949 receiving yards during his first two healthy seasons. The Panthers had a glut of wide receivers with upside at the time and decided to move the 2014 first-round pick," Sobleski wrote.
"For Buffalo, Benjamin was supposed to be a legitimate X receiver with the size on the outside to consistently create mismatches, particularly in the red zone. However, the version of Benjamin seen earlier in his career never showed up in Buffalo. He caught 39 passes and only two touchdowns in 18 appearances before the Bills released him during the 2018 campaign."
Benjamin, who had 1,008 yards as a rookie in 2014, was signed by the Kansas City Chiefs after the Bills moved on. He appeared in three games with the Chiefs and had just two catches. He attempted a comeback in 2021 with the New York Giants, where he tried out at tight end, but never played in a regular season game again following the short stint in Kansas City.
It was surprising to see how quickly Benjamin fell off following such a promising start to his career.

title: Bills-Ravens Incidents Lead to Multiple Fines for Roquan Smith
full_text:
Josh Allen scored during the first quarter of the Buffalo Bills one-sided victory over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8. That's no surprise, since Allen scores touchdowns at an incredible rate. In fact, he has nine in the first eight games of the season.
What was shocking was the way he had his head completely twisted by Baltimore linebacker Roquan Smith. Even more shocking is the fact that officials missed it entirely, and didn't throw a flag on Smith.
Check out the video below to see just how wild (and obvious) the play was.
Is Josh Allen part owl? Roquan Smith twisted his neck nearly 180 degrees on his touchdown run. #BillsMafia @BuffaloPlus pic.twitter.com/92orE2nEeJ
As expected, the league reviewed the play and on Saturday, Smith was hit with a fine. This was the second time he was penalized for such a play, which means his fine amounted to $17,911.
Roquan Smith of the Ravens was fined $17,911 for his pulling of the helmet/facemask of Bills QB Josh Allen last Sunday," Sal Capaccio wrote on X . "The amount is because it was Smith’s second offense this season. He had previously been fined $11,941 for this same infraction in Week 2."
Bills On SI's Mike Moraitis wrote about the play after it happened and said it was hard to give Smith the benefit of the doubt . The veteran linebacker was fined for his Week 2 face mask on New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough. He wasn't flagged for that play either. Moraitis said he did something similar in 2025 to Los Angeles Rams tight end Davis Allen, which makes it even more difficult to think that Smith isn't playing recklessly.
As is more proof was needed, Sal Capaccio says Smith was hit with a second fine from the same game. Also during the first quarter, Smith hit DJ Moore across the middle. It was deemed Moore was a defenseless player. There was no flag on that play either.
"Smith was ALSO fined an additional $17,911 for a hit on a defenseless player when he hit Bills WR DJ Moore going across the middle in the 1st quarter as the ball was thrown elsewhere," Capaccio wrote .
At this point, it's fair to ask what Smith needs to do to earn a suspension from the league. It's also fair to ask how the refs continue to miss such obvious penalties.

title: Bills-Falcons Trade Proposal Sends Jessie Bates to Buffalo
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have become a team to watch as the 2026 NFL trade deadline approaches. They have one glaring need, with safety standing out as their most concerning position.
Buffalo hoped C.J. Gardner-Johnson would solve their problems at the spot, but he proved to be unreliable and inconsistent. He alsp showed that he can't be trusted when he was suspended for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers, leading to his release following a one-game suspension.
General manager Brandon Beane has been criticized for refusing to pull the trigger on big moves, but there are reports that he could be more aggressive this year at the deadline. If so, PFF's Gordon McGuinness has a dream trade for Beane to consider. McGuinness says the Bills can fill their biggest need by sending a second-round pick to the Atlanta Falcons for safety Jessie Bates III.
McGuinnes says that Bates would be a major swing for the Bills, and while Atlanta hasn't been shopping him, Bates is on an expiring contract. That being the case, there's a chance the 3-5 Falcons could be willing to add draft capital as they look toward the future. For Buffalo, it would mean they could get someone who is far better in coverage than their current options.
"The Bills just released veteran C.J. Gardner-Johnson, and fellow safety Cole Bishop ranks 63rd out of the 80 safeties with at least 200 snaps this season with a 48.3 PFF coverage grade. They also know they are serious Super Bowl contenders with Josh Allen, so a big swing to fix a position of weakness could make sense. Jessie Bates III of the Atlanta Falcons is on an expiring contract, and it's worth seeing if there is a price that makes the Falcons willing to sell at the deadline," McGuinness wrote.
Bates is in the midst of another fantastic season. The ninth-year pro currently has an overall PFF grade of 84.1, which is fourth among all safeties. His coverage grade is what should really appeal to Buffalo, as he enters Week 9 ranked second at the position with an 87.8 .
Giving up a second-round pick for a player who is slated for free agency in the offseason is a tough pill to swallow, but there's no denying that Bates would be a massive upgrade for the Bills. If that's what it takes to get them over the hump in the playoffs, it's a move Beane absolutely must explore.

title: Bills' Biggest Defensive Matchup Could Decide Monday Night Outcome vs. Vikings
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have a tall task awaiting them on Monday night - shutting down All-Pro receiver Justin Jefferson.
Cam Lewis is no longer on the team, but memories of Jefferson's 10 receptions for 193 yards and a score back in 2022, highlighted by a ridiculous one-handed catch, still haunt this Bills vs Vikings matchup.
Now, almost exactly four years later, the teams will face off again, and an already struggling Buffalo defense is going to need a better plan in place to shut down the former Offensive Player of the Year.
Minnesota starting Wentz over Kyler Murray is actually good news for Jefferson and bad news for Buffalo's secondary, as my Bills ON SI co-writer Randy Gurzi described earlier this week .
Over the last two seasons, Jefferson averages 37 more yards per game and 2.36 more yards per target under Wentz than Murray. His 30.4% target share with Wentz also tops the 23.3% share he's seen with Murray this year.
Jefferson's had a modest start to the season (by his standards), recording 28 catches for 335 yards and four touchdowns in six games. Despite the statistical slump, the receiver is still winning at an above average level versus man coverage, and at an elite level versus zone coverage.
His new QB knows he needs to see more targets, saying in a press conference this week that he needs to "just get him the rock. He's as good as I've been around," he continued, "I'm confident he'll get his this week."
Buffalo's CB1 hasn't had his best season to start 2026, but he's still playing at a reasonably high level.
Benford is around 80th percentile in separation allowed and about 55th percentile in on ball grade, both above average numbers for CBs that have played at least 85 snaps this season. He also ranks first in target separation per Player Profiler and fourth in blanket percentage per Fantasy Points Data Suite .
The cornerback is also sixth in shadow rate, highlighted by his matchups against Nico Collins and Brock Bowers specifically. Jim Leonhard has already kept Benford on an island against elite receivers before, so why not do it against Jefferson on Monday night?
The matchup between Jefferson with a Wentz boost and Benford ideally shadowing the All-Pro has the ability to determine the outcome of this Monday night matchup, making it imperative that Leonhard takes advantage of the top tier CB the Bills roster.

title: Bills Trade Rumor Confirms Brandon Beane is Making Calls About Two Positions
full_text:
With just days to go before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, we have some new trade rumors for the Buffalo Bills.
According to The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , the Bills are "in the market, or at least dabbling in the market, for defensive help," which is exactly what Bills fans want to hear.
Jones goes on to add that general manager Brandon Beane has two focuses specifically, including cornerback and safety, and Buffalo's interest in the latter spot was before the release of mercurial safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson.
"The Bills are in the market, or at least dabbling in the market, for defensive help," Jones said.
"I think, specifically, Buffalo would like to add to the defensive backfield. The Bills have made calls on safeties and cornerbacks. The Bills parted ways with C.J. Gardner-Johnson this week, but they were already sniffing around before that transaction."
Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer is reporting the same.
"I had it in my last trade column, and will add it here — The Bills are still looking in to adding a piece on the defensive side of the ball. And specifically at corner and safety," Breer wrote.
We already knew about the focus on defense because we got that straight from the horse's mouth when Beane told the Associated Press' John Wawrow his plans.
"Yeah, I think probably," Beane said when asked if he wanted to add to the defense. "We'll look anywhere that can help us, not just one side of the ball. But I would say where we're at, if you have one bullet, that probably makes more sense there, if it's the right move".
The Bills' defense has been bad this season , so no surprise Beane is looking to make an addition there.
Entering their Week 9 game, the Bills rank 24th in total yards allowed per game, 30th in passing yards and 24th in points.
The release of C.J. Gardner-Johnson no doubt made things worse, but the Bills weren't in great shape even before that move because Gardner-Johnson wasn't playing well this season, and Cole Bishop has only been OK.
Without Gardner-Johnson, the Bills are depending heavily on Damar Hamlin for a bigger role and we know he's not suited for that. Rookie Jalon Kilgore is also in the mix, but his lack of experience makes the rookie a total wild card.
At cornerback, Christian Benford has been disappointing, but we know he isn't going anywhere. The bigger issue is the spot across from him with guys like Davison Igbinosun and Maxwell Hairston.
The former has been up and down and the latter has already lost his starting job, so there isn't much faith there.
The boundary isn't the only spot that could use an addition. Dee Alford hasn't been great in the slot and injuries have been an issue. Buffalo is hoping Te'Cory Couch might be able to step in that role after playing well in Week 8, but that remains to be seen.
Along with cornerback and safety, the Bills should also be looking at making an addition at linebacker, where the team could use a better starting option next to Terrel Bernard.
When it comes to potential cornerback options, our favorite is Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen.
At safety, we like either Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker or Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker. Derwin James of the Los Angeles Chargers would be nice, but it continues to look like the Chargers aren't trading anyone. He's hurt, also.
At linebacker, Jordyn Brooks is the dream addition, but it remains to be seen if the Miami Dolphins would move him, especially to a division rival. Cody Barton of the Titans is another name to keep an eye on as a lesser but still effective potential addition.
Whatever the Bills do, they will have to be conscious of the salary cap, as Buffalo has just $3.9 million in cap space currently.

title: Bills' Week 9 Updated Injury Report: Dalton Kincaid's Huge Step, Two Starters Absent
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills ' official Week 9 injury report has increased to 21 players.
Six of those 21 were unavailable for Friday's practice while four others participated in a limited capacity as the Bills prepare to visit the Minnesota Vikings for Monday Night Football on November 9.
For the second day in a row, starting left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson were absent .
Defensive tackle Greg Gaines, who injured his calf last week in practice, remains out as does wide receiver Josh Palmer. The Bills are expected to be without Palmer for multiple weeks after he pulled him hamstring while running a first-quarter route on November 1 against the Baltimore Ravens.
Special teamer Sam Franklin and wide receiver Khalil Shakir both missed Friday's practice for non-injury related reasons. Franklin was ill while Shakir had a personal matter.
In a positive development for his potential availability, starting right tackle Spencer Brown was a limited participant for the third consecutive practice.
Meanwhile, wide receivers DJ Moore and Keon Coleman practiced in a limited capacity as well. Defensive back Jordan Hancock was limited after the Bills opened his 21-day activation window earlier this week.
Kincaid is nearing full strength, if not there already.
For the first time since tweaking his ribs during the third quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders on October 18, Kincaid recorded full participation at practice. He was officially limited on Thursday before the upgrade on Friday.
Even more encouraging, Kincaid was no longer wearing a red non-contact jersey on the field. Although questionable to face the Ravens in Week 8, the tight end saw 57 percent of snaps en-route to four catches for 86 yards and one touchdown.
Josh Allen. Dalton Kincaid. All Buffalo in this one. BALvsBUF on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/StHo4EOPvC
Moore's shoulder injury continues to linger, but the worst appears to be behind the Bills' top wide receiver.
After missing back-to-badk games heading into the Week 7 bye, Moore return to the starting lineup against the Ravens. Playing 66 percent of snaps, he totales four receptions for 82 yards and one touchdown.
It's certainly good to see Moore's knee not listed on the injury report. He appeared to suffer a hyper extension on his final catch in Week 8, but received clearance following a quick visit to get blue medical tent.
Coleman led all Bills' offensive skill players with 63 reps against the Ravens, but apparently picked up a shoulder injury along the way. He was limited in practice for the second day in a row.
Like Moore, Coleman was seen wearing a red non-contact jersey.
DJ Moore and Keon Coleman in the red pic.twitter.com/2f6AO5ZAsH
It's certainly a bit worrisome for the Bills up front with two starters absent and another limited, especially considering they're set to face the NFL's second-ranked defense.
Although Brown is trending toward availability , back issues are fickle, and plans can change in an instant.
As for the left side of the line, Dawkins appears more likely to be ready by Monday night than Anderson. The left bookend is fighting through a ribs injury that occurred during the first half this past Sunday.
Dawkins did not miss any snaps due to the in-game injury, and he boasts an impressive track record of durability. He's missed only two starts since being drafted in 2017.
"I'm blessed that I'm getting through it. I pushed through it through the Ravens game, and I'm trying to push through it for this game as well," said Dawkins after Friday's practice.
As for Anderson, he's dealing with an ankle injury that popped up on the game's opening possession last time out. He gave way to Austin Corbett for two snaps before returning and finishing the game.
Anderson was reportedly seen wearing a walking boot when leaving the locker room postgame.

title: Bills Could Revisit Familiar Safety Option After Broncos Release
full_text:
As we enter Week 9 , the Buffalo Bills sit atop the AFC with a record of 6-1. Josh Allen and the offense is among the best in the league, but there's still a major concern on the defensive side of the ball.
Buffalo is currently 30th in the NFL against the pass , and while they've seen some improvement at cornerback with Davison Igbinosun trending up lately, the safety position is still suspect. The depth is also more of a problem after they released C.J. Gardner-Johnson , which was 100 percent the right call following his spitting suspension.
With the NFL trade deadline approaching , the calls for Brandon Beane to get aggressive and add a difference-maker have been growing. Beane is apparently open for business , but if he's unable to get a starting-caliber safety, there might be another option on the table. Former Buffalo safety Taylor Rapp, who signed with the Denver Broncos this offseason, was released on Friday.
It might be easy to shake off the idea of bringing Rapp back to Buffalo since he wasn't the same player in Denver that we saw during his three-year stint with the Bills. We shouldn't do that, however, with Beane's track record. Beane loves bringing back players he knows well. Just last season, he signed Tre'Davious White, Jordan Poyer, Gabe Davis, Dane Jackson, and Shaq Lawson to help fill holes.
This year, he signed Kyle Allen as a backup quarterback. Allen was with the Bills in 2023, making this his second stint under Beane. The Bills also recently re-signed White to their practice squad , giving them some much-needed depth at cornerback. His desire to sign players he knows well makes Rapp a realistic option to fill some depth at safety.
Rapp was originally a second-round pick for the Los Angeles Rams in 2019. He spent four years in Los Angeles before signing with Buffalo ahead of the 2023 season.
Now in his eighth year in the NFL, Rapp has appeared in 96 games with 73 starts. He has 502 tackles, 11 tackles for loss, 31 pass breakups, and 12 interceptions in his career. In three games with the Broncos, Rapp has an overall PFF grade of 50.1 and a coverage grade of 54.1.
He's not exactly a game-changer, which is why a reunion should only be on the table if the Bills strike out at the trade deadline.

title: Dion Dawkins Misses Second Bills' Practice, Reveals Injury Status for Monday Night
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have rarely had to worry about left tackle availability since drafting Temple's Dion Dawkins in 2017.
The 32-year-old Dawkins has totaled 150 career regular season appearances, including 144 starts, en-route to five Pro Bowl selections, but his Week 9 status remains up in the air.
As the Bills prepare to visit the Minnesota Vikings for Monday Night Football on November 9, their starting left tackle missed practice for the second day in a row due to a rib injury.
Making matters even more tenuous, starting right tackle Spencer Brown missed the Week 8 game due to a back flare-up, causing backup bookend Tylan Grable to hold down the right side . In a positive development, Brown participated in a limited capacity for the second straight practice.
Still, with only one proven backup (Grable), the Bills would be in a pickle should both Dawkins and Brown be unavailable on Monday in Minnesota.
Despite not practicing on Friday, Dawkins fulfilled his weekly media obligation at the podium.
"I feel good," said Dawkins. "I've been winning my battles off of the field to try my best to be available on Monday."
After listening to his words, there's little doubt that Josh Allen's blindside protector takes pride in being consistently available.
"I've had thousands and thousands of reps on the football field, and I've only missed two games my whole career. The only two games that I missed was one for COVID and one for a concussion. I do anything and everything to try to be as available as possible," said Dawkins, who arrived at training camp in prime physical condition this past summer .
Coincidentally, Dawkins and Brown both missed last year's road game against the Pittsburgh Steelers with the former being concussed. Ryan Van Demark, who is now with the Minnesota Vikings, filled in at left tackle while current starting left guard Alec Anderson replaced Brown on the right side.
The rib issue popped up during the first half against the Baltimore Ravens on November 1.
"It was tough. I think it was at the end of the first quarter, second quarter. I felt it immediately. I was like 'dag, something's up,'" said Dawkins.
Despite the injury, Dawkins did not miss a single snap in the 36-10 win until being removed, along with other starters, for the final possession as the Bills ran out the clock.
"Football comes with its highs and its lows, and you just have to figure out what's the best way to go about it. It was tough pushing through it, but that's ball," said Dawkins.
Although it has been far from an ideal week, the 6-foot-5 bookend sounded semi-hopeful for Monday night.
"Im blessed that I'm getting through it. I pushed through it through the Ravens game, and I'm trying to push through it for this game as well," said Dawkins.
The Bills will visit the Vikings for an 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff on November 9.

title: Former All-Pro Safety 'Saw This Coming' as Bills Cut Bait on CJ Gardner-Johnson
full_text:
Under former head coach Sean McDermott , the Buffalo Bills had the same safety duo for the majority of seven straight seasons from 2017 to 2023.
Former All-Pro defensive backs Micah Hyde and Jordan Poyer, despite being somewhat lesser known names at the time of their signing with the Western New York franchise at the beginning of McDermott’s tenure back in 2017, wound up becoming the definition of what it means to play the position professionally in the National Football League.
And, in addition to their statistical contributions between the white lines, both defenders were leaders for the franchise on and off the field for their entire time on the roster.
In fact, Poyer and Hyde will likely find their names etched somewhere inside the new Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park when all is said and done because their presence within Bills Mafia meant so much to the entire operation .
So, when the Bills seemingly shifted to a completely new dynamic in the backend of the secondary under first-year head coach Joe Brady and new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard this offseason, some people questioned how it would work with a player like veteran C.J. Gardner-Johnson and young Cole Bishop as a pairing.
Well, ultimately—and very clearly—the combination of Bishop and Gardner-Johnson didn’t work , which was part of the reason the Bills chose to release the well-traveled vet prior to Week 9, which leaves Buffalo in an interesting situation moving forward with the season.
In the end, however, the decision to move on from Gardner-Johnson will likely end up being the right plan of attack for Brady, Leonhard, and Co. going into the second half of 2026-2027 campaign . . . even if his replacement isn’t set in stone just yet.
And, apparently, the previously mentioned Poyer agrees with that sentiment.
In an appearance on CBS Sports ’ Just Football on Wednesday, Poyer revealed his thoughts about the recent flip of the script within Buffalo’s secondary, and it’s something he apparently saw written on the wall all the way back in the summer months at St. John Fisher University in Pittsford, New York
“Look, man, I’m not gonna’ lie. I saw this coming in training camp when [Gardner-Johnson] was live streaming during training camp. And, you know, as someone who’s been in that building—who’s been a part of the standard that was there—that was when I almost [thought], like, ‘Okay. What are those conversations going to be like throughout the week, right?'" said Poyer on the CBS show earlier this week.
“I’ve played with Cole [Bishop]. I’ve played with a lot of those guys (on that defense), and communication is huge on the backend of that defense. And, when you watch the Bills play with CJ on the field . . . his style of play just didn’t necessarily fit what the Bills were trying to do in that defense.
"I saw this coming in training camp ..." Former Bill Jordan Poyer breaks down why C.J. Gardner-Johnson didn't fit in Buffalo. #justfootball pic.twitter.com/68mEQwLI3E
“You have to be able to communicate. You have to be able to talk to each other, (and) you have to be able to trust each other. And, it just seemed like there was a boundary—a barrier—between what they were trying to do and what C.J. wanted to do out there on the field. So, I’m not surprised by the move.”
Keeping that in mind, it appears that many Bills’ fans weren’t surprised either. And, the showing on the field from Leonhard’s defense last week against Baltimore, although somewhat skewed , certainly provided plenty of hope that moving on from Gardner-Johnson was indeed the correct choice by Brandon Beane.
Now, the only remaining question seems to be whether or not Beane will choose to pluck a different safety off the trade market to pair with Bishop or if the current crop of available players on the roster are deemed enough for the defense as the calendar turns toward the second full week of November.
Only time will tell, but it’s something to monitor with the trade deadline approaching on Tuesday, November 10.

title: 5 Key Things to Know About Broncos vs. Panthers in Week 9
full_text:
The Denver Broncos defy explanation. Sean Payton’s team entered Week 9 with the league’s 30th-ranked offense and the NFL’s 25th-ranked defense in terms of yards. But the defending AFC West champions simply find a way. Five of the club’s six wins have been by seven points or less. Quarterback Bo Nix has shown a penchant for late-game heroics. After a lopsided 31-10 loss at Kansas City in Week 1, the team has won four straight and six of its last seven games.
At the moment, the defending NFC South champion Carolina Panthers appear headed in the opposite direction. After a 59-37 home loss to the Chicago Bears to kick off the season, Dave Canales’s inconsistent club won three out of four and had few problems putting points on the board.
In their last two games, the Panthers have been outscored a combined 70-32 in losses to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (43-13) and Green Bay Packers (27-19). By all indications, quarterback Bryce Young could be in for a long day against a potent Denver pass rush. He’s been sacked a combined 11 times and committed four turnovers in those aforementioned losses.
However, inconsistency obviously swings bo th ways in what should be a very intriguing interconference tilt. It’s also the debut for defensive line coach Todd Wash as the Panthers’ interim defensive coordinator, who takes over for Ejiro Evero.
Including Denver’s 24-10 victory over Ron Rivera’s Panthers in Super Bowl 50 at Levi’s Stadium, the Broncos own a 7-2 edge in the lifetime standings in a series that dates back to 1997. This marks the third meeting in five years between the club, with Canales’s club falling, 28-14, in 2024 at Denver in the teams’ last encounter. However, the Broncos’ last appearance in Charlotte resulted in a 23-10 setback in 2022.
The final plays of the thriller between the Chiefs and Broncos 👀 pic.twitter.com/D7Ap6b5UPt
Sean Payton’s team owns a 6-2 record but just a plus-7 scoring differential. The Denver offense has scored 17 touchdowns and the Broncos’ defense has allowed 17 offensive TDs. Payton’s gritty team has totaled a combined 99 points in their first three quarters, and scored 73 points in the fourth quarter and overtime.
It would be imperative for Canales’s club to get off to a good start. In their three wins, the Panthers have outscored the opposition a combined 46-26 in the first half and either led or were tied at intermission. In four losses, Carolina has been outscored 94-43 in the first 30 minutes and trailed at the half in each game.
Chuba Hubbard runs it in for 6️⃣ CARvsGB on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ZWJfACla4x
The Broncos have led the league in sacks each of the previous two seasons, totaling 63 QB traps in 2024 and 68 sacks a year ago. This season, Vance Joseph’s defenders have dropped opposing quarterbacks 23 times in eight games (tied for 4th in the NFL). Ironically, Carolina’s Bryce Young has been sacked 23 times.
Injuries saw him take a back seat to Rico Dowdle a year ago. Hence, Chuba Hubbard totaled 134 carries for 511 yards and one TD in 15 regular-season contests (6 starts). In seven games this season, he’s run for 540 yards and five scores on 118 attempts. Denver’s defense is giving up 127.9 rushing yards per game.

title: Will the Panthers Beat the Broncos? Here Are Our Staff Predictions
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have to find a way to win a game. They have lost two in a row in ugly fashion, and they risk this devolving into a totally lost season. Unfortunately, the Denver Broncos and their devil magic are coming to town.
The Panthers are underdogs. No one seems to be willing to predict an upset this week despite the fact that Denver is travelling across the country after an emotional win. Can the Panthers pull it off in Charlotte?
Here's what the Panthers On SI staff thinks.
Five of Denver’s six victories this season have been by seven points or less. And this clash of defending division champions looks like it may be the same.  The Broncos have struggled to run and have had issues stopping the run. Look for a 25-plus carry day from Chuba Hubbard, and for the Broncos’ PK Wil Lutz to miss late on a potential game-winning field goal.
Don't get me wrong, there is a path to victory. If Brad Idzik can scheme up quick passes or have hot routes available for Bryce Young when pressure comes, because it absolutely will, the offense will be fine and can also lean on Chuba Hubbard with a boatload of carries.
On defense, this is actually a good matchup for the Panthers. The Broncos don't have the guns to take advantage of the cornerback depth issues, and Denver hasn't run the ball terribly well all season. The Panthers' weaknesses won't be taken advantage of.
That said, that Broncos defense is really good, and we're not confident Idzik will have the answers all game long. The Broncos have won games they have no business winning all year, and that should continue with some more magic this weekend.
The Panthers have a chance to pull off an upset at home, but their offensive line remains a major concern heading into Sunday’s matchup. Bryce Young has been sacked 11 times over the last two games, and now Carolina faces a Denver defense that has already recorded 23 sacks this season.
The Broncos haven’t exactly been lighting up the scoreboard offensively, so Carolina should have opportunities to keep this game close. However, unless the Panthers can protect Young and avoid costly mistakes, Denver will likely make enough plays to leave Charlotte with the win.
Carolina is in desperation mode this week after two horrendous losses, and yet they face their toughest test yet. The Broncos are tied for the most wins in the AFC and are elite in one area where Carolina struggles most to counter: the pass rush. Bryce Young has his hands full once again; Denver ranks No. 1 in the NFL in pass rush win rate, PFF pass rush grade, and total QB pressures.
Against an offensive line that has been nothing short of abysmal, that matchup could be the deciding factor in the game. Young has to find ways to be productive despite the real possibility of not having any time in the pocket.
Denver’s pass defense is exploitable, and their offense is still figuring itself out. With clean pockets, the Panthers can move the ball on this defense, but the Broncos always seem to figure things out as the game gets into the fourth quarter. Carolina hasn’t shown that they can withstand what’s coming from Denver’s pass rush, and that will be the difference.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: Panthers Coach's Robert Hunt Admission Raises More Questions About Monroe Freeling
full_text:
Carolina Panthers guard Robert Hunt was supposed to be a solid member of the offensive line this year. Unfortunately, the former Pro Bowl player hasn't been able to consistently perform at the same level as he did during previous years with the team.
Carolina Panthers offensive line coach Joe Gilbert said recently that the struggles of veteran guard Robert Hunt are partly due to the adjustment to playing alongside rookie offensive tackle Monroe Freeling.
In 2024, the Carolina Panthers signed guard Robert Hunt to a four-year, $100 million contract. Hunt was a Pro Bowl guard in 2024 but missed almost the entire 2025 season with a torn biceps injury. So far in 2026, Hunt looks like a different player.
Is Robert Hunt struggling on his own, or is it because of the rookie tackle next to him?
Gilbert also noted that Hunt is still adjusting to the young tackle on the line.
"I think part of it goes to working with a young guy with Monroe and getting that comfortability," Gilbert stated.
As noted, Hunt previously lined up next to Taylor Moton, one of the most experienced offensive linemen on the Panthers' roster. Now, Hunt is working with Freeling, a rookie still trying to figure out how to play in the NFL.
The Panthers selected Monroe Freeling with the 19th overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. F reeling was a highly touted offensive tackle prospect out of Georgia. He has a lot of potential, but there is going to be a learning curve for Freeling. He is currently playing tackle for the Panthers, and Carolina needs him to be good while they are trying to win games.
The Panthers are trying to protect Bryce Young and help their running backs find some running room. Right now, the right side of the offensive line is struggling, and that is going to make it even harder for the Panthers to accomplish either of those things.
However, the struggles of Robert Hunt can't be blamed entirely on the rookie, Monroe Freeling. The former Pro Bowl guard is making a lot of money, and the Panthers need more from him than they are currently getting.
There have been some signs of improvement from Hunt in recent weeks, but he still has a ways to go before he is playing at the level Carolina expected when it signed him in free agency.
The Carolina Panthers did not use a first-round pick on Freeling expecting him to become a problem for the rest of the offensive line. They believe Freeling can develop into a reliable starter, but right now, his growing pains seem to be affecting more than just his own performance.
There's time for Freeling to grow, but not forever. If Hunt continues to struggle with Freeling on the line, then the Panthers are going to have to find a way to get both players to perform better.
