title: Panthers' Offensive Line Shakeup Could Put Two Starters on Notice
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have reached the point in the season where something has to change on the offensive line. Bryce Young has been sacked 11 times in the last two games, and the Panthers have struggled to get anything going on offense because of the protection problems.
Panthers On SI's Zach Roberts wrote about some possible changes that the team could look into along the offensive line and even gave his preferred starting five for the Panthers. Now, with Dave Canales considering some different combinations along the line, we take a look at the possible players that could be starting for the Panthers on Sunday against the Broncos.
The Panthers have several options to consider, and some of those decisions will likely depend on the health of Damien Lewis as well as whether or not Brady Christensen is activated for the game on Sunday.
While the Carolina offense has struggled to protect Young in the last two games, the problems have been at more than just one position. Rasheed Walker has struggled at left tackle this season, while Luke Fortner and Robert Hunt have struggled with pressure up the middle as well.
The Panthers are also dealing with injuries to several key players along the offensive line. Taylor Moton is out for the season, while Ikem Ekwonu is still recovering from his knee injury. That has forced the Panthers to insert rookie Monroe Freeling into the starting lineup earlier than they likely would have wanted to.
Christensen has been practicing fully this week as he recovers from a hamstring injury, so there is a chance that he could return to the field for Sunday's game. His ability to play all five positions on the line would give Canales another option.
The Panthers also need to determine the status of guard Damien Lewis for the game against Denver. He was inactive last week and was still missing practice earlier this week. If he is unable to play on Sunday, then the Panthers will have another decision to make regarding the starting five on the offensive line.
The Panthers can't keep doing what they are doing up front. Young has been hit too many times, and the offense can't afford another game in which the line struggles to protect him.
Left tackle: Monroe Freeling
Freeling has been playing right tackle but could move to left tackle in order to give Carolina a look at the rookie at that position. Walker has struggled at left tackle this season, and Carolina needs to consider making a change at that position.
While there will be some growing pains for Freeling, Carolina did draft him in order to help build the future of its offensive line. He has to start somewhere, and giving him a chance at left tackle while Ekwonu recovers from his knee injury is the best way to see what the rookie has to offer.
If Lewis is healthy enough to play against Denver, then he should return to the starting lineup. The Panthers have a lot of problems on the interior of the line, and Lewis would bring some stability to the position.
If Lewis isn't able to play, Corey Bullock could be an option for the Panthers. Bullock returned to full participation in practice this week, which gives Carolina another healthy player to consider. For now, this projection has Lewis returning to the starting lineup.
Sam Hecht could be inserted at center in place of Fortner, but this would create another change on an offensive line that has already dealt with several different combinations this season.
For now, Fortner will remain at center, but that doesn't mean his position is safe for the rest of the season. If the protection problems continue, then the Panthers may have to make a change at center as well as at both tackle positions.
Hunt has not played well this season, and the Panthers are paying him a lot of money to be a good player. Roberts thinks that Christensen should be inserted at right guard, but Canales may not be ready to make that kind of change.
The Panthers have a lot of money tied up in Hunt, and the coaching staff has spoken on numerous occasions about the challenges of building chemistry with different players along the line. It would be very surprising to see the coaching staff bench a player that the Panthers are paying so much money to after only seven games.
But the Panthers have to have better play from Hunt than what he has provided this season. He needs to start playing at the level that the Panthers expected when they signed him to a big contract.
Right tackle: Stone Forsythe
Forsythe would be the best option on the right side of the line if Freeling moves to left tackle. While Forsythe has not been spectacular in his opportunities on the field, the Panthers don't have a lot of options with the healthy tackles that they have on their roster.
This would be a good opportunity for Forsythe to show that he can handle the position while the Panthers wait for Ekwonu to return from his knee injury. It would not be ideal, but then again, what would be?
Brady Christensen is the one player who could throw this entire projection off. He has experience playing all five positions on the line, and that could be very valuable for Canales and the Panthers as they try to find the best lineup.
If Christensen is activated for the game on Sunday, then Canales could use him at guard, center or tackle. This would give the Panthers another option instead of continuing to rely on players who have struggled to protect Young in the last two games.
The Panthers don't have to replace three or four starters on the line in order to improve their offense. They need to find five players who can work together in order to protect Young and allow the running game to get going.
Canales has some difficult decisions to make before Sunday, but the Panthers need better play from the line than what they have shown in the last two games.

title: Todd Wash Takes Over Panthers Defense, but Will Anything Really Change Against Broncos?
full_text:
Sunday, November 8, marks the first time Carolina Panthers interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash will call the plays for the Panthers. While Wash has been with the defense all season, he hasn't had much time to make any changes to the current scheme. Many fans have heard what Wash intends to do with the defense, and on Sunday, they'll see what he actually does with it.
Carolina must stop the run. Right now, the Panthers are allowing an average of 140.7 rushing yards per game. What's worse, other teams know that the Panthers can't stop the run, and they are taking advantage of it. It has been one of the most frustrating things to watch this season.
While many have speculated on the possibility of a change to a 4-3 defense for the Panthers, Wash stated that the Panthers have the personnel to play in a 3-4 defense. While there are several things that Wash could change, trying to completely change the defense in such a short amount of time would likely cause more problems than it would solve.
Wash can implement more four-man fronts in certain situations and have the edge rushers attack instead of dropping back into coverage. It will be interesting to see how much freedom Wash gives his defensive linemen to try to get into the backfield to make plays.
The Panthers have had issues with players not being in the right position to make a tackle or even being able to tackle the ball carrier at times this season. This is a problem regardless of who is calling the plays and something that Wash will have to address.
There is also the question of how much freedom Wash will give his players. He has been with this group of players all season, so he should have a good idea of what they are capable of doing and not doing. On Sunday, fans will see if Wash's approach to the defense will make a difference.
Sean Payton has been in the league long enough to recognize a defense that is struggling to stop the run. If the Denver Broncos are able to gain yards against the Carolina Panthers on the ground, Payton will not hesitate to return to the running game.
Broncos rookie running back Jonah Coleman had 104 yards of total offense in last week's game against the Chiefs, including 41 yards rushing and 63 yards receiving. Coleman can be a factor for the Broncos even when he's not carrying the ball.
The Panthers have many players on defense who will need to step up on Sunday. However, Carolina will need big games from players like Derrick Brown, who can make plays in the backfield but needs the rest of the defensive line to do its job. The linebackers will need to read the play and get to the ball carrier before the running back has gained several yards.
Carolina can't allow five yards on first down and then watch the other team convert on third down after third down. It's frustrating to watch and puts the defense in a tough situation for the rest of the series.
The Panthers' new defensive coordinator knows the problems with the current defense, but will he be able to fix them? The Broncos will not stop running the football just because the Panthers have a new defensive coordinator. If Carolina continues to allow yards on the ground, Payton will continue to take advantage of it.
Broncos quarterback Bo Nix is in his third season with the Broncos, so he's pretty familiar with what Denver's offense is trying to do. This is another area of concern for Carolina, as the Panthers have struggled to put pressure on opposing quarterbacks all season. If Wash is able to get after Nix, it could make things very difficult for Denver's passing attack.
The Panthers have not been able to generate much pressure on opposing quarterbacks this season, so that will be another area for Wash to address. Whether that means bringing extra linebackers or allowing the edge rushers to attack more often remains to be seen.
One of the big problems with the Panthers' defense this season has been giving up big plays. This is something the Broncos' receivers are capable of taking advantage of when a defender gets caught out of position.
A lot will depend on what happens on first down. If Denver is in second-and-short situations all game, Payton will be able to do whatever he wants. However, if the Panthers can force the Broncos into some third-and-long situations, Wash will have more opportunities to get creative with his pressure.
No one expects Wash to turn the Panthers' defense into the No. 1 unit in the league in his first game as defensive coordinator, but there should be some improvement from what Carolina has shown so far this season.
There is still plenty of time for the Panthers to turn their season around and start playing better defensively. Carolina does not have to play a perfect game on Sunday, but it must be able to stop the run, put pressure on the quarterback and avoid giving up easy yards on defense.
Otherwise, the Panthers will be right back in the same situation they were in before Wash was hired.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: Ranking the Panthers’ Top NFL Trade Deadline Targets From Realistic to Delusional
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are in a difficult spot with trades. Sunday's game, win or lose, will tell us a lot about what the Panthers should do at the deadline next week. Before that, though, there are several intriguing candidates on the trade block, allegedly.
So, here are the players we think could be good trade candidates for the Panthers, ranked from most realistic to most delusional.
There are two things that make this almost a no-brainer: the connection and the need. Riq Woolen played on teams that were coached and managed by both Dave Canales and Dan Morgan, so it's clear they know him and know what he can do.
The Panthers have been decimated by injuries at cornerback, and there's no help on the way soon. If there's a move the Panthers might make, it is more than likely this one because of the connection, need, and the fact that Woolen is almost assuredly available.
We love what Josh Downs could bring to the table at wide receiver. He's a man coverage savant, and he'd be an excellent, reliable outlet for Bryce Young when opposing teams bring pressure (which is all the time).
Unfortunately, wide receiver isn't a big need. The Panthers aren't going to invest more in the position when Xavier Legette is coming back soon. So, as much as this makes sense, it's the exact sort of move the Panthers just don't make.
The main problem here is that when healthy, Damien Lewis is elite. And Robert Hunt makes too much to invest more at guard. Unless the Panthers trade Hunt, they aren't bringing in another guard. And they're probably not going to trade Hunt because his value is so low and there's no depth up front.
The same logic sort of applies here. The Panthers need an edge rusher, but they have plenty of bodies and are expecting Jaelan Phillips to return soon. They know the position has been underwhelming, but it doesn't seem like they plan on addressing it externally.
Still, it is a need. The only problem with Josh Sweat is that he's just too good. He's going to be expensive and highly sought-after. Are the Panthers going to win a bidding war with other contenders? They probably won't even engage in one.
Vita Vea is one of the best interior defenders in the NFL. The Panthers need help stopping the run and rushing the passer. Check and check. Vea does both those things and would be an insane force next to Derrick Brown.
The Buccaneers probably won't trade him with the division in sight. They absolutely, unequivocally will not trade him to the division-leading Panthers, though. Maybe Vea is dealt, but it will not be to a division rival. We can dream, though.
Zachary Roberts is a journalist with a wide variety of experience covering basketball, golf, entertainment, video games, music, football, baseball, and hockey. He currently covers Charlotte sports teams and has been featured on Sportskeeda, Yardbarker, MSN, and On SI.

title: 3 Ways the Panthers Can Do the Impossible and Beat the Broncos
full_text:
Coming off two straight horrendous losses , the Carolina Panthers are back home and face their toughest test yet. The Denver Broncos visit Bank of America Stadium for the first time since 2022. Denver is currently tied for the most wins in the AFC, with a 6-2 record entering Week 9.
Carolina is 3-4 and is on the verge of an all-out freefall, with major issues on this roster. The offensive line has been the main issue, with Bryce Young being heavily pressured through the first seven games.
The Panthers are, and deserve to be, underdogs, entering Sunday, and they could pull off one of the weekend's bigger upsets with a win. If Carolina is to do so, three key things need to happen.
If the Panthers roll out the same starting offensive line , that's bad news for Bryce Young. Carolina has allowed the fourth-most pressures, 23 sacks in seven games, and is missing one of its best pieces, Taylor Moton.
The Broncos can take advantage of the poor pass blocking, as they rank eighth in team pressure rate. Denver also has one of the league's best pass rushers in football, Nik Bonitto, who ranks sixth in the league in pass-rush win rate.
Against a team that does so well in pass rush, there's no better time to make a change. Rasheed Walker and Luke Fortner have been especially awful; both lead their positions in pressures allowed. Walker has surrendered 31 pressures; Fortner has surrendered 18.
Carolina needs to see what they have at left tackle in Monroe Freeling. He's been a right tackle all season, but they drafted him for how well he played at left tackle at Georgia.
At center, the Panthers drafted Sam Hecht in the fifth round of the NFL Draft. At Kansas State, Hecht posted over 850 pass-blocking snaps; he allowed zero sacks in those snaps. Yes, the NFL is a different level, but Fortner is already the worst pass-blocking center in the NFL, so it can't get worse.
The last thing Carolina needs is Bo Nix getting outside of the pocket and creating plays with his legs or off-schedule throws. Stopping the run has been an uphill climb for the Panthers overall; adding Nix's scramble ability and him catching a rhythm early would be a death sentence.
Carolina will once again be without Jaelan Phillips, but still needs to find a way to fluster Nix. Inside linebackers Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke have both shown the ability to be disruptive blitzers, that could be a path to disrupting Nix in the pocket.
It may sound weird at first, because Denver has Patrick Surtain II, one of the best corners in football, but this passing defense can be vulnerable.
Denver ranks 20th in passing yards allowed per game, surrendering 227, and 25th in total pass yards allowed this season. Before Week 7, Bryce Young led the league in passing yards per game; if there are any clean pockets, he has to take advantage of them and find his playmakers.
This all hinges on the offensive line, but Young has shown with clean pockets that he can dice up defenses, and that shouldn't change against Denver.

title: Bryce Young Keeps Taking Sacks, but the Numbers Point to a Bigger Panthers Problem
full_text:
Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young has spent plenty of time on the ground this season. Although he is frequently criticized for holding on to the ball too long, the numbers indicate that he is not responsible for most of the sacks he takes.
A chart shared by Patton Analytics using StatRankings data breaks down the sacks taken by starting quarterbacks this season . It shows that Young was responsible for only 17.4% of the sacks he has taken this season.
Young may have done some things wrong, but the Panthers aren’t giving him enough help to succeed.
The Packers hit Young nine times and sacked him six times in the 27-19 loss to Green Bay. For most of the game, the offensive line struggled to protect Young in the pocket.
Young is under a lot of pressure from opposing defenses while also dealing with injuries along the offensive line, including those to Taylor Moton, Ikem Ekwonu and Damien Lewis.
This is also reflected in the distribution of sacks among other quarterbacks. Sam Darnold was responsible for 52.9% of his sacks, while Aaron Rodgers was responsible for 39.1% of his.
Again, the offensive line is not to be blamed for every sack that Young is not responsible for. There are numerous factors that can lead to a sack, including a receiver not getting open, a missed block and the offensive play call.
A good portion of the Panthers’ protection problems appear to go beyond Young. Young is thrown into situations where he is forced to run for his life almost immediately after the snap. In many cases, he is behind the eight ball before the play even gets started.
NFL Next Gen Stats charted Young being pressured on 48.9% of his dropbacks during the game, nearly half of the times that he went back to pass. This was clearly a big problem for the Panthers as they were unable to establish any sort of offensive rhythm.
The responsibility for those sacks shouldn't fall solely on the shoulders of the quarterback. The Panthers’ offensive line has to execute better to protect Young on passing plays.
Young still has to recognize pressure and get rid of the football before a play breaks down. Some of the blame for his play has to go to the offensive line. They have to do a better job of protecting Young on passing plays.
The coaching staff, led by Dave Canales, must find more ways to help Young succeed. That means giving him more protection on passing plays, throwing the ball more quickly, and using different blocking schemes.
That doesn’t mean the Panthers have to completely change up their offensive scheme. Simply getting the ball out of Young’s hands faster or adding another blocker to protect him from the pass rush would help the quarterback.
As Canales noted after the game, Carolina needs to find more answers when opposing defenses are bringing pressure. The Packers used a variety of different looks to get pressure, including four-man rushes that the Panthers struggled to block. Those are the types of situations where the coaching staff has to make adjustments rather than relying on Young to find a way out of trouble on each and every play.
The Panthers have too much invested in Young to keep putting him in situations where he is trying to avoid another sack. Carolina has to give its quarterback a chance to succeed.
While Young isn’t perfect, the numbers suggest that the majority of the sacks he takes are not his fault. The Panthers’ issues with protection must be addressed before they become even more of a problem for the team.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: The Derrick Brown Trade Question Dan Morgan Can't Afford to Get Wrong
full_text:
The Athletic reported Wednesday that the Carolina Panthers have received calls from several teams inquiring about the availability of defensive tackle Derrick Brown. According to reporter Joe Person, however, the team has no interest in trading the Pro Bowl tackle prior to the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
But, as any general manager should, Morgan will have to consider any offers that come in for Brown.
For the Panthers, trading Brown would mean receiving some serious compensation for his services. At 28 years old, Brown is a Pro Bowl player and is under contract until the 2028 season. For teams trying to build out their defensive lines, Brown is a player that can add value for many years to come.
Jacksonville is another team that has reportedly been searching for some defensive line help. The Jaguars have been connected to Brown as well as other defensive tackles. No offer has reportedly been made for Brown by the Jaguars though.
There would need to be several premium picks involved for Morgan to even consider trading Brown. The Panthers currently have several holes to fill on the roster, so more picks in the draft would be very beneficial for the team.
Brown’s contract will cost the Panthers a lot of money in the next few years. Brown signed a four-year, $96 million contract extension with the Panthers in 2024.
Brown’s cap number for 2027 will be $31.4M and for 2028 it will be $32.4M. That’s a lot of money to be paying one defensive tackle and it will limit the Panthers ability to spend elsewhere on the team.
The Panthers could look to move the defensive tackle in order to free up future cap space to spend on other players on the team’s roster. However, that wouldn’t immediately solve the team’s current salary cap woes.
Derrick Brown is a very good player on defense for the Panthers. He is not a sack artist but he is very vital to the Panthers defense as a whole.
Brown is often overlooked as a defensive tackle, as his low number of sacks makes him less noticeable to some fans. But what Brown lacks in sacks, he makes up for as a vital member of the team’s defensive line, helping to control the line of scrimmage for the team.
Brown has 21 tackles, three quarterback hits, and five passes defended through seven games this season. While none of his stats are particularly impressive, Brown’s contributions to the Panthers defense are very important.
Brown is a player that Carolina has already invested a lot of time and money in. Brown was the seventh overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft by the Panthers and signed a major contract extension with the team in 2024.
The other concern with trading Brown is how to replace him. While the team has added some other defensive linemen to the roster, including 2nd round pick Lee Hunter, none of them are guaranteed to be able to replicate Brown’s play for the Panthers.
Removing Brown from the Panthers’ defense would pose a huge challenge for Wash as the team’s interim defensive coordinator.
As the Panthers are trying to develop a team to compete on a week-in, week-out basis, they have already lost a lot of their better players in trades, including Christian McCaffrey, DJ Moore and Brian Burns. Trading Brown could put the team in a similar situation, trying to replace another talented player.
The Panthers can listen to trade offers for Derrick Brown and then say no. Carolina has no reason to trade Brown, unless of course another team makes an offer that is too good to refuse.
First-round picks are still very valuable in today’s game, so a first-round selection would likely need to be included in any offer the Panthers consider for Brown.
Brown is under contract for several more years and is still in the prime of his career. So, if another team is looking to add the Panthers’ defensive tackle, then they must be willing to give up similar value to what the Panthers are losing in Brown.
A first-round pick and more significant draft compensation would be a good starting point for Morgan to consider whether or not a trade would be beneficial to the team in the long run. That is an assessment of Brown's value, not a reported asking price from Carolina.
The other thing to consider is Brown’s contract. Brown’s deal was restructured prior to the start of the season and so the Panthers would have to account for the money already paid to Brown in any potential trade. This would make the financial side of a trade more complicated than simply removing Brown's contract from the roster.
The Panthers are still trying to build a team to compete on a weekly basis, and the player that can be a cornerstone of that defense is Derrick Brown.
Morgan can always look to better the Panthers, even if that means trading some players for more draft picks. But the Panthers also have some good players on their roster that the team should look to keep.
The Panthers do not need to create another hole on defense in order to garner more draft picks to fill said hole.
Unless an offer comes in that Morgan simply cannot say no to, the Panthers should keep Brown on the team and try to build the rest of the defense around him.

title: Khalil Mack Could Give the Panthers a Much-Needed Boost, but the Price Might Be Too High
full_text:
One of the NFL's most accomplished pass rushers could be an option for the Carolina Panthers before the trade deadline. He would immediately fill a need for the Carolina Panthers’ defense. But acquiring Khalil Mack would not be easy for Dan Morgan and the Panthers’ front office.
At 35 years old, Mack is still one of the better pass rushers in the NFL. But the Panthers would need more than just his ability to get to the quarterback over the next couple of months.
According to reports, the Los Angeles Chargers have not shown interest in trading Mack. The team has reportedly refused to trade several of its veteran players, including Mack, who is in the final year of his contract with the team.
Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that he wants Khalil Mack to stay with the team for the rest of the season and believes the veteran pass rusher wants to stay in Los Angeles as well.
But, as with most things in the NFL, situations can change quickly. Mack is in the final year of his contract, and the Chargers could receive something in return for the pass rusher rather than risk losing him in free agency.
NFL.com suggested that an early Day 3 draft pick could be a fair return for Mack’s services. This would likely involve a fourth-round pick being traded for the veteran pass rusher, although it is unclear whether the Chargers would be willing to make such a deal.
While a fourth-round pick would be worth considering for the Panthers, Carolina still has a number of holes to fill and they can’t afford to give away another draft pick for a player who will likely only play in a few games for the team.
A fifth-round pick would be more appropriate for a player of Mack’s age and current contract situation, though that might not be enough to convince the Chargers to make a deal.
The cost to acquire Mack would also include his contract, which is one year and $18 million. Carolina has very little cap space for the current season, according to Over the Cap, leaving Morgan with little financial flexibility to make a deal.
As Over the Cap reports, Mack’s contract with the Chargers is for one year and $18 million. He has an $8 million base salary for the season, and a $10 million signing bonus that the Chargers have already paid. The acquiring team would be on the hook for the remaining unpaid portion of Mack’s base salary for the season.
The amount of the unpaid portion of Mack’s base salary that the acquiring team would be responsible for could be several million dollars. This would likely be too much for the Panthers to handle given their current cap situation of less than $1 million.
Perhaps the Chargers would pay some of the remaining salary before a trade. Perhaps the Panthers can make some moves with some of the players on their roster to free up some space. But those are both big ifs.
Of course, giving up a draft pick for a player to help immediately is one thing. Giving up that pick and then having to make salary cap-related moves to get the player on the field is another.
In addition to acquiring a veteran pass rusher, Carolina would be acquiring a player who can become a free agent at the end of the season. Thus, Carolina would be spending money and draft picks for a short period of time to acquire a veteran pass rusher.
He would be able to give the Panthers another option to create pressure on opposing quarterbacks, even if they aren’t sending extra defenders to the quarterback. This would also allow other players to create pressure on the quarterback, as Mack would draw a lot of attention to the edge.
Mack has three sacks in his seven games this season for the Chargers. While his numbers may not be great, his presence on the field creates opportunities for his teammates and can force opposing offenses to change their game plan.
This would be particularly important for the Panthers right now, as they are suffering from a rash of injuries in the secondary. To have more players up front able to put pressure on the quarterback would allow for the cornerbacks to have more time to cover receivers downfield.
He can also bring a lot of leadership to a young team and help them to prepare for the big games.
But can Mack turn the Panthers’ defense around? No, because he would have to learn the team’s defense and adapt to his teammates. This would have to happen in short order because of Todd Wash taking over as the team’s interim defensive coordinator.
The Panthers are still building their roster and need to acquire several positions through the draft over the next couple of years.
Mack would be a great addition to the Panthers’ defense and Morgan should consider making a trade for the veteran pass rusher if the Chargers are willing to part with him for a fifth-round pick and some of his remaining salary.
A fourth-round pick would be more difficult to justify as the Panthers would need to believe that Mack would provide enough immediate impact to warrant the loss of another draft pick, possibly to be used on a younger player down the road.
If the Chargers want more than a fourth-round pick for Mack then Carolina would be better off looking for help elsewhere and keeping their draft picks.
The biggest issue with trying to trade for Mack is that Los Angeles head coach Jim Harbaugh has already said that he wants the veteran pass rusher to stay with the Chargers for the remainder of the season.
He is a big name and would be a great addition to the team but Morgan must not get caught up in chasing a big name and must make sure that the price is right for a team that is still trying to get better.

title: Bears Trade Deadline Big Board: What Other Moves Could Chicago Make?
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are currently second in the loaded NFC North with a 6-2 record. Even after pulling off a blockbuster trade for defensive game-wrecker Jeffery Simmons last week, some believe they might not be done navigating the trade market ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.
The Bears already boast one of the league's most talented rosters. However, they might still look to package a few late-round draft picks if they want to add another piece for a potential Super Bowl run.
There are really only two positions they might target ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. One has been a major weakness this season, while the other is an area where they've been rumored to be looking.
Which players stand out as the most logical candidates for both spots?
Titans cornerback Alontae Taylor is probably at the top of Chicago's wish list . He played under Dennis Allen for three years in New Orleans and has experience playing both in the slot and on the perimeter.
Taylor has struggled to catch on in Tennessee after signing a three-year, $60 million deal this offseason. The only question is whether they'd be willing to move him for a late-round pick. If they are, then the Bears would make a lot of sense, as he already has a firm grasp of Dennis Allen's scheme.
Speaking of familiarity, the Bears might also be interested in bringing back Nahshon Wright if they think he could provide a boost to their struggling cornerback room. The 28-year-old is still waiting to play his first defensive snap with the Jets after signing a one-year, $3.5 million deal with the Jets this offseason.
Chicago would provide Wright with his best chance to contribute. The only question is whether they'd be willing to look past his coverage warts to inject some playmaking ability into the secondary. It'd cost next to nothing (a late-round pick swap would probably suffice) to get him back into the building.
Riq Woolen has the highest ceiling among all cornerbacks that the Bears could (realistically) target on the trade market . In the right scheme, he's a solid man coverage cornerback who has a solid track record making plays. That's the player the Eagles thought they were getting when they signed him to a one-year, $12 million deal this offseason.
With that said, he also has a very real floor, and it's been on display lately. He had a strong start to the season for Philadelphia, but like virtually every other position on their roster, has struggled to hold up in recent weeks. The Eagles would be willing to deal, as they're in the midst of a lost season. He'd be slightly more expensive than Wright, though.
Mike Sainistril burst onto the scene with a rock-solid rookie campaign for Washington in 2024. He also showed some promise last year, picking off four passes. Unfortunately, he hasn't shown nearly as much success this season and is allowing a 140.1 passer rating when targeted.
Sainristil has effectively been benched this season, playing only 39% of the Commanders' defensive snaps after playing 90% over his first two seasons. He's due for a change of scenery, and the Bears might be able to provide it if Washington is willing to sell low (are you noticing a theme?). He's another player with inside/outside versatility. A low-cost dart throw.
A reunion with Khalil Mack felt a lot more likely before they traded for Simmons. If Monday night's game against Seattle is any indication, they don't really need to add an edge rusher. However, NFL teams can't have enough quality defensive linemen, and meeting with Jordan Elliott reinforces that notion.
Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh being in denial about the state of the 0-7 Chargers might throw a wrench into their plans, though. He has maintained that Los Angeles isn't selling, and seems dead set on holding Mack hostage. Maybe if they lose their eighth straight contest on Sunday, he'll change his mind and do Mack a solid by shipping him off to a contender.
Again, this doesn't feel necessary . However, the Bears were rumored to be interested in Jermaine Johnson II ahead of last year's trade deadline , and they've reportedly still been in the edge market after landing Simmons. Johnson is equally effective against the run as he is at pinning his ears back on passing downs.
The Titans are obviously in sell mode after starting the season 1-7. He'll be a free agent in the offseason and might not want any part of a rebuild. Offering a fifth-round pick for a player Tennessee will lose anyway would be shrewd if they think he can provide a substantial impact for a Super Bowl push.
Jerry Markarian has been an avid Chicago Bears fan since 2010 and has been writing about the team since  2022.  He has survived the 2010 NFC Championship Game, a career-ending injury to his favorite player (Johnny Knox), the Bears' 2013 season finale, a Double Doink, Mitchell Trubisky, Justin Fields, and Weeks 8-17 of the 2024 NFL season. Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Will Kyle Monangai Play Tonight? Injury Update, Fantasy Advice For Bears RB in Week 9
full_text:
Unlike the last handful of weeks, there is at least some hope that Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai might be able to play against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9.
Monangai has missed each of the last four games with a turf toe injury he suffered in Week 4 versus the New York Jets.
However, Monangai was able to turn in a limited practice on Friday, which amounts to his first participation since his injury. After that, Monangai drew the questionable tag for Sunday.
Now, a look at what we know about his chances of suiting up on Sunday night against Tampa Bay.
UPDATE: According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Monangai will not play in Week 9, but the good news is he is expected to be ready to return in Week 11 after the bye.
"Bears RB Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) won't play today, but he's expected back in Week 11. Fresh legs for Chicago," Rapoport reported.
We do not have a definitive answer yet, but all signs point to the Bears running back sitting out.
The first sign is Monangai only putting in one limited practice. We find it hard to believe the Bears are going to have him suit up off just one limited session after missing four games.
We also know the Bears elevated running back Salvon Ahmed from the practice squad and we suspect that's because they're expecting Monangai to sit out.
Then, there's the fact that the Bears have a bye in Week 10 and The Chicago Tribune's Brad Biggs believes Monangai's return to practice is a "positive sign for a potential return on the other side of the bye week" rather than a sign he will return in Week 9.
When putting it all together, we just don't see Monangai suiting up on Sunday night. We'll know for sure around 6:50 p.m. ET, when the Bears drop their inactives.
If Monangai is active and there are no reports about him being on a limited snap count, he should be in lineups.
The Bucs are ceding the fewest fantasy points per game to backs in 2026, according to CBS Sports , but Monangai also ranked as RB13 overall in the four games he played in this season, per Fantasy Pros , which makes him an every week RB2 play, regardless of matchup.
However, the tricky part here is that Monangai plays on Sunday night and if you wait on him and he gets ruled out, your pool of potential replacements is very thin.
If you do plan on waiting on Monangai, grab Roschon Johnson if he's available on waivers as a last-second replacement. You'll also want to put Monangai in a flex spot if possible so that gives you more options to replace him.
All that said, barring a desperate situation, you should just keep Monangai on the bench this week because, as we previously discussed, all signs point to him sitting out.

title: In a Bad Sign for Kyle Monangai's Status, Bears Elevate Salvon Ahmed From Practice Squad
full_text:
Even though Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai finally practiced on Friday , it's unlikely that he'll see the field on Sunday night against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. On Saturday, the Bears announced that running back Salvon Ahmed would be elevated from the practice squad , a strong sign that Monangai will once again be inactive in Week 9. And with the Bears' bye week up next, his next chance to play won't be until Week 11.
Monangai hasn't played since he popped off in the Bears' dominant Week 4 victory against the New York Jets . By the end of that matchup, Monangai was on pace for a monster season. He had carried the ball a career-high 30 times for 146 yards and a pair of touchdowns. Unfortunately, he exited that game early with what turned out to be a pretty bad case of turf toe.
If the Bears do indeed make Monangai an inactive player for this game, it will be the fifth straight game that he's missed. This after playing in all nineteen games last year, including the Bears' two postseason games, and averaging an impressive 4.6 yards per carry.
Keeping Monangai on the sideline for another week is probably the best course of action, both for Monangai and for the team. With just one limited practice under his belt since his Week 4 injury, Monanga isn't ready for live action, especially against a defensive front as ferocious as Tampa Bay's. Give him this week and the bye week to recover, and then see what Week 11 has in store.
The Bears will certainly miss Monangai's hard-charging running yet again, but they'll be in capable hands. For one thing, D'Andre Swift's three-touchdown performance in the Bears' statement primetime victory last week proved that he can make the plays that count. Additionally, the Bears will have Roschon Johnson and now Salvon Ahmed at their disposal.
Ahmed had himself a solid performance in the preseason this year, averaging almost seven yards per carry on eight rushing attempts. He also showed himself to be a willing and able blocker when his number is called. He's unlikely to get much of a workload on Sunday, not unless the Bears somehow race out to a massive early lead, but at least the coaches don't need to worry about their third running back option.

title: 4 Edge Rushers Chicago Bears Should Target With Khalil Mack Trade Unlikely
full_text:
Chicago Bears fans have been dreaming for a reunion with Khalil Mack ever since the Los Angeles Chargers' season started to go south.
And, that dream appeared to have legs after it was reported that the Bears had put in a call to the Chargers about a Mack trade.
But, despite the fact that the Chargers are 0-7 and have no hope to make the playoffs, Los Angeles reportedly has no desire to trade the veteran edge rusher.
"Despite their 0-7 record, the Los Angeles Chargers continue to tell teams that they have no interest in trading Khalil Mack, and the veteran pass rusher will not be going anywhere before Tuesday's deadline, according to sources," ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported on Saturday.
Mack has expressed his desire to stay in Los Angeles, so he also presents a roadblock for a potential trade to Chicago.
With that in mind, here's a look at four other edge rushers who could be available for trade that the Bears should target.
After the Jets made some additions to their edge rushers room this offseason, including using a high draft pick on David Bailey, McDonald has seen his playing time drop from 66% of snaps in each of the last two seasons to 48% in 2026.
That could signal the Jets might be open to trading him, and we know the Jets would love more draft capital for their rebuild.
McDonald, who has one year left on his contract after 2026, has notched three sacks this season and had 18.5 in the previous two campaigns combined, so he has a strong history of production.
After striking gold with the Jeffery Simmons trade , perhaps the Bears should go back to the well in a trade with the Tennessee Titans for Johnson.
In the final year of his contract , it remains to be seen if Johnson is going to be part of the team's long-term plans. If not, Tennessee might be willing to move him to get more draft capital for the rebuild the team is currently going through.
Johnson has tallied three sacks in seven games and posted 7.5 in 2023, the season before he suffered a significant injury. Johnson posted three sacks in 2025, so he's about to surpass that mark midway through the season.
The Indianapolis Colts are primed for a fire sale after trading both Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, so it makes sense for the Bears to check in on Latu.
Latu has just two sacks in eight games, but he has shown he's capable of more after posting 12.5 over his first two years in the league, including a career-high 8.5 in 2025.
And he wouldn't just be a rental, either, as Latu has one more year left on his rookie contract after 2026.
Sweat may be the best edge rusher available on the market ahead of the deadline, assuming the Arizona Cardinals want to trade him. It makes sense for them to with Sweat approaching 30 and Arizona in the midst of a rebuild.
The Cardinals edge rusher has twice posted double-digit sacks in a season, and he has 7.5 or more in four of the last five years. Through eight games this season, Sweat has three.
Along with his history of sack production, Sweat has a Super Bowl ring, also, which is the kind of experience the Bears could covet given their legitimate Super Bowl hopes.
While Sweat is our favorite player on this list, he's probably the least likely to land in Chicago. It will probably take a third-round pick to acquire him and it's hard to imagine the Bears giving up that much after the Simmons trade .
But, after seeing the Bears make that deal, never say never for just about any trade.

title: How Iceman Handles Bucs' Heat Seems the Big Unanswered Bears Question
full_text:
It's possible Caleb Williams hasn't lined up against a defense so consumed with blitzing or pressuring the line of scrimmage since the Bears lost at home to Minnesota in Week 2, 9-3.
The ability of the Bears quarterback under pressure has been bandied about by the talking heads at ESPN and Fox all week with some concluding Williams can't handle pressure.  They see the iceman melting down under heat. The statistics they throw around sound impressive but the real value of those is in question.
In truth, Williams has an EPA of .14 per play when blitzed and that's eighth among NFL starting quarterbacks according to Sumer Sports analytics . When pressured, no starting quarterback in the NFL has a higher EPA per play than Williams at .008. His success rate on plays when pressured in seventh best, and combined with his high EPA rank it suggests he creates big plays under pressire.
Williams should be able to stand in or move around and beat a blitz because he has faced many of them. Last year, he saw blitzes on 174 plays. That was the most in the NFL, per Pro Football Reference.
Nick Wright thinks the Bucs beat the Bears this weekend. Argues Caleb is having a good year but modest bc he doesn’t have enough passing yards. Does not acknowledge  he missed three games. #DaBears pic.twitter.com/Z1Gxjyvf9y
The pressure the Bears will see from Tampa Bay and coach Todd Bowles is a little different than what the saw from the Vikings earlier.
“Chaos," is how coach Ben Johnson described it. "I think that's what stands out. I think he's always defended the run really well, and whenever you play single high to the rate that he does, it's different than what we've seen earlier this year.
"A lot of these teams were playing shell and two high (safeties), and he's predominantly single high, and I think that always gives you an extra defender in the box that you've got to account for. So schematically, it's very challenging to run the ball, and then when you have the talent on the defensive line and in the linebacker crew that they have, those are tough yards to come by."
“Under pressure Caleb Williams is very pedestrian.” Gerald McCoy doesn’t think Caleb Williams can handle Todd Bowles Blitz package and doesn’t think the WRs can consistently get open vs the Bucs. 👀 #DaBears #Bears pic.twitter.com/jzo5Zm9Z1S
The single high also invites big plays by opposing quarterbacks.
It's the same old same old of staying in manageable down-and-distance situations.
"Whether it's second and long or third down, that's where he draws up all these exotics and creates a lot of issues for the quarterback," Johnson said of Bowles. "I think the linebackers are doing a great job just sniffing out pass concepts and understanding what windows to be in.
The last time Ben Johnson went against Todd Bowles, the Buccaneers defense wasn't half as good as it is now - and the Bucs still held him to 16 points at home. Clearly he's coaching a different team, but let's not forget he led the #1 offense in the league that year. Bears fans… https://t.co/A16A9KdCCC pic.twitter.com/30OVZJJCmP
"He mixes up man and zone, and I think (safety) Antoine Winfield, he's a ballhawk back there. And then when he comes down, he'll light you up as well in the running game. So it's a good mix of talent, and then the scheme certainly is coming from all angles. So you try to be as sound as you possibly can.”
The Buccaneers allowed more than 17 points only once in their last five games, yet, they lost all five games they played against teams with winning records and their three wins came against teams with three wins each. They lead the league in takeaways with 16, half coming against three-win opponents in their last two games.
"They do a great job," Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor said. "But then the structure, the way they play, the way they shed blocks, the fundamentals, it's a good tackling unit in the core. They present a lot of different looks, and a lot of variety."
I keep seeing people say the Bucs are a trap game for the #Bears on Sunday night & I disagree. TB is better than their record says. I also love how the Bears matchup against them. Slow down the run game & Baker Mayfield will be in hell. TB’s defense is good but #Bears have…
Williams explained the 0-4 start by the Buccaneers and more than 26 points a game allowed in those by simply being out of sorts following the dislocated thumb their quarterback, Baker Mayfield suffered.
It affected the Bucs' defense when the offense didn't have its passer, he said. He should know. Something similar happened to the Bears without Williams against Green Bay.  Tampa has made corrections and is rolling defensively. The question is whether they can manage pressure on a quarterback some people seem to think will bend or fold under it.
"You find your flow, you find out what works well, you find out what doesn't, and then you make corrections," he said.
How has it gone from the Seahawks being the best defensive test the Bears will see all season to now the Bucs are the best defense in the league ??
No quarterback does thrive under pass rush pressure but the ones who can punish the defense enough for gambling will enjoy the most success.
Williams never got to win that game against Minnesota when he was pressured so much because he suffered an injury with the Bears on the verge of going ahead in the fourth quarter. They also fumbled at their own 1, which never helps.
It's time for another pressure test but the really impactful numbers so far suggest he can hold up.

title: Bears and Lions Trade Rumor Could Lead to NFC North Battle Over Players at Same Position
full_text:
The Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions are in the market for help at a specific position, and that could lead to a battle between the NFC North squads over the same players.
According The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , the Lions and Bears are two teams exploring the cornerback market ahead of the NFL trade deadline, which passes on Nov. 10.
Jones also notes that cornerback-needy teams could give the Denver Broncos a call given their depth at the position.
"Detroit and Chicago would each love to add a cornerback if the price is right. I would suspect teams will call the Denver Broncos, who have some depth at that spot," Jones reported.
The Bears have seen No. 1 cornerback Jaylon Johnson struggle this season, which leaves a gaping hole at one boundary spot.
Malik Muhammad has been very good on the other side, but the Bears don't have a contingency plan in place for Johnson, as Tyrique Stevenson has been just as bad as Johnson.
In Detroit, the Lions never replaced Terrion Arnold, who was cut loose during the offseason after getting into legal trouble .
The Lions currently sport the league's worst pass defense, with Detroit ceding 276.6 passing yards per game, which is a huge problem in an NFC North that has three dangerous passing attacks.
The Bears haven't been anywhere near that bad at defending the pass, with Chicago ranking 14th. However, as we saw against the Green Bay Packers in Week 5, good passing attacks can fully exploit the Bears' weakness on the outside.
One of the hottest names out there on the cornerback market is Phildelphia Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen, who is on a one-year deal and on a team that is going to miss the playoffs.
We've also seen New York Jets cornerback Nahshon Wright identified as a player the Bears could add . Wright has zero role with the Jets and would be a fantastic fit in Chicago after he thrived in Dennis Allen's defense last season.
Jones mentioned the Broncos as a team that others could target for a cornerback trade given their depth.
Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine are likely names to watch there since they aren't starters, although we're skeptical the Broncos will deal anyone with their 6-2 record.
This is an area where the Lions have an advantage after the Bears unloaded two firsts in the Jeffery Simmons trade, which likely makes Chicago less aggressive moving forward.
Chicago has picks in the second , third, fifth, sixth and seventh rounds next year, and is missing its first in 2028.
The Lions are fully stocked with nine picks in next year's draft, including at least one in every round and three in the seventh round. Detroit has all of its picks in 2028, also.
If the Lions and Bears do end up competing for the same player, the Lions are better positioned to win that battle.

title: Bold Predictions For Bears Week 9 Matchup Against Buccaneers
full_text:
The Chicago Bears host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for their third straight primetime contest on Sunday night. They'll hope to repeat their Monday night performance against the Seattle Seahawks, when they won 34-17 on the road.
According to DraftKings Sportsbook , the Bears are favored by 6 points for the matchup. While the vast majority of the experts like their odds of coming away with their fourth straight win, the Bucs are no slouch.
They've given up the second-fewest rushing yards per game (80) and are coming off two straight blowout wins over division rivals. They also boast the league's best rushing offense with 168.6 yards on the ground. Jeffery Simmons and Co. will have their hands full on Sunday night.
While the outcome might be a toss-up, there are a few bankable players on both sides of the ball. We wanted to go out on a limb with a few bold predictions surrounding those players.
Colston Loveland has begun heating up in recent weeks after a rough start to the season. He's had between 65 and 69 yards in each of the past three weeks. He'll continue that positive momentum (and take it to another level) against Tampa Bay.
The Buccaneers have a strong rushing defense, but their passing defense ranks squarely in the middle of the pack. To their credit, they've held opposing tight ends in check thus far this season. Mike Gesicki (78 yards) is the only TE to exceed 54 yards against them this season, and that was in the season opener.
That won't matter against Loveland on Sunday night, who plays more like a big receiver anyway. They haven't played a pass-catching tight end like him this season, and he'll reach the century mark on Sunday night.
Jeffery Simmons was as advertised in his debut against Seattle . He completely unlocked Chicago's defense and was a one-man wrecking crew up front. We also saw Montez Sweat reap the benefits of playing next to his college teammate. He would've had three sacks if two hadn't been taken away for penalties in the secondary.
Austin Booker will have a tough draw against Tristan Wirfs on the left side. Sweat's matchup against Luke Goedeke isn't nearly as daunting, though.
We think he'll pick up right where he left off against Tampa Bay. He'll take down Baker Mayfield for two sacks, capitalizing on the Bucs ' focus on slowing Simmons down. The early-season concerns (which were valid at the time) will fall by the wayside.
As we mentioned above on Loveland, the Bucs have a stout run defense. That'll mean this is another week where Caleb Williams has to put the offense on his shoulders. Luckily for Chicago, he's well equipped to handle those duties .
Williams will continue his ascension to one of the league's best young signal-callers. No one has benefited from the Bears' recent primetime matchups more than Williams, who will have another chance to put on a show with all eyes on him.
The Buccaneers have allowed only one 300-yard passer this season, and no quarterback has thrown for 3 touchdowns on Todd Bowles' talented unit. That changes on Sunday night.

title: Governors' Comments Reflect Significant Change in Bears Stadium Saga
full_text:
The pendulum in the Bears stadium saga has seemed stuck on the Indiana side of the border for months but for the first time it seems to be moving back the other way.
The Bears are not saying this as much as the governors of each state have.
On one hand, Illinois Gov. J.B. Pritzker said he wants legislation for a stadium plan to be ready for the first week of the legislature's veto session, which starts Nov. 17. A vote wouldn't be immediate but within a few weeks after.
"This is up to the Bears. You know, there's a bill that's being put together that gives the Bears the opportunity to choose where they want to build a stadium in Illinois, and then it's going to be up to them where it goes," Pritzker told reporters.
Hey guess who was right if he had just said by Friday! Statements from Governor Mike Braun and from Hammond Mayor Tom McDermott. Sorry for the timing being off. pic.twitter.com/6f12Fs0Aio
The idea being put forward and discussed most is similar to one Barrington area state representative Marty McLaughlin proposed, which would let the Bears build the stadium in a suitable lcoation but they would then lease it and avoid taxes.
It wouldn't necessarily be the Arlington Heights stadium but could be. Another plan for the far south part of the Lake Michigan shore in Chicago is gaining some support but there is no word from the Bears about considering this site.
In fact, the Bears were only issuing a lengthy non-committal statement over the entire topic.
Gov. Mike Braun suggests a deadline is approaching for the Chicago Bears to make a stadium decision This statement is in response to the team meeting with Illinois lawmakers this week The Bears previously said it’s “sole focus” was building a new stadium in Hammond pic.twitter.com/Fmm014u61I
"The Chicago Bears remain committed to building a world-class stadium and mixed-use district for our fans, the Chicagoland community and the team," the team's statement said. "We continue to work collaboratively with local and state leaders in Indiana to advance our stadium development plans in Hammond, where we are finalizing due diligence details across two sites in the Wolf Lake area.
"At the same time, we appreciate the recent engagement from Illinois leadership to explore legislation which has allowed us to share our feedback. We expect productive dialogue with both leadership teams in the coming weeks. We have a responsibility and obligation to explore every option available to the club, and we look forward to developing a transformational project that will attract global events and deliver jobs and economic growth to all of Chicagoland."
The really big development in all of this was a statement issued by Indiana Gov. Mike Braun. Until now, that state quietly went about trying to get a plan finalized and had quickly passed needed legislation. It's why they were the side being mentioned prominently by the Bears all spring and summer.
With Illinois getting more Bears attention lately, and wheels turning finally in the Land of Lincoln largely because the election is finally over, Braun for the first time expressed the thought that Indiana's patience could be wearing thin.
"Indiana has assembled an excellent deal to build a world-class stadium in Hammond, Indiana," Braun said in a statement. "All negotiations have been done in good faith and to ensure that Hoosier taxpayers are protected.
"We encourage the Chicago Bears to fully commit to a stadium in Indiana because it is nearly time for the state to shift its energy and resources to the next opportunity."
There's no mention of the other "opportunity."
Indiana's governor is unhappy the Bears are continuing to play footsie with Illinois. "We encourage the Chicago Bears to fully commit to a stadium in Indiana because it is nearly time for the state to shift its energy and resources to the next opportunity." - Gov. Mike Braun pic.twitter.com/oKSxBu3UuF
It's ridiculous that this has been delayed so long mainly because of politics, the ineffective leadership from Pritzker on this topic and also a refusal by the city of Chicago to acknowledge team desires to move to the suburbs.
The new plan being talked about in the area of where the Calumet River runs into Lake Michigan, is so far south that it might as well be in Hammond.
It's often pointed out that Hammond and now, also this south Chicago location, are closer to Soldier Field than Arlington Heights is. That statement is largely irrelevant because the majority of Bears season ticket holders are not in the south part of the suburbs or city and are in the northwest suburbs and northern burbs.
Regardless, it is at least good to see movement within and toward Illinois at last. Getting the vote from the state legislature in early December needs to be a priority as Pritzker said. Wasting more time on new plans like the south can only lead the project to wind up across the border near Hammond.
Creation of a Chicago Bears 70k domed stadium and entertainment district at the 326 acre site they own in Arlington Heights. pic.twitter.com/j4EDG1g2jB

title: Khalil Mack Trade Rumor Slams Door Shut on Chicago Bears Reunion
full_text:
It looks like there will not be a reunion for the Chicago Bears and Los Angeles Chargers edge rusher Khalil Mack
According to ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport , the Chargers remain steadfast in their desire to hang on to the veteran.
As a result, the expectation is that he will not be traded before the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Rapoport and Schefter say.
"Despite their 0-7 record, the Los Angeles Chargers continue to tell teams that they have no interest in trading away Khalil Mack, and the veteran pass rusher will not be going anywhere before Tuesday's deadline, according to sources," they wrote.
The report states that the Chargers "have prioritized keeping Mack for the leadership he provides and the talent he brings, characterizing him as a pillar of the organization."
"(The Chargers) might be winless, but they are not acting that way in any trade discussions with other teams regarding any of their players," the ESPN reporters added.
Delusion at its finest, but I digress.
Los Angeles has made it quite clear it has no desire to trade Mack, with head coach Jim Harbaugh saying as much .
"I want Khalil Mack here," Harbaugh told reporters. "Khalil Mack wants to be here."
But Mack has also expressed his desire to stay with the franchise, which is the ultimate showing of loyalty.
"Yeah, they know how I feel, man," he said when asked if he has notified the team he wants to stay for 2026. "It's just tough with all the outside noise. And so, ultimately I want to be here and I want to help them win. Even though it's tough right now, you always see the light at the end of the tunnel."
So, not only does the team want the player to stay, but the player also wants to stay with the team.
Now, Mack doesn't have a no-trade clause or anything like that, so the Chargers can deal him without his consent, but because of the level of respect they have for the future Hall of Famer, we don't think that's going to happen.
It's a truly head-scratching situation. You would assume that, in the twilight of his career, Mack would want to give himself a chance to win a Super Bowl, something that has eluded him his entire career.
You would also assume that the Chargers would want to make the best move for the franchise, which in this case is trading Mack to grab some draft capital before he potentially leaves in 2027.
But, unless this is an elite head fake from both Mack and the Chargers, neither of those things are true here and instead Chicago is going to have to look elsewhere for help.

title: Joe Burrow Rocks New Cleats For Spain Battle Against Falcons
full_text:
Joe Burrow is rocking some cool new cleats for today's game against the Falcons in Madrid, Spain.
Cincinnati's elite passer is sporting an orange and white pair of cleats with an interesting design on the side.
Burrow is eager to perform in front of the masses as one of the most popular football players on earth. This is going to be his first NFL game action.
The two teams are battling at the Santiago Bernabeu, home to international soccer powerhouse Real Madrid.
"I've followed international sports for a long time. Followed Real Madrid for a long time. Watched Barcelona play Real Madrid a lot. Played with both of those teams on FIFA a lot when I was a kid," Burrow said in his press conference this week. "And loved watching soccer my whole life, really. I wish they played while we were here at their home stadiums so we could go."
He can't wait to showcase this Bengals offense, which has been easily the most efficient in the NFL over the past month.
Cincinnati ranks first in offensive EPA/play since Week 5 began (0.216 EPA/play, only team above 0.2).
"I think, number one, we have great players, players that want to be great. We work really hard at it," Burow said to the collected group of media on Friday. "We have coaches who want to put us in the best position to go and do what we do and utilize our strengths and minimize our weaknesses. We've been playing together for a long time now, so we know how to play off of each other and complement each other well.
"Our offensive line is protecting great. I think this is the best that group has played since I've been here, which is really exciting to see. And a lot of our young players are getting better and better. We have the right guys who attack every day with the intent to be better than the day before, and I think that is so valuable in this sport."
It's a great chance for Cincinnati to make a swift statement in Week 9 starting with kickoff at 9:30 a.m. ET.

title: Injured Bengals Defender Good to Go Against Falcons as Team Announces Inactives
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Cedric Johnson is active for today’s NFL International Game in Madrid against the Atlanta Falcons.
Johnson was listed as questionable on the injury report with an ankle/foot designation after suffering the injury in last week’s 43-36 overtime win against the Tennessee Titans.
Safety Kyle Dugger was ruled out Friday with the quad injury that has forced him to miss three of the last four games.
The other inactives are offensive tackle Myles Hinton, center Connor Lew and defensive tackle Landon Robinson.
The Bengals only need four inactives today because their roster is currently at 52.
Cornerback DJ Turner II injured his foot last week against the Titans and was limited to start the week, but he did not appear on the injury report and is expected to start and play his full role.
The Bengals arrived in Madrid on Wednesday and practiced Thursday and Friday to get back on a normal weekly schedule.
"I think this is the best compromise we found to make sure that we can get acclimated by Friday, get a really good practice where we feel better, and then play our best on Sunday," head coach Zac Taylor said on Thursday. "So we've all embraced that mindset, and I think it's working well for us so far."
"We're back on schedule,” he added. “Our meetings were the same as they've always been on Thursday. So today is more of a third-down emphasis with some normal downs, and then tomorrow will be red zone-based."
Quarterback Joe Burrow said he and his teammates are excited to be representing the NFL abroad and about being in a stand-alone window as the only game on Sunday morning.
“It means a lot to me that we're here,” he said Friday. “I think this is Year 7 for me, and I haven't been overseas yet. And we keep adding more and more games to try to build the NFL globally. I think it's worked over the last five years, and I'm hoping to add more and continue to build, and I love being part of that, and I want to help grow the game, and so I love being here.
"I love being the only game on TV on Sunday morning when people back home wake up, and I love showcasing our talents abroad and trying to bring attention to what we do, as far as what our offense brings. I think we're explosive, we're dynamic, we're fun to watch, and I think we're going to put on a show on Sunday."
The team will fly home immediately after the game and, unlike their previous two international games when they had a bye to recover, will start preparations for a key AFC North game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday Night Football.

title: NFL Analyst Calls Joe Burrow ‘As Good as There Is in the League’
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow earned high praise from NFL analyst Greg Cosell for the way he handles an offense before and after the snap.
During an appearance on the Ross Tucker Podcast, Cosell highlighted Burrow's ability to attack outside the numbers with Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. His assessment placed Burrow among the league's best in two essential aspects of playing the QB position.
“Burrow is as good as there is in the league, both in terms of the pre-snap operation and the post-snap operation,” Cosell said . “He’ll work outside the numbers for sure. He’s phenomenal at that with Higgins and Chase.”
Cosell also highlighted another important aspect of Burrow's game: his ability to extend plays. When discussing QBs such as Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes, and Lamar Jackson, he noted that Burrow's mobility deserves attention, too.
“He’s very, very controlled and calculated in the way he moves,” Cosell said.
Cosell cited a 30-yard touchdown pass to Chase in Week 8 as an example of how Burrow can navigate pressure while keeping a passing option alive.
“He threw a touchdown this past week to Chase for 30 yards, where he sort of stepped up, climbed the pocket, avoided, almost jumped over a defender,” Cosell said.
A classic Joe Burrow scramble and Ja'Marr Chase TD catch 🔥 Like clockwork 🤝 (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/WHK4ErW2jd
That sequence is what Cosell was describing — Burrow's under-the-radar ability to move and avoid the rush while still being able to deliver the ball accurately. He added that Burrow's precise ball placement "always just really stands out" on tape.
For Cincinnati, those skills give its passing game another way to succeed when pressure disrupts a play. Burrow's ability to create room within the pocket helps keep Chase and Higgins involved even after the initial protection breaks down.
Through seven games this season, Burrow has completed 73% of his passes for 2,115 passing yards and 20 touchdowns. He is well on his way to another 4,000-yard season, his fourth in seven seasons.
The Bengals are in Madrid to play the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. Burrow is hoping to lead Cincinnati to a fourth-straight victory. He's thrown for at least four touchdowns in each of the Bengals' wins during this streak.
Cincinnati could move into a tie for first place in the AFC North with the Steelers at 6-2 with a victory.

title: 'Great To See Us Play' - Bengals Stars Eager to Perform in Front of Real Madrid Star Kylian Mbappe
full_text:
Bengals stars Dexter Lawrence and Tee Higgins are hoping to see another big-time star at the Spain game on Sunday . Both voices spoke to the media on Thursday and noted how impressed they are with Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe.
The international soccer star wowed on the biggest stage at the 2026 World Cup in the United States and is widely considered one of the five best players in the world.
Mbappe is reportedly aiming to attend the game between Cincinnati and Atlanta on Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET.
"It could be somebody's first time watching us play. So you want to make your first impression the best one, and I don't know if it's his first time, but it probably will be his first time in person. So, it'll be special to go all out," Lawrence said to FOX 19 and others at the podium.
Higgins was all smiles answering questions fresh off of his first career AFC Offensive Player of the Week award.
"Dope to have him there," Higgins said. "Cause I watch him on TV all the time. You know what I mean? It's so crazy, bro. We just talk about how fast this dude is, right? Like, how do you run that fast, dribbling the ball on your feet? Like, that's crazy. And then the moves, it's amazing. So just having that type of player at the game would be great to see us play."
Cincinnati has one more day of practice before an off day on Saturday.
Zac Taylor and the whole team are exploring the city of Madrid in their free time this week.
"No, I have not. I'm sure they have their own. But so far my communications with them have been mostly football," Taylor said about the sightseeing so far. "But, again, yesterday the guys had an opportunity to walk around and go eat dinner and enjoy all the things that Madrid has to offer. And I would imagine most of them did that."
Time will tell if Mbappe rolls into his home stadium, Santiago Bernabeu, for the afternoon kickoff in Spain.

title: Bengals Trade Idea Would Add Experienced Veteran to Cincinnati's Defense
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are one of the better teams in the AFC, but they need to make a few big moves if they want to separate themselves as serious contenders in the NFL.
They could use some supporting help on offense. They have one of the best offenses in the league, but it's because of Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins. They could use an additional wide receiver or some help at running back. They could also use some support on defense, especially in the secondary. Their cornerback room is decent, but it might not be good enough to win the Super Bowl. Adding some support at the trade deadline would help quite a bit.
The Athletic and their writers, including Daniel Popper, recently put together a mock NFL trade deadline scenario in which the Bengals swung a trade for Los Angeles Chargers cornerback Donte Jackson in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick.
"Jackson is on an expiring deal with the Chargers, who have the worst record in the league at 0-7," Popper wrote . "His 23 career interceptions rank fifth among active players. Jackson has missed four games with a hamstring injury but was back in practice all three days last week in a limited capacity. The Bengals offered a 2027 sixth-round pick. The Lions offered a 2027 seventh-round pick. The Chargers accepted the Bengals’ offer."
Jackson is the perfect combination of impactful and affordable. The Bengals don't need a superstar on defense, as they already made their big trade to acquire Dexter Lawrence a few months ago. But their cornerback room needs some support, and Jackson has enough gas left in the tank to help them make a run for the Super Bowl.
Jackson being on an expiring deal would be a benefit for the Bengals, as they wouldn't be tied to him beyond just this season. Adding him in exchange for a late-round draft pick, while paying him pennies on the dollar compared with other starting cornerbacks, would be a move too good for Cincinnati to pass up.
The NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET. Cincinnati has made an in-season trade in each of the past two seasons. They're guaranteed to be at least 5-3 at the deadline and could improve to 6-2 with a win over the Falcons in Madrid. title: Three Edge Rushers the Bengals Could Target Before the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals escaped Sunday with a win, but their depth at defensive end took a hit. Cashius Howell suffered a right wrist injury that will require surgery during a 46-36 overtime victory over Tennessee, while Cedric Johnson exited with a left ankle injury.
Cincinnati improved to 5-2, and Boye Mafe increased his team-leading sack total to 5.5. Adding another veteran could help protect the pass rush from further injuries and give defensive coordinator Al Golden more options down the stretch.
The NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET, giving the Bengals time to evaluate their needs and explore the market. Here are three edge rushers to consider as potential targets.
Mack would give Cincinnati an experienced option for its playoff push, but it won't come without competition to acquire him. The Chargers are 0-7, and Mack is on an expiring contract. The Chicago Bears are believed to be interested in acquiring him.
The 35-year-old is on a one-year, $18 million contract, which would make him a rental unless the Bengals negotiate an extension. That structure could appeal to a team seeking immediate help while continuing to develop its younger defensive ends.
Mack would work opposite Mafe, giving Golden another option in obvious passing situations. The Bengals would need to weigh the draft compensation against the remaining salary.
For the Bengals, Sweat would be a bigger investment with potential value beyond this season. The 29-year-old recorded a career-high 12 sacks in 2025 and is under contract through 2028.
The asking price could be the obstacle. PHNX’s Johnny Venerable reported that Arizona is seeking a high Day 2 pick for Sweat, who reportedly requested a trade after Jonathan Gannon’s dismissal.
For Cincinnati, the appeal would be adding another proven pass rusher alongside Mafe, with Dexter Lawrence creating problems inside. Sweat would make the most sense if the Bengals view him as part of their plans beyond 2026, since that reported price would be difficult to justify as injury insurance alone.
Uche would be a more affordable option for the Bengals. His one-year contract is worth roughly $1.4 million, and PFF included him among its potential trade candidates in October.
He has two sacks this season, including one against New England on Sunday. Cincinnati also saw him during its Week 5 win over Miami.
If Howell and Johnson avoid extended absences, Uche could still strengthen the rotation at a manageable salary, provided Miami’s asking price reflects that supporting role.
