title: 'Going To Put On A Show' - Joe Burrow Hammers Home Love For International Games Ahead of Falcons Madrid Battle
full_text:
Joe Burrow seems really excited to represent the NFL on its international stage Sunday morning. He spoke to all the gathered media at the podium on Friday.
Cincinnati's most important player has been dreaming of playing an international NFL game for years.
"It means a lot to me that we're here. I think this is Year 7 for me, and I haven't been overseas yet. And we keep adding more and more games to try to build the NFL globally," Burrow noted. "I think it's worked over the last five years, and I'm hoping to add more and continue to build, and I love being part of that, and I want to help grow the game, and so I love being here.
"I love being the only game on TV on Sunday morning when people back home wake up, and I love showcasing our talents abroad and trying to bring attention to what we do, as far as what our offense brings. I think we're explosive, we're dynamic, we're fun to watch, and I think we're going to put on a show on Sunday."
Cincinnati has a couple more days to explore the Spanish capital as Burrow faces the harrowing trials of packing up all his clothes on Saturday night.
He told the media he does not like packing at all and that his mom put his things together for this trip. A little home feeling to carry him across this journey. All in all, Burrow's stayed largely anonymous in Spain; he likes not getting recognized as much in a new country.
"I was really excited about it. I hadn't been here yet, so that was exciting for me," burrow said about visiting Spain. "This is somewhere that I've always wanted to go, and so to be able to do it while doing what I love, playing football, is really a dream come true for me. I talked about last week how one of my favorite times of my life is playing AAU basketball and traveling around with my friends and staying in the hotels, and that's really what this is, just in the NFL, which makes it that much more special. As far as my recognizability abroad, sometimes, sometimes not.
"I ran into some students studying abroad from the United States the other day when I was walking around, and that was certainly surprising. It's often a little more than I expect when I'm in a different country; I usually expect to go pretty incognito and not have anybody recognize me. It's a little more than that, but I love being out here because I can feel like a normal person for a little bit."
Excited and feeling normal.
Just what Bengals fans want to hear from their star at roughly the midway point of the 2026 regular season.

title: 'Everything Is Always Blown Out Of Proportion' - Ja'Marr Chase Sets Record Straight Following Titans Outburst
full_text:
There are zero hard feelings between Ja'Marr Chase and Zac Taylor in Spain. Chase spoke to the media on Friday and detailed why he got so upset on the sideline late in last week's 43-36 win over the Titans.
The Bengals star wasn't happy with how the offense executed, and he talked to Taylor after the game about the situation.
"I'm a leader," Chase said in Spain. "I want the best for everyone around me, especially when the offense isn't clicking. They let me speak my mind and opinion at the end of the day as long as I do it with respect. And I believe Zac can vouch for me. He and I already talked. Everything is always blown out of proportion with whatever I do."
Chase had his best game of the season, posting 10 catches for 141 yards and a score. He clearly wasn't upset about his individual play; Chase has never fit the diva stereotype like that.
All in all, it's just a captain wanting to make sure his unit executes at the highest level.
"A lot of different things. It was an emotional game; I didn't hit him on the deep one, and we turned it over too many times. He wants to win and wants to execute on every snap, as do I. That's how it goes," Joe Burrow said about the emotion following Sunday's game.
Chase and Higgins have been the best wide receiver duo in the NFL this season. The latter is establishing himself as not just the best WR2 in the NFL, but Higgins is arguably a Top-10 receiver in the league alongside Chase.
The latest AFC Offensive Player of the Week one-upped Chase with 10 catches for 155 yards and two scores on the other side of the formation.
"Honestly, he's a whole different receiver this year than last year — run after the catch, more on back shoulder throws with Joe (Burrow). It's hard to cover that when you're constantly switching it up every game. I love what they're doing and can only be better from here," Chase said about Higgins.
Both are trying to keep that production going for the Bengals this week against Atlanta's 11th-ranked NFL defense by EPA/dropback allowed.

title: Bengals' Pursuit of Jonathan Taylor May Be More Fantasy Than Reality
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals have been named as a potential trade suitor for Indianapolis Colts superstar running back Jonathan Taylor, even though a deal isn't very likely to come to fruition.
There are a few teams reportedly in the mix. The Bengals' biggest issue with a potential deal is the fact that the return for him in a trade would need to be massive to get him out of Indianapolis. The Bengals would need to cut ties with multiple valuable draft picks to land Taylor.
The Athletic and writer Daniel Popper recently put together a mock NFL trade deadline scenario in which Taylor wasn't traded, even though the representative for the Bengals made a run at him.
"The Colts received offers on Taylor from three teams," Popper wrote. "The Vikings offered a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fourth-round pick. The Bengals offered a 2027 third-round pick.
"The Giants made the most aggressive offer: a 2027 second-round pick, a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fourth-round pick. This package aligns pretty closely with what the 49ers gave up for Christian McCaffrey ahead of the 2022 deadline. The Colts rejected the Vikings’ and Bengals’ offers. Those teams did not want to counter and dropped out of the race. That left the Giants’ offer."
It would be shocking to see the Bengals give up enough draft capital to bring in Taylor. The Colts are likely asking for a package similar to the blockbuster deal that sent Christian McCaffrey to the San Francisco 49ers a few years ago.
The Bengals would instantly jump a few slots in the power rankings if they added Taylor. Their offense would no longer be one-dimensional like it has been this season.
Still, it's difficult to imagine them giving up a second-round pick and then some in order to land Taylor.
The asking price is a lot, and the Bengals might not be willing to pay it.

title: 3 Wide Receivers That Bengals Could Trade for to Bolster Their Offense
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals could've pursued receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. before the Arizona Cardinals traded him to the Houston Texans. Harrison would have come to Cincinnati and slotted in as a much-needed wide receiver No. 3.

Still, he has some potential left to provide to a high-powered offense. Jennings would be very affordable to acquire in a deal, and he would give the Bengals a veteran to add to their depleted wide receiver room. At the very least, he would be a solid veteran in a room with multiple young wide receivers.

title: 3 Things Shedeur Sanders Needs To Do To Take the Browns’ Starting Job From Deshaun Watson
full_text:
For the second year in as many professional seasons, a concussion to the Cleveland Browns’ starter has opened the door for Shedeur Sanders to come in and play quarterback .
Last year, as a rookie, it was fellow rookie Dillon Gabriel’s head injury in Week 11 that paved the way for Sanders to eventually take hold of the starting quarterback position. This year, Deshaun Watson reported concussion symptoms after a Week 9 contest, opening the door for Sanders to start for the first time during his sophomore season.
However, things are a lot different this year for Sanders and the Browns. Unlike last year’s 2-8 outfit, this time Cleveland is 5-3 at the time of Sanders’ opportunity, with the club thinking about the postseason .
That means it’s far more difficult for Sanders to block the incumbent from reclaiming the top spot on the depth chart this time around. Nonetheless, his odds are still above zero, if ever so slightly.
Here are three things Shedeur Sanders needs to do starting Week 9 against the New Orleans Saints to take the starting spot from Deshaun Watson:
Yes, the Browns are winning with Watson under center, but it’s fairly easy to argue that the team is winning despite Watson, rather than thanks to Watson.
Watson’s elongated dropbacks and tendency to hold on to the ball have led to a league-leading 33 sacks. His accuracy has also been an issue, oftentimes overthrowing his targets, and he’s averaging less than one touchdown pass per game.
Additionally, Watson ranks near the bottom of the league in metrics such as Total QBR (40.9), average depth of target (6.7), and batted passes (9). All of those are great places to focus on for Sanders.
Last year, Sanders led the Browns to three wins over seven starts, despite not playing great football, either.
The most common knocks against Sanders included a low percentage of completed throws (56.6) and a lack of decisiveness when going through progressions. If Sanders can show his process has sped up and he can complete passes at a much higher rate than a coin toss, that’s something.
There’s no substitute for winning, which partially explains why Watson has held on to the starting gig despite not performing at a high level.
But there is something Sanders could do that Watson hasn’t done yet, regardless of the Browns’ five wins so far—he could lead Cleveland to a comfortable victory. Every single victory has required some sort of last-minute heroics by the Browns, because Watson has suffered slow starts in practically every game.
If Sanders can find rhythm early, put the Browns ahead, and keep them there through four quarters, that could really become a factor in keeping him in the lineup.
Sanders’ path to regaining the starting job is much harder this year than last season, but it’s not impossible. Cleveland’s record says they’re a team fighting for a spot in the postseason, but quarterback play seems to suggest otherwise. It’s now up to Sanders to change that .

title: An Infamous Draft Night Prank Gives Shedeur Sanders Extra Motivation Against Saints
full_text:
During the 2025 NFL Draft, Shedeur Sanders had a historic slide all the way down to the fifth round.
Eventually, the Cleveland Browns took the Colorado Buffalo with the 144th pick in the draft.
However, when the Browns called Sanders, it was not the first call he received during the draft process.
An NFL official said the league is looking into how Shedeur Sanders’ private number was leaked and then used for this prank call: pic.twitter.com/h5P1CIIQlI
On night two of the draft, Shedeur received a call from someone pretending to be Mickey Loomis, the GM of the New Orleans Saints .
During the call, the prankster told Sanders that New Orleans would be selecting him soon. Eventually, the caller went on to say, "Actually, you're going to have to wait a bit longer. Sorry about that."
What Sanders didn't know at the time was that the caller was not Loomis or even anyone in the Saints organization.
Instead, the call came from 21-year-old Jax Ulbrich. Jax is the son of Jeff Ulbrich, who is the defensive coordinator for the Saints' rival, the Atlanta Falcons. Reportedly, Jax got Shedeur's number off an iPad he found at his parents' home.
In the end, the prank really had nothing to do with the Saints, other than the fact that they were the team used as a cover-up.
However, New Orleans just so happens to be Sanders' first opponent in 2026 as the starting quarterback.
Unlike last season, when Sanders came in at a time when wins did not matter, the Browns are actually in a place to compete in 2026. With a chance at the playoffs and a potential first-ever AFC North title on the line, every game, every drive, and every play matters.
By far, this will be the highest-stakes game of Sanders' professional career.
Depending on how Sanders performs and the injury status of Deshaun Watson, this game could be one of the only chances Shedeur gets to show Cleveland his potential as the starting quarterback.
Coming into this season, many fans thought Sanders would be the starter over Watson, or at least take over after Watson performed poorly. With the shocking start, Sanders has settled in as the number-two option.
But this can't distract the Browns from remembering that Deshaun Watson is 31 years old and in the last year of his contract.
If Shedeur is able to play well, get wins for the Browns while Watson is out, and leave the organization with some impressive film to watch, the 2027 NFL Draft and future quarterback plans may look different than many think.
Regardless, we can only think one week at a time, and a win for the Browns is the most important thing at the moment.

title: Insider Shuts Down Shedeur Sanders Trade Rumors, Browns Backing QB2
full_text:
It is time to see what Shedeur Sanders has in the tank.
And no matter how he performs, the Cleveland Browns have no plans to move on from him this season.
On Friday, Nov. 6, the Browns announced that Sanders would be starting the team's Week 9 clash with the New Orleans Saints. All week long, speculation had been running rampant about who the team's starter would be, with eight-week starter Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol.
Although Watson looked like he might be good enough to go by the time the Browns made their way to Caesars Superdome, head coach Todd Monken is going to stand behind his second-year signal caller, giving him his first start of the 2026 season.
"He's very diligent and he likes to play football, has a natural confidence about him," Monken said when speaking about Sanders' growth. "Just like any young player, they've got to play... where he's improved is his footwork, his drops, his mechanics, understanding where to go with the ball, sense of urgency in terms of working through his progressions, protections.
"There were so many things he needed to work on, and he's done that like any young player..."
Sanders' last start in the regular season came at the end of the 2025 season, where he went 11-for-22 for 111 yards, zero touchdowns and zero interceptions. He finished with 1,400 passing yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions.
This season, he has attempted just three passes in moments when Watson had to leave the game for a few snaps, but he didn't get a chance to flash much. Each time he entered, Watson would get cleared and return just a few plays later.
With plenty of growth being made this past offseason, according to Monken, all eyes will be on how he looks in his first real opportunity of 2026.
And while some speculated that Sanders getting the nod on Sunday was a way for the front office to show off what he has as potential trade bait, NFL Insider Jeremy Fowler shot down such a sentiment.
"One thing to keep in mind: This is not a trade showcase. The Browns have no plans to deal Sanders at the deadline," Fowler recently wrote in a post on X.
More on Shedeur Sanders getting the start Week 9 with Deshaun Watson in protocol, via @DanielOyefusi One thing to keep in mind: This is not a trade showcase. The Browns have no plans to deal Sanders at the deadline. https://t.co/Ph0ljiLyeZ
The Browns could explore moving one of the other two quarterbacks on the roster not named Watson or Sanders, though, with second-year Dillon Gabriel still looking for another chance to show the league what he has to offer and rookie Taylen Green being a pretty athletic piece for a team to test the waters with.
Over the last few weeks, quarterbacks have been moved left and right due to injuries, and as the deadline approaches, the Browns could be called to give up one of their four.
For now, though, the focus is on Sanders and whether he can lead the Browns to a 6-3 record, potentially earning another chance as the franchise quarterback in the process.

title: Browns Just Made A Batch of Roster Moves and One Position Group Deserves More Attention
full_text:
As the Cleveland Browns (5-3) gear up for a Week 9 road trip to face the New Orleans Saints (2-5) on Sunday, the team completed a number of roster moves over the past few days.
Among these transactions, one specific position group stands out.
During the week, the Browns signed guard Austin Blaske and tackle Xavier Truss to the practice squad , while also releasing tackle Andrew Coker and guard Vershon Lee from said practice squad.
While these moves don’t affect the active roster, they do come at a point where Cleveland leads the league in sacks allowed by a large margin. The Browns, coming off their second eight-sack game of the season, have now reached 33 allowed sacks for the campaign, with seven other teams tied for second place at a very distant 23 sacks allowed.
And Cleveland hasn't been able to establish the running game , either.
Most probably, that the team isn’t quite comfortable with the low end of the depth chart, either.
As the team is still waiting to see its starting five gel into a cohesive and well-oiled unit, Cleveland is shuffling some of the players on the practice squad just in case. And even if that doesn’t mean that Blaske or Truss will get some playing time soon, it could point to some changes on the horizon for the unit as a whole.
As things stand now, right tackle Tytus Howard and left guard Zion Johnson have been frequently singled out as the weakest link on a line that includes two rookies. Veteran Teven Jenkins, projected as a starter before the season began, hasn’t played a snap all season long and is currently on IR. Backups Dawand Jones at tackle, KT Leveston at guard and/or rookie Parker Brailsford at center could be close to getting a shot in the lineup.
If so, the depth behind any promotion to the first-team unit could get a makeover as well, and that’s where Blaske and Truss could find a way toward the 53-man roster.
Trading Howard or Johnson away after just half a season on the team doesn’t make much sense because of the heavy dead cap hits the Browns would incur for next year. But giving guys like Jones or Leveston a chance to see if they can gel with the rest of the unit does.
And taking a good look at other options for depth purposes, with an eye on the future, makes sense, because there’s no way Cleveland will want to keep playing behind the offensive line as it’s currently built in 2027 and beyond.

title: What Browns Head Coach Todd Monken Had To Say About Shedeur Sanders Starting
full_text:
It's not every day that a second-year signal-caller is thrust into a starting role in Week 9 of the NFL season.
Let alone when that opportunity comes after the starting quarterback is placed in concussion protocol midweek, despite clearing it in each of the two previous days.
But that's the situation Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders finds himself in.
On Friday, Nov. 6, the Browns officially confirmed that Sanders would start this weekend in an outing against the New Orleans Saints. Heading into the contest, the Browns are 5-3, with a spot atop the AFC North still in reach.
With Deshaun Watson leading the team in all of the eight previous weeks, Sanders jumping headfirst into the fire this weekend has drawn an awful lot of attention.
Fortunately, he has all the support of head coach Todd Monken.
When asked about his thoughts on Sanders getting his first start of the season, he didn't hold back, expressing his excitement to the highest degree.
“Oh yeah, I’m fired up," he said. "I’m fired up to see him play. I mean, who wouldn’t be?... This is what he’s wanted, right? He wants to be a starting quarterback in the NFL. Let’s go. Let’s let it rip. Let’s see what we got. We’re not holding anything back."
#Browns HC Todd Monken said he's "fired up" to see Shedeur Sanders play on Sunday. “Oh yeah, I’m fired up. I’m fired up to see him play. I mean, who wouldn’t be?... This is what he’s wanted, right? He wants to be a starting quarterback in the NFL. Let’s go. Let’s let it rip.… pic.twitter.com/6NWSa8AfnJ
Sanders comes into Sunday's game with 1,402 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions across 10 games on his resume. He has also flashed a bit of versatility in his game, rushing 21 times for 169 yards and one touchdown.
He isn't a stranger to regular season NFL action, but he hasn't had a legitimate taste of it since January 4th of last season.
This time around, Watson's not in a bad situation, though.
The Browns are playing competitive football, Monken has helped round out the team on both sides of the ball to a respectable spot and there are new weapons for Sanders to be surrounded by.
And with improvements made across the board this past offseason on the fundamental and technical sides of his game, the 25-year-old has every avenue to succeed on the road from Caesars Superdome.
“He’s improved is his footwork, his drops, his mechanics, understanding where to go with the ball, sense of urgency in terms of working through his progressions, protections," Monken said. "There were so many things he needed to work on, and he’s done that like any young player. Any young player has a lot to work on, especially at the quarterback position. And you could see that from the moment we got here.
"And that’s why we opened up the competition and we split the reps, was because of his ascent. That’s what we did. And again, this is just another piece of that. Just like this weekend will be another piece of that.”
#Browns HC Todd Monken on where Shedeur Sanders has improved most in his game: “Where he’s improved is his footwork, his drops, his mechanics, understanding where to go with the ball, sense of urgency in terms of working through his progressions, protections. There were so many… pic.twitter.com/OhwAUkfupV
Sanders may not have this starting spot for longer than a single weekend, which is why leaving everything out on the gridiron is so important.
But who knows, if he goes out there and dominates , maybe the Browns will give him another opportunity to show what he has in the tank.
The Browns and Saints will collide at 1:00 p.m. EST on Sunday, Nov. 8.

title: Todd Monken Makes His Call: What's Ahead for Browns Second-Year QB Shedeur Sanders?
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have a new starting quarterback for the Week 9 matchup against the New Orleans Saints.
Deshaun Watson returned on a limited basis for the final practice ahead of the Saints matchup, but remained in concussion protocol.
#Browns QB Deshaun Watson (concussion protocol) returned to practice today. pic.twitter.com/LHaXZFaXl3
Despite this, Browns head coach Todd Monken announced that Shedeur Sanders would be the starter against the Saints. Monken even went as far as to say, "I'm fired up to see him play. I mean, who wouldn't be?" The question now is whether Sanders will rise to the occasion.
Sanders showed confidence early in the week ahead of the matchup with the Saints. Speaking during the media slot typically reserved for starting quarterback Deshaun Watson, he was asked what he saw on film from the Saints' defense. The Browns' new starter said, “Yeah, I’ve seen a lot. When I smile, just know that means something. I’m maturing. I’m maturing.”
#Browns QB Shedeur Sanders on the Saints defense: "Yeah, I've seen a lot. When I smile, just know that means something. (laughs) I'm maturing, you know what I'm saying? I'm maturing. Like, I could have gave that a decent answer, but now I'm just going to smile." pic.twitter.com/z9yKqtluRH
Some took it as confidence; others saw it as a way to give the media a non-answer and move on. After all, it isn’t like the starting quarterback is going to give away the team's game plan to the media. Regardless, Sanders has always been confident in himself, and with a full week of practice under his belt as the starter, he now has a chance to turn that confidence into results on Sunday.
Shedeur Sanders will be making his first start of the season against the Saints. Sanders started seven games for the Browns last season, passing for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions.
Sanders’ record as the starter for the Browns was 3-4, and while he showed flashes of what made many think of him as a first-round talent, it was clear the young QB needed more development.
After an offseason of development , a preseason quarterback competition, and eight games spent learning behind Watson , Sanders now has a chance to show his progress. Monken said during OTAs on June 3, ‘I just tell you, we got two starting-level quarterbacks. We really do.” Sunday will test that assessment.
some of Shedeur Sanders best throws vs. the Titans from the All-22 tape. #Browns The first ball to Fannin with a DE barreling down in his face is just silly... pic.twitter.com/zsZSNHxgbT
Will his performance be reminiscent of the 2025 matchup against the Titans, where he threw for 364 yards and three touchdowns? Or will Sanders fall back into bad habits and have an outing like the 2025 Bears matchup, where he threw three interceptions?
Only time will tell. But one thing is for sure: Shedeur is confident in his ability to perform in year two.

title: Rumors Swirling About Browns Trade Deadline Plans: Are New Additions on the Horizon?
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns haven't been rumored to do too much at the upcoming 2026 NFL Trade Deadline.
But reports from Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer show the front office could at least explore the market.
On Friday, Nov. 6, Breer released an updated look at the league at large, exploring different agendas teams will be heading into the deadline with. For the Browns, they are reportedly expected to look around for an additional rotational edge rusher and a blocking tight end.
"The Browns are actually positioned now as buyers , which is pretty fascinating," Breer wrote. "Cleveland has looked around at adding a rotational edge rusher and perhaps a blocking tight end, which would free them up to move Harold Fannin Jr. around even more."
Trade deadline updates, per @AlbertBreer : • Giants, Jaguars, Vikings looking for help at DT • Texans checked in on available RBs and safeties • Browns looked at adding rotational edge rusher and perhaps a blocking TE • Steelers monitoring WR market and could deal LB Cole…
While Breer didn't list any players specifically, there are a few notable names the front office could be taking a look at.
If the Browns are looking to add another body opposite or behind Jared Verse, there are a few options the front office could consider.
Just a week ago, the Tennessee Titans made a major trade, sending away defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons to the Chicago Bears. In return, they landed a handful of valuable picks to re-up the squad in the coming NFL Draft.
But they may not be done making trades just yet.
. @JFowlerESPN lists the Browns as a fit to trade for: - EDGE Khalil Mack - EDGE Jermaine Johnson - EDGE YaYa Diaby pic.twitter.com/Eau26cu7Ew
Rumors have swirled that the Titans could consider sending 27-year-old Jermaine Johnson on his way. Sitting on a $13 million deal, the interest around the league will be high for an edge rusher like him who is in the heart of his prime.
Over the last two years, he has totaled six sacks and consistently ranked in the top half of PFF ratings at his position.
If the Browns can move around the cap space needed to land him, they have the draft capital to bolster the line even more.
Outside of Johnson, the New York Giants' Kayvon Thibodeaux has been rumored to be on the trade block , alongside Los Angeles Chargers veteran Kahlil Mack. Both would likely be one-year rentals, but could end up securing an extension by the end of the season.
Even if the team goes a different route, adding a lesser-known name to bolster the depth, such a move would be smart given how lackluster Verse's play has been this season.
There really aren't a lot of tight ends that have ended up in trade conversations this season.
But that doesn't mean the Browns are flying in the dark.
A lot of the NFL's best teams are not going to part ways with their blocking tight ends, most notably the San Francisco 49ers, who have George Kittle, and even the Minnesota Vikings, who have Josh Oliver.
However, one addition that could make sense, while also being realistic, is John Bates from the Washington Commanders. With the Commanders performing so poorly this season, sitting at a record of 2-4-1 and third in the NFC East, moving on from Bates could land them important draft capital as they look to retool this offseason.
The 29-year-old isn't a headline-grabbing tight end, but he does provide unmatched consistency. Across the last six seasons, he has hauled in 77 passes for 722 yards and three touchdowns , all while being a top blocker in both the rushing attack and pass protection.
In his 2021 rookie season, he earned the highest PFF run-blocking grade ever recorded by a first-year tight end, before finishing first in run-blocking that season.
Currently signed to a three-year deal, the Browns would be able to keep Bates around for a good amount of time, making him less of an immediate fix but a long-term solution to the tight end room.
Such a trade would also create more opportunities for Harold Fannin Jr. and give him that receiving-first role full-time.
The Browns are certainly going to take a look at the trade block with the deadline approaching, especially if they can take down the New Orleans Saints this coming weekend and maintain a top spot in the division.
The only question is if the front office will be willing to pull the trigger on any deals.

title: Cleveland Native and Former NFL Player Calls Out Jared Verse's Recent Comments
full_text:
When Jared Verse joined the Cleveland Browns this past offseason, he quickly emerged as a leader both on the field and off.
He was seen numerous times helping the younger members of the team, including recently drafted offensive tackle Spencer Fano, while also maintaining a consistent presence in the media spotlight as he hyped up the Browns' potential for the 2026 season.
But as the year has ticked along, Verse has put himself in some uncomfortable situations.
That mouth that led to him being beloved his first few months now has him in hot water, especially following a loss to the rival Pittsburgh Steelers this past weekend , 27-6. All week leading up to the game, Verse bantered with the Steelers' Cam Heyward and called out numerous aspects of their game.
Obviously, as the scoreline shows, he wasn't able to back it up.
Cleveland native and former NFL offensive lineman LeCharles Bentley recently spoke out and criticized how loud Verse has been off the field and how quiet he has been on the field.
"I had a friend growing up… he always wanted to start fights with folks… it was cool for a while, until I realized, he just talked too much," a post on X from Bentley wrote. We stopped being friends when he got beat up for talking and I didn’t help. But he learned a lesson… stop talkin."
I had a friend growing up… he always wanted to start fights with folks… it was cool for a while, until I realized, he just talked too much. We stopped being friends when he got beat up for talking and I didn’t help. But he learned a lesson… stop talkin. #LessonLearned https://t.co/P1OTOtPI8S
Verse has seemingly been all bark, no bite, to begin the season, as through eight games he has a whopping 18 combined tackles, 10 solo, and four tackles for a loss . He has yet to record a sack, but has gotten into the backfield to at least produce six quarterback hits.
Either way, that productivity off the edge ranks him towards the bottom of the league in multiple areas.
To add insult to injury, Verse tried to blame the situations the defense has been put in for his inability to affect the game.
“I think attention has been focused on me not doing enough on this aspect, that aspect, I don’t think we’ve been getting enough 3rd and longs to put myself in the position to get the stats,” Verse said recently.
“I think attention has been focused on me not doing enough on this aspect, that aspect, I don’t think think we’ve been getting enough 3rd and longs to put myself in the position to get the stats,” Jared Verse on his lack of production this season. pic.twitter.com/0T8eD5RAOb
Bentley's comments echo the sentiment that a lot of people around the league seem to be feeling right now about Verse. For how vocal he has been, he just simply hasn't backed up the talk with productivity on the gridiron.
There is still plenty of season left to play, giving the freshly 26-year-old time to rebound and prove the doubters wrong, but he may want to lay low and pull himself out of the spotlight.
The Browns return to the field on Sunday, Nov. 8, for a road matchup with the New Orleans Saints . The two sides will go toe-to-toe at 1:00 p.m. EST from Caesars Superdome.

title: Will George Pickens Play Today? Injury Update, Start-or-Sit Advice for Week 9
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have some uncertainty on the offensive side of the ball this week for the game against the Indianapolis Colts thanks to wide receiver George Pickens.
Pickens was again listed on the injury report this week, albeit with one less issue. Pickens battled hamstring and shoulder issues in Week 8 but is only dealing with the former this week.
And, just like last week, Pickens practiced on a limited basis all three days before drawing the questionable tag for Sunday.
Here's what we know about Pickens' chances of suiting up as kickoff approaches.
We're getting mixed signals from the Cowboys when it comes to Pickens' status for Sunday.
On one hand, the Cowboys elevated wide receiver Jordan Hudson from the practice squad, which could indicate the Cowboys are at least not optimistic about Pickens' chances of playing.
The Cowboys are missing fellow wide receiver KaVontae Turpin, but they did not elevate a wide receiver in each of the past two weeks Turpin has been ruled out, so that's noteworthy.
On the other hand, Pickens did travel with the team to Indianapolis and that is a good sign for his chances of suiting up, although certainly not a definitive one.
We also know that head coach Brian Schottenheimer said he was "hopeful" Pickens would play on Friday.
Based Schottenheimer's comment and the fact that he's traveling, we'd say Pickens has a better chance to play than not in Week 9. We'll know for sure around 11:30 a.m. ET on Sunday, when inactives drop.
Pickens could be limited if he does play this week, but that has been the case in each of the past two weeks and he was still over 40 snaps in each game and that's enough for him to produce a strong fantasy outing.
Despite the fact he's in the midst of a down season, the Cowboys wide receiver still ranks as WR17 overall , according to Fantasy Pros, which makes him a WR2 play every week.
The Colts actually present a tough matchup for wide receivers, with Indy giving up the 11th-fewest fantasy points to wideouts , according to CBS Sports.
However, Pickens has been productive enough that he should be in lineups on a weekly basis, regardless of opponent. Adding to that, the Colts are in the midst of a fire sale and we could see a mail-it-in kind of performance out of Indy on Sunday.
If Pickens doesn't play, Dallas' No. 3 wide receiver, Ryan Flournoy is a viable replacement in your lineup. Over the past three weeks, the Cowboys wideout ranks as WR14 overall after tallying 14 catches, 148 yards and two touchdowns in that span — and that was with Pickens in the lineup.
Verdict: Start Pickens (or Flournoy if Pickens is inactive)

title: Dallas Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown Fined by NFL for Controversial Hit
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys suffered an embarrassing loss to the Arizona Cardinals last week, and that's putting it lightly.
Dallas collapsed in the worst of ways, choking away a double-digit lead while letting Cardinals backup quarterback Gardner Minshew lead a miracle rally. The Cowboys would go on to lose 33-30 in overtime, marking their third loss in four games and dropping Dallas to a 3-5 record.
Now, to add insult to injury, the NFL is fining Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown before Dallas heads into Lucas Oil Stadium for Sunday's matchup with the Indianapolis Colts.
Per reports from Tom Pelissero , the NFL is fining Overshown $9,528 for the hit that knocked Cardinals running back Bam Knight out of last week's game against Dallas. Knight was diagnosed with a concussion and has already been ruled out for Arizona's Week 9 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.
Overshown led with his shoulder but his helmet makes contact with Knight's, who fumbled the ball as a result of the hit.
However, there's certainly room for debate when it comes to deciding whether or not Overshown's hit should be deemed worthy of a fine for the NFL.
Though the helmet makes contact, it's clear that Overshown is intentionally leading with his shoulder in order to avoid a penalty. The officials on the field clearly didn't feel it was illegal in real time, as a flag wasn't thrown.
The NFL fined Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown $9,528 for use of the helmet on this hit that knocked out Cardinals RB Bam Knight last week. pic.twitter.com/9mWFJVbfn9
He doesn't lower his head toward Knight, something that would have put both players at risk of a serious injury.
It's unclear at this point if Overshown will look to appeal the fine. Even though he has a good argument, it's unlikely the NFL would overturn the ruling but you won't know until you try.
Regardless, it's obvious the NFL doesn't feel the hit was as serious as it could have been or else the fine would have matched some of the others that the league handed down on Saturday.
Despite Overshown forcing a turnover for the second straight week, it didn't matter in the end for Dallas.
Still, it's hard not to feel pleased with what he's been able to do since coming back from the hamstring injury that forced him to miss five straight games.
In his return to the field in Week 7 against the Philadelphia Eagles, Overshown came up with his second-career interception. Along with the forced fumble against the Cardinals, he had a season-high eight total tackles.
Overshown is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Colts due to a hamstring issue once again. Hopefully he can suit up to continue what has been some solid individual production for him the past two games.

title: George Pickens' Week 9 Status Now More in Question After Cowboys' Roster Move
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys made an eyebrow-raising roster move on Saturday that might indicate wide receiver George Pickens is in danger of sitting out in Week 9 against the Indianapolis Colts.
Pickens has been on the injury report the past two weeks with a hamstring issue. He was listed with a shoulder injury last week, also, but that was negated from the injury report this week.
The Cowboys wideout practiced on a limited basis all three days this week before drawing the questionable tag, but there wasn't really any concern for him because he followed the same path before playing in Week 8 .
However, the Cowboys announced on Saturday that they have elevated wide receiver Jordan Hudson from the practice squad, which could indicate they think Pickens won't play.
"They also elevated rookie WR Jordan Hudson and TE James Mitchell from the p-squad," Joseph Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News relayed.
The Cowboys are short-handed at receiver with KaVontae Turpin ruled out once again this week, so on the surface one could assume that's why Hudson was elevated.
However, the Cowboys, who normally dress five wide receivers, did not elevate a wide receiver in each of the previous two weeks Turpin missed and instead made rookie Camden Brown active as the fifth receiver, which is why this week's elevation is noteworthy. Hudson would be the fifth receiver if Pickens is ruled out and Brown is active once again, which we expect him to be.
At the very least, this appears to be a sign that the Cowboys aren't totally confident Pickens will play. We'll get our final answer on his status an hour and a half before kickoff on Sunday, when the Cowboys release their inactives.
When addressing Pickens' Week 9 status on Friday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer made no promises and said he was only "hopeful" Pickens would play .
The elevation of Mitchell likely means at least one of Jake Ferguson or Luke Schoonmaker won't play. Both players are listed as questionable.
Ferguson appears to have less of a chance to play, as his ankle injury, which was diagnosed as a low-ankle sprain , led to him turning in just one limited practice during the week.
Meanwhile, Schoonmaker, who missed last week's game with his groin injury, turned in three limited practices this week, which amounted to progress for him.
If both players sit, the Cowboys will be seriously short-handed at the tight end spot, as Mitchell would only give Dallas two healthy tight ends, along with Brevyn Spann-Ford.
Mitchell was elevated last week, also, but did not play any snaps on offense and instead appeared for 10 plays on special teams.
Dallas will need him for some offensive snaps this week if Schoonmaker and Ferguson are sidelined.

title: George Pickens Trade Rumor Confirms Cowboys' Stance on Dealing Star WR at Deadline
full_text:
With the Dallas Cowboys on the fast track to nowhere at 3-5 this season, there has been increasing buzz about the team possibly trading George Pickens .
However, if you're one of the people in the trade Pickens camp, or if you're here because you want your team to trade for Pickens, don't get your hopes up for anything to happen.
According to the Fort Worth Star-Telegram's Nick Harris , there is no interest on the Cowboys' part in trading Pickens before the Nov. 10 deadline on Tuesday.
"The fifth-year pass-catcher and second-year Cowboy is playing this season on the franchise tag after the team elected not to discuss a long-term contract with him in the offseason. Despite trade rhetoric around the time of that decision being announced, the Cowboys never engaged in trying to send him away. Seven months later, that strategy remains the same ahead of the deadline, according to multiple sources," Harris wrote.
This isn't the first report we've seen about the Cowboys' lack of interest in a Pickens trade, as NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said there's simply "nothing there" with a Pickens trade.
"As of right now there's nothing there," Rapoport said of a Pickens trade on The Pat McAfee Show .
Perhaps things will change if the Cowboys drop yet another game to the lowly Indianapolis Colts on Sunday , but we wouldn't even bet on that being enough.
Let's be real here: Dallas isn't going anywhere in 2026 with the awful defense it has and there is nothing to be gained by the Cowboys keeping Pickens.
We still don't envision a scenario in which the Cowboys extend the mercurial wide receiver, as they cannot afford to have two big wide receiver contracts on the books, something even Stephen Jones has said will be difficult to do .
"The situation we have with George Pickens going alongside CeeDee... I don't know of any teams that really can pay two top receivers top of the market," Jones said. "So, yeah. That's going to be a real difficult situation as we move forward. We've managed to figure out how we can do it for this year."
When we say "cannot afford," we don't mean strictly from a cap space standpoint because the Cowboys can make it work. But having two big wide receiver contracts on the books will be a major hinderance to Dallas being able to improve its roster elsewhere.
The most the Cowboys are going to get for Pickens is a second-round pick, but we're doubtful they can get that much, especially because of his contract situation. More realistically, a third-rounder is probably the most Dallas will get.
If a team comes through with a third-round pick, which is the best the Cowboys can hope for in a compensatory pick if the team allows Pickens to walk in free agency, they should take it.
If there's a team willing to offer more, the Cowboys shouldn't think twice about trading the star wideout.
There's also a scenario in which Dallas could dangle Pickens in a trade for an impact defender, like an edge rusher, for example. If that opportunity presents itself, the Cowboys should spring, especially if minimal or no draft compensation is required.

title: NFL Insider Identifies Dallas Cowboys' Most Logical NFL Trade Deadline Approach
full_text:
We are just days away from finding out if the Dallas Cowboys are going to add to their defense ahead of the trade deadline.
As we sit here on Saturday, the deadline is rapidly approaching on Tuesday, Nov. 10. The Cowboys certainly need help on defense , but Jerry Jones also has to weigh if its worth it to make a trade given how hopeless Dallas' unit looks this season.
When it comes to what the Cowboys might do at the deadline , The Athletic's Jonathan Jones believes a player-for-player swap is the only kind of trade that makes sense for Dallas.
"The only sort of trade that makes sense for Dallas would be a player-for-player deal involving someone on defense," he said.
The Cowboys have depleted their draft pick stockpile in recent years with some big trades, including the ones for Rashan Gary, Quinnen Williams and Joey Porter Jr., among others.
As a result of those deals, the Cowboys have just four picks in next year's draft, including one in the first, second, fourth and seventh rounds.
Then, in 2028, the Cowboys don't have their second- and seventh-round picks, although they do have two in the sixth.
Outside of being able to make a huge blockbuster trade that will add a premier edge rusher, which is the only kind of move that has any hope of saving Dallas' awful defense, it just does not make much sense to sacrifice more draft capital.
As we said, the Cowboys need a massive upgrade at edge rusher to even have a chance to turn their defense around.
Getting that kind of player is difficult in and of itself, but trying to land a top-notch edge rusher in a player-for-player trade will be impossible.
The only player who could come close to garnering that type of  return that the Cowboys could afford to trade is wide receiver George Pickens, and even then he probably won't be enough alone and draft capital would still be required.
We also know that the Cowboys are unlikely to have any interest in trading Pickens, even though it makes sense to do so given the fact he probably doesn't have a future in Dallas.
"As of right now there's nothing there (with a Pickens trade)," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said on The Pat McAfee Show .
Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram is saying the same.
"“The fifth-year pass-catcher and second-year Cowboy is playing this season on the franchise tag after the team elected not to discuss a long-term contract with him in the offseason," said Harris.
"Despite trade rhetoric around the time of that decision being announced, the Cowboys never engaged in trying to send him away. Seven months later, that strategy remains the same ahead of the deadline, according to multiple sources."
We would not rule out Jerry saying "F them picks" even more and going out and making a significant trade, but it just doesn't seem like the most likely scenario at this point given everything we know.

title: Cowboys' Jonathan Mingo Trade Lands Among NFL's Worst Deadline Mistakes
full_text:
As the 2026 NFL trade deadline approaches , fans are anxiously awaiting the news that their favorite team made a huge move to improve their chances of making a postseason run. While some of the moves made at the deadline do allow a team to take a huge step forward, there are also plenty of trades that don't work out.
That was the case for the Dallas Cowboys in 2024 when they sent a fourth-round pick to the Carolina Panthers for wide receiver Jonathan Mingo and a seventh-round pick. At the time, Jerry Jones praised himself for the move, saying they had their eyes on Mingo in the draft the previous year, and he felt they landed someone who could develop into a potential starter opposite CeeDee Lamb.
That hasn't happened as Mingo has just nine receptions for 101 yards in 22 games for the Cowboys. His lack of production , as well as the fact that there were better options available, led Brent Sobleski of Bleacher Report to name the Mingo trade among the worst 10 deadline trades over the past decade .
"The amazing part of the Dallas Cowboys' acquisition of Jonathan Mingo is how little they've received in return even though he's still on the team. To make matters worse, the Kansas City Chiefs flipped a lower draft pick to acquire DeAndre Hopkins prior to the same trade deadline," Sobleski wrote.
It's shocking to realize that Mingo is still on the Cowboys' roster. As Sobleski stated, he hasn't been a "friendly" target for Dak Prescott. Mingo has caught just 31 percent of the passes thrown his way, and while he has had some great moments in the preseason and training camp, he hasn't found success on the field.
Dallas has tried multiple ways to get Mingo involved, even using him as a return man this season. With KaVontae Turpin banged up, Mingo has seen time as a punt returner as well as on kickoffs. He has 47 yards on seven punt returns and 69 yards on three kick returns.
Even with that usage, it's hard to justify his spot on the roster. It's even more difficult to defend the trade. And while hindsight is 20/20, this is a move that was ridiculed from the moment it was announced. Perhaps that's why Jerry Jones won't move on, since he may be desperate to prove his investment was worth it.

title: Jerry Jones Reaches New Level of Absurdity Defending Cowboys Coaching Salary Stance
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is known for giving some of the wildest answers when asked about his franchise. One of the hottest topics as of late is his stance on coaching salaries .
Jones is facing criticism for hiring Brian Schottenheimer in 2025, a coach who was on no one's radar during the hiring cycle. The belief is that Jones wanted Schottenheimer since he wasn't an expensive coach, and Jones was being criticized for refusing to pay top dollar for a legitimate head coach.
In response, Jones went off the rails and went on a nonsensical rant about how there's no correlation between paying coaches and winning. It was a ridiculous, and factually inaccurate statement, but Jones might have made it even weirder somehow with his latest comments.
While appearing on 105.3 The Fan, Jones was asked about the criticism he's been facing for his refusal to pay coaches a top salary. Instead of addressing that, he decided to remind everyone just how rich he is.
“I drill wells. I have five wells going right now that cost more than any coach,” Jones said via Jon Machota of The Athletic.
It's really hard to think of a response to that. It's even more difficult to try and figure out how in the world Jones thought that was an adequete responese. Jones has been known to get defensive in the past, and that appears to be the case here. Instead of realizing that he is being asked why he doesn't believe coaching matters as much as every other franchise believes, Jones seemed to take this as an attack on his filthty richness.
What's even more ironic about his response is the fact that he made himself look even worse. Jones made sure to let the world know that money is no object for him, but that makes his refusal to pay for a championship-caliber coach even worse.
There is no salary cap when it comes to coaching staffs, meaning that Jones could decide to pay a coach whatever he wanted. By reminding the world that he makes billions outside of football, he's also proving his critics right. Jones has the means to pay any salary and it wouldn't make a dent in his pocketbook. Instead, he continues to pay his players while going cheap on the coaching staff.
Perhaps it's because he's still sour over Jimmy Johnson getting more credit than him in the 1990s or if he devalues coaches, which is what Colin Cowherd recently accused him of . Either way, Jones continues to be his own worst enemy as he pursues his first title run in over 30 years and his latest defense proves that he still doesn't understand how much of a problem he truly is.

title: Steelers Trade Rumor Gives Cowboys Potential Target for Addition on Defense
full_text:
If the Dallas Cowboys are looking to make an addition at the linebacker spot before the NFL trade deadline hits on Nov. 10, they might want to give the Pittsburgh Steelers a call.
According to Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer , the Steelers could sell at least one player at the deadline next week.
And that player, Breer says, is linebacker Cole Holcomb.
"Then there’s the Steelers, who, again, are sniffing around at receiver, and could deal veteran LB Cole Holcomb," he said.
Of course, the Cowboys and Steelers are no strangers to making trades with one another, as Dallas has acquired George Pickens , Broderick Jones and Joey Porter Jr. from Pittsburgh since 2025.
The Steelers don't profile as sellers with a 6-2 record, but based on what Breer is saying, it appears they could at least move Holcomb.
The veteran has no role on defense, as evidenced by his playing on just 4.3% of snaps this season, which could make him expendable for the right price.
On paper, the Cowboys are in good shape at the linebacker spot with DeMarvion Overshown, Dee Winters, Jaishawn Barham and Shemar James.
However, Overshown is once again proving to be unreliable after having injury issues this season. He has already missed a handful of games in 2026, and now he's back on the injury report in Week 9 with a hamstring issue.
As a result, the Cowboys might consider making a small move at linebacker, and trading for Holcomb would qualify as that kind of move.
Linebacker certainly isn't the Cowboys' biggest need, so they are not going to want to spend much if they do decide to add there, and that's especially true with Dallas not having many draft selections over the next few years.
Holcomb would be cheap and can likely be had for a late Day 3 pick, which wouldn't put much of a dent in Dallas' dwindling stockpile of picks .
Not only would Holcomb provide depth on defense, he can also make a big impact on special teams, where he thrives the most.
While that's all well and good, we'd like it's more likely Dallas won't be making a move at linebacker and will instead focus all of their attention on their biggest need, which is edge rusher.
Truth be told, the Cowboys should probably stand pat all together, as chances are there isn't a player out there who can save them.

title: Broncos HC Sean Payton Explains Importance of LT Garett Bolles
full_text:
Denver Broncos mainstay left tackle Garett Bolles impacts the game week-to-week in ways that even a well-trained observer couldn't notice.
"A lot" of ways, according to Broncos head coach Sean Payton, who explained that Bolles' high-level ability in pass protection directly translates to the opponents' defensive approaches.
“You can’t chip, nudge everyone and you want flare control into the route," Payton told reporters during his post-practice availability on Wednesday. "A lot of times it might be one rusher that you really want to help with. Yes. I know the whole story of the blind side, but you want one of those... In other words, that left tackle, there are times where I’ll say to ‘Bollesy’ (Bolles), ‘Hey, you’ve got him.’ He can do that. Yes, if we’re having to make... Now there’s times if [Charger OLB] Khalil Mack lines up there, we might move the tight end over there with a Mack protection and just nudge wherever he’s at. Last week we had a little protection plan for where [Chiefs DT Chris] Jones was. So I think that’s tonight’s meeting and it takes a while. Yes, we appreciate the skillset he has.”
A first-team All-Pro last season, Bolles is in the midst of another all-star campaign -- one that could earn him the NFL's Protector of the Year Award. Entering Week 9 , he ranks as Pro Football Focus ' No. 6 offensive tackle among 69 qualifiers; the ninth-best run blocker and the fourth-best in pass-pro.
Across 492 offensive snaps, Bolles has yet to allow a sack on quarterback Bo Nix while surrendering just one hit and three pressures. This, despite facing some of the league's top defenses (Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, Seahawks) to open the season.
“Nobody scares me," the tenth-year veteran told The Denver Post earlier this week. "I respect all these guys, but nothing scares me. I’m not scared to go against those dudes like some people are in the league. I think that’s what separates me from everybody else.”
Bolles' next mission, one that comes before the Week 10 bye, will be to keep Nix upright on Sunday against the middling Carolina Panthers, whose interim-coordinator-led defense ranks 28th in the NFL in sacks this year with 11. Their 11.5% pressure rate ranks 30th among all teams.
Though some view this as a classic trap game for Denver, Bolles and the rest of his offensive line mates should be able to weather the Panthers' toothless pass-rush, and the Broncos likely coast to an easier victory than most other weeks.
Beyond that is the NFL trade deadline in which the Broncos could be active -- perhaps along the front-five. ESPN recently suggested that the club acquires former Pro Bowl OL Landon Dickerson from the Philadelphia Eagles, presumably to replace the man to Bolles' right, incumbent starting guard Ben Powers.

title: Broncos at Panthers: 5 Explosive Predictions
full_text:
No one should be sleeping on the Carolina Panthers , because they have a penchant for pulling off upsets.
The Denver Broncos are riding high after their big divisional win secured them sole possession of the AFC West lead, with NextGenStats giving them a 64% chance of winning the division . But the Broncos can't overlook the Panthers.
It's time to drop this week's bold predictions. If any of these predictions come true on Sunday, it will go a long way toward flying out of Carolina with another win as the Broncos head into their bye week.
With that said, it's time to be bold.
Waddle has an excellent matchup, no matter who he lines up against. The Panthers do well in eliminating explosive pass plays, but they still have weaknesses that Waddle can exploit.
With his after-the-catch ability, Waddle takes a short pass for over 30 yards, then adds a deep shot for another big gain.
Coleman hasn't played much, with only four games under his belt, touching the ball in three of them. But his season has been like one of his runs: he gains momentum as time goes on.
The rookie broke the century mark in scrimmage yards against the Kansas City Chiefs last week, and now he hits triple digits as a rusher against a bad run defense that's been getting worse each week.
Bryce Young has the fifth-highest pressure rate in the NFL, despite being blitzed at the 12th-lowest rate. Meanwhile, the Broncos have the fourth-highest pressure rate, while blitzing at the ninth-highest rate.
Denver also has the third-highest pressure rate without blitzing, which is actually higher than its pressure rate with blitzing. The Broncos have the horses to win with four, especially against a struggling Panthers offensive line.
The Broncos don't need to blitz a lot and still generate a lot of pressure. They get to Young four times without blitzing more than 25% of the time.
The Panthers do alright protecting the football, with just 10 giveaways this season, which is tied for the 16th-fewest. Meanwhile, the Broncos are tied for the 12th-most takeaways, with 10 thus far.
Given the advantages up front in the trenches and Young's issues under pressure, Denver should create ample opportunity for multiple takeaways in this matchup. Look for the Broncos to finish with three, especially if Talanoa Hufanga plays .
The Panthers' special teams unit hasn't been great, while Darren Rizzi has the Broncos' third phase among the best in the NFL.
The Broncos are clicking in all phases, and it leads to a big play against the Panthers with either a blocked field goal or a punt.

title: Pat Bryant's Return Sparks Unexpected Broncos Roster Shakeup
full_text:
After four weeks on injured reserve, the Denver Broncos officially activated Bryant on Saturday. In a corresponding move, the Broncos placed defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike on IR.
With a road game against the Carolina Panthers on deck for Sunday, the Broncos also elevated safety Taylor Rapp and running back Cody Schrader from the practice squad and signed cornerback/returner Sean Fresch Jr. to the 53-man roster.
Bryant suffered a scary ankle injury in Week 4 against the San Francisco 49ers that looked much worse than it ended up being. He was carted off, but fortunately, it was just a sprain and nothing more.
The Broncos could really use Bryant as their passing offense begins to take flight. He can win off the line of scrimmage and use his big 6-foot-2 frame to his advantage, boxing out defenders.
Bo Nix has forged a strong connection with Bryant, so I would expect to see the ball going his way often, even with other mouths to feed, like Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle. Nix trusts Bryant, and the second-year receiver's blocking on the perimeter will be a welcome bonus for the Broncos' still fledgling run game.
As for Uwazurike, he suffered a shoulder injury in last week's win over the Kansas City Chiefs. The Broncos must have believed that his recovery window will stretch beyond three weeks, so they placed him on IR. That means he'll be eligible to return in Week 14.
Meanwhile, the Broncos' defensive line rotation will have to step up. There will be a shift, as Uwazurike has been the fourth guy up front, which means we're either going to see a lot more of the veteran Jordan Jackson, or maybe even rookie third-rounder Tyler Onyedim, the last of whom has been a healthy scratch in all eight games thus far.
Sai'vion Jones might be the guy to move up into Uwazurike's spot as the fourth guy onto the field, but it wouldn't be a shock to see Jackson leapfrog him. And give Onyedim's stoutness against the run, I'm hopeful that Uwazurike's injury opens up some opportunities to not only dress the rookie, but also maybe even actually play him.
It's cool to see the Broncos reward Fresch with a roster spot. The first-year pro has been elevated from the practice squad a few times this season, and he's contributed well on special teams, including as a returner.
The Broncos like the former UFL standout a lot, but when it's time for other players to return from IR, he'll likely be the first guy to go, though the team will certainly hope to re-sign him to the practice squad.
As for the Broncos' two practice squad elevations, this is Rapp's third and final. After Sunday, the Broncos will either have to release him or sign him to the 53-man roster, as he has maxed out his three allotted elevations.
If the Broncos release Rapp before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, he could immediately re-sign to the practice squad, where his three elevations would reset to zero. After the trade deadline, as a vested veteran, the Broncos would have to waive him, which means that another team could claim him, before re-signing him to the practice squad.
I would expect the Broncos to release Rapp immediately after Sunday's game, or at least, well before the trade deadline at 2 p.m. MDT on Tuesday, at which point, he could promptly be re-signed to the practice squad. Clear as mud?
With RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie both on IR, the Broncos only have two healthy running backs on the 53-man roster — Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins — so they've elevated Schrader once again. Schrader stood out in the preseason back in August, and this will be his second elevation of the season, though he's yet to touch the ball.
There's a good chance Talanoa Hufanga will play on Sunday, though he's officially listed as questionable . He's been out for three games with an ankle injury, so if he were to miss this game, it would raise questions about why the Broncos didn't place him on IR and make use of his roster spot.
Fellow starting safety Brandon Jones has been ruled out with a hamstring, so it should be Hufanga and Rapp at safety, with a strong dose of Devon Key to boot.
Broncos-Panthers kicks off at 11 a.m. MDT on Sunday. The game will be broadcast locally by CBS , with Ian Eagle and Ross Tucker calling the game.

title: Broncos Made 'Outrageous' Trey McBride Trade Inquiry, Insider Claims
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have been linked to the running back trade market ahead of Tuesday's deadline, but they've been looking for other ways to improve their bottom-10 offense.
The tight end position has been a bit of a weakness for Denver. According to ESPN 's Adam Schefter, the Broncos have checked around the league, including one bold, outrageous call to Arizona to check on the availability of Cardinals All-Pro tight end Trey McBride.
"The Denver Broncos have checked in around the league on tight ends, going so far as to ambitiously -- and some would say outrageously -- check on Cardinals star Trey McBride, who is from Fort Morgan, Colorado, and played at Colorado State. The Cardinals made it very clear they have zero intention of trading McBride," Schefter posted on Saturday .
It never hurts to ask, though it could ruffle some feathers. The Broncos' interest in McBride comes from an obvious place.
Not only is a Colorado native and a life-long Broncos fan, but against Denver in Week 7 , McBride had his best game of the season, catching 10 passes on 13 targets for 111 yards and a touchdown. Broncos head coach Sean Payton spent a good long while after the game chopping it up with McBride in admiration of his game.
But the Cardinals aren't interested in trading McBride. So that's that.
Maybe not, though. Arizona could be playing hard to get, and everyone has an offer they'd accept. For the Cardinals, it would take a king's ransom to give up arguably the best tight end in football, but again, everything has a price.
Given McBride's age — he's only 26 — who knows what it would take for Arizona to give him up. Maybe a pair of first-round picks for the 2022 second-rounder out of Colorado State?
My question would come down to usage. Given Bo NIx's middle-of-the-field avoidance and his relative neglect of targeting tight ends, would the Broncos really want a Ferari like McBride sitting in the garage every week? A car such as that is meant to be driven.
That's not a knock on Nix, by the way. It's just a fact. The Broncos spent to sign Evan Engram in free agency last year, and while he finished third on the team in receiving, he failed to meet expectations, and turned in one of his worst statistical seasons as a pro.
It's gotten even worse for Engram this year. So, on one hand, of course I understand the Broncos' interest in McBride, but I don't think he's meant to be in Denver — not right now, at least.
I certainly applaud the Broncos' boldness to call and ask about McBride. Fortune favors the bold, after all, and you miss 100% of the shots you don't take.
The NFL trade deadline is on Tuesday, so the Broncos have one more game between now and then. I believe the focus remains on upgrading the running back position, but if nothing else, Schefter's report on McBride hints that the Broncos may be cultivating an aggressive mindset ahead of the deadline.

title: Why Broncos Could Target Eagles OG Landon Dickerson in Trade
full_text:
Jonathan Taylor is the biggest name the Denver Broncos realistically could target on the trade market ahead of Tuesday's NFL deadline.
But he might not be the only one.
ESPN recently named Philadelphia Eagles offensive guard Landon Dickerson as the player the Broncos should pursue , "rolling the dice" on a three-time former Pro Bowler who's already missed five games this season -- but also a veteran who'd arguably upgrade the starting lineup.
"One of the reasons quarterback Bo Nix had early career success was that he played behind one of the best offensive lines," national NFL analyst Seth Walder wrote on Nov. 4. "This season, that hasn't been the case with the Broncos ranking 20th in pass block win rate. Dickerson is not a guarantee after his performance fell off last season and a knee injury cost him a slew of games this season. But he doesn't have guaranteed money after 2026. The Broncos can be the team that rolls the dice on him returning to form."
The 37th overall pick of the 2021 draft, Dickerson has started 80 career games (predominatly at left guard) for the Eagles, winning a Super Bowl and along the way establishing himself among the sport's premier multi-faceted linemen. In college, the Alabama alum was named the nation's best center and a unanimous All-American, as well as taking home a slew of other blocking awards.
That ability carried over -- and blossomed -- in the pros. While he's suffered through an injury-ruined 2026 campaign, Dickerson graded out as the 27th- and 8th-best qualified guard in the league, respectively, across his last two seasons with the Eagles, according to Pro Football Focus' rankings.
For context, starting Broncos left guard Ben Powers, whose spot presumably would be given to Dickerson, finished 33rd and 38th over that same period, per PFF. Powers currently ranks 51st among  75 qualifiers.
That also, presumably, is why ESPN suggested Dickerson rather than Taylor or another offensive or defensive talent. Another positive is that Dickerson doesn't turn 29 years old until next September, and his position typically has a better long-term shelflife.
Although his best spot is guard, Dickerson is fully capable of holding his own at center, which would also provide some experienced depth behind incumbent starting pivot Luke Wattenberg.
While there's much to like about the prospect of adding Dickerson, any smoke that's billowed from Broncos Park has signaled an offensive acquisiton -- be it a running back, wide receiver, or tight end. There haven't been indications that they're looking to make a splash along the front-five, however.
The front office could sell it easier if Powers were injured or playing at an unprecendently poor level. Neither is the case as of this writing. He certainly isn't performing like an All-Pro -- there's an argument he's the weakest OL link -- but not alarming enough to lose his job. Yet.
With Denver sitting at 6-2 ( very likely 7-2 after facing the Carolina Panthers on Sunday), holding a first-place lead in the AFC West, and with a bye week next up, there's also an argument to avoid fixing what isn't ( that ) broken, uprooting the protection of franchise quarterback Bo Nix.
The only caveat: there's one more game to be played until the deadline, and the bye would be the perfect time to execute any unsuspecting changes. Everything is always possible.
Just don't hold your breath.

title: Broncos' Week 9 Injury Report: Final Decisions on Jones, Uwazurike
full_text:
The Denver Broncos released their final Week 9 injury report on Friday -- and in doing so, ruled out a trio of defensive players, including two starters.
Among those inactive against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday will be safety Brandon Jones, defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, and cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, all of whom suffered injuries during the team's Week 8 win over Kansas City.
Neither of the players got in so much as a limited practice this week -- three consecutive DNPs -- so the writing was on the wall for defensive coordinator Vance Joseph's esteemed unit.
Also on that side of the ball, the Broncos listed safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) and outside linebacker Dondrea Tillman (hip) as questionable to play at Carolina. Hufanga has missed the last three games due to his injury, while Tillman popped up on the injury report Friday despite a full practice.
Per The Denver Gazette's Chris Tomasson , "it's very uncertain" as to whether Tillman, who's classified as "week to week," will see the field at Bank of America Stadium. Perhaps he's given some time off ahead of next week's bye.
Elsewhere, wide receiver Pat Bryant is questionable for a Week 9 return following a four-game absence with his own ankle issue. Denver designated Bryant to return from injured reserve and he's expected to be activated to the 53-man roster.
Defensive end Zach Allen, receiver Courtland Sutton, and receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) were given no designation and are good to go versus Carolina .
The Panthers, meanwhile, ruled out four starters including cornerback Will Lee, linebacker Bobby Okereke, outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips, and left guard Damien Lewis.
The good news as it relates to Jones' absence is that it appears to be aligning with the return of Hufanga, and Denver demonstrated that on Friday by releasing fill-in starting S Taylor Rapp, presumably signaling that Hufanga will play in Week 9. Look for Devon Key and/or JL Skinner to also see an uptick in snaps.
Second-year corner will take Abrams-Draine's reps as the No. 4 CB behind Pat Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian. It's possible the Broncos promote one of their three defensive backs, Sean Fresch Jr., Brent Austin, or Ugo Amadi to help provide some depth.
With Uwazurike sidelined, the onus will fall more on DE Sai'vion Jones opposite Zach Allen, though it's also likely that third-round rookie Tyler Onyedim, a weekly healthy scratch, finally makes his NFL debut.
If Tillman can't go, Que Robinson could assume the lion's share of reps as the No. 3 OLB behind Nik Bonitto and Jonathon Cooper.

title: Mile High Roundtable Drops its Predictions & Picks for Broncos-Panthers
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are 6-2 at the midway point, riding a four-game winning streak.
After defeating the Kansas City Chiefs last week, the Broncos now lead in the AFC West . If the Broncos want to retain their position atop the divisional mountain, they must take care of business and beat the teams they're supposed to.
The 3-4 Carolina Panthers may seem like just another sub-.500 opponent, but they can be dangerous. The Broncos must guard against the "trap-game" nature of this matchup and handle the Panthers on the road.
It's an East Coast road game with an early start, which has traditionally been an obstacle for the Broncos, but not since Sean Payton became the head coach in 2023. The Broncos have turned that particular ship around.
The Panthers have some young playmakers on offense and a defense that's better than some people realize. But if the Broncos play up to their potential, it's hard to see the Panthers keeping up with them.
That's a big if , though, as the Broncos have been frustratingly inconsistent on both sides of the ball, despite their winning streak.
How will this shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI Mile High Huddle staff see this one unfolding on Sunday.
Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 6-2 : East Coast road swings are never easy. Thankfully, the Broncos are a team that knows how to win late. Against the Panthers, the Broncos get an early lead and use Jonah Coleman to the maximum in a lopsided win.
Pick : Broncos 31, Panthers 17
Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 6-2 : Thanks to all his years in New Orleans, Payton has a special place in his heart for NFC South opponents; he's undefeated against them as Broncos head coach. Bo Nix is 4-0, including a 28-14 drubbing against the Panthers in 2024. Outdueling Bryce Young won't be quite so easy this time around, though, as the Panthers' young quarterback has improved dramatically since then, but Nix's confidence has come flooding back over the past two weeks, and that leads to a romping day for the Broncos' offense on the road. Nix has his best statistical game of the year, with 280 passing yards and three touchdown passes.
Pick : Broncos 31, Panthers 16
Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 6-2 : Unlike some, I’m not buying into the "trap game" element for the Broncos, facing a lesser opponent, an early East Coast game, right before their bye. There should be enough trust and confidence at this point that Denver can dispatch the mediocre Panthers under these circumstances. It might not be a true blowout. It might not even be pretty. They could make us sweat, as they like to do. But they’ll ultimately get the job done.

Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 6-2 : The Broncos can’t keep getting away with this... or can they? For another week, I think so. Carolina is playing football, but boy, they aren't good on the lines of scrimmage. Can they win up front as thoroughly as Denver has this year? Another win. Although this game does have “trap game” all over it, Denver has enough veterans not to falter.

Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 6-2 : The Broncos showed two weeks ago against the Cardinals they can pull away in the second half against a team that has talent but isn't strong overall. The Panthers are similar to the Cardinals, in that they can challenge the better teams. But with the way the Broncos have executed, for the most part, in recent weeks, I believe they will have a similar performance as they did in Arizona, with a close, low-scoring first half, but they pull away in the second for a double-digit win.

Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 5-3 : There are certain instances where a team matches up well against an opponent and its weaknesses. This is one of those times for the Broncos. The Panthers struggle with protection, and the strength of their weapons lines up with the strength of Denver's defense in the cornerback room vs. their receivers. The Broncos and Panthers will both try to establish a run game in this one, shortening the contest. I expect a big effort from Coleman, as the Broncos escape another game too close for comfort.

Erick Trickel ( @ErickTrickel ) 4-4 : With the bye week coming up, there's a chance the Broncos could overlook the Panthers. Dylan Von Arx ( @DylanVonArxMHH ) 4-4 : The Broncos have a chance to cruise into their bye week as they face a Panthers team reeling from injuries.
