title: Broncos' Stance on Jonathan Taylor Trade Has Shifted, Insider Claims
full_text:
Time is running out on the Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes.
The Indianapolis Colts have upped the ante, reportedly asking for a first-round value in exchange for the three-time Pro Bowl running back ahead of this coming Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. If the Colts can't get a first-round value for Taylor, they're looking for a Christian McCaffrey-type haul, which would be something like a second-, third-, fourth-, and fifth-round draft pick, according to Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer.
The Broncos have called the Colts; GM George Paton and head coach Sean Payton have discussed Taylor, but per Breer, Indy's steep asking price for the soon-to-be 28-year-old running back has cooled Denver's heels.
"The Giants, Broncos and Vikings have inquired, and discussed it, and it appears Denver and Minnesota might be a little less inclined to trade for Taylor now," Breer wrote on Friday .
The Giants are serious suitors for Taylor, and if the Broncos and the Vikings are bowing out, Taylor's market could dry up quickly. The Colts claim they want to keep Taylor as the cornerstone of their coming rebuild, and if they were to trade him, it would be at a premium.
Time will tell on that front.
If the Broncos make a move ahead of the November 10 trade deadline, they're expected to be buyers, not sellers. Even Payton said as much at the podium this week.
At 6-2, the Broncos are poised to make a run as their schedule opens up, but they're in dire need of a reliable run game, as that will separate the men from the boys down the stretch and into the playoffs.
Jonah Coleman has offered the Broncos they're only glimpse of rushing hope thus far. He's only touched the ball in three games this season — spending four weeks on injured reserve with an ankle sprain — but he's averaging 4.5 yards per carry and has been instrumental in the Broncos' last two wins, as well as Week 2's home victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars.
J.K. Dobbins, however, has been a near-bust this season. He's appeared in all eight games with seven starts, but he's averaging a career-low 3.3 yards per carry, and has seen his RB1 role erode in the wake of Coleman's rise.
Coleman had 41 snaps to Dobbins's 13 last week, and out-earned him in touches by far. Dobbins doesn't appear to be happy with how things are shaking out in Denver, which makes it no surprise that Breer has heard his name floated in trade talks.
"J.K. Dobbins’s name was raised in some trade talks, as Broncos rookie RB Jonah Coleman broke out, but it’s less likely now that RJ Harvey is hurt," Breer wrote on Friday.
That's the rub: Harvey's injury. The second-year back suffered a knee injury during practice last week and was placed on IR. That puts him out of commission until Week 13, at the soonest — assuming his knee is healthy.
For this reason and more, the Broncos are looking to add to their running back stable ahead of the deadline, but because of Dobbins's veteran presence, they won't overpay. And unless Dobbins was included in a trade for, say, Taylor or another back, like Tennessee's Tony Pollard or Baltimore's Derrick Henry, he'll serve as the fail-safe behind Coleman.
Complicating matters is Tyler Badie's thumb injury. He's got two more games to go on IR himself, which is why the Broncos elevated Cody Schrader from the practice squad last week against the Kansas City Chiefs.
There's one more game to go before Tuesday's deadline. Barring a massive maneuver, the Broncos are likely going to see how Sunday's road game against the Carolina Panthers shakes out before deciding on a path forward.
If the Broncos are able to run the ball well with Coleman and Dobbins, perhaps the Broncos stand pat and bide their time for Harvey's return. If it's another inconsistent struggle session, even if Coleman flashes a few big plays, it might be enough to spur the Broncos to action before 4 p.m. EST on Tuesday.
I can't see the Broncos giving up a first-round pick for a running back so quickly nearing the 2,000-carry milestone, but if Sunday is another rough rushing outing, perhaps Paton and Payton come around to the idea of giving up a few early- and mid-round picks in a facsimile of the McCaffrey trade.

title: 3 Keys to a Broncos Victory Over Panthers: Avoiding the Trap
full_text:
The Denver Broncos hold first place in the AFC West and are now entering the less daunting part of their schedule — at least, on paper. The Broncos have faced five playoff contenders in their first eight games, and while it hasn't been perfect, they can feel good about being 6-2.
The Carolina Panthers might not be as formidable as some of the other teams the Broncos have faced thus far, but they can't be taken lightly. The Panthers already hold a win over the Detroit Lions and have shown they can do good things on offense.
The Broncos will also have to travel, and both of their losses have come on the road. The Broncos also have just one double-digit win this season and need to show they can get those victories against the opponents that might not rank among the top in the NFL.
The Broncos have to respect their opponent this week and treat this game no differently than they would a top team. The Broncos' fourth-quarter comebacks may be fun to watch, but that's not something you want to do when the matchup favors you on paper, especially on the East Coast with an early start.
Let's break down three things the Broncos must do to come away with another road win before they go into their bye week — and to show they must be taken seriously as a playoff threat.
It's easy to look at the Panthers' starting quarterback and assume he's no threat. In Young's first two seasons, he had just 26 touchdown passes, though he did better in his third season with 23 passing scores. But one could still point to his 17-34 record as a starter and assume too much.
However, Young has made steady progress as a passer and is on pace to surpass 30 passing touchdowns this season. He could stand to improve his completion percentage, which stands at 58.7%, but he has improved his yards per attempt to 7.1 and his adjusted yards per attempt to 7.3, per Pro Football Reference .
Young also has the ability to extend plays if he gets out of the pocket, and he can be a threat to run with the ball if he escapes pressure, as evidenced by the 752 yards rushing and nine touchdowns he's totaled thus far in his career.
The main thing is for the Broncos' defense to keep Young in the pocket, where he becomes more vulnerable. Though he isn't taking sacks at the pace he did as a rookie — he took a whopping 62 sacks — he still has a tendency to take too many. He's been sacked 23 times in seven games, already nearing the 27 he took last year in 16 games.
With the Panthers dealing with injuries on the offensive line, this could be a game in which the Broncos pass rush could have a big day. But to do that, the Broncos can't underestimate Young, who can do plenty of damage if you aren't disciplined on defense.
Along with giving Young his respect, the Broncos have to be aware of two key playmakers on the Panthers' offense. You may not hear their names called among the top offensive playmakers in the NFL, but they are players capable of a big game at any time.
Hubbard already has a pair of 100-yard rushing games to his credit, with 120 yards against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6 and 122 yards against the Lions in Week 4. He's averaged 4.6 yards per carry, scored five rushing touchdowns, and has caught 22 passes for 150 yards and two scores.
More importantly, Hubbard does a good job of taking care of the football. His career high is four fumbles in 2024, but he's never had more than two otherwise. This season, he has yet to lose the football.
Meanwhile, McMillan has proven to be a good find for the Panthers, who took him in the second round of the 2025 NFL Draft. He surpassed 1,000 yards receiving as a rookie, with 70 receptions on 122 targets and seven touchdowns.
This season, McMillan remains Young's favored target, with 42 receptions on 65 targets for 569 yards and two touchdowns. McMillan had a strong outing against the Lions, with 192 yards on 14 receptions, scoring both of his touchdowns this season.
While McMillan's scoring has been limited, he's still a threat, and it's not a given that Patrick Surtain II will match up with him on every play . One should expect McMillan to test everyone in the Broncos' secondary.
As with Young, the Broncos must respect these playmakers. If the Broncos can contain both Hubbard and McMillan, it will go a long way toward securing a win.
There's a lot of excitement surrounding Jonah Coleman and no small amount of skepticism surrounding J.K. Dobbins , but this could be the game that allows both — perhaps —  to stand out.
Through seven games, the Panthers have given up 4.8 yards per carry to opposing running backs and 12 rushing touchdowns. The Chicago Bears, Lions, and Eagles all had at least 100 rushing yards against the Panthers.
The Panthers aren't exactly a standout at defending the pass, though they have been better in that respect, giving up 5.8 yards per reception and holding their last two opponents —  Tampa Bay and Green Bay — to under 200 receiving yards.
So if the Broncos are going to get that running game going, this may be the week to do it. This could be especially true for Coleman, who has averaged 4.5 yards per carry and might be in position to have a big game.
As for Dobbins, he's had his moments, but not enough of them. But if there's a game that he has a chance to make an impact, this is it.
If Coleman and Dobbins play well, it will take some pressure off Bo Nix to carry the load. It should also help Nix build on the good things he's done the past couple of weeks and allow him to make the most of the opportunities he gets against the Panthers.
This may not be a "get-right" game for the Broncos' offense, but it could be the game that shows they can be productive at running the football — and that they can do better than the 3.8 yards per carry average they have in the first seven games.
The Panthers aren't as strong as the Kansas City Chiefs, Seattle Seahawks, and Los Angeles Rams — all teams the Broncos have found a way to beat — but Carolina isn't a team to take lightly. The Panthers have been able to do well against playoff contenders, as evidenced by their win over the Lions.
While the Panthers aren't loaded with playmakers, they do have capable players who shouldn't be overlooked. On defense, they aren't a top team but that doesn't mean the Broncos can get away with a bad performance.
The Broncos need to build on what they've done well in recent weeks and continue to improve in areas that may need attention. They're at the midway point of the season and need to show they should be taken seriously as a team poised to make a deep playoff run.
A blowout win isn't what's needed here, but the Broncos must look to build an early lead as they did against the Arizona Cardinals, then make sure they don't let the Panthers back into the game.
While the Broncos have shown they can work that fourth-quarter magic, they don't want this game to come to that. Better to show that they can build a comfortable lead going into the fourth quarter, then put it away, to show they can be a serious playoff threat.

title: Broncos' Week 9 Injury Report: Concerning Brandon Jones Update
full_text:
Denver Broncos starting safety Brandon Jones was among three players who missed practice for a second consecutive day and now appear highly questionable to play in Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers.
Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's victory over the Chiefs and has yet to resume practicing. Ditto for defensive lineman Eyioma Uwazurike, whose shoulder issue has held him out. Ditto for cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine, who's dealing with an ankle affliction.
Each player will need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up at Carolina.
In more fortunate news, Denver's other starting safety, Talanoa Hufanga, was upgraded from DNP (Did Not Practice) to a limited participant on Thursday, giving him a shot at returning after being sidelined for the last three games with his own ankle malady.
Wide receiver Courtland Sutton and defensive end Zach Allen were also upgraded to full following a veteran rest day on Wednesday. Both will be active in Week 9.
WRs Jaylen Waddle (chest) and Pat Bryant (ankle) were full participants, as well. Bryant will return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury.
On Carolina's side, five players did not practice: OLBs Jaelan Phillips and Trevis Gipson, CB Will Lee, OG Damien Lewis, and LB Bobby Okereke. Quarterback Bryce Young (ankle) was a full participant and will play against the Broncos.
“You’ve definitely seen his ascension, and he’s very comfortable with what they’re doing," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Young on Wednesday. "It’s an explosive team. I think they’re seventh or eighth in explosives. They do a great job mixing the play action, the ‘RPO’ (Run-Pass Option) game. They’ve drafted well. So all those numbers are different today than they were two years ago.”
Assuming Jones is ruled out, Taylor Rapp would likely fill in as a starting safety at Carolina. If Hufanga can't go, Devon Key or JL Skinner would slot in next to Rapp. Skinner, in particular, had a standout game in last week's comeback victory over the Chiefs .
Assuming Uwazurike is scratched, Sai'vion Jones would likely be penciled in as a starting DE opposite Allen, with third-round rookie DL Tyler Onyedim a possibility to make his NFL debut.
Assuming Abrams-Draine is out of commission, second-year CB Jahdae Barron could see an uptick in snaps behind CBs Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss, and Ja'Quan McMillian.

title: Lions Week 9 Updated Depth Chart Against Dolphins
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have an opportunity to win a fourth-straight game Sunday against the Miami Dolphins.
After back-to-back emotional wins over divisional opponents, the Lions must now avoid a let-down against a struggling but competitive Dolphins squad.
Here's an updated look at the Lions' depth chart heading into their matchup with the Dolphins.
Starter: Jared Goff. Backup: Joshua Dobbs.
Goff threw his first interception of the season last week, so the perfect streak is over. However, he remains playing at a high level and his efforts thus far this season have warranted inclusion in the MVP conversation.
Starter: Jahmyr Gibbs. Backup: Sione Vaki (Questionable, Ankle) Reserves: Jacob Saylors (Questionable, Neck), Jabari Small (Practice squad elevation).
The elevation of Small suggests that the Lions could be without Vaki or Saylors . Vaki's ankle injury popped up late in the week, and if he's out Small could get a decent opportunity spelling Gibbs to limit the star's workload.
Starters: Amon-Ra St. Brown (Questionable, Rib), Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa. Backups: Tay Martin, DeAndre Carter. Inactive: Kendrick Law (Injured reserve), Tom Kennedy (Injured reserve)..
St. Brown is one of the NFL's most durable receivers, and even with the rib injury he'll likely be impactful against the Dolphins. Williams has the ability to burn the defense and could get an even bigger workload with St. Brown dealing with an injury.
Starter: Sam LaPorta. Backup: Brock Wright. Reserves: Tyler Conklin, Jackson Meeks.
LaPorta has had a smaller role in the passing game over the last two weeks, so he could be due for a big game. With some uncertainty surrounding the run game behind Gibbs, he'll also be a big part of that aspect of the game with his ability to block.
Starters: Penei Sewell (left), Blake Miller (right). Backup: Larry Borom. Inactive: Gio Manu (Non-Football Injury).
The Lions continue to lean on this tackle tandem and have gotten good results up to this point. Sewell is coming off a rough game after being whistled for four penalties, which was very uncharacteristic for the multi-year All-Pro.
Starters: Christian Mahogany (left), Tate Ratledge (right). Backup: Miles Frazier Inactive: Ben Bartch (Injured reserve).
With the injury to Cade Mays, Miles Frazier will be tasked with providing depth at guard in the event of an injury. Mahogany and Ratledge are both playing at a high level, and have been able to succeed at paving run lanes in recent weeks.
Starter: Juice Scruggs. Backup: Ratledge Reserve: Seth McLaughlin. Inactive: Cade Mays (Out, Ankle).
Scruggs will make his sixth start of the season at center with Mays sidelined due to an ankle injury. Ratledge will likely slide over as an emergency option, while McLaughlin could be active after being a healthy scratch in recent weeks in case of injury.
Starters: Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams. Backups: Skyler Gill-Howard, Levi Onwuzurike. Reserve: Mekhi Wingo.
The Lions' defensive line rotation has produced a lot of success up to this point in the season. McNeill continues to be a multi-faceted contributor both against the run and in pass-rush, while Williams and Gill-Howard complement each other very well with their abilities in run defense and pass-rush, respectively.
Starters: Aidan Hutchinson, Tyler Lacy Backups: Derrick Moore, Anthony Lucas (Practice squad elevation). Reserves: Eric O'Neill, Ahmed Hassanein. Inactive: DJ Wonnum (Out, Concussion), Payton Turner (Injured reserve).
With Wonnum out, there was speculation that Hassanein may get an opportunity after being a healthy scratch in every game this season. However, that may not change as Lucas got the call to join the active roster for the first time this year.
Lacy will serve as the big end, while Moore will likely get more snaps as a pass-rusher throughout the game. It will be intriguing to see Lucas in what will be his NFL debut Sunday, as he had a strong preseason and made a solid case to make the roster.
Starters: Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez. Backups: Trevor Nowaske Amen Ogbongbemiga, Joe Bachie. Reserve: K.J. Britt. Inactive: Jack Campbell (Injured reserve), Jimmy Rolder (Injured reserve), Damone Clark (Injured reserve), Devin White (Injured reserve).
Campbell's absence will be a big one, and Rolder was coming on strong prior to his season-ending injury as well. The Lions have veteran depth at the position, and Rodriguez has made the most of his opportunities in the past.
Britt was signed of the New England Patriots' practice squad, and time will tell whether or not he's active after joining the roster mid-week.
Starters: Roger McCreary, Ennis Rakestraw Backups: Khalil Dorsey, Rock Ya-Sin. Reserve: Nick Whiteside. Inactive: D.J. Reed (Out, Hip).
Reed is out, which will allow the rotation of cornerbacks to truly play out on Sunday. With the top cornerback out, Rakestraw could get more snaps as well as Dorsey, Ya-Sin and even Whiteside who was signed to the active roster Saturday.
Whiteside had a very strong start to training camp, and now will get his first chance in the regular season to potentially contribute.
Starters: Brian Branch, Chuck Clark. Backups: Keith Abney (Nickel), Christian Izien. Inactive: Kerby Joseph (Physically Unable to Perform), Avonte Maddox (Injured reserve), Thomas Harper (Injured reserve).
It will be at least one more game before Joseph gets an opportunity. The former All-Pro continues to work his way back into the fold, but with a Germany trip looming perhaps he doesn't get activated until the following week which would be the deadline for his return from the PUP list.
Branch began the week in Concussion Protocol, but was able to clear all the steps and get back into the fold in time for the game. In a week with so many injury challenges, this is a positive development for Detroit.
Kicker: Jake Bates. Punter: Jack Fox. Long-snapper: Hogan Hatten. Kick returners: DeAndre Carter, Jabari Small Punt returner: Carter.
If one of Saylors or Vaki is able to go, they will handle kick return duties along with Carter. However, if not then Small could get the chance to return kicks and make an impression on the coaching staff in his first game of the season.

title: Expert Predictions For Detroit Lions Matchup With Miami Dolphins
full_text:
On Sunday afternoon, the Detroit Lions will attempt to notch their fourth consecutive win when they square off with the Miami Dolphins.
The Dolphins, which have won just one game this season (1-6), are coming off a 24-19 defeat at the hands of the New England Patriots. Meanwhile, Detroit prevailed against Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings a week ago, 19-15.
Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 9 matchup with Miami.
The Detroit Lions have had to navigate some uncharted territory emotionally after the injury to linebacker Jack Campbell. A leader of the defense, Campbell's absence will be tough to account for as he had a huge impact on the operation. While Derrick Barnes is a veteran with plenty of experience, he could need some time to adjust to the new role he's expected to be in.
However, I think Dan Campbell's mettle as a motivator will be tested. He was adamant about the importance of remaining focused amidst the adversity, and I think he'll have the team ready to go. They could start slow, but I expect that the offense will get it together quickly. Even with some injuries on the defensive end, the Lions are able to get enough stops to earn a victory in Sunday's game.
Yes, the Lions will be playing without multiple core defenders on Sunday in Miami (i.e. Jack Campbell, D.J. Reed and DJ Wonnum).
And sure, Detroit could be looking ahead to its highly-anticipated Week 10 clash with the New England Patriots in Germany.
However, I don't think any of that will matter in the Lions’ Week 9 contest with the 1-6 Dolphins.
Yes, Miami is likely better than that record indicates. Yet, Detroit, even with the various injuries, is still the superior team, and I believe will show that early and often on Sunday.
Deploying their “next man up” mantra, the Lions pull out a gritty win on the road against the Dolphins.
The Detroit Lions are hoping to avoid an emotional letdown for multiple reasons. The team is coming off a tough victory against a division rival in the Minnesota Vikings.
Unfortunately, linebacker and defensive captain Jack Campbell will be out of action for the foreseeable future after being carted off the field last week. Some may think the Dolphins are a trap game, but Dan Campbell's squad should rally and find the resolve needed to come away with the victory this week.
Campbell's injury may also galvanize the roster beyond Week 9, similar to how the 1991 team rallied after Mike Utley suffered a serious injury.
Detroit's offense should be able to move the football up and down the field against a young Dolphins team that is still learning how to close out games and win with a new head coach. Tight end Sam LaPorta could be targeted heavily this week, as the Dolphins' defense has given up plenty of yards to opposing tight ends on a weekly basis.
The Lions take on the Miami Dolphins, which were not projected to be that great this year. So far, the Dolphins have met that expectation, ranking among the worst in the league. However, that screams “trap game,” especially with the Munich game next week and the Lions’ minds obviously and rightfully elsewhere with the Jack Campbell injury.
The key to the game here is to force more turnovers with quick pressure and to stuff the run game, as the Lions are missing three expected contributors from their linebackers room alone. On paper, this should be an easy Lions victory.
Personally, I think the Lions take full control during the game and fly home from Miami with an easy victory after 175 total yards from Jahmyr Gibbs and 100 yards and a touchdown from Amon-Ra St. Brown.

title: Roundtable: Previewing Lions Week 9 Matchup Against Dolphins
full_text:
The Detroit Lions OnSI staff previews the Detroit Lions Week 9 matchup with the Miami Dolphins.
Christian Booher: I think with the emotions that have been felt throughout the week, there is a chance that the Lions come out sluggish against Miami. The Jack Campbell injury has been tough for many to process given how severe it was, and the Lions will be without a key player within their defense. His absence will have a big impact, and as a result the defense in particular could struggle.
Still, Dan Campbell has proven to be one of the league's best motivators. Because of that, I think the Lions will come out with plenty of fire against the Dolphins.
Vito Chirco: Even with all the injuries, I just don't see it. I think Miami is a bit better than its 1-6 record indicates, based on how close it's been in a variety of its losses this season. However, that doesn't mean the Jeff Hafley-led team is going to surprise Dan Campbell's squad on Sunday. I still believe Detroit plays more than well enough to emerge victorious in the Week 9 contest.
Emmett Matasovsky: I think there is very much a chance, but I am not saying it is a high one, mind you. The Lions have had an emotional week with Jack Campbell’s injury, and this Dolphins team is one that gets overlooked in the stretch.
Additionally, Malik Willis being a mobile quarterback always makes this a potential trap game for Detroit, given its struggles in the Campbell era with mobile quarterbacks.
Booher : I do think the team will rally around Campbell, and we've already started to see elements of that this year. Campbell was a captain of the defense and a massive leader in the locker room. He leaves big shoes to fill for the time being, but I think the Lions will embrace the challenge and they do have the depth to navigate this injury.
Chirco : Yes, I believe it could have that effect. It doesn't take away from the fact that the Lions still need to make a move or two to upgrade their defense. But yes, I believe that Dan Campbell and the players will use Jack Campbell's injury as an extra source of motivation the rest of the way this season.
Matasovsky : I absolutely think it can. Campbell is a leader for this locker room and one of the most productive members on defense. The linebacker’s presence will be sorely missed, but the unity in the team at this time can also lead to a more close-knit locker room and better performance.
That said, it is not going to be easy to replace the veteran backer, especially with the injuries to Devin White and Jimmy Rolder both factored in. There are not many players with experience in Kelvin Sheppard’s system left.
Booher : The Lions need to get a cornerback. D.J. Reed is out Sunday, so the team will get a long look at its depth throughout the game. If things don't go well, it will further amplify the need for general manager Brad Holmes and company. Of the options expected to be available, I think Riq Woolen is the best fit for the defense. He has high-level experience having won a Super Bowl last year, and can be extremely good in Detroit's scheme. Donte Jackson of the Los Angeles Chargers is another good veteran option, though he has had some injury issues this year.
Chirco : I'd like to see the Lions make a move for Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker. But because of the draft capital that would likely be involved to land Baker, I don't envision it being very likely. That's why I'm going to say Detroit GM Brad Holmes must go out and land Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Riq Woolen. Woolen would be a solid acquisition for Detroit's secondary and provide the organization with a capable No. 2 corner behind D.J. Reed. If I'm Holmes, I'm targeting Woolen leading into Tuesday's NFL trade deadline.
Matasovsky : A true impact corner, and for me, the ideal target is Riq Woolen from the Philadelphia Eagles. Another much more expensive option would be Sauce Gardner from the Indianapolis Colts, although I am not sure if I see the returns outweighing multiple first round picks.
A shutdown corner alongside a healthy Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch makes things scary for opposing offenses, and that is before a healthy DJ Wonnum, Alim McNeill, Skyler Gill-Howard, and Aidan Hutchinson are chasing quarterbacks down.
Booher : I think the defense will come up big in Sunday's game. With Campbell out, they'll be motivated to produce to show support for their injured teammate. Because of that, I think Aidan Hutchinson will lead the charge and get after Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis. I think Hutchinson sets the tone with an early sack and generates a turnover with a strip-sack later in the game to help fuel the team to a win.
Chirco : I'm going to go with Jameson Williams, who has scored each of his five touchdowns over the course of the last three weeks. With Amon-Ra St. Brown a bit banged up, I believe that Williams will put together another strong effort and record his fourth straight game with a TD reception.
Matasovsky : I think Jahmyr Gibbs will be the game MVP. Sonic is going to get his yards, and this is not a defense that could compete with any NFC North offense on a good day, let alone a mostly healthy Lions offense.
Gibbs is going to top 100 yards by the midway point of the third quarter and finish at 175 total yards on the day, if I predict.
Booher : There are a pair of teams that I think match up well with the Lions and could give them some fits. One is the San Francisco 49ers. When they're clicking, the 49ers are a tough team to beat due to their array of weapons such as running back Christian McCaffrey and tight end George Kittle. I also think the Bears could give the Lions some fits. Ben Johnson is one of the best offensive minds in football, and Caleb Williams has been playing at a very high level. That Thanksgiving matchup is looming, and could have massive divisional stakes.
Chirco : It's the Bears with Caleb Williams, Jeffery Simmons and the great collection of talent they've assembled. They are the one team that might be better than the Lions in the NFC North, which adds further intrigue to their Thanksgiving Day clash with Ben Johnson's team.
Matasovsky : It’s the NFL, so any given Sunday. Mostly kidding. On a real note, the San Francisco 49ers look dominant and just re-acquired DeForest Buckner, which makes them a massive threat. If Brandon Aiyuk pays his fines and is in condition to play, they gain another weapon on offense, too.
It is going to be hard to get through that San Francisco team, and they are my midway pick for the NFC representative in the Super Bowl thus far.

title: Spot the Ball: 10 Thoughts Ahead of Lions Matchup With Dolphins
full_text:
After two straight emotional wins over divisional opponents, the Detroit Lions ’ next challenge is to avoid a let-down.
They’re traveling to Miami to take on a sputtering Miami Dolphins team, which has shown flashes of competitiveness under first-year head coach Jeff Hafley. Though this game appears to be a mismatch on paper, the Lions are navigating adversity and need to avoid any sort of trap game ahead of a pivotal stretch in order to keep up in the competitive NFC North race.
Here are 10 thoughts surrounding the Lions’ Week 9 game against the Dolphins.
With the injuries to Jack Campbell and Jimmy Rolder, Derrick Barnes is stepping into a big leadership role for the Lions on Sunday. As the veteran of the group now, Barnes may be tasked with some extra responsibility on top of his typical duties as Detroit’s second linebacker.
Campbell’s absence will leave a big void in Detroit’s defense, and they will need others around to step up. It appears as though Barnes will take over as the green-dot linebacker in place of Campbell, at least for the time being.
Malcolm Rodriguez has a new opportunity to prove his abilities, while Trevor Nowaske has seen his usage increase as the season has gone on. Ultimately, Sunday’s game is a prove-it opportunity for Detroit’s current linebacker group ahead of the trade deadline.
Sunday marks the first time that Dan Campbell will return to Miami as the head coach of the Lions. Campbell served as the Dolphins’ interim head coach for 12 games during the 2015 season, ascending from his role as tight ends coach when Joe Philbin was fired.
In his stint as head coach, Campbell went 5-7. Now, he returns to take on a struggling Dolphins team that is under a first-year head coach in Jeff Hafley.
During his press conference Wednesday, Campbell stated that the Dolphins this year remind him of how the Lions played in his first year as a head coach. While that 2021 team didn't always get the desired result under Campbell, they showed plenty of fight and competed every Sunday.
A great example of that is Miami's most recent outing against the New England Patriots. The Dolphins built an early lead against the defending AFC Champions, but were unable to withstand a late rally from Drake Maye and company and ultimately came up just short.
In addition to Campbell and Rolder, the Lions will be without a trio of other key players in defensive end DJ Wonnum, center Cade Mays and cornerback D.J. Reed.
In addition to those three, wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and running backs Sione Vaki and Jacob Saylors are all questionable. As a result, the Lions could be counting on their depth in a number of areas Sunday.
The Lions will utilize undrafted defensive end Anthony Lucas as a practice squad elevation in place of Wonnum. Additionally, Juice Scruggs will likely make another start at center in place of Mays.
Jabari Small was elevated from the practice squad to provide depth for Sunday'sgame at running back. With Reed out, the Lions signed Nick Whiteside to the active roster after placing Jack Campbell on injured reserve.
The Lions have made a trio of moves to bolster their depth at linebacker heading into this week. Jimmy Rolder was placed on injured reserve already, and the team also waived safety Bishop Fitzgerald to clear space for a pair of signings at linebacker in K.J. Britt and Joe Bachie.
Fans likely remember that Bachie, a former Michigan State Spartan, was on the active roster to start the year before ending up on the practice squad. Britt, meanwhile, comes to Detroit by way of New England’s practice squad.
To fill Detroit’s open practice squad slot, veteran linebacker Owen Pappoe was signed to give the team additional depth.
On paper, the Dolphins aren’t exactly the team that could dominate the Lions’ defense. However, given all the emotions surrounding last week’s win and what’s to come, this has the possibility of being a trap game for Dan Campbell’s team.
Being without Campbell will hurt, as he’s their defensive play-caller as well as a leader on and off the field. Dan Campbell talked Tuesday about the importance of staying focused on the opponent amidst the uncertainty, as preparing poorly could have dire consequences for the Lions.
Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis has the ability to extend plays with his legs throughout the game, and Detroit’s defense will have to be disciplined in their pass-rush lanes so as not to let him get out. If they struggle early, things could be difficult for them late in the game.
According to Sumer Sports, the Dolphins currently have the worst defense in the league against play-action with a +0.59 EPA per play-action dropback. This is a warm sight for the Lions, who come in as one of the most frequent users of this type of play and boasting a cquarterback that thrives in this setting.
Goff and company could thrive on Sunday against the Dolphins' defense if they keep up their use of play-action. Sumer Sports states that one in five play-action passes goes for 20-plus against this Dolphins defense, so look for Goff and wideouts Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams to take full advantage.
Sunday will be Detroit’s final game before the trade deadline, and as such their final look at whether or not the team would benefit from any deals being made. The cornerback position is the most obvious area of need, but the group has been playing better as of late.
Additionally, the linebacker spot has become an area of need with the recent array of injuries. The Lions have stabilized the group for the short-term with recent signings, but could be looking to upgrade as well. The Dolphins have some intriguing potential trade candidates who could fit this bill, such as cornerback Julius Brents and linebacker Jordyn Brooks.
Sunday’s game will give the Lions a look at both players, as neither are on the injury report.
The Lions play inspired. With the Jack Campbell situation looming, Dan Campbell has the team motivated and ready to go and they exact their will on the Dolphins. The offense hums with touchdowns on its first three drives, while the defense is opportunistic and forces an early turnover.
Even with all the changes that may come, the Lions defense uses their internal motivation to avoid any sort of trap game leading up to a showdown with the reigning AFC champions. They win comfortably, as the defense pitches a near-shutout and the offense rolls.
The flip side of using emotion as motivation is that it can hamstring a team, which is what the worst-case scenario would be. Detroit comes out sluggish on the road, as the Dolphins set the tone from a physical standpoint and leave the Lions to catch up.
Detroit is able to score points, but Willis causes problems for the defense with his mobility. A short-handed Lions defense isn’t enough, and the Dolphins emerge victorious on a stunning last-second field goal.
Detroit needs to be emphatic in this game and leave no doubt. The Dolphins are battered and struggling, and while the Lions have had an emotional week of their own, head coach Dan Campbell has proven to be a good motivator in times of adversity.
Because of this, I’m expecting a big game from the Lions on both sides of the ball. While offensive coordinator Drew Petzing has earned his praise, it’s worth noting that Kelvin Sheppard’s defense has been much better of late.
While the offense is capable of putting up points, my bold prediction is that Detroit gets its first defensive touchdown of the season via an Aidan Hutchinson strip-sack that leads to a Derrick Barnes scoop-and-score.
Willis has been sacked 21 times in seven games, and against a sputtering Dolphins’ offensive line Hutchinson could wreak havoc. Barnes is also around the ball a lot, and would be in prime position to take the fumble to the end-zone.
Sports journalist who has covered the Detroit Lions the past three NFL seasons. Christian brings expert analysis, insights and an ability to fairly assess how the team is performing in a tough NFC…

title: Two Detroit Lions Must Pay The Price For Taunting Against Vikings
full_text:
Two Detroit Lion s offensive weapons are lighter in the wallet, following their Week 9 victory against the Minnesota Vikings
Wideouts Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams were both fined $11,941 for taunting calls against their division rival.
This season, the league has again emphasized that taunting calls will be strictly enforced, sending teams' multiple memos that express just how important sportsmanship is to the growth of the game.
The New Orleans Saints and Dallas Cowboys were each fined a total of $500,000, following a joint practice that was marred due to several brawls during training camp.
“The Competition Committee has made sportsmanship–including at joint practices–a point of emphasis over the past several years,” the NFL shared in a released statment. “All clubs were reminded by memo prior to training camp of their responsibility in preventing unsportsmanlike behavior at joint practices that has the potential to result in injury.”
According to Front Office Sports , "There were 28 taunting penalties called league-wide last season. That was up from 21 such penalties in the 2024 season; 18 in 2023; and 22 in 2022, though players were warned about the taunting rules before the 2025 season started. The recent high came with 61 taunting penalties called in the 2021 season."
With sportsmanship being a point of emphasis, it is interesting that Detroit's offensive leaders both continue to spin the football regularly, even after earning first-downs.
"I know Troy addressed this in the annual video that all of the clubs see during training camp from the standpoint of our taunting was up in 2024," said NFL Executive Vice President of Football Operations Troy Vincent back in 2025. "Unsportsmanlike gestures, whether they were either simulating either shooting a gun or brandishing of a gun or inappropriate gestures like a throat-slash or unfortunate sexual gestures that were made, those were up almost 133 percent. The officials have made it a point of emphasis to all of the clubs.”
Against Miami, the Lions revealed on social media the team will be donning all-blue uniforms at Hard Rock Stadium.
It was expected the team would be wearing a dark color, as the Dolphins previously announced they would be donning their all-white home uniform.

title: 3 Lions Players Under Most Pressure Against Dolphins
full_text:
The Detroit Lions head into their Week 9 matchup with the Miami Dolphins needing increased contributions from multiple players.
With a plethora of injuries creating opportunities across Detroit's defense, three players, in particular, will face heightened pressure to produce.
Without further ado, here are those three players who need to step up as Dan Campbell's squad looks to capture a third straight win.
The Lions will need Moore to step up in the absence of DJ Wonnum, who was ruled out for Sunday's contest with Miami with a concussion. Wonnum suffered the ailment a week ago after colliding with Detroit safety Brian Branch on a tackle attempt of Vikings wideout Justin Jefferson.
Moore went on to log a career-high 22 defensive snaps last week against Minnesota, recording two total tackles and earning a 61.1 Pro Football Focus overall grade for his efforts.
The 2026 second-round pick is still looking to make a name for himself, and will have a prime opportunity to do so in the Lions’ Week 9 tilt with the Dolphins.
Just like Wonnum, Rodriguez has a chance to earn additional playing time this week due to an injury at his position. Most notably, the Lions lost Jack Campbell to a gruesome neck injury which has caused him to spend this week in a local Detroit hospital. Plus, rookie Jimmy Rolder, the Lions’ fourth-round draft choice this past April, suffered a season-ending hamstring injury in the Week 8 contest with Minnesota.
Subsequently, Rodriguez will be relied upon in a much bigger fashion Sunday afternoon against the Dolphins. This far this season, the fifth-year linebacker has amassed 18 total tackles and two QB hits. Plus, he's earned an 82.7 PFF overall mark for his efforts across 120 total snaps.
He needs to be a constant presence in Miami's backfield in this Week 9 matchup .
In recent weeks, Ya-Sin has found himself in a cornerbacks rotation with the likes of Roger McCreary, Khalil Dorsey and Ennis Rakestraw Jr. It's resulted in improved play from the Lions’ defensive backs group and increased overall production from defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit .
You can almost certainly bet that Ya-Sin will receive an increased amount of playing time in Detroit's Week 9 affair with the Dolphins, though. With D.J. Reed going down with a hip injury last week against Minnesota, Ya-Sin will need to step up his play and be much better than he has been all season long.
Through six games in 2026, the veteran defensive back has yet to record a single pass defensed or interception. And for his efforts, he's earned a measly 46.7 PFF overall grade, ranking 91st out of 103 qualified cornerbacks.
Ya-Sin will have a terrific opportunity to get back on track against Miami's lackluster pass attack (30th in passing yards).

title: Detroit Lions Place Jack Campbell on IR, Sign CB, Elevate DE, RB
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have announced Week 9 roster decisions, ahead of their Week 9 road contest against the Miami Dolphins.
According to the team, linebacker Jack Campbell was placed on injured reserve after suffering a neck injury while cornerback Nick Whiteside was signed to the active roster in a corresponding meeting. Additionally, running back Jabari Small and defensive end Anthony Lucas were elevated from the practice squad.
Head coach Dan Campbell was asked earlier this week if second-year defensive end Ahmed Hassanein or Eric O'Neill would take over the role for veteran D.J. Wonnum this week, as he was ruled out due to a head injury.
He instead mentioned Lucas, who impressed in camp before landing on the team's practice squad.
“Well, I think another guy is Anthony Lucas. (He) is somebody we've been repping a little bit here for whoever that defensive line, that extra spot there for Wonnum," said Campbell. "So, I mentioned this before, (Lions Executive Vice President and General Manager) Brad (Holmes)’s done a good job with the depth that we've got. And so, we'll be able to weather the storm and those guys are going to get an opportunity and adversity hits with injuries.
"That's the tough part, but the encouraging part is now guys get new opportunities. There are new guys now. You get your chance and what are you going to do with it? And that's encouraging because that's going to help us grow.”
Typically, teams will narrow down the number of players utilized as the season progresses. With Detroit having to mix and match the roster, due to players getting injured and players returning, the coaching staff has increased the number of players being called upon.
Defensive back Khalil Dorsey and rookie Keith Abney have earned increased roles in the Lions' secondary due to their play to start the 2026 season.
"It's unique. I think it's unconventional and unique in totality the way we've structured this and played. But again, we talked about what is coaching? What is it really? It's developing. That's number one. It's developing players. It's developing and being able to tap in and touch everybody in the room," said defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard. "That's number one. Number two is being adaptable and being able to adjust and have answers when these guys are big eyed and looking at you. You have got to have an answer for them, whether that be schematically, personnel, technique based.
"Your job is to adapt, adjust and have an answer for these players to go out and play at a high level," Sheppard added. "But again, I definitely want to make sure I credit the assistants, because those are the guys that spend the bulk of the time with some of the guys on the practice squad , some of the rookies in these developmental setting and making sure those guys were prepared when they got their big moment.”

title: Burning Question: Are Lions Playing Trap Game Against Dolphins?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions, winners of three in a row, will take on the lowly Miami Dolphins Sunday afternoon.
The Dolphins have won just one game this season, and currently possess the third-worst record in the NFL (1-6). So, the Lions have nothing to worry about headed into the Week 9 matchup, right?
Not according to CBS Sports/Westwood One NFL analyst Ross Tucker. During his weekly segment on 97.1 The Ticket's “Costa and Jansen with Heather,” he expressed he views the contest as “a trap game” for Dan Campbell's squad .
“(It's a) terrible, terrible spot for the Lions. I do not feel comfortable at all,” Tucker said. “They're coming off a monster win. They're actually coming off two home division wins in a row. Now, they got to play a team, everybody thinks they stink. They're competitive and you wonder just how locked in the Lions are. It would be unnatural if they weren't thinking about their teammate Jack Campbell, and weren't concerned about him and his well-being.
“This is a very dangerous game for the Lions. As I said on the ‘Even Money’ betting podcast, I really like the Dolphins getting the points. I think the Lions will pull through at the end, but I would not be surprised at all if the Dolphins win. This is how the NFL works.”
Ross Tucker thinks this might be a trap game for the Lions pic.twitter.com/qCQBlNOPZQ
The Lions, which are seven-point favorites, will be playing with heavy hearts after losing linebacker Jack Campbell to a gruesome neck injury a week ago against the Minnesota Vikings.
Campbell, the team's defensive captain, laid motionless on the field for several minutes following the injury, and proceeded to be loaded onto a stretcher and taken to the locker room on a cart. He's been in a local Detroit hospital ever since, and there's still a solid degree of uncertainty regarding the seriousness and long-term impact of the injury for Campbell.
On top of that, Detroit could be looking ahead to its Week 10 matchup with the reigning AFC champion New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. That has been one of the most highly-anticipated games on the Lions’ 2026 schedule since the schedules were released in May.
Consequently, the Lions’ Week 9 tilt with the Dolphins has all the makings of a trap game.
Yet, I don't envision Dan Campbell allowing his team to take Miami lightly. To me, it's why he made the comments he did earlier this week about the Dolphins being a “hungry” team that tries “to play disciplined ball.”
I believe Miami is a bit better than its record shows, and the Lions are fully aware of that. It's all the more reason why I believe Detroit will bring its “A-game” on Sunday in Miami.

title: 5 Players Detroit Lions Must Scout in College Football Week 10
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions take on the Miami Dolphins at 1 p.m. EST in a matchup between two teams headed in opposite directions. For Lions fans in the Mitten State, it has the chance to be a special weekend following the yearly Battle for the Paul Bunyan Trophy between Michigan and Michigan State on Saturday.
While this rivalry does not have the same hype as in most years, with the Spartans possessing a paltry 2-6 record and Michigan sitting at 5-3, the game still matters for in-state supremacy and bragging rights.
This game, along with multiple other premier matchups this weekend, will draw in NFL scouts to check out the myriad of players that will become draft picks this upcoming NFL Draft.
Here are five players the Lions must keep an eye on.
Fraley, the son of Lions offensive line coach Hank Fraley, is a player that the Lions obviously have some of the best intel on. However, this is to introduce the younger Fraley to the fans, considering the season the Spartans are having.
Trent Fraley earned FCS All-American honors with North Dakota State, starting alongside Mason Miller, a stalwart of the practice squad in his two years with Motown. For his final season, Fraley headed to East Lansing, located roughly 90 minutes from the Allen Park Performance Center and Ford Field.
A draft selection of Fraley would be far from nepotism, as the center currently is ranked in the top five on Pro Football Focus for overall center grades. He has only allowed two pressures on the season and a single penalty through eight games for MSU. Michigan’s defensive line will be one of his best tests of the year.
With the center room holding the expiring contract of Juice Scruggs, the Lions could be looking for a backup center behind Cade Mays. The Spartans kick off at 7:30 p.m. EST in the Big House.
Although it has not been the dominant senior season that Hill was expected to have, the cornerback is still viewed in the early Day 3 range of the NFL Draft as things stand. Hill will be tasked with shutting down a Spartans receiver core that has struggled mightily this season and will be potentially trotting out a true freshman to start.
Hill has the ideal size at 6-foot-2 that teams want in a corner, and his year has not been shabby, either. His yardage allowed is only at 173 yards on the season, alongside one touchdown allowed (offset by an interception). However, his penalty count, at five, is by far the worst of his collegiate career.
Considering the lack of production from the Spartans receivers group entering the contest, an off day from Hill should be treated with alarm. The Lions need corner help as much as they can get, and they double-dipped on Michigan defenders during the last NFL Draft cycle .
The Notre Dame vs. Miami matchup is one of the most intriguing battles of the weekend, but the excitement was dampened following a practice injury that is holding Hurricanes star receiver Malachi Toney out.
Moore was a player identified as a super star and top-five draft pick early in the season, and had been chosen to be a headline player for this week’s matchup in the scouting guide. Moore will be tasked with shutting down the No. 4 passing offense in the country, led by potential first-round pick Darian Mensah.
The corner has gotten routine praise from analysts, his coaches, and opposing coaches alike, including Pat Fitzgerald calling the corner a player that “should be the top overall pick” before his Spartans battled Notre Dame in September.
Moore is a player that, barring significant injury or extreme underperformance in the final few games of the year or the pre-draft cycle , the Lions would need to move extreme capital for. That said, he is called the top corner in the draft for a reason.
The Fighting Irish host the Hurricanes at 7:30 p.m. EST.
The Utah Utes have been on fire to start the season, being one of the last remaining teams with a perfect record. That will be put to the test in their rivalry “Holy War” matchup with BYU.
A main reason for the Utes success this year has been from Wayshawn Parker, the third-year back in his second season with Utah. Parker ranks out as the second-best rusher in all of college football right now on PFF, and his 726 yards sit just outside the top 25 in the nation.
Parker is a compact back, at 5-foot-10, and shifty enough to make players miss, forcing 39 failed attempts this year. He is a threat out of the backfield as well, with 26 catches for 264 receiving yards, alongside making another 16 tackle attempts fail as a pass catcher.
Those scores combine to make him the top running back in all of college football, per PFF’s grading system. While Parker has likely talked him out of draftable range for what the Lions would need to give up, he is a star that teams will be dying to lay eyes on.
The “Holy War” commences at noon EST.
Jackson has had a long-traveled career, now at his fourth school in five seasons. The Group of Six representative for this list recorded nearly 1,000 yards as a true freshman with St. Francis (PA) before heading up a level to Appalachian State, where he recorded over 1,100 yards and seven touchdowns between two campaigns.
That caught the eye of Curt Cignetti, but Jackson was buried on the depth chart behind multiple NFL Draft picks, including Omar Cooper Jr. and potential first-rounder Charlie Becker. By the fifth game of the season, Jackson was no longer on the Hoosier football roster .
That led to a bump back down the group of six for Jackson, where he has soared with the Flames.
Amidst their 7-1 start, Jackson has added 626 yards on under 30 catches, with his 21.6 yards per catch ranking sixth in the country. He ranks in the top 20 among over 500 qualified receivers in this season on PFF. All this has came with the Flames not passing much, as the receiver has been on the field for 173 passing snaps this year, which is outside the top 500 for receivers.
Jackson has rebuilt his career with the Flames, but it will be an interesting pre-draft cycle regarding the pass catcher not finishing the 2025 season with Indiana. He has the talent, but the mental element will be the top question for Makai Jackson.
The Flames kick off against New Mexico State at 8 p.m. EST.
Sports writer since 2022. Emmett Matasovsky started covering the Detroit Lions in 2025. He has extensive experience covering Michigan State Spartans athletics, including MSU basketball and football. Has demonstrated passionate, in-depth coverage of college athletics.

title: Everything Lions Fans Need to Know From a Dolphins Insider
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have a showdown Sunday with the Miami Dolphins. After back-to-back emotional wins over NFC North opponents, the Lions must now avoid an emotional let-down and handle business against a Dolphins team that continues to improve.
Alain Poupart covers the Dolphins as the publisher of Dolphins OnSI . He recently spoke with Lions OnSI and answered five questions to preview the matchup.
Poupart : "This might be a tricky question because the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild and it’s a very, very young team that lacks talent and depth. What they have shown is they will play hard and not give up, which admittedly should be the bare minimum for any team. Stylistically, the Dolphins look like they want to be a running team and defensively they play mostly zone."
Poupart : "I think the physical attributes are pretty obvious, and have been obvious since the start of camp, but he’s still a very inexperienced QB despite having been in the league for five years. He’s also operating with a less-than-ideal supporting cast and a lot of youth, which leads to rookie mistakes like receivers running the wrong routes. His play has been a bit uneven in terms of decision-making, but he’s actually made improvement in that regard in recent games. I still think more data needs to be collected, but I would say right now there’s not a screaming need for the Dolphins to absolutely draft a quarterback near the top of the 2027 draft."
Poupart : "I’m going to guess Lions fans probably don’t know a lot of Dolphins players because Miami is a pretty nondescript team, so I’ll go with one of the good-looking rookies, third-round pick Caleb Douglas. He’s a wide receiver from Texas Tech who’s long and also runs very good routes. He looks like an absolute keeper for Miami."
Poupart : "The Dolphins are not like other teams with bad records because this season never was about wins and losses but rather player development and evaluation. Because of that, nobody should assume they’ll be in selling mode because hanging on to players who could help in 2027 and beyond will be more valuable than marginal draft picks. The Dolphins already have done their salary cap dumps, they don’t need to do any more. So they’ll trade only if the offer because too good to pass up; for example, a second-round pick for Brooks would be hard to turn down, but I don’t see anybody offering that. Brents is a really promising-looking corner who’s had injury issues, but again the Dolphins aren’t simply going to give him away. And, yes, both players would be good additions for the Lions."
Poupart : "The Dolphins are last in the NFL in pass defense and allow 76.9 completion percentage with little pass rush. I just don’t see how they stop the Lions offense. But with Kadyn Proctor coming back after missing Week 8, I think the Dolphins also can score some points. It probably won’t be enough to pull off an upset. The Lions should win, and I’m thinking something along the lines of 34-24 or 38-27."

title: Can NFL Trade Deadline Help Packers Fix Broken Running Game?
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers’ ground game is awful. You knew that by simply watching the games.
The Packers have changed offensive line combinations. They’ve changed carry distribution for their backup running backs. They’ve even changed their starting running back with Josh Jacobs returning to the lineup before Green Bay’s showdown against the Lions.
Nothing has worked. The Packers are ranked 32nd in the NFL with 60.6 rushing yards per game. The next-closest team is the Raiders, who average 17 yards more per game than Green Bay.
With the NFL trade deadline approaching on Tuesday, the Packers have been noted to be poking around at running backs and offensive linemen. Jordan Love has said that his team needs to fix the ground game in order to be the team it wants to be. The question is, can they do it? Who are some pieces they could acquire to try and do it?
The Packers need another running back. That’s true whether Josh Jacobs remains on the team or not. As of now, the working assumption is that Jacobs is going to be part of the team, as coach Matt LaFleur said in his opening statement earlier in the week.
That likely takes the Packers out of the running for more of the high-end solutions at running back, such as Indianapolis star and former Wisconsin Badgers phenom Jonathan Taylor.
Perhaps the Packers could view adding a high-end running back as a luxury they can afford due to the uncertain nature of Jacobs’ status with the team on a weekly basis. The reported asking price for Taylor is either a first-round pick or a re-creation of a first round pick in the aggregate.
The Packers do not have a first-round pick. That was sent away in the deal to acquire Micah Parsons a year ago. They do have second-, third-, and fourth-round picks this year. Those picks, along with a fifth-round pick in the following year’s draft, is what the San Francisco 49ers sent to Carolina to acquire Christian McCaffery in 2023.
That trade has been worth its weight in gold for the 49ers. McCaffery has been their best player on offense since arriving in San Francisco. Oddly enough, one of the picks that Carolina received from Carolina was combined to trade up to select edge player D.J. Johnson, who recently signed to Green Bay’s practice squad .
The Packers, however, are a team that typically holds on to their draft choices. Making that exact trade would mean that Brian Gutekunst would not hold one of his own draft choices until the fifth round.
Would he do that? That seems far-fetched to me, even if the Packers did not have Jacobs. Would he do it for a luxury player to combine with Jacobs? That feels even more unlikely.
Some more cost-effective options could include one we floated earlier in the week with Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard. Pollard has been good this season for a Tennessee team that is going nowhere fast and just traded one of its biggest stars in Jeffery Simmons to Chicago for two first-round picks. The Titans are looking to rebuild their roster.
Pollard could work alongside Jacobs without having to outright replace him as someone like Taylor would do.
One other possibility is Baltimore’s Derrick Henry. Henry is stuck on a Ravens team that is likely going nowhere with Lamar Jackson sidelined for the rest of the season. Henry was brought into Baltimore to be the final piece for a Super Bowl push. Could he be that in Green Bay now?
He has history with Matt LaFleur, as the two were together in Tennessee in LaFleur’s lone season. Henry is a cold-weather back, as evidenced by the beating he handed the Packers last December, and could give the Packers a punishing presence as the elements turn.
ESPN.com’s Adam Schefter reported the Ravens are not expected to move Henry, but one phone call can change everything.
With all the discussion surrounding one former Badger in Taylor, what if another became Green Bay’s target?
The New York Jets are another team spiraling to nowhere, and it looks like their coaching staff, at minimum, is set to meet their maker at the end of the season.
Could the Jets kickstart a rebuild by moving one of their talented running backs? Breece Hall could be intriguing, but the Jets just paid him in the offseason. Teams typically don’t move players who were just signed to contract extensions.
Braelon Allen is coming off one of the best games of his career. In fact, Allen has 251 rushing yards the last two games. The Packers’ top two rushers have combined for 253. Allen’s 147 yards that he ran for last week against the Raiders are just 2 fewer than Marshawn Lloyd’s team-leading 149 yards.
Allen is a young player who appears to be ascending. That’s the type of player that Gutekunst has typically targeted when he’s gone shopping outside of the draft. It’s probably far-fetched, but in the search for improvement in the backfield the Packers should be leaving no stone unturned.
This position group is where things get interesting.
The Packers could clearly use an upgrade on the offensive line. The running backs are not the sole reason the run game is so bad. The Packers came into the season with a flawed group up front that has since been patched together with bubble gum and rubber bands.
After starting the trio of terror that was Donovan Jennings, Jacob Monk and Jager Burton for the first three games of the season at guard, the Packers signed three veteran offensive linemen during their mini-bye after a 35-14 shellacking at the hands of the Falcons.
Mekhi Becton, Laken Tomlinson and Kevin Zeitler were signed before Green Bay took the practice field in Week 4.
Tomlinson started immediately, taking the left guard spot against Tampa Bay. He has started every game since signing in Green Bay off the Cowboys’ practice squad, including at right guard last week.
Becton and Zeitler have yet to play any offensive snaps. Becton was just promoted from the practice squad before the Packers played in Detroit. Zeitler’s situation is well documented, but the Packers insist he has not hit a wall and could play if he was asked to as soon as this weekend.
Left guard Aaron Banks returned to the lineup last week against the Panthers and struggled, but the Packers have made a massive investment in him.
That last line is where the problem lies for Green Bay in terms of upgrading its offensive line. It’s invested a lot in the position group. Things simply have not worked out.
If the Packers acquire another interior offensive lineman, that would mean Banks or Tomlinson would have to go to the bench.
The Packers put Banks right back into the starting lineup after he missed more than a month with knee and toe injuries, so clearly they like him at left guard. They moved Tomlinson from left guard to right guard last week against Carolina, even though Tomlinson had not played that position in 10 years.
An acquisition of someone like Philadelphia’s Landon Dickerson could make sense if the Packers wanted to move him to center, where he has played before.
The problem is that Sean Rhyan is their center who they paid in the offseason. They don’t expect him to land on injured reserve, which means he could be back in the lineup in a week or two.
They drafted offensive tackles Jordan Morgan and Anthony Belton with first- and second-round picks, respectively. They like both players, and it would seem unlikely they’re looking to replace either one.
Acquiring a new offensive lineman means putting someone like Banks or Rhyan on the bench to make them a very expensive backup. It could also mean removing Tomlinson, who has been perhaps their best player up front since he was signed.
The argument could be made that the Packers should just suck it up in terms of having an expensive player on the bench considering neither Banks nor Rhyan has been a dominant force. Banks remains on the injury report every week and his knee feels like a ticking time bomb.
It’s the argument I would make. Is that how the Packers feel? That remains to be seen.
What we do know is the run game is not good enough. There…

title: Saturday’s Packers Roster Moves: What They Mean for Sunday at Patriots
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have some tough decisions to make at running back. Those decisions were not made on Saturday.
The Packers made only one roster move before hopping on a plane for a flight to Foxborough for Sunday’s game against the New England Patriots. Here’s our weekly breakdown of the roster moves that were made and not made.
The elevation of tight end Drake Dabney was the only roster move made on Saturday. His addition to the gameday roster comes after Josh Whyle suffered a concussion last week and did not practice this week while in the protocol
Dabney, 24, initially signed to Green Bay’s practice squad last year after Tucker Kraft’s torn ACL. He wound up playing in two games at the end of the season, including starting and playing almost every snap in the Week 18 game at Minnesota. He caught one pass for 3 yards.
In this year’s preseason, with Tucker Kraft and Luke Musgrave out with injuries, he caught three passes for 15 yards. He fell short of a roster spot, though, as the Packers opted to sign Jonnu Smith and trade for Mark Redman at the end of camp.
He emerged as a solid blocker during camp.
“I think mindset for one – obviously, those guys are really good – but knowing that you can go attack as well and block those guys and then just refining your technique, hands, and feet,” Dabney said during camp. “Everyone's good in this game but it takes technique in this game to block the really good guys in this game.”
The Packers had only three tight ends active against Carolina, with Smith a healthy scratch. They were quickly down to two after Whyle’s concussion. Either the Packers will be back to four with Kraft, Redman, Smith and Dabney or Smith really is the odd man out in the rotation.
The Packers have four running backs on their roster with Josh Jacobs, MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong and Kaleb Johnson.
This week, Chris Brooks was designated for return from injured reserve after missing four games with the ankle injury sustained at Tampa Bay. He was limited participation at all three practices and questionable on the injury report.
Brooks’ return to game action will have to wait another week. That means the decision on who to release at running back can also wait a week. Strong has played key snaps and is a proven player on special teams. Johnson has been a healthy scratch the last two weeks, but he’s a former third-round pick that the Packers acquired at the end of camp for a 2028 sixth-round pick.
Speaking of the running backs, Lloyd popped up on the injury report for the first time this season on Thursday due to a knee issue but he practiced on Friday and is questionable.
The Packers elevated edge Arron Mosby from the practice squad each of the last three weeks. That was the maximum number allowable, so the Packers had to either sign him to the 53-man roster or not use him at all.
The Packers, who have a full roster, opted to hold Mosby out of this game. In three games, he’s played 43 snaps on special teams and has two tackles.
That means Green Bay will be without a key member of its special teams against the Patriots, who have one of the better special-teams units in the league.
This one is no surprise, but it’s worth pointing out the Packers did not elevate rookie cornerback Domani Jackson from the practice squad. Veteran starter Keisean Nixon did not practice on Thursday and was questionable on Friday’s injury report with a groin injury, though he was obviously feeling good at Friday’s practice .
Including playoffs, Nixon has played in all 80 games since joining the Packers. He hasn’t missed a game since the 2021 season with the Raiders.
Limiting it to just regular-season games and dating back to his final season with the Raiders, Nixon has played in 82 consecutive games. This will be his 40th consecutive start.
Coach Matt LaFleur called Nixon a “G.”
“It’s not really a streak that means something to me. I just don’t want to not play,” Nixon said. “Technically, I don’t look at it as, ‘Oh, I never missed a game.’ I just want to play every week, so I get my body prepared for it to play. Me just not missing a game is just because I want to play.”

title: Three Bold Predictions on Why Packers Will Beat Patriots
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have their eyes on the Super Bowl. So do the New England Patriots, who lost in last year’s Super Bowl.
On Sunday, these storied teams will collide in Foxborough. The Patriots are three-point favorites. With Tom Brady on the call and Rob Gronkowski being inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame, here are three reasons why the Packers will spoil the party and earn a statement win.
The Patriots reached the Super Bowl last year despite the lack of a legit threat at receiver. So, they attempted to rectify that problem by signing Romeo Doubs, who had a solid four seasons with the Packers, and trading for A.J. Brown, a three-time Pro Bowler who had surpassed 1,000 yards in six of his first seven seasons.
Neither player will be on the field for this game, though. Doubs is on injured reserve with a shoulder injury and Brown is out again with a knee injury.
Combined with the questionable status of top tight end Hunter Henry, who leads the team in receptions, the Packers’ strong defense will face a diluted New England attack.
Without Brown and Doubs and with Henry limited to eight snaps with an injured foot, the Patriots needed to rally past the lowly Dolphins last week. The Patriots were held to merely 313 yards.
The key for the Packers will be limiting the Rhamondre Stevenson-led running game and putting the pressure on New England’s passing game to make plays against a Packers defense that ranks fourth in opponent passer rating.
“I think first of all, he’s an elite quarterback in the pocket, out of the pocket,” cornerback Brandon Cisse said of Drake Maye. “He’s extremely dangerous. He can make any throw. Obviously, he’s super-smart.
“They got a great offensive coordinator, great receivers, great playmakers around him and, obviously, when the run game’s going they can do everything and they can throw it just as good as they can run it. So, we’re going to have our hands full for sure and got to make sure that we’re ready to play.”
Prediction: The Patriots are going to have a hard time stringing together sustained success on offense.
Patriots quarterback Drake Maye is one of the best in the business. He was one vote away from winning NFL MVP last year.
However, unless you’re one of the undisputed elite quarterbacks, a quarterback oftentimes is only as good as his supporting cast. So, while Maye is seventh in completion percentage, third in yards per attempt and fifth in touchdowns, only three quarterbacks have thrown more than Maye’s eight interceptions and his six fumbles are one off the unwelcome NFL lead.
“I think speaking from playing zone coverage, they’ve got great eyes,” Maye told reporters this week. “They got eyes on the quarterback, they make plays on the football. They can, obviously, catch well. The safeties are great players. They do a lot of things well and they read the quarterback very well, mix up in zone looks. Tip balls have turned into picks that they’ve shown.
“So, they’ve just had a habit of creating turnovers in the pocket with the quarterback. They have got some free rushers’ help, too, of the quarterback panicking and trying to fit some stuff to tight windows. They’re good at keeping you in some negative plays. They make you go longer distances. It’s hard.”
In the Patriots’ three losses, Maye has thrown three touchdowns vs. six interceptions. In the five wins, it’s 12 touchdowns and two interceptions. His eight interceptions equal last year’s total (in less than half the attempts) are only two off his total from his rookie season in 2024.
Prediction: It only takes one big mistake to swing a game between equal teams. Based on this season, Maye is more apt to make that mistake.
“The ball” is the most important thing in the sport, coach Matt LaFleur likes to say. Teams that take away and protect the ball tend to win; teams that don’t tend to lose.
The Packers are tied for fourth in the league at plus-4 in turnovers. After creating only 14 takeaways last season – when Micah Parsons was on the field for 14 games – they rank second in the league with 15 takeaways this season.
The Patriots this year are minus-7 overall; only the white-flag-of-surrender-waving Colts are worse at minus-11. Their 15 giveaways are the third-most in the league.
Added together, you get this chart.
Points Off Turnovers through Week 8 pic.twitter.com/UmVq9xw7uU
The Packers are third in the league by scoring 52 points off takeaways; the Patriots are tied for 23rd with 20 points off takeaways.
Green Bay’s aggressive, playmaking defense works hand-in-hand with quarterback Jordan Love’s aggressive, playmaking approach to the position.
“Nobody’s had more 20-yard pass plays,” Patriots coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Wednesday. “(Love is) a quarterback that’s wildly efficient. He has a few off-days, but they’re few and far between. They throw shots. They’ve, obviously, great speed on the edges. They have an excellent tight end, Tucker Kraft, and now getting [Josh] Jacobs back, it seems like they’re trying to work him back in there a little bit more and see what he can do for them in the red zone and things like that. I think they’ve protected better the last few games.
“I think that when one of your best players for them is their quarterback, or their best player, that’s an emphasis that they try to make because when you give him time, he’s able to find [Matthew] Golden, [Christian] Watson or Tucker Kraft. Defensively, very physical. They have the second-most negative plays and created the second-most negative plays in the league. Seventeen percent of their drives end in a turnover, so that leads the league, as well.”
Love is cooking. He and Kirk Cousins are the only quarterbacks with at least two touchdown passes in seven games this season.
“Our goal every week is to go 1-0, and this is a very good team,” Love said. “Like you mentioned, they were in the Super Bowl last year for a reason. They’re very good in, really, all three phases. They got an elite defense. I think they do a lot of things really well. They got two really good corners on the outside.
“Yeah, I got a lot of respect for them. It’s always a good test, but I think the goal for us to see how we can go out there and execute the plan, and the goal is to come away victorious. We know to put ourselves in the best position late in the season. We got to really just win every game, and that’s the mindset of going 1-0 every week. It’ll be a good test for us.”
Prediction: The Packers have at least two takeaways in five consecutive games. If they can do it again, they’ll win.
