title: Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson Releases Statement Regarding 'Unexpected' Medical Emergency
full_text:
TreVeyon Henderson released a statement addressing his extended absence from the New England Patriots, revealing that he recently experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency. Henderson had been away from team activities with what was initially reported as an illness. He was seen leaving the Patriots' facility on Wednesday, Oct. 28, ahead of the team's Week 8 matchup against the Miami Dolphins. He ultimately did not travel with the team. In his statement, Henderson revealed that the medical emergency involved unexplained neurological symptoms that required several days of hospitalization. Although extensive testing has produced reassuring results, the cause of his symptoms remains unknown. Here is Henderson's full statement, released Friday morning.
"I would like to provide an official statement regarding the medical condition I’ve been experiencing. "Recently, I experienced an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days. During that time, I underwent extensive medical testing and evaluation. While the results of my comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, the cause of this remains unknown and unexplainable. "I will continue working closely with specialists and physical therapists to focus on my recovery, as these symptoms have affected my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions. I am committed to doing everything necessary to return to full health. My health and long-term well-being remain my foremost priorities. "I want to thank my wife for being by my side throughout all of this, and most importantly, I want to thank Jesus for giving me a peace that surpasses all understanding. Despite all of this, my heart rejoices in The Lord and my heart is at peace knowing that He is always faithful and His promise of Romans 8:28 always remain true. “And we know that all things work together for good to those who love God, to those who are the called according to His purpose.” The purpose of trials in life is not to drive us away from God, but to only bring us closer. May God’s Will be done, not mine. "My wife and I are deeply grateful for family and loved ones, the New England Patriots organization, my agent, my medical team, teammates, and everyone who has offered prayers, encouragement, and support. "We respectfully ask for continued prayers and privacy as we focus on my health and recovery. Love, Trey"
🙏🏽 pic.twitter.com/l52XuixPOc
In light of this information, the Patriots will need to prepare for the possibility of being without Henderson for an extended period of time as he focuses on his recovery. New England's running back room currently consists of Rhamondre Stevenson, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison, who was notably signed to the active roster ahead of this news. Terrell Jennings remains on the practice squad.

title: After Ravens' TNF Loss, Should Patriots Trade for Future Hall of Fame RB?
full_text:
The New England Patriots currently have four running backs on their active roster , plus a fifth on the practice squad. But could they — or should they — end up making a deal for another?
Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry, one of the greatest to ever play the game and stuck on a team trending all the way downward, could potentially be on the trade block ahead of the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline .
Do the Patriots swing for the fences?
Last night, the Ravens looked really bad in a Thursday Night Football loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. After injuries decimated the quarterback postion, the Ravens are trying to make it work with rookie Joe Fagnano (and potentially a trade for former Patriots captain Jacoby Brissett). Sitting at 4-5, now is the time for the Ravens to start selling off some of their pieces for something of value.
The Patriots' running game, despite the logjam on the roster, hasn't been all that. Sure, Rhamondre Stevenson has looked great as the starter, but TreVeyon Henderson has been out of sorts for weeks as he works his way through two ankle injuries and now an illness certain to hold him out of Week 9. Corey Kiner, a trade acquisition in August, is a fine runner, but won't light the world on fire. Lan Larison and Terrell Jennings follow up behind.
Operating under the assumption that Henderson will be out for a bit, the Patriots could use another solid runner. Who better than Henry, who spent six seasons with now-Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel in Tennessee. After Vrabel was fired in 2023, Henry departed in free agency to Baltimore.
The Patriots are reportedly interested.
According to AtoZ Sports , both the Patriots and the New York Giants (Henry's former head coach with the Ravens, John Harbaugh, is now the Giants head coach) have reportedly been in conversations for the future Hall of Famer.
It doesn't feel like the Patriots would have to give up the world to acquire Henry. Whether it's a fourth or fifth round pick, that would be a move that a team looking to buy should absolutely pounce on. Henry signed a two-year extension prior to last season, so he's under contract until after 2027. He's only making $1.25 million this year as a base salary ( which the Patriots can afford after restructuring Hunter Henry's contract last week ).
Yes, Henry's 33. But he's shown how good he can be in an offense that's firing. Right now, with Drake Maye playing as well as he is, Henry could thrive.
Vrabel has said all the right things about potentially adding someone or reworking the roster via trade, and you could expect him to be thrilled about the idea of Henry's skill set in this offense.
"I've said this a bunch, and I'm sure that Eliot (Wolf), when he speaks, and Ryan (Cowden) and whoever else speaks on our behalf, we'll always try to look and see ways to make the roster better and make our team better," Vrabel said this week. "There's certainly a lot of things that we have to look at with the roster."
Now, the Patriots should only do this move if they feel like Henderson's illness/absence will bleed deep into the regular season. If it is, pounce. If not, it might not be worth giving up something for another running back and shove your second round pick from a year ago further down on the depth chart.
There are other burning needs that could be addressed further, like another offensive guard or some help along the defensive front, but passing up on a talent like Henry is going to be hard to do.

title: Looking Back at the 5 Best Rob Gronkowski Moments with Patriots
full_text:
Rob Gronkowski was a football unicorn, a man amongst boys, a one-man wrecking crew. Whatever analogy you prefer, they all tell the same story; Gronk was truly one of a kind. His otherworldly athletic ability and Adonis-like stature, paired with his carefree, childlike personality, made him a Hall of Fame talent who captured the hearts of fans across New England. With his Patriots Hall of Fame induction set for Saturday, Nov. 7, l et's take a look back at some of his greatest moments in a Patriots uniform .
Late in the fourth quarter of the Patriots' 42-20 dismantling of the Indianapolis Colts in 2014, Gronkowski delivered one of his most memorable moments in a New England uniform. However, it wasn't a touchdown. He didn't even have the ball. As Patriots running back Jonas Gray scored his fourth touchdown of the day (yes, four), Gronkowski was nearly 10 yards out of bounds, still executing his block on Colts safety Sergio Brown.
When Rob Gronkowski threw Sergio Brown “Out Of The Club.” pic.twitter.com/zp1BRCMGRs
The two former teammates (Brown played for New England from 2010-11) had some history before that moment. Brown was the player who broke Gronkowski's arm during an extra-point attempt in 2012. According to Gronkowski, he had also spent much of their 2014 matchup talking trash. "He was just yappin' at me the whole time," Gronkowski said at the time. "So I took him and threw him out of the club." Gronkowski's postgame comments perfectly captured his hard-nosed play style and instantly became a fan-favorite moment.
In their 2011 bout against Washington, Gronkowski delivered one of the most incredible individual efforts seen on the gridiron. After a diving below-the-knee catch, Gronkowski rolled back to his feet and carried two Washington defenders another five yards toward the sideline. At this point, nearly everyone in the stadium assumed the play was over, including the players on the field. Everyone except Gronkowski. He somehow shook off both defenders, stayed in bounds, broke another tackle, and gained a substantial chunk of yards in the process. "He almost had no room to work with on the sidelines," Bill Belichick said after the game. "He is a tough guy to cover, a tough guy to match up on. We don't tackle him every day in practice, but we have seen plenty of people try to do it." The incredible 49-yard reception set up an even bigger moment. On the very next play, Gronkowski hauled in an 11-yard touchdown, recording his 14th receiving score of the season and breaking the NFL record for most touchdown receptions by a tight end in a single season.
Following New England's 13-3 victory over the Los Angeles Rams in Super Bowl LIII, the Patriots traveled to Fenway Park to participate in the Boston Red Sox's home opener, where several players were set to throw out the ceremonial first pitch. Before the festivities got underway, a handful of Patriots players took some time to practice their throws. That's when Gronkowski had an idea. What if he stepped into the makeshift batter's box against Julian Edelman, using the Lombardi Trophy as his bat? And so it was. Edelman wound up, ready to deliver the pitch, while Gronkowski stood with the Lombardi Trophy in hand. "We're all under the impression, 'No way is he going to swing the Lombardi Trophy,'" safety Devin McCourty said. As Edelman released the pitch, Gronkowski lifted the trophy off his shoulder and positioned it in front of him in a bunt stance. The ball collided with the trophy, leaving a baseball-sized imprint in the team's crowning achievement. "Gronkowski's parting gift," McCourty said. The dented trophy is still on display in the Patriots Hall of Fame.
One of the things that made Gronkowski so feared by opposing defenses was how fluid an athlete he was for his size. Standing 6-foot-6-inches and weighing roughly 265 lbs., you usually aren't supposed to make the acrobatic plays Gronkowski did. Especially the one he made against the Buffalo Bills in Week 16 of  the 2017 season.
Inside the Buffalo 20-yard line, down 10-3 in the second quarter, Tom Brady fired a back-shoulder pass to Gronkowski, who was blanketed by a Bills defender. Despite this, Gronkowski adjusted to the throw, extending his right arm out to haul in the pass before turning his body to get both feet in. Touchdown. Plays like these made Gronkowski a nightmare to cover.
With less than a minute remaining in the first half of Super Bowl XLIX , a game that would ultimately be decided by the thinnest of margins, Gronkowski hauled in a 22-yard touchdown pass from Brady over Seahawks linebacker K.J. Wright . Arguably the most important of Gronkowski's five Super Bowl touchdowns, the score helped give New England a 14-7 lead heading into halftime. Gronkowski finished the night with six catches for 68 yards and a touchdown, earning another championship ring in the process.
At this point in his career, Gronkowski wasn't quite the same player. Injuries had taken their toll, limiting both his availability and effectiveness throughout the season. But when New England needed him most, he came through. With the game tied 3-3 and just under eight minutes remaining, Brady found Gronkowski down the seam for a 29-yard completion, with the tight end making a diving catch to bring New England to the 2-yard line. This catch led to the eventual winning score, as Sony Michel punched it in on the very next play for the game's only touchdown. Gronkowski finished the night with six catches for 87 yards. A fitting stat line for No. 87 in what would be his final game as a Patriot.

title: Saints vs. Browns Predictions: Will New Orleans Take Advantage of Cleveland's QB Change?
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints will take on the Cleveland Browns at noon Sunday.
The Saints are coming off a much-needed bye week after a 2-5 start to the year. Meanwhile, the Browns are off to an unexpected 5-3 start but will be without starter Deshaun Watson .
Here are our staff predictions.
This is a game I would have picked the Saints to lose, but things change.
Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson is questionable for Sunday’s game, so the organization will start Shedeur Sanders . Because of this revelation, it 100% benefits the Saints.
Watson has been one of the league's better quarterbacks all season. However, with him out for this game, the Browns’ offense is less of a threat, even with solid receiving options in wide receiver Denzel Boston and tight end Harold Fannin .
Then, add to the fact that left tackle Kelvin Banks is back after missing significant time due to an ankle injury and rookie wide receiver and first-round pick Jordyn Tyson will finally make his debut after suffering a hamstring injury during fall camp, the Saints’ odds of winning only increase.
This is a great opportunity for the Saints to get a win, especially with a three-game slate coming up.
However, if the Saints don’t get a win, there will be a lot more questions than answers in New Orleans, especially for head coach Kellen Moore and the man who hired him, general manager Mickey Loomis .
The Saints made some moves after the bye week, firing their run game coordinator and bringing in a familiar face at kicker. I asked earlier this week in my column if it was a step in the right direction or window dressing.
This week also carries with it the return of Kelvin Banks Jr. from injured reserve after limited practice opportunities Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.
Add to that first-round pick Jordyn Tyson makes his debut in a Saints regular-season uniform this weekend.
The surprise move for me was the timing of cutting 4th year running back Kendre Miller . Though I have been on the "get rid of Miller ASAP" train for a while, I did not expect it to happen the day before a game.
These moves force me to look back at the first half of the season and wonder if this Saints team has gotten better as the year has worn on. The answer is no.
The kicking game move to Charlie Smyth is a lateral move, maybe a little better. The return of Banks will be an improvement, but the Saints weren't doing all that well running the ball with him in the lineup before the injury. Replacing a run coordinator cuts down the amount of feedback you're getting as a coach about your rushing attack. That could be good and bad. The defense cannot stop the run, while the offense can't get it going.
This is not a good team. Some want to blame Mickey Loomis, some Kellen Moore, some want to put the onus on the athletes that have been brought into the fold (or kept).
I say all that to say this: Even with Shedeur Sanders starting at quarterback Sunday for the Browns, a definite step back from the usual starter Watson, this Saints team has quite a lot to prove before I can say with confidence that they can scratch out a win.
I would love for this to be the game where the Caesars Superdome regains its reputation as a hell-hole for visiting teams. I would love to see Audric Estimé be the back who makes the difference (the way Saints fans would love him to be) instead of a guy who has bounced around from practice squad to practice squad his entire career. I would like to have Chase Young continue to hunt down opposing quarterbacks, and while he's at it to stop the run, too.
And I'd love to see the Saints win Sunday. I just don't see it.

title: Saints vs. Browns: 3 Things to Know About Cleveland's Defense
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints will look to get their offense back on track Sunday when they face a Cleveland Browns defense that has experienced its share of ups and downs this season.
Despite losing superstar defensive end Myles Garrett , Cleveland has remained a formidable defensive opponent, especially at generating pressure and creating turnovers.
However, the Browns have also struggled to stop the run, giving the New Orleans offense an opportunity to exploit that weakness.
For quarterback Tyler Shough and the Saints, exploiting Cleveland's weaknesses while limiting costly mistakes could be the difference between another frustrating offensive performance and a much-needed bounce-back win.
With New Orleans preparing for its first game following the bye week, here are three things to know about the Browns' defense heading into Sunday's matchup.
Cleveland made significant offseason changes, but none were bigger than trading superstar defensive end Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams.
Garrett was coming off a historic 2025 season in which he established an NFL record with 23 sacks and recorded 33 tackles for loss.
His departure, combined with defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz's resignation, raised questions about whether Cleveland could maintain its defensive identity.
However, the Browns have remained competitive defensively under first-year coach Todd Monken .
Cleveland has recorded 21 sacks through eight games, ranking ninth in the NFL, while collecting six interceptions.
Several young defensive players have also contributed, including defensive end Jared Vers e, who arrived from Los Angeles as part of the Garrett trade.
The Browns are allowing 126.9 rushing yards per game and 4.7 yards per carry, ranking among the league's bottom 10 in both categories.
Those struggles were especially apparent against Pittsburgh, which rushed for 200 yards in Sunday's victory.
That's an encouraging matchup for New Orleans, which has struggled to establish a consistent rushing attack throughout the season.
The Saints managed just 18 rushing yards in their 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh before entering their bye week.
If New Orleans can exploit Cleveland's defensive weaknesses on the ground, it could take considerable pressure off quarterback Tyler Shough and create more opportunities through the passing game.
Although Cleveland has struggled against the run, its secondary remains one of the defense's more dependable units.
The Browns are allowing 214.6 passing yards per game and have surrendered 11 passing touchdowns through eight games.
However, they have also intercepted six passes and held opposing quarterbacks to a relatively modest 6.6 yards per pass attempt.
Much of Cleveland's success in coverage begins with veteran cornerback Denzel Ward .
Ward has continued to establish himself as one of the NFL's premier coverage defenders, earning a 91.6 coverage grade from Pro Football Focus, the highest among qualified cornerbacks entering Week 9.

full_text:
The New Orleans Saints received encouraging injury updates Wednesday as left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. and rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson returned to practice ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Cleveland Browns .
Meanwhile, Cleveland could be without starting quarterback Deshaun Watson , who entered the NFL's concussion protocol Wednesday after reporting symptoms following Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers .
Watson initially passed concussion evaluations and finished the game but reported symptoms Monday night, putting his availability against New Orleans in question.
If Watson cannot play, second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders is expected to make his first start of the season.
Sanders started seven games as a rookie in 2025, throwing for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. However, he has seen limited action this season, completing just three passes for 2 yards.
Watson has started all eight games for Cleveland this season, completing 65.5% of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions.
Despite his efficiency, the Browns have struggled offensively, ranking 29th in the NFL with just 17.4 points per game.
For New Orleans, Wednesday's biggest development was the return of Banks, who practiced for the first time since undergoing ankle surgery in September .
The second-year left tackle has progressed considerably faster than initially expected, returning more than a month ahead of schedule.
The Saints now have a two-week window to activate Banks from injured reserve, potentially providing a significant boost to an offensive line that has struggled in his absence.
Backup left tackle Asim Richards has experienced difficulties adjusting to coach Kellen Moore's offensive scheme while filling in for Banks.
Initially expected to return in mid-December, Banks could reclaim his starting role once medically cleared, giving the Saints additional protection up front.
New Orleans also welcomed back Tyson, the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft out of Arizona State.
The rookie wide receiver participated on a limited basis Wednesday after missing the entire season to this point with a hamstring injury suffered during training camp .
Although his availability for Sunday's matchup remains uncertain, Tyson's return represents another encouraging development for a Saints offense looking to improve its passing attack.
With Banks and Tyson progressing toward their respective returns and Cleveland potentially facing a quarterback change, Sunday's matchup could feature a considerably different outlook for both teams than initially anticipated.

title: Saints Make Coaching Staff Changes, but Mickey Loomis Shouldn't Escape Blame
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints have fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti following their Week 8 bye, according to Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football.
The decision comes as head coach Kellen Moore attempts to fix one of the NFL's least productive rushing attacks, with New Orleans sitting at 2-5 through seven games.
The Saints have parted ways with run game coordinator TJ Paganetti, according to sources. Paganetti came from Philadelphia, where he helped architect the run game and was part of developing one of the league’s best offensive lines
The Saints are averaging just 86 rushing yards per game and 3.5 yards per carry, with their struggles reaching a low point in a 16-10 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris on Oct. 25.
New Orleans had one of the most embarrassing rushing performances in franchise history, managing only 18 rushing yards on 17 attempts and averaging a dismal 1.1 yards per carry.
Paganetti joined Moore's staff in 2025 after spending 10 seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles , where he helped develop one of the NFL's most dominant rushing attacks.
During Philadelphia's Super Bowl-winning 2024 season, the Eagles rushed for a franchise-record 3,048 yards and averaged 179.3 yards per game, ranking second in the NFL.
However, that success never consistently translated to New Orleans.
While Paganetti deserves some responsibility, the Saints' problems extend beyond coaching.
While Moore is getting heat for the Saints’ offensive struggles, ultimately the biggest issue with the New Orleans Saints is the person who hired him: general manager Mickey Loomis .
Loomis is responsible for building the roster, including the backfield and the offensive line, the two weakest links on the Saints.
The running back room, featuring Alvin Kamara , Travis Etienne , Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson , hasn't delivered consistent production.
Etienne's placement on injured reserve has further complicated matters, especially when the Saints signed him on a four-year, $52 million deal.  Kamara, by contrast, hasn't shown the same explosiveness that made him one of the NFL's most dynamic playmakers.
The offensive line also remains a concern despite significant investments, including first-round selections Kelvin Banks Jr. , Taliese Fuaga and Cesar Ruiz along with the free agent signing of David Edwards for $76 million
New Orleans has struggled to consistently create running lanes, particularly along the interior, leaving its running backs with limited opportunities.
Paganetti arrived in 2025 after spending 10 seasons with Philadelphia, where he helped develop one of the NFL's most productive rushing attacks. However, the Eagles also had considerably better offensive line personnel.
Moore and Loomis must now share responsibility for determining whether the Saints' struggles stem from their offensive philosophy, player development or questionable roster construction.
Firing Paganetti sends a message that the current production is unacceptable, but changing coordinators won't automatically solve personnel deficiencies.

title: Saints Midseason Stock Report: 4 Bright Spots Amid a Disappointing Start
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints enter their bye week with a disappointing 2-5 record despite the hype around the Saints being contenders to possibly win the NFC South.
While the season has been anything but positive, the team still has bright spots on both offense and defense.
Here's a look at four players who have performed above and beyond as we reach the midseason point.
Tyler Shough hasn't been perfect, but the second-year quarterback continues to show encouraging signs of development under coach Kellen Moore .
Through seven games, Shough has completed 67% of his passes for 1,721 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions. He's also contributed 111 rushing yards and two touchdowns.
His pass yardage and touchdown totals are both in the top 10 as he is tied for seventh in passing touchdowns and ninth in passing yards, but for a majority of the season he was either No. 1 or No. 2 in passing yards.
Those numbers are impressive considering New Orleans' struggles establishing a consistent rushing attack and protecting its quarterback.
Despite occasional mistakes, Shough has demonstrated improved accuracy, pocket presence and command of Moore's offense.
If he continues developing and limits turnovers, the Saints should feel increasingly confident about their quarterback situation.
Wide receiver Chris Olave has shown why the Saints gave him a 4-year, $132 million extension.
Through seven games, the former first-round pick has caught 49 passes (fourth in the NFL) for 636 yards (third in the NFL) and two touchdowns, averaging 90.9 receiving yards per game.
He opened the season with four 100-yard performances in his first four games, including a dominant 182-yard outing against Detroit .
Chase Young has arguably been New Orleans' most impressive player on defense through seven games.
The former No. 2 overall pick has recorded seven sacks, establishing himself as one of the NFL's most productive pass rushers.
Out of 50 edge rushers with at least 125 pass rushes, Young ranked second with a 90.0 Pro Football Focus pass-rush grade.
Young is on pace to record over 15 sacks, potentially putting him in the conversation for Pro Bowl recognition.
Though Young draws much of the spotlight, Carl Granderson is quietly putting together a standout year as well.
Across seven contests, the experienced defensive end has registered 25 tackles alongside 5.5 sacks, highlighted by a 1.5-sack effort versus Pittsburgh .
Granderson's current trajectory puts him on track for roughly 13 sacks, setting up a potential career mark.
Combined, Granderson and Young have racked up 12.5 sacks, forming one of the few reliable highlights for New Orleans' defense.
Even with the unit's broader difficulties, his growth paired with Young gives the Saints a high-caliber pass-rush duo for the future.

title: How to Watch Giants at Eagles: Time, TV, Radio and Referee for Week 9
full_text:
When it comes to the New York Giants ’ heated rivalry with the Philadelphia Eagles, the Giants have often been on the receiving end of punches from their foes down I-95.
For some Big Blue fans, it almost requires a trip into the time machine to recall the last time the Giants had a legitimate shot to walk into “The Linc” and upset their NFC East counterparts, who’ve run into nothing but success for most of the last decade.
Heading into Week 9 of the 2026 season, the window is as open as it’ll ever be for head coach John Harbaugh and the Giants. They return from their bye week at 4-2-1 and seek a solid outing against a divisional opponent to extend their quest for a first postseason berth since 2022.
Meanwhile, it hasn’t been as much of a storybook year for the Eagles, who sit in last place in the NFC East at 2-6 thanks to a six-game losing streak and a bevy of injuries that have sidelined starting quarterback Jalen Hurts and limited a few other key players on both sides of the ball.
The Eagles’ struggles have also been exacerbated by recent changes along their once-impenetrable offensive line, including the trade of center Cam Jurgens to Baltimore and the sudden retirement of All-Pro right tackle Lane Johnson, and by the porous coverage of a secondary whose success hinges on the pass rush getting home.
All those factors have put a wrench in Philadelphia’s ability to remain the division's alpha team and left the fate of its season hanging by a thread.
The Giants are coming in with one of the league’s better offenses since J.J. McCarthy took over as the starting quarterback, hitting the scoreboard at the 13th-highest rate and reviving an explosive RPO-style attack that had been their biggest weapon before Jaxson Dart got hurt.
While they won’t let themselves forget their bad history in a highly unfriendly environment, the Giants are hungry to unleash that offense on their hated rivals, snap their 13-game losing streak in Philadelphia and get one inch closer to doing the unfathomable in Harbaugh’s first year in command.
Teams coming off a bye week often get off to sluggish starts, which could be a problem when they face their past demons in the Eagles’ nest.
Harbaugh has shown all season why coaching matters in football, getting his men prepared to play no matter the circumstance and bringing grittiness to every down that matters. That mindset will be needed if the Giants want to become the big dogs in a matchup where they’ve long been the little brother.
It’s hard to imagine anyone in the Eagles organization taking this version of the Giants lightly. Still, to be taken seriously as a postseason contender, Harbaugh and company have to handle their business and hit the reset button in Philadelphia with a dominant win at the perfect time.
Check out New York Giants on SI for pregame, in-game, and postgame coverage.
The Giants and Eagles will square off for the 188th time dating back to the 1933 season, including five postseason meetings, with the most recent being the 2022 NFC Divisional Round at Lincoln Financial Field, where the Eagles routed the Giants 38-7.
Entering Sunday, Philadelphia holds a 96-89-2 advantage in the all-time series, but the Birds have largely dominated New York, winning 13 straight games on their home turf and 16 of the past 21 meetings.
The Giants’ last win in the City of Brotherly Love came on Oct. 27, 2013, when they escaped with a 15-7 victory behind two-time Super Bowl champion quarterback Eli Manning.
Last season, Jaxson Dart powered the Giants to a 34-17 rout of the Eagles in Week 6 under the primetime lights at MetLife Stadium before Philadelphia avenged the loss two weeks later with a 38-20 home win to split the 2025 series.
This weekend’s game will be broadcast on FOX. Joe Davis will be the play-by-play announcer, joined by former NFL tight end Greg Olsen as the analyst and Pam Oliver as the sideline reporter.
Giants fans can listen to the game on WFAN 101.9 FM. Bob Papa will handle play-by-play, joined by Giants legends Carl Banks as the analyst and Howard Cross as the sideline reporter.
Bill Vinovich will officiate Sunday’s game. The 65-year-old joined the NFL in 2001, starting as a side judge until 2006. He returned to the league in 2012 as a referee and has since served as the lead official in three Super Bowls (XLIX, LIV, and LVIII).

title: What to Know About Bill Vinovich’s Officiating Crew for Giants vs. Eagles
full_text:
Bill Vinovich, the NFL’s second-longest tenured referee behind Carl Cheffers, has been assigned to officiate the New York Giants ’ Week 9 game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Vinovich has been an NFL official for 21 years and a referee for 18, second in tenure behind Cheffers, who has 27 years of NFL officiating experience, 19 of them as a referee.
Vinovich brings with him a mostly experienced crew , with members having at least 10 years of experience. Those members include line judge Brian Bolinger (10 years), field judge Aaron Santi (12 years), side judge Jimmy Buchanan (18 years) and back judge Rodd Prukop (18 years).
Bolinger, like down judge Frank LeBlanc, joins Vinovich’s crew for the first time after serving on Ronald Torbet’s crew last year.
Vinovich also has a new umpire this year: Scott Campbell, who was on Clete Blakeman’s crew last season.
The rest of his crew includes replay official Chad Wakefield and replay assistant Patrick Kepp.
Kepp is in his first season as an NFL official after serving in a CIP consisting of three FCS-level conferences: the Coastal Athletic Conference, the Ivy League and the Patriot League.
Through six games this season, Vinovich’s crew has thrown the fewest penalty flags (89), with six of those dismissed. However, his crew has thrown more flags against the road team (45) than the home team (38), averaging 13.83 flags per game.
Last season, Vinovich’s crew worked two Giants games: Week 2 against Dallas and Week 15 against Washington. In Week 2, the crew threw a whopping 26 flags, 12 against Dallas (the home team) and 14 against the visiting Giants.
In Week 15, the crew threw 17 flags: six against the Giants, the home team, and 11 against the Commanders.

title: Giants Sign WR Jalin Hyatt to 53-Man Roster Ahead of Eagles Game
full_text:
The New York Giants have signed wide receiver Jalin Hyatt to their 53-man roster as part of a series of moves to finalize their game-day roster ahead of Sunday’s Week 9 matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles.
Hyatt, the team’s 2023 third-round draft pick, received his first game action in Week 7 as a standard practice squad elevation. After missing the roster out of training camp, he signed to the practice squad, where he remained until this latest move. He did not receive any pass targets, playing just four snaps on offense and six on special teams.
On special teams, Hyatt is expected to contribute in Sunday’s NFC East clash with the Eagles, particularly on the kickoff return team, where he is likely to line up next to Devin Singletary with receiver Charlie Jones (hand) ailing.
The Giants also elevated two players from their practice squad: running back Phil Mafah and outside linebacker Dewuane Smoot. Both were elevated for the first time this year.
Mafah will give the Giants an extra body at running back if Cam Skattebo, listed as doubtful with a hamstring strain, can’t play on Sunday.
The 6-foot-1 Mafah was originally a seventh-round pick by the Dallas Cowboys in 2025. He has appeared in just one game, rushing five times for 18 yards and a touchdown, and he has two receptions (on two targets) for 11 yards.
The Giants also signed quarterback Jake Haener, whom they had waived from their 53-man roster on Friday, to their practice squad.

title: Giants Can Lift 13-Year Curse in Philadelphia With J.J. McCarthy Leading the Way
full_text:
In the classic NFC East rivalry between the New York Giants and Philadelphia Eagles, the twice-a-year series has been painted green.
Philadelphia, the host for the first of two regular-season meetings with Big Blue in Week 9, has rarely let the Giants find success when they visit Lincoln Financial Field.
In fact, the Giants’ last victory on their divisional opponent’s turf came back in 2013, when two-time Super Bowl champion Eli Manning was still handling the offensive reins. The franchise hasn’t swept the Birds since 2007, the season it went on to win Super Bowl XLII.
From front office and coaching leadership to the talent on the field, the Eagles have long held the edge over the Giants. Still, for the first time in well over a decade, the tide could be turning as New York holds the division lead at 4-2-1 and sits 3.5 games ahead of Philadelphia’s banged-up roster in the loss column.
The Eagles are in a rare, compromised position. They are finding that the Giants’ early success stems from major improvements on offense under John Harbaugh and offensive coordinator Matt Nagy, a unit that will challenge Philadelphia’s fading defense on Sunday.
“Good,” Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio told local media on Wednesday about what he’s seen from the Giants’ revamped offense on tape.
“They’ve got a really good offense and a lot of skill at the receiver position. They did a nice job of raiding the Ravens not only for John [Harbaugh], but [Isaiah] Likely, [Patrick] Ricard, and they’ve got a lot of the Ravens-type offense that they had when [senior offensive assistant] Greg Roman was there.
“And they’ve intermixed some of the Kansas City-type passing in there with Matt [Nagy], so they’ve got it going now; good wideouts, good tight ends, two good backs, and the quarterback has come in a short period of time and done a really nice job.”
The Eagles have grown accustomed to facing some mediocre offenses in their recent history with the Giants, who’ve finished in the bottom half of the league in scoring seven times in the past decade.
Meanwhile, that same side of the ball has been Philadelphia’s calling card, with six seasons of owning a top-15 offense and three consecutive years in the top seven from 2022-2024, when they made two Super Bowl appearances and captured their second franchise title in 2024.
One strange storyline heading into their latest meeting is the complete reversal: the Birds’ offense has crumbled under the weight of injuries, including to starting quarterback Jalen Hurts, and has fallen to No. 32 in total production , marking their worst output since the turn of this century.
An unexpected change at quarterback hasn’t dealt the same fate to the Giants, who’ve gone from Jaxson Dart to their third starter, J.J. McCarthy, in the span of four weeks.
McCarthy has defied expectations in his early reps under center, completing 63.3% of his passes for 495 yards, one touchdown, and an interception, helping lift New York to the division lead.
Taking on a rejected former first-round pick was once labeled a desperation move by Harbaugh and the Giants.
Now, with the offense operating at its highest level in five seasons and a real chance to march into their toughest road environment and widen the lead on the pack with an upset over the Eagles, the vibe has shifted to the Giants having committed highway robbery.
“For them to get him for a fifth-round pick is a steal,” Fangio added on McCarthy’s early impact.
McCarthy has reopened the RPO-style system that Nagy prepared with Dart at the start of the season, and he has been the catalyst in bringing the threat of big plays back into an offense that could present a major mismatch for the Eagles defense on Sunday.
In his first 54 dropbacks this season, McCarthy holds a team-high 9.1% big-time throw rate , second-best in the NFL, with only one attempt that could have been a turnover.
That efficiency in airing out the football, built on trust in his two biggest weapons, Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely, has given the Giants an average of 5.6 explosive plays per game, ranking 17th in the league entering Week 9.
Philadelphia’s defense, which has sent five or more pass rushers on 27.5% of the 298 dropbacks it has faced, has seen the aggressive approach largely backfire. The effort to help their dismal secondary contain key targets has led to 6.5 explosive plays per contest (24th), with a large share of those plays coming on the ground.
It’s a perfect storm that could guide McCarthy and the Giants, especially on the ground, where they’ve made 39 rushes of 10 or more yards yet only three carries of 20 or more yards, two of which came in Week 7 as Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary combined for 72 yards on consecutive attempts to punch in the game-winning touchdown in overtime against the Houston Texans.
The Giants will certainly need those big punches to stack points onto an Eagles squad that finds ways to stiffen up its defense inside the 20-yard line, and to lift the 13-year curse that has followed them on every trip to the City of Brotherly Love.
All the confidence is on Big Blue’s side as the Eagles continue sliding down the NFC East standings on a six-game losing streak, and McCarthy has been oozing it since taking over two weeks ago.
Another solid outing could cement the Giants’ hold on the division and only increase the good vibes that have the Eagles taking their rivals seriously in this meeting.

title: Giants Midseason Stock Report: Risers and Fallers Through Seven Games
full_text:
The New York Giants have had their foot on the gas during John Harbaugh’s first year as their head coach. They have hit a few cones and veered into a ditch or two along the way, but a clear path to the franchise’s first NFC East title since 2011 has emerged.
Big Blue attacked free agency, made four picks in the first two days of the NFL Draft, and focused on developing struggling talents who seemed to have overstayed their welcome. This comprehensive approach has produced positive results overall.
Several players are on the rise through seven games of the 2026 campaign, but there are also some who have fallen, even drastically so in certain cases. Let’s break it all down in the Giants’ first-half stock report.
The No. 6 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft thrived in his rookie campaign, largely despite an unpredictable quarterback situation. Now, after recovering from a 2025 season-ending knee injury, Malik Nabers is essentially doing the same thing.
The 23-year-old wide receiver has caught passes from Jaxson Dart, Jameis Winston, and J.J. McCarthy in two months. Despite the changes at the position, he continues to bloom.
After taking some time to readjust to NFL action, Nabers has accumulated 509 receiving yards across his last four games. Fans were hoping he would regain his pre-injury form by Thanksgiving. He surpassed it by Halloween.
Because he hasn’t yet become a sack machine, people may hesitate to crown Abdul Carter a star NFL edge rusher, but he has arguably earned the title.
The 6-foot-3, 252-pound outside linebacker continues to make quarterbacks squirm, recording two sacks and 25 total pressures, per Pro Football Focus, but he is also much more well-rounded this year.
Carter is holding his own against the run, has just one missed tackle, and is drawing holding penalties thanks to his elusiveness.
Offensive linemen must prepare extensively for No. 3 moving forward.
The former Baltimore Ravens tight end has posted a few quiet outings this season, but he is fitting in excellently overall. Isaiah Likely has been one of the most impactful free-agent signings so far.
Leading New York with five receiving touchdowns and ranking second with 395 receiving yards and 41 receptions, the 26-year-old is puncturing holes in defenses all over the field.
He is quite dangerous on deep routes (20 or more yards), registering three catches for 73 yards and two TDs, which adds a vital new layer to the offense.
John Harbaugh gave Deonte Banks another chance, one many fans felt he didn’t deserve after a rough couple of years under former defensive coordinator Shane Bowen.
The 2023 first-rounder has seized this opportunity , and with guidance from new DC Dennard Wilson, he has become a highly reliable coverage cornerback.
Banks is making game-saving plays and displaying impressive hustle. If you had to encapsulate the Harbaugh effect in one player, you would probably point to No. 2.
Last offseason, the consensus opinion on veteran offensive lineman Jermaine Eluemunor was that the Giants had to pay him, even though it seemed unlikely that he would replicate his 2025 output at almost 32 years of age.
The Giants wisely committed more than $25 million guaranteed to their starting right tackle, as he has somehow managed to level up.
Father Time is nowhere to be found. Despite frequently being left on an island, Eluemunor has surrendered just one sack and seven total pressures in 368 offensive snaps.
Jevon Holland has cooled off a bit, but the sixth-year safety is still instrumental to the Giants’ strong start. He recorded an interception in each of the first three games, with the last one sealing a 12-7 home win versus the Tennessee Titans.
He is also an asset on run defense, notching 30 combined tackles, and has the versatility needed to prosper in Wilson’s system.
D.J. Reader is supposed to be a mere stopgap until New York can acquire a suitable long-term replacement for Dexter Lawrence. That may still be true, but few stopgaps make such a consistent impact .
The 32-year-old defensive tackle is performing at his peak, and possibly beyond. The Giants still have improvements to make on run defense, giving up more than 128 rushing yards per game, but Reader’s stout resistance is preventing disaster from taking shape. He has 15 stops in 251 defensive snaps.
He has 15 stops in 251 defensive snaps .
John Harbaugh went the unconventional route, acquiring a young quarterback instead of placing complete trust in a respected backup like Jameis Winston. The Minnesota Vikings, a team brimming with QB uncertainty, decided that J.J. McCarthy was expendable.
For only the price of a 2027 fifth-round selection, the Giants gambled on the former No. 10 pick. They are cleaning up on that deal so far.
McCarthy survived a couple of early mistakes in his Big Blue debut and threw for 243 yards in the fourth quarter of the team’s near-comeback against the New Orleans Saints. He proved his eruption was no fluke in his first New York start, completing 71.4 percent of his passes and displaying superb touch in a 27-21 overtime win versus the Houston Texans.
Has McCarthy arrived? Who knows, but he is definitely surging .
Top-five picks are expected to make a difference in their rookie year, but Arvell Reese still deserves his flowers for establishing himself as one of the defense’s most important players in two months.
The young linebacker covers incredible ground , showing the ability to rush a QB and then dart downfield to bring down the pass-catcher. He is physically gifted and relentless, qualities that bode well for his NFL ceiling.
Reese boasts a team-high 56 combined tackles, along with 1.5 sacks, five tackles for loss, one fumble recovery, one interception, and four passes defended.
A wild card entering the 2026 campaign, former Cleveland Browns and Jacksonville Jaguars cornerback Greg Newsome II has found a home for himself in the Meadowlands.
Following a solid first half that includes a 62.0 passer rating allowed , the offseason addition inked a three-year, $46 million contract extension worth $32 million guaranteed. He has earned his spot in a surprisingly stingy secondary.
The undrafted 2024 offensive lineman has overtaken John Michael Schmitz for the starting center slot. He has yet to give up a sack through four games, while allowing three pressures and two hurries.
There is no denying that this undrafted rookie kicker has ability, but promise can only hold so much value at this position. Although Dominic Zvada still has some leeway , he is declining rapidly.
The former Michigan standout and Big Ten Kicker of the Year has converted 13-of-18 field goals, missing twice from 40-49 yards and three times from 50 yards or more. He isn’t missing the easy kicks, though.
Zvada also failed to kick the ball out of the back of the end zone in a 34-27 loss versus the Saints, costing the Giants precious seconds that could have changed the outcome.
Perhaps a revival is plausible, but he has to win back the trust he lost in recent weeks.
Odell Beckham Jr., Saquon Barkley, and Tyrone Tracy Jr. are the only Giants players to record 1,000 scrimmage yards in each of their first two NFL seasons. Earning that distinction has done little for Tracy in the present.
Despite scoring three touchdowns in his last two games, the WR-turned-RB is occupying a much smaller role than he did last year.
Tracy, who is currently on IR with a hamstring injury, has a modest 19 carries for 55 yards, averaging a worrying 2.9 yards per attempt.
He is firmly behind Cam Skattebo on the depth chart, and Devin Singletary might even cut into his workload.
Giants fans did not have much confidence in center John Michael Schmitz going into the season, but he still had management on his side. That is no longer true.
The No. 57 selection in the 2023 NFL Draft lost his spot to Bryan Hudson and is running out of time to impress Harbaugh before free agency arrives.

title: Giants Scouting Report: Eagles’ Run Defense Is Vulnerable, but Fangio Is Dangerous
full_text:
In Week 9, the New York Giants offense faces a Philadelphia Eagles defense that has been under significant pressure all season because of injuries to the Eagles’ offense.
Because Philadelphia’s offense has struggled with three-and-outs and ball security, the defense has faced many short fields, creating lopsided scoring opportunities for opposing offenses.
Vic Fangio remains one of the NFL’s better coordinators, and the Giants won’t easily break down his defense. Let’s take a look at what the Eagles will bring to the table in Week 9.
The Eagles spend 80% of their defensive snaps in a 4-2-5. It is their de facto base package because of the offenses they face, not only in the division but around the NFL.
They will utilize traditional 3-4 and 5-2 looks against heavy run packages like 12, 21, and 22 personnel. All of that up front supports a Fangio staple: his two-high safety shell.
That system relies heavily on multiple coverages and disguising pre-snap, while adjusting post-snap to various looks.
The Eagles rank 28th in rushing yards allowed per game at almost 132 yards, and they are 20th in yards per carry.
That is a far cry from some of the dominant units we’ve seen in the past, but those units were also supported by a ball-control offense that let them play much fresher on a series-by-series basis.
Their scheme is predicated on interior defensive linemen being able to two-gap and close down interior rushing lanes, forcing runs to spill outside, where their perimeter speed can attack the ball.
This season, fatigue has led to missed tackles and breakdowns in second-level gap integrity.
Jalen Carter is the most disruptive penetrator on the front line. He is a mandatory double team and cannot be left to one offensive lineman on the interior.
Jordan Davis and Moro Ojomo are two other quality defensive linemen who make a real impact, with Davis manning the nose while Ojomo rotates between 3-technique and 5-technique.
Linebackers Zack Baun and Jeremiah Trotter are a strong pairing of a veteran and a young, up-and-coming starter. With Jihaad Campbell banged up, Trotter takes on a more prominent role.
The coverage scheme is based on a split safety look, which includes quarters as well as cover six (quarter-quarter-half).
They will change and disguise at will to bait quarterbacks into bad throws. They are currently ranked 24th in passing yards allowed, at 235 yards per game.
They’ve struggled most to generate turnovers, with three interceptions through eight games, a far cry from their ability to turn over offenses in previous seasons.
When their pass rush is locked in, they pose a major threat by jumping passes and getting offenses off the field.
That pass rush consists of an interior push from Carter and others, with Jonathan Greenard leading the edge rotation, along with Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith.
Quinyon Mitchell is the defense’s top lockdown corner. He consistently guards the offense’s best receiver in man coverage and in quarters when they try to match up with receivers.
Cooper DeJean is also a high-level slot defender who can play corner. His versatility makes him dangerous because he can cover both inside and outside.
Riq Woolen, who came over from Seattle, is a big, athletic cornerback who gets targeted heavily because offenses stay away from Mitchell. He can be something of a boom-or-bust player at the position.
Jihaad Campbell, along with defensive backs Michael Carter II and Jonathan Jones, are out with various injuries. Both Greenard and Hunt are questionable with ankle injuries.
On the interior, Jordan Davis, Moro Ojomo, and Zack Baun are all dealing with injuries but are probable to play on Sunday.
While everyone has been excited about J.J. McCarthy’s play, make no mistake: the key to victory for the Giants has been, and remains, running the ball and controlling the line of scrimmage. It is the metric you can point to in every game the Giants have succeeded in this season.
With the Eagles struggling to stop the run consistently, the Giants should lean into getting them on their heels early and often with the run.
From there, it is important to get the ball into the hands of Isaiah Likely, who does a good job of pulling the defense in at the short and intermediate levels, which will allow Malik Nabers to operate more freely on the outside.

title: Four 2027 NFL Draft Prospects the Giants Should Watch This Weekend
full_text:
As the New York Giants (4-2-1) prepare for a Week 9 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles (2-6) at Lincoln Financial Field, several Big Blue scouts will be watching closely as college football’s Week 10 slate unfolds.
After a much-needed Week 8 bye, this could be a good time to scout potential targets as they make their cases for selection in the 2027 NFL Draft.
While the rumor mill continues to churn for running back, the team’s biggest need remains along the defensive line. Coach John Harbaugh and his staff may also want to add a player to bolster their tight end depth chart.
Here are four players the Giants may keep an eye on this weekend.
Fresh off the Tigers’ bye week, Green has declared himself “ready to go” while showing few signs of lingering effects from a knee injury that sidelined him two weeks ago. He is expected to play a major role in LSU’s offensive game plan against Alabama this weekend.
In four appearances this season, Green has caught 19 passes for 272 yards and two touchdowns. At 6-foot-7 and 242 pounds, the Jackson, LA native has the length and sure hands to be an effective weapon in contested-catch situations. Green can split out wide, line up in the slot, or control the perimeter when matched up against linebackers or safeties.
With New York’s depth at the position uncertain beyond starter Isaiah Likely , Green could be a highly productive fit within offensive coordinator Matt Nagy’s offense. A strong showing against the Crimson Tide in Week 10 would go a long way toward bolstering his draft stock.
Given the Giants’ need for an imposing presence on the interior of their defensive line, Scott could be an intriguing fit.
The 6-foot-4, 300-pound lineman moves well for his size, especially sideline to sideline. In seven games this season, he has collected 25 total tackles, two fumble recoveries, and 0.5 sacks.
Most importantly, Scott could strengthen the Giants’ run defense. The Chicago native anchors well thanks to his wide base. He is at his best absorbing double teams while stacking and shedding blocks.
Combined with his explosive first step, Scott should contribute to an NFL team right away. As such, expect the Giants to keep the Hurricanes’ tackle in their sights against Notre Dame on Saturday.
If New York wants a dedicated run-stopper, Jackson should be on their list of potential targets. The 6-foot-2, 310-pound tackle has logged 29 total tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, and 0.5 sacks this season. In 2025, PFF gave him a 70.5 run defense grade and credited him with 11 pressures.
At the pro level, Jackson projects as a true nose tackle who contributes on early-down run responsibilities.
Given New York’s difficulty in consistently stopping the run, Jackson could be an enticing mid-to-late-round option, especially if he helps to contain the Florida Gators’ star running back Jadan Baugh during this weekend’s prime-time showdown in Gainesville.
Following a standout season at Michigan in 2025, Haynes has used his second trip through the transfer portal to become a significant force in the Yellow Jackets’ running game.
In his first season with Georgia Tech, the 5-foot-11, 210-pounder has compiled 548 yards on 112 carries and four touchdowns. He has also caught 13 passes for 71 yards and two touchdowns.
While much of the Giants fan base remains intently focused on established pros such as Jonathan Taylor and Derrick Henry to provide an immediate upgrade to New York’s running game, a player with Haynes’ versatility is always worth watching as a draft prospect.
His breakaway speed and ability to read the box would complement Cam Skattebo’s strength-based style.

title: Giants Reportedly Eye Ravens’ RB Justice Hill While Jonathan Taylor Talks Linger
full_text:
The New York Giants seem to want to add a running back, not only to reinforce depth in their depleted backfield, but also to add a potential bell cow who can carry the bulk of the load.
To that end, ESPN insider Adam Schefter reported that the Giants reached out to the Baltimore Ravens , head coach John Harbaugh’s former team, to inquire about a running back, but not Derrick Henry, whom Schefter said the Ravens have not considered trading before Tuesday’s deadline.
Instead, the Giants have reportedly inquired about obtaining running back/kickoff returner Justice Hill from the Ravens.
Hill, 5-foot-10 and 195 pounds, was selected by Harbaugh and the Ravens in the fourth round of the 2019 draft following a strong career at Oklahoma State, where he earned two first-team All-Big 12 honors and was named the Big 12 Offensive Freshman of the Year in 2016.
The 28-year-old Hill has appeared in 93 games for the Ravens with five starts. He has 301 regular-season rushing attempts for 1,495 yards and nine touchdowns, and has caught 136 of 177 pass targets for 1,017 yards and five scores.
Hill also has kickoff return experience, having recorded 1,009 yards on 39 kickoff returns (25.9 yards per return).
Hill is currently in the final year of a two-year extension, which pays him $2.75 million in base salary and $14,705 per game he’s active.
Harbaugh and the Giants are believed to want a running back not just for the short term but for the long term.
While they could easily seek to extend the expiring contract of a player they acquire, such as Hill, it might make more sense in this case for the Giants to try to sign him in free agency so they don’t have to give up any draft assets (assuming they don’t land their other reported option, Colts running back Jonathan Taylor).
Speaking of Taylor, there may be some gamesmanship at play if the Giants’ reported interest in Hill is accurate. The Colts are thought to be holding out for the best possible deal for Taylor, which means any trade is likely to go down to the wire.
The Giants currently have a thinned-out running back room. They released Najee Harris a few weeks ago, and Tyrone Tracy Jr. is on IR with a hamstring strain. In addition, their de facto RB1, Cam Skattebo, is dealing with a hamstring strain of his own and is listed as “doubtful” on this week’s injury report.
The Giants have two critical divisional games, against the Eagles and the Commanders, sandwiched around the Nov. 10 trade deadline. New York is also thought to be exploring options at defensive tackle, but it’s unclear whether it can satisfy both reported needs or will have to prioritize one over the other.

title: Giants Mailbag:  Trade Winds, Deonte Banks, Game Stuff and More
full_text:
Welcome to the weekly New York Giants On SI mailbag! From offseason moves to game-day strategies, we'll do our best to answer your questions. (Some questions have been edited for brevity and clarity.)
How do you compare Thomas Fidone’s skillset to Theo Johnson? Any chance he pushes him for playing time once Johnson is healthy?
Truth be told, I am not sure a fair comparison can be made given the small sample size of Fidone's snaps in this offense.
That said, Johnson has more explosive straight-line speed, while Fidone, with a leaner frame, is more agile and more effective in short-area lateral explosion.
Hi Patti, Has the compensatory pick we'll be receiving in 2027 moving up from a 5th to a possible 4th Rd. pick satisfied the requisite number of snaps that C Austin Schlottmann has played? Or, does it appear that Schlottmann will reach that threshhold? Please check Thanks, Lyle
Lyle, per Over the Cap's Nick Korte , who does a great job at tracking and calculating these things, the projected comp pick is NOT for Schlottmann but rather for Wan'Dale Robinson, and it's a projected fourth-round pick.
Let's wait until the season draws to a close though before counting our chickens on this so as to not end up disappointed if something throws a monkey wrench into the plans.
Can you explain why a “virtual measurement” takes five times as long as two guys with chains? Is the NFL using dial-up? A slide rule?
I do not know what parameters they have been given. If you want a conspiracy theory, maybe it's to allow another commercial break and, hence, more money for the network?
Are there plains to use Hyatt more?
Possibly. He has two more practice squad elevations to go, and with receiver Charlie Jones ailing due to a hand injury, I could certainly see Hyatt getting the call-up from the practice squad.
What's the consensus feel about Jj
By "consensus," do you mean the locker room? Fans? Another group? (All of whom I'm not the appointed spoeksperson by the way.) But if you want my opinion, I'm encouraged based on what I've seen on the small sample size so far.
most likely giants acquisition at this point?
I mean, right now all signs point to Jonathan Taylor, right? Personally, I still think they should try to land a defensive lineman—I'm just not sure there is one out there worth trading for after the Buckner and Simmons deals.
That John Harbaugh got involved with the Titans to try to get Jeffery Simmons after reportedly hitting a stonewall with Titans' GM Mike Borgonzi tells me they agree that they need and desperately want a defensive lineman in the worst way. The fact that they were aiming for Simmons tells me they're not messing around.
Fans have seen the on field difference John Harbaugh has made.  Are there other subtle things you see day to day that have made a difference that aren’t as noticeable to the fans?
Not really, Kris. Harbaugh has great attention to detail, and he has shown that he can handle adversity when it pops up, better than some of the previous head coaches who preceded him and followed Tom Coughlin.
I suppose that's the biggest thing I've noticed: in tough times, players want a leader who doesn't let the world see him sweat. But I'm sure Giants fans have probably drawn that conclusion as well so I'm not sure the answer fits your question.
how likely is JT to become a giant
I’m not one to assign a percentage to what should be a “yes or no” response question, but what I will tell you is that unless the Colts come down off their reported asking price, which, depending on what report you believe, either includes a first-round pick or a Christian McCaffrey type of haul (second, third, fourth, and fifth), I’d say zero chance if either of those is true.
The Giants don't have a fourth- or fifth-round pick in next year’s draft, so unless the Colts are willing to take their 2028 picks, I don’t think a deal gets done unless, again, the Colts become more reasonable with their asking price.
What  do you attribute Deonte Banks’ turnaround to this season? Is it more about the defensive scheme putting him in better positions to succeed, or has there been a significant shift in his confidence and mental approach to the game?
I think it's a combination of scheme and coaching. The scheme being run is a better fit for what Banks does well.
The Giants, under Shane Bowen, played a lot of soft zone coverage, which forced the cornerback to play about eight yards off the receiver and often led to disaster because Banks had to second-guess what was unfolding in front of him.
Dennard Wilson has deployed tighter press-man and man-match coverages for Banks, bringing him closer to the receiver so he can use his physical toolbox to disrupt receivers as they look to get off the line of scrimmage and make breaks. Banks has the speed to keep up with the league's better receivers, and Wilson's approach has proven that.
Then, in defensive backs coach Addison Lynch, you have a coach who has clearly made a connection with Banks, in which he's helped to build up the cornerback's confidence and also get it through to Banks that one bad play shouldn't be the catalyst for giving up, thinking he's not good enough or that he'll be pulled from the lineup.
From Gary W. (via e-mail): Can someone please tell me why the league insists on the ridiculous 35-second rule? A stupid penalty or a forced timeout should decide no game. It certainly doesn't add anything or improve the game.
Gary, did you mean the 25-second clock, which is used after specific administrative stoppages?

title: Giants RB Cam Skattebo Doubtful for Eagles Game After Missing a Third Straight Practice
full_text:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (hamstring) missed his third day of practice since the team returned from its bye, raising doubt about his availability for Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Skattebo worked with a trainer during the last three days of the media viewing periods. While head coach John Harbaugh said that they’re going to keep the door open for Skattebo to play on Sunday, things do not appear to be heading in the right direction for Skattebo.
Even if Skattebo, who received a "doubtful" game status, were to play, he’d likely be significantly limited in terms of his snaps. That means the Giants are probably planning to add a running back from their practice squad, either via a signing or a standard elevation.
“I'm not making any announcements at this meeting, this particular press conference,” Harbaugh said in response to a question about the roster spot the team opened by waiving quarterback Jake Haener. “We have certain roster moves we need to make with our various situations.”
Skattebo, who usually takes to the podium on Fridays, did not do so this week, another sign that he likely won’t play on Sunday.
The Giants are all but certain to tap into the practice squad for a running back to fill the empty roster spot.
A best guess would be that Eric Gray, signed to the practice squad this week, gets the spot that opened following the waiving of Haener, as Gray, who not only knows the system but can also contribute as a return specialist with receiver Charlie Jones (hand) ailing and listed as questionable for Sunday's game, would make the most sense.
Harbaugh and Malk Nabers (knee) both confirmed that the receiver practiced fully after sitting out Thursday’s session.
It’s unknown if the knee issue that Nabers has been listed with is the same one that he suffered the torn ACL in last year or something else. Regardless, Harbaugh said Nabers’ issue was “an in-season type thing,” without elaborating, adding. “It's not an issue. He'll be full-go for the game.”
All other Giants on the injury report are good to go, with tackles Andrew Thomas (groing) andJermaine Eluemunor (calf) both having practiced in full on Friday.

title: What Jets Are Saying About Week 9 Injury Report Ahead of Sunday
full_text:
There is good news and bad news when it comes to the New York Jets injury report heading into Week 9 against the Kansas City Chiefs.
The good news is that edge rusher David Bailey and running back Breece Hall are both expected to play. Bailey missed Week 8 with a groin injury while a quad injury kept Hall out for the last five. Even better, the team could have their full collection of edge rushers with Joseph Ossai potentially back as well.
But with every piece of good news there is also bad. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson has been ruled out for Sunday's contest with a concussion. He reported the injury on Monday and has been in protocol ever since.
His absence, coupled with the return of some key veterans, have Jets players and coaches talking about their chances in Week 9 against Kansas City.
Here's the full injury report from the Jets' practice on Friday with three clear distinctions on who is out for Sunday:
Friday’s injury report for #NYJvsKC pic.twitter.com/S8vga27YX3
Of note, the three players that are out extend beyond Wilson. Special teamer Trevin Wallace is also out while Ossai, rookie safety VJ Payne, defensive tackle Harrison Phillips, and corner Nahshon Wright are all listed as questionable.
The good news is Mason Taylor, Hall, and Bailey are all starters and will need to be on the field for the Jets to have any chance against the Chiefs.
Speaking to reporters before practice on Friday, Glenn was clear: the team was prepared to play without Wilson, but that doesn't mean his absence will be anything less than a major blow to the entire unit.
"I think it speaks for itself," Glenn said. "Any time you lose a player of that magnitude, it's always tough, right, but we do have other players, and those guys will look forward to the challenge."
Glenn did acknowledge the benefit that came from having Hall back in the lineup . He made it clear that the former second-round running back was going to have a role in the offense on Sunday, and it will be to work with rising star Braelon Allen.
"I know we're trying to get in this who's going to be the starter and try to spin sort of a negative situation, but nothing's changed from how I see this," Glenn said. "Both of those guys will play and that's just what it is."
The same can be said for the second-overall pick in Bailey. His return gives the team more flexibility to rush the passer—even one as elite as Patrick Mahomes.
"He (Bailey) just has to understand that with Mahomes is going to fake throw," Glenn said. "He's going to move around, and we just got to make sure we squeeze the pocket and make sure we don't let him out of the pocket in situations like that."
It's hard to envision a Jets victory on Sunday without Wilson. But getting several starters back healthy will certainly help.

title: Taking Braelon Allen Out of RB1 Role Would Be a Huge Mistake as Breece Hall Returns
full_text:
Coming off a second-half collapse against the Raiders last Sunday, the Jets hit the road to face the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium with a 2-6 record and their season all but lost at this point.
Injuries have been an issue all season for the Jets, which have kept them from being at full strength and forced them to test their depth chart each week.
While that's not an excuse for the poor coaching and lackluster defensive play so far, it has been a prevailing theme since the season began and has continued this week with some key players finding themselves on the injury report once again .
Wide receiver Garrett Wilson has been ruled out of Sunday's game against the Chiefs due to a concussion. But running back Breece Hall appears set to return from a five-game absence due to a quad injury after ESPN's Rich Cimini noted in Thursday's injury report that Hall "practices fully for the first time since his injury and later said he will play Sunday."
Jets injury report: Breece Hall practices fully for the first time since his injury and later says he will play Sunday. Not looking good for Garrett Wilson. #Jets pic.twitter.com/KwpP20EOGf
While head coach Aaron Glenn has insisted that both Hall and Braelon Allen will play in Sunday's game, it remains to be seen how much of a workload Hall will have as he returns to the field amid what has been a breakout season for Allen.
Offensive coordinator Frank Reich seemingly made it clear that the Jets plan to use both RBs instead of exploring a trade for their RB1, but his return from injury should not take away from what Allen has accomplished in his absence.
With back-to-back 100-yard rushing games and three of the five games Hall has missed, it could prove costly for Gang Green if Allen is not the lead back amid Hall's return, at least for another week as the latter gets back up to speed.
Before the 2025 season, Allen only had three rushing touchdowns and had never rushed for more than 55 yards in a single game. While he has two rushing TDs in the five games without Hall, Allen has equaled his previous number of scores on the ground in eight games this season and has had at least 14 carries in each of the last five games.
Even more impressive, Allen's 5.0 yards per carry are considerably better than Hall's (3.2), albeit in five more games. Pro Football Focus paints an even bigger picture, giving Allen the eighth-best overall grade (82.4) and sixth-best rushing grade (85.6) out of 45 qualified RBs in the league.
Something else to keep an eye on is Wilson's absence from the WR room and the impact it could have on the depth at that position. While Reich's inability to consistently get his WR1 touches has been a recurring issue, the recent returns from rookie Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell should still give quarterback Geno Smith some trusty options downfield. We also shouldn't rule out Hall's potential usage in that area.
Allen and RB3 Isaiah Davis have a combined 149 yards on 22 receptions this season. Hall has had a much greater impact in the pass game with 198 catches, 1,744 yards, and nine TDs in 59 career games, including 10 catches on as many targets for 102 yards this season. Hall already faces more pressure to perform after the Wilson news , but this could be the ideal way to ease him back into things in an area he has excelled in more than Allen.
It is hard to ignore the explosiveness Allen has shown in Hall's absence and how impactful his physical downhill style of play between the tackles has given this offense a nice balance that has proven to be hard to contain at times. Look no further than the fact that they scored on each of their first six drives in the Week 8 loss to Las Vegas, which was a huge improvement from the slow starts they have gotten off to earlier this season.
It seems like Hall is likely to stay around in Gotham as the trade deadline looms on Tuesday, especially with $14.5 million and $15.5 million cap hits in 2026 and 2027 , respectively, but regardless of how everything plays out between now and then, it would be a huge mistake if the Jets pivot away from Allen in favor of Hall, considering how productive he has been.
If anything, this could be a case of workload management as Hall returns to full strength and potentially splits carries with Allen while being a solid contributor in the passing game. Hall has not forgotten how to play, but Allen's emergence should be enough to keep him as the lead back for at least another week as Hall makes his long-awaited return.
