title: 3 Matchups That Will Decide Jets’ Week 9 Game Against Chiefs
full_text:
After dropping two winnable games at home, the Jets will look to end their three-game losing streak when they head to Arrowhead Stadium to take on the Chiefs in Week 9.
Kansas City is also on a losing streak of its own, falling to the Seahawks and Broncos in the last two games. Despite this, the Chiefs are widely viewed as heavy favorites to win, given how poorly New York has played the past few weeks.
With head coach Aaron Glenn’s job on the ropes, he’ll need an upset victory over the Chiefs to have any chance of saving his job. Otherwise, the Jets could be compelled to make some deals ahead of the trade deadline.
For New York to come away victorious, it will need to win these three key matchups.
Kenneth Walker has picked up right where he left off in the 2025 playoffs and has been a dominant force on the ground with the Chiefs. Head coach Andy Reid has made the reigning Super Bowl MVP the offense’s engine, unlocking a new dimension with his high-impact production that Kansas City hasn’t had in years.
Through seven games, Walker ranks third in the league in rushing yards (770) and second in rushing yards per attempt (5.5). He’s been one of the key ingredients to the Chiefs' 5-2 start, with his success on the ground playing a significant role in determining the outcome of their games.
Kansas City is 5-0 when Walker rushes for over 70 yards, whereas it's 0-2 when he rushes for fewer than 70. Those losses came in the past two weeks to the Broncos and Seahawks, who prioritized neutralizing Walker, limiting him to a combined 105 yards.
Seattle played nickel or dime personnel on all 50 defensive snaps, stacking the box on just 7% of its plays. As a result, Walker rushed for just 36 yards and had zero explosive runs.
Although Seattle’s approach was effective, the Jets shouldn’t necessarily follow the same blueprint. The Seahawks have one of the best defenses in the league, with elite defenders at each level who can fly to Walker without committing additional players to the box.
New York doesn’t have that luxury, nor has it been effective at containing the run. Through eight games, the unit ranks 21st in rushing yards allowed per game (123.6). To limit Walker’s impact, head coach Aaron Glenn should emphasize clogging the interior lanes and preventing him from reaching the second level with room to operate.
Walker’s patience, elusiveness and tackle-breaking ability make him one of the best runners in the league. If New York is to beat Kansas City, the defense has to win at the point of attack and make the offensive line work to create running lanes.
Linebackers Demario Davis and Jamien Sherwood will need to play a critical role in that effort. The pair have struggled with missed tackles this season, combining for 17, and must clean this up to contain Walker. Giving him extra opportunities to break tackles could quickly turn a stop into a big gain.
If New York can limit Walker’s impact and hold him to minimal gains, it will force the Chiefs to become more dependent on Patrick Mahomes and the passing game.
Through seven games, Geno Smith has been sacked 23 times, which is tied for the second-most. While the blame will be placed on the offensive line, it’s not entirely their fault. Smith shares responsibility for this.
The 14-year veteran has played too conservatively this season. At times, he’s held onto the ball too long, waiting for deep or developing routes instead of throwing it away or checking down.
Things changed dramatically last week against the Raiders. Smith made quicker decisions and attempted more downfield passes, recording a 31.3% deep rate, per Next Gen Stats. The offensive line played a key role, limiting Max Crosby and Las Vegas’ pass rush to just two sacks and seven pressures.
Although the Raiders didn’t have the best pass rush heading into this matchup, New York’s line did a terrific job of limiting its impact. They’ll hope to replicate that success against the Chiefs' pass rush, which has also struggled to generate consistent pressure.
Through seven games, Kansas City is tied for last in sacks (9) and ranks 29th in pressure rate (19.3%). A major reason is that star defensive tackle Chris Jones’ production has dropped significantly this season, with just half a sack and just 16 pressures.
This has put immense pressure on edge rusher George Karlaftis, who leads the team in sacks (2) and pressures (34). Even though Kansas City hasn’t done well generating pressure, it’s been among the best teams against the run, ranking eighth in rushing yards allowed per game (96.3).
Even with star receiver Garrett Wilson sidelined , the Jets can exploit the Chiefs' lack of a pass rush. New York needs to take advantage of the Chiefs' inability to create pressure by giving Smith enough time to sling the ball around and attack downfield.
Even though Jones has been quiet, the emphasis should be on not giving him one-on-one opportunities. The Jets will need to slide protection and use chip blocks to limit his impact.
While this creates more opportunities for Karlaftis, New York should be encouraged by Olu Fashanu and Armand Membou’s recent play, as the two have allowed just seven pressures and zero sacks over the past two games.
Pre-snap communication will also be critical against defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo, as he’ll try to test the line with simulated pressure and timely blitzes. And with Arrowhead Stadium being one of the loudest stadiums, having everyone on the same page will be crucial.
If the offensive line can give Smith enough time to work through his progressions and find open receivers, the Jets should find success through the air.
Although New York won’t have Wilson on Sunday, rookie edge rusher David Bailey should be returning to the lineup after missing Week 8 against the Raiders with a groin injury. Without their No. 2 overall pick, the defense wasn’t nearly as productive generating pressure without him, posting just 12 pressures and one sack.
Despite missing the game, Bailey still leads the team in pressures (26), quarterback hits (5), and sacks (5.5). If New York is going to have any chance of upsetting the Chiefs, they’ll need Bailey to apply consistent pressure against Mahomes.
Getting to Mahomes won’t be easy, as he’s been sacked just nine times this season. However, with Bailey primarily lining up on the left side, he’ll have a favorable matchup against right tackle Jaylon Moore, who’s struggled in pass protection.
According to Next Gen Stats , the 2021 fifth-round selection has allowed a 12.6% pressure rate, which ranks fourth-highest among right tackles with at least 100 pass-blocking snaps. Moore has also had his share of penalty issues, most notably last week against the Broncos, where he committed a false start that nullified a potential game-winning touchdown.
With Bailey generating the fifth-highest pressure rate this season (20%), per Next Gen Stats, the Texas Tech alum must have a big day against Moore.
The top priority for Bailey will be getting to Mahomes quickly. With his elite burst and speed, he can make life difficult for the heavier Moore, who has had difficulty against explosive edge rushers.
If Bailey can wear down Moore with his relentless motor, it could force him into making similar mental mistakes as he did last week and potentially force the Chiefs to double-team him. With more eyes on Bailey, it could create more opportunities for Joseph Ossai or Will McDonald IV to get to Mahomes or force him to make a quick decision.

title: Breece Hall Returns to Jets With Clear Message About Trade Rumors & Starting Job
full_text:
Just two months ago, New York Jets running back Breece Hall was considered one of the top running backs in the game. His ability as both a runner and pass catcher comes in rare form across the NFL.
But as former coach Jerry Glanville once said, the NFL's best acronym is "Not For Long."
A quad injury cost the Jets' running back the last five weeks. In his absence, Braelon Allen has turned into one of the more productive runners in team history. The former Wisconsin product is the first Jets running back to record three straight 100-yard rushing games since Curtis Martin in 2004.
Heading into Week 9, Hall is back. And with it, questions about his future with the team, where the depth chart stands, and how things will look for the offense going forward.
Speaking to reporters this week, Hall made it clear: he remains the team's starter regardless of what Allen has done over the course of the last month.
"I'm still a starter, still a very good running back in this league," Hall said. "Obviously, Braelon's been playing good. I think him and the offense have caught their stride after the first three, four games. So it's going to be good to just get in there, just play some ball."
In a modern offense, both Hall and Allen can coexist in a way that is great for the Jets. New York can scheme open Hall in the passing game while using Allen up the middle and between the tackles. The more the two play on the field together, the harder it will be for opposing teams to stop Gang Green.
That task, though, will be based on the creativity of offensive play-caller Frank Reich .
"We have some plays that are tagged for one or the other, but it's a great problem to have," Reich said. "You've got two No. 1 backs. Breece is, obviously ... our guy, but it'll be a mix."
Reich's comments also pour cool water on the heated rumors of a potential trade of Hall. New York is refusing to open trade dialogues at this time for their running back, but with Allen's breakout, the team may simply want to keep Allen as the starter going forward.
Hall, though, believes any trade rumor is based on the fanbase's point of view. Not with what the team wants.
"It's like if I have 100 yards, they love me," he said. "If I don't, everybody's like, 'Get him out of here.'"
The former second-round pick out of Iowa only further increased awareness of his standing with the Jets after seemingly deleting his social media this week. In the modern age of professional athletics coupled with social media, it's common to see outspoken individuals make cryptic posts or delete pages altogether to convey deeper meaning.
That doesn't appear to be the case either, though.
"I've had people threatening me and my family on social media," Hall said. "So that's not something that's good for your mental health that you should be looking at. So I'm just like, all right, if people think it's that serious, if you're willing to go that low, then it's like nothing that I need to look at."
There will always be a good and bad side to NFL fandom. Passion and loyalty are rare throughout modern society, but with that passion comes an overzealous attitude toward trolling their own athletes. Hall should never have to go through threats made on social media simply because he was injured over the last month.
That doesn't mean he wants out of New York, or the Jets want to move on from him either. Since arriving at the team last year, head coach Aaron Glenn has shared his intention to run a "by committee" approach to their running back room.
In short, it doesn't seem like Hall is going anywhere, but his role as the feature back in New York's offense has fundamentally changed—for better or worse.

title: 3 Ways Jets Can Still Upset Chiefs In Week 9 Without Garrett Wilson
full_text:
To the surprise of absolutely no one, the New York Jets announced that star receiver Garrett Wilson will not play on Sunday due to a concussion reported earlier in the week. Wilson will be out until he clears protocol.
Over the last few years, an injury like the one suffered by Wilson would normally sink the team's chances to succeed on gameday. An infusion of young talent, though, means New York has a small but fighting chance against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium.
In order for that to happen, three things must be accomplished.
For any upset to take place, it's important for the underdog to control the line of scrimmage and keep a high-powered offense like Kansas City's off the field. Jets running back Braelon Allen should help tremendously in that regard, following his 504 yards and two touchdowns in his last five contests.
Without Wilson, the Jets are expected to still find a way to throw the ball effectively. Their collection of receiving targets, including Omar Cooper Jr., Adonai Mitchell, Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq, are all capable of keeping the passing game afloat.
While Wilson will be out, running back Breece Hall is expected to return , right in time ahead of the trade deadline.
More importantly, though, as long as the Jets run the ball well, they should be able to keep Mahomes and the Chiefs off the field. If they don't, they will struggle mightily on the road.
Another piece of good news for the Jets is that they will get their star second overall pick back from injury. David Bailey returned to the practice field after missing last week's game with a groin problem.
By being on the field, he takes his team-high 5.5 sacks into a game against Kansas City, where their offensive line has crumbled over the last several weeks.
Over eight weeks, the Chiefs' offensive line is ninth in the NFL in pressure rate allowed. Over the last two weeks, though, the team is 20th in Pressure Rate Over Expectation.
If New York can get pressure on Mahomes and keep Kenneth Walker at bay running the ball, they should be able to keep the game close.
New York's talent is clearly better than it has been in recent years. Their offense appears to be hitting its stride, and their defense (while banged up) still has several All-Pro-caliber players on their roster.
The thing that is holding the group back more than anything, though, is their coaching staff.
Aaron Glenn and his assistants have held the roster back due to poor play-calls, bad adjustments and mind-numbing in-game decisions. A matchup against Andy Reid and his staff will be one of the bigger coaching mismatches we have seen in years.
The Jets can win on Sunday but will need Glenn and his staff to outcoach Reid. Kansas City has lost games to inferior teams before, but has rarely been outcoached by people who struggle with the fundamentals.  A die-hard fan may want to see Glenn take the next step as a head coach and prove he can make calls necessary to pull off an upset.
But with a 5-20 record through his first year and a half on the job, it's hard for anyone to see that happening. In fact, unless there's a coaching swap for the first time in an NFL game, it's hard to envision anything keeping the Jets in the game on Sunday.

title: 3 Trade Partners That Make Sense for Jets Ahead of Deadline
full_text:
No one is going to expect the New York Jets to turn around their season at 2-6. Two upcoming games against the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills could end up being the final nails in the coffin for the Aaron Glenn era and for many veterans on the roster .
Even a loss on Sunday to the Chiefs could lead New York to find trade partners for some of their veterans who are not considered part of the future of the organization.
There are plenty of teams who could see themselves as possible trade partners with several players on the Jets. It all comes down to the Jets' asking price and how desperate other teams are to get a deal done.
Here are three possible trade partners the team could be working with over the next few days.
Chicago wants edge rusher help, and it could certainly use help in the secondary. A potential trade for either Will McDonald or slot cornerback Jarvis Brownlee could work out for both teams. New York would get quality draft capital back, and the Bears would add to a roster that is Super Bowl-ready.
The question will be compensation and alignment fit. If the Bears want an edge rusher who can stop the run, McDonald probably isn't the guy for them. If Chicago believes it needs more of a boundary player at corner, Brownlee won't be the fit for them.
At the end of the day, though, Chicago is desperate for a title. And it may push them to be aggressive with a team like the Jets on Tuesday.
Minnesota being a trade partner is based on two things:
1. Jonathan Taylor ends up with the Giants or another team 2. The Jets decide to move off from Breece Hall after all
I remain steadfast in the belief that the team won't move on from Hall this offseason unless they are blown away by a trade offer. Hall is a valued member of their offense and someone who will garner touches when he sees the field on Sunday.
That said, with Braelon Allen's breakout, it appears to be somewhat understandable for the Jets to get out of Hall's contract just months into a new deal. Minnesota is another playoff contender that needs more running back help.
Wait, why are the Titans here? They aren't competing for a playoff spot!
True, but Robert Saleh is running the show in Tennessee, and we've already seen him be willing to bring back former Jets players that fit his wide-nine defensive alignment. Could Tennessee try to bring in McDonald as a way to bolster their pass rush beyond the 2026 season? It makes a lot of sense considering Saleh isn't going to be a one-and-done coach.
Saleh's infatuation with his former players could open a trade partnership with his former team and give New York further draft assets to build their roster.

title: Aaron Glenn's Rebuilt Jets Staff Only Making His Seat Hotter
full_text:
When Aaron Glenn was first hired as head coach of the New York Jets, his chief calling card was his perceived ability to bring with him a highly touted staff. As a former player and well-liked coach, people thought Glenn would be able to bring with him great assistants to build the team.
Through two years, though, the opposite has happened. After a three-win season in 2025, Glenn revamped almost his entire coaching staff, including both offensive and defensive coordinators and up to five positional assistants.
Hard to say he can build a good staff.
As the 2026 Jets continue to bungle through a current 2-6 mark, some of the answers from Glenn's assistants have already gotten worse.
And it all came to a head on Thursday.
On offense, the Jets believed going with a veteran guy like Frank Reich would be the right move for the organization. His experience with talented units and veteran quarterbacks was seen as a major positive.
Through eight games, though, it's clear that the Jets' talent is keeping things afloat and coaching is only holding them back.
It's even  worse on the defensive side.
Brian Duker is the Jets' defensive coordinator but he doesn't call plays. That distinction is in the hands of Glenn as a defensive-minded individual. Duker's job is to help with gameplanning and adjustments—two things the Jets defense has struggled with the most.
His answer on Thursday on the team defending tight ends—a problem over the last several weeks—only raised further eyebrows on the coaching staff. Last week, Brock Bowers caught two touchdown passes en route to a Raiders win. Going against the Kansas City Chiefs and Travis Kelce could add consistent problems.
But Duker saw things differently.
"I would not anticipate reading their mind on that, so we'll wait and see how that goes," Duker said. "He [Kelce] probably is used a little bit differently."
What? The Jets may not prepare or assume that the Chiefs will use Kelce in a similar way to Bowers simply because they are different players? Kansas City's coaching staff remains one of the best in the league. You better believe they'll have a plan to use their tight ends in a similar way to how the Raiders did.
The fact the Jets are even thinking they may not is a failure in preparation, coaching and imagination.
And it only highlights how bad the staff has been so far in 2026.
Glenn is not at fault for a slip-up answer like this. All coaches have answers they would probably want back. But as a head coach who reshaped his staff specifically because he wanted more people that thought like he did, a 2-6 start makes his seat among the league's hottest.
And as these slip-ups continue, it only paints a further picture of his staff being unprepared for the modern NFL when it matters most.

title: Darren Mougey Needs to Follow 3-Step Guide for Jets' Successful Deadline
full_text:
Last year, the trades of both Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams were blockbuster moves from which the New York Jets came away as clear winners.
What does general manager Darren Mougey have as an encore?
Mougey has just a few days left to determine if he wants to move any current members of the Jets. They won't get nearly the same return as they did in 2025, but they could still come away as clear winners once again.
And there are three ways for Mougey and the Jets to accomplish that.
This isn't the NBA or MLB. Teams do not have to make a move just because they aren't making the playoffs. Sometimes, not making a move is the best for teams like the Jets at this point. New York doesn't have any top talent that they used to like Gardner or Williams.
That said, by not making moves, the Jets would still have three first-round picks and $80 million in cap space to work with for 2027. They aren't getting any top draft compensation for some of the players that are drawing interest.
Because of that, there may be no reason to open up more holes on the roster. And if that is the case, New York's best move to have a successful deadline is to make no moves at all rather than forcing something that isn't there.
If the Jets are going to sell off their talent, Mougey needs to make sure to sell high. That means if the team is moving off from players like Will McDonald or Breece Hall , they need to make sure they get the right draft compensation for each player moved. Anything less will put the team in worse shape going forward.
It also is a reminder of Mougey understanding both the talent on the roster and the needs of others across the NFL.
Mougey proved last season that he isn't afraid to get aggressive when it comes to the trade deadline. Last season, he shipped off two of his best players for three first-round picks, two players and a second-rounder.
He isn't afraid to make a big deal. And he shouldn't be passive now.
There are multiple ways for the Jets to improve the team. If the Jets choose to sell off some of their talent for quality draft picks , the long-term future will be even better than it already is. If they choose to buy (a thought most Jets fans won't allow themselves to have), it could be to bring in players with multiple years of control. It would, again, improve the team.
Mougey won't have to worry about his seat getting hotter either. His work so far has been quality enough where he won't be tied to the team's record through two seasons. That should give him the flexibility to improve through draft picks or pure talent.

title: Joseph Ossai Will Be on the Clock to Prove Himself to Jets Upon Returning From Injury
full_text:
As the Jets' Week 9 clash with the Chiefs nears, veteran pass rusherJoseph Ossai is back at practice after his ankle injury . The 26-year-old has missed five games this season and has not lived up to his $34.5 million price tag in the games he has played.
With the money he is promised, Ossai will already be under scrutiny when he takes the field Sunday.
Ossai is coming off a 2025 season in which he recorded five sacks and earned a 64.0 Pro Football Focus grade . This year, Ossai has yet to bring down the QB and has a 49.6 PFF grade. The former Bengal's time is running out to prove he was worth the price New York paid, especially if he can't make an immediate impact.
Ossai potentially returns to a Jets defense that got rang up for 38 points in Week 8. New York only sacked Kirk Cousins once and gave up 95 rushing yards to a Las Vegas team ranked 31st in the category in 2026. The bar is low for Ossai to show his value coming off a game like that.
Ossai must show up in some way on the stat sheet. He has 10 total tackles this season, with seven against the Bears. The real issue is the lack of pressure that Ossai has put on opposing quarterbacks. In 49 pass-rush snaps this season, Ossai has yet to record a single pressure. For comparison, he had 43 in 14 games with the Bengals last season—an average of 3.1 per outing.
The veteran disruptor has to find himself in the backfield soon.
New York may start to feel buyer's remorse if the fifth-year veteran does not start to impact games. Missing five games and not pressuring the quarterback won't keep Ossai employed; stats will. Whether it's in the running or passing game, Ossai must perform in his first game back to prove he is worth his contract.
Joseph Ossai doesn't need to sack Patrick Mahomes multiple times in Week 9 or become the Jets' sack leader to meet expectations. He just needs to be a legitimate option for the Jets' defensive line. If Ossai is to be back for the trip to Kansas City, he has a chance to stake his claim.
The Chiefs' offensive line has been less than stellar in pass protection this season. Kansas City allows a 37% pressure rate, ranking 19th in the NFL. This is the type of welcome back that Ossai should be clamoring for. If the veteran can get in the backfield and impact the passing game, questions about his contract will begin to dissipate.
Ossai can also help against Kenneth Walker and the run. The end had a 70.7 grade against the run in 2025; this year it's a measly 54.3. Ossai needs to return to form against the NFL's third-leading rusher. As a Bengal, Ossai showed he could impact the run, with 21 stops in 2025. He needs to show that he still has that skill set against Kansas City and for the rest of the season.
For the rest of 2026, the defensive end has to perform. Whether sacks or pressures, Ossai needs to start affecting the passer. He also needs to be the run-stopper the Jets know he can be. With zero sacks and only two run stops this season, the defensive end has been a far cry from his best.
Ossai will look to return and be the game-changer he and the organization know he can be.
He's yet to live up to his three-year, $34.5 million contract. Three games of subpar football are not what Ossai was paid to do. The clock is ticking for the 26-year-old, and every game he doesn't show up for gets him one step closer to midnight. A trade after June 1, 2027, would save the Jets $10.5 million in cap space while only taking on $1.75 million in dead money, per OverTheCap .
Ossai must return to form if his career as a Jet is to be anything but a mistake.

title: Forgotten Jets Rookie's Potential Return Could Signal the End of Andre Cisco in New York
full_text:
With another crushing loss behind them and a difficult road test ahead against the Chiefs in Week 9, the 2026 season continues to get away from the Jets as some coaching malpractice and struggles getting off the field defensively continue to plague them.
A double-digit lead was not even enough as the Jets orchestrated a second-half collapse and completely gave the game away at home. That said, injuries have also been a talking point all season, as multiple players have dealt with setbacks since the season began, and that has been no different for rookies VJ Payne and Anez Cooper, as they have still not played a single snap despite being eligible to return since they started the season on injured reserve.
That is about to change for Payne after ESPN 's Rich Cimini reported on Wednesday that "the Jets are opening the 21-day practice window" for him.
The Jets are opening the 21-day practice window for rookie S V.J. Payne, per source. They also signed rookie WR Joe Manjack (Broncos UDFA) to the practice squad. #Jets
That does not necessarily mean that Payne will play on Sunday, but it does suggest his return is on the table after remaining on the injury report coming out of the Week 8 loss .
That is not a good sign for safety Andre Cisco, who had a big role early in the season with at least 44 defensive snaps in the first three games before playing nine or fewer in each of the last five.
For someone who already needed to prove himself coming into the season after a torn pectoral muscle forced him to miss nearly half of his first season in Gang Green in 2025, a one-year, $2.5 million contract would make it easy for the Jets to turn the page on him either by cutting him or trading him by the Nov. 10 trade deadline .
While Cisco's lack of long-term stability is clear, and the questions surrounding his health coming into the season, his outlook grew even murkier after general manager Darren Mougey signed Dane Belton and acquired veteran Minkah Fitzpatrick from the Dolphins to bolster the secondary before the season even began.
Although he had an opportunity to change his Jets future when Fitzpatrick was sidelined by a groin injury earlier this season, Cisco did not exactly make the most of that opening. Even after playing 44 snaps in the Week 1 win over the Titans, he still finished with the third-worst Pro Football Focus grade (52.6) among defenders on the team in that game, which was a sign of what was to come from him in the ensuing weeks.
To be fair, we still have not seen Payne on an NFL field after he suffered a bone bruise in his knee during training camp. However, while he was the last player drafted in this rookie class, the seventh-rounder has the speed, versatility and overall intangibles to likely be able to contribute at some point.
If anything, the Jets may want to see what they have in Payne to see if he has a shot at competing for a role next season. After all, this season is all but lost for the Jets, especially if they lose the next two games to the Chiefs and Bills, as expected.
Even if the Jets don't get rid of Cisco this season and let him finish out the season, knowing that Payne can slot in could lead them to letting the former walk in free agency. With the 39th-ranked overall grade (63.2) and 60th-ranked coverage grade (54.1) out of 98 qualified safeties from PFF , Cisco clearly has some work to do to retain his spot on the roster, even if the Jets keep him around past the deadline.
Cisco may not officially be a lost cause heading into Week 9 like some players are, but he certainly has his work cut out for him with Payne's potential return and a cheap deal that is set to expire at the end of the season. His time in Gotham may not be over at the trade deadline, but if he is fortunate enough to make it past that, Payne could still get pushed out the door by season's end.

title: Eagles vs. Giants: Who Wins and Why in NFC East's Week 9 Matchup
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – The Eagles will reach their bye after hosting the New York Giants on Sunday (1 p.m.). Will they make it there with a seven-game losing streak and a 2-7 record, or will the slide end against their NFC East rival?
The Giants are the Eagles’ third straight opponent coming in rested. New York was on its bye last week. The Washington Commanders entered last week’s game off their bye, while the Dallas Cowboys entered Monday night’s matchup two weeks ago with11 days off.
Here are some matchups to watch:
Joe Milton will make his first career start against a Giants defense ranked 11th overall, and he will do so without the team’s top two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Tay Wicks. Smith has played just four games for the Eagles this season, yet still leads the team in receiving yards with 310. This will be Wicks’ third straight game missing from the lineup.
Milton gives the Eagles more mobility in the pocket than Tanner McKee did, but he has only been with the Eagles for three weeks.
“How much of the playbook do I think I know? Shoot, whatever’s in this week,” said Milton earlier in the week. … it’s a rough estimate for the percentage, but I feel like I know what I need to know for sure.”
New York has one of the best secondaries in the game and is ranked third in the league in pass defense, allowing184.9 yards per game. Milton could lean on the rookie in the pass game.
Lemon has had at least six catches for 50-plus yards in his last two games. His 31 catches are fourth-best among all rookie receivers, behind Carnell Tate (34), KC Concepcion (33), and Germie Berand (32).
Philly has been historically bad at stopping the run this year, surrendering more than 100 rushing yards in every game this year. It is the longest streak to start a season since 1968, when the Eagles went 2-12.
The Eagles may catch a break with Cam Skattebo listed as doubtful. Devin Singletary would likely get the bulk of the carries if Skattebo can’t play.
Left tackle Jordan Mailata is the only player on the Eagles’ offensive line who has played every snap and is the only OT in the league in the top five in run blocking (83.7) and pass blocking (82.2), per Pro Football Focus. Rookie right tackle Markel Bell struggled mightily in last week’s loss to the Commanders.
The Giants’ primary edge rushers are Abdul Carter and Keyvon Thibodeaux after losing Brian Burns to a season-ending injury. Carter has two sacks while Thibodeaux is still looking for his first of the season.
The Giants receiver was named the NFC player of the Month for October after a having 36 catches for a league-high 509 yards and two touchdowns.
The All-Pro Mitchell is quietly having a good season despite the team’s poor play overall. PFF has him ranked second in passer rating allowed at 65.5 just behind Jacob Parrish’s 65.3. Mitchell has given up 27 receptions on 50 targets for 293 yards, per Next Gen Stats.
Predicted season record: 8-0

title: Eagles' Bet on Joe Milton's Unique Trait Could Actually Pay Off
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - The Eagles have spent the past six weeks watching their season slowly drain away one disappointing drive and stalled possession at a time. Now, with the record at 2-6 and the offense looking lifeless, they’ve decided the only remaining move is a fastball.
They’re handing the keys to Joe Milton and his souped-up right arm.
It’s a pure talent bet, the kind of Hail Mary organizations make when conventional options have already failed. Jalen Hurts is out indefinitely with blood clots. Tanner McKee went 0-3 as the starter despite “solid” play, according to head coach Nick Sirianni.
The offense has been outgained by nearly 900 yards during the Eagles’ six-game losing streak. So they reached for the 6-foot-5, 236-pound quarterback with the rocket launcher hanging from his right shoulder who was still on the Dallas practice squad three weeks ago.
That arm talent, coupled with impressive mobility, are the selling points with Milton.
“Obviously, he's talented, and he's been here for a couple weeks now,” Sirianni said. “Very talented arm, very talented athlete, can process and make decisions out there. Just a lot of good qualities that he has. I like his confidence and everything that he brings, and it's been fun getting to know him and working with him."
At the 2024 NFL Scouting Combine, Milton unleashed a 62 mph throw—the hardest recorded that year and a mark that sits near the top of combine history. Teammates have already started using the same language when discussing Milton’s juice when throwing the football.
“It is a f@#king cannon,” offensive tackle Jordan Mailata said after watching Milton throw. Both Eli Stowers and Makai Lemon marveled at the RPMs of his passes.
Milton doesn’t just have arm strength; he has the kind of velocity that changes the calculus for a defense. In theory at least, windows that close on other quarterbacks stay open longer when the ball arrives that fast.
On Thursday, speaking for the first time as the Eagles’ starter, Milton sounded like a man who had spent years waiting for exactly this moment.
Three weeks ago he was on the practice squad for Dallas behind Dak Prescott and former Eagles backup Sam Howell.
“I was just pretty much going through the plays, going through the week like I was a starter, or like I was playing, and just being ready,” Milton said. “And that’s what the NFL is about: just being ready when your name is called, and just preparing for those moments.”
The moment is here despite only a three-week crash course in Philadelphia’s offense. When asked how much of the Eagles’ playbook he’s mastered, Milton laughed.
“Shoot, whatever’s in this week.”
It’s the answer of a player who understands the assignment. This isn’t a long-term developmental plan. It’s a short-term attempt at creating a spark and keeping hope alive in one of the NFL’s worst divisions.
Milton has never started an NFL game. In five career appearances, he’s completed 37 of 53 passes for 424 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions.
The most extended look came in the 2024 season finale with New England, when he went 22-of-29 for 241 yards and a touchdown while also scoring on the ground. The physical tools have always been obvious. The consistency has always been the question.
Milton’s approach on Thursday was about being present in the moment.
“Just be where my feet are. Smile,” he said. “I love seeing people around me smile, so just making sure everyone around me is smiling. Whatever the play call comes through my helmet, just call that play and execute.”
Milton has an ebullient personality. He often bounces around to the music during stretching and made sure to introduce himself to as many teammates as possible when he arrived in South Philadelphia.
It’s easy to be loose when you’re a backup, though. Now, the microscope is on Milton against the NFC East-leading New York Giants and QB J.J. McCarthy, like Milton, a former “Michigan Man” and a friend.
“I’m going to play my game and stay within the offense, and that’s the job,” said Milton. “It’s football and I’m looking forward to the opportunity to lead this team and play the game I love."
“This is a great opportunity.”
The Eagles are betting that the combination of arm talent and that mindset can create the explosive plays the offense has lacked.
Whether Milton can process quickly enough, throw with touch and accuracy when velocity isn’t the answer, and protect the ball while doing it remains the great unknown.
But the Eagles are out of better options. On Sunday against the Giants, they’ll find out whether the strongest arm in the game can do what the other options could not: make the season feel like it still has a pulse.

title: Nick Sirianni's Eagles QB Change Secrecy Shows His Desperate State
full_text:
Nick Sirianni wanted to keep the lid on his quarterback switch for as long as he could. The big secret lasted about an hour, when the information was given to a national media outlet instead of the 15-20 members of the local press who cover the team on a day-in, day-out basis.
Instead of telling the beat writers at his early afternoon press conference on Wednesday that Tanner McKee was being benched after three games and newcomer Joe Milton would be taking his place, the Eagles' head coach chose not to give up that information.
ESPN’s Adam Schefter broke the story. Sirianni defended his decision not to reveal the news an hour earlier when he talked to local beat reporters on Friday.
“I was going to hold onto that as long as I possibly could, every second, every minute,” he said on his final day of media availability before the first-place New York Giants visit on Sunday.
So, Sirianni clung to his secret for roughly 60 minutes , or 3,600 seconds. The coach clings to the idea of competitive advantage, but did it really matter that the Giants were in the dark for an extra hour?
“Again, I'm not real shy with you guys,” he said. “I'm going to tell you what I want to tell you guys. I respect the job that y'all have to do, but I'm going to tell you what I want to tell you guys because I'm always going to protect the team first and foremost.
“Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold onto information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game. I know there's a lot of interest in everything that you all want to hear, the fans want to hear. My job is to win football games, do everything we can do to help win football games, protect the guys here on this football team, and handle everything that I can inside.”
Sirianni’s secret left his players hung out to dry , to field questions about the QB switch. Jordan Mailata and Landon Dickerson tried to protect their coach’s competitive advantage by saying Milton and McKee split reps at Wednesday’s practice.
The coach said on Monday that McKee was “our guy,” which is what he told reporters during his Monday Zoom call. It was on Tuesday that he decided he was no longer the guy. What changed ?
“We had just gotten off of the game, and then you're starting to look through the game and the game plan,” he said. “As you start to put ideas down—and things are fluid, things are fluid. Like I said, the toughest part about this, in my mind, is that, again, I felt Tanner did solid. I thought he did a lot of good things. That's always tough, and you wear that as the coach. I know it's tough for Tanner, too.”
Sirianni said the decision to make the move was talked through in “great detail” with general manager Howie Roseman and a slew of offensive assistants, including offensive coordinator Sean Mannion and QB coach Parks Frazier.
“We just talk through it,” said the coach. “At the end of the day, my job as the head coach is to make these decisions that I think is best for the football team, but you discuss everything with everybody.”

title: 3 Potential Eagles Trade Candidates Must Be Showcased vs. Giants in Week 9
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is just a few days away (Nov. 10). Philadelphia general manager Howie Roseman has a chance to flex his negotiating prowess , though in a different capacity than in years past. A six-game losing streak and a laundry list of injuries have the Eagles lined up as mild sellers.
Week 9 represents a final opportunity for trade chips to display their talent. A game-changing sack or a thrilling touchdown catch could be all it takes for a player's trade value to skyrocket. That can't happen if they are sitting on the sideline.
Here's a look at three potential Eagles trade candidates that must be showcased versus the Giants.
Trade chatter surrounding defensive tackle Moro Ojomo is growing by the day . It makes sense, considering he has shown improved technique as a pass rusher and run stopper. Ojomo is playing on the final year of his rookie deal, and Philly has already inked extensions with two defensive tackles.
Rotating defensive tackles to keep them fresh has been Philly's style for years. It's the main reason why Ojomo has played less than 60% of the defensive snaps in three of the Eagles' previous four games. That percentage needs to be closer to 70-80% on Sunday, as Ojomo aims to put on a show.
Roseman has given teams the impression that he'll try to extend Ojomo rather than trade him (h/t Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer). It's possible he's being truthful, but it's also possible he's striving to create leverage. Ojomo posting his first sack of the season would go a long way in achieving that.
An ankle injury and Philly's wide receiver depth kept Hollywood Brown sidelined for almost all of the team's first six games. The veteran has played in over 50% of the offensive snaps during the last two weeks, though, as DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) battle their own injuries.
While the results haven't been astounding (four receptions for 47 yards), being on the field gives Brown an opportunity to show contending squads he still has the talent to compete. The 29-year-old speedster has racked up 4,369 yards and 33 touchdowns on 375 catches in his career (93 games).
The Eagles have named Joe Milton their starting quarterback in Week 9. His strong arm and scrambling ability plays right into Brown's strengths as a deep-ball threat. Brown should be the WR3 running routes on passing plays as much as possible, so Philly can net a late-round draft pick.
It'd be easy to cap this list with cornerback Riq Woolen or tight end Dallas Goedert. That said, those are two pros who will be on the field for the majority of the snaps. Defensive tackle Byron Young is a trade candidate who should see more playing time after playing only 15 defensive snaps in Week 8.
Young has the frame (6'3", 292 lbs) needed to drive back offensive linemen in pass defense and stand his ground in run defense. The 25-year-old has room to develop after logging 56 tackles and 2.5 sacks in 31 games. Teams in need of interior defensive line depth should be keeping an eye on Young.
Allowing Young to take on a bigger role against the Giants would give front offices a chance to see if he can be impactful beyond small spurts. Trading Young for a late-round pick should remain a priority. It would send away an expiring contract and open playing time for second-year pro Ty Robinson.

title: 3 Realistic Tanner McKee Trade Destinations to Help Eagles Turn the Page
full_text:
Tanner McKee's days as the interim starting signal-caller for the Philadelphia Eagles are over, as the team has decided to go in a different direction with Joe Milton against the New York Giants in Week 9.
Given how he performed as the starter for Philadelphia over the last three weeks, it's fair to wonder whether the Eagles could even get anything in return in a potential trade for quarterback Tanner McKee. But they should at least try.
McKee will be a free agent next offseason, and it seems very unlikely he'll be back in Philly. So the Eagles should try to recoup some sort of value before losing him for nothing in free agency.
No team will likely view McKee as a starting option, but he could potentially be of interest to teams that could use some added depth at the position. With that in mind, here's a look at three potential trade destinations for McKee that could help the Eagles turn the page.
The Jets currently have just two QBs on their active depth chart: Geno Smith and rookie Cade Klubnik. So, they could be interested in some additional depth and experience at the position behind Smith. Plus, it remains to be seen whether Smith is their long-term answer , as he's currently playing on a one-year deal.
New York could bring in a guy like McKee to see what he has, and if they're impressed, perhaps they'd look to bring him back as a backup next season, or maybe he could even fight for the starting spot. This is the Jets we're talking about, after all.
The Cardinals are undergoing a bit of a transition at the QB spot. Gardner Minshew II has taken over the starting spot heading into Week 9, with rookie Carson Beck as his backup. Meanwhile, Jacoby Brissett, who began the season as the starter in Arizona, has been traded to the Baltimore Ravens to help address their QB injuries.
With the future of the position unsettled, perhaps the Cardinals would want to take a flyer on a guy like McKee, who has shown potential in the past and could be had for a cheap price.
The Lions fancy themselves as a legitimate Super Bowl contender this season after a 5-2 start, but they're a little thin behind starting QB Jared Goff. If Goff goes down, Joshua Dobbs would take over as the starter, and Detroit doesn't really have an option behind him.
Adding McKee could provide the Lions with a third signal-caller that they could call on, if necessary. McKee likely would never see the field in Detroit, but the Lions could do worse than have him as an emergency option.

title: Eli Stowers Taking Positive Steps, but Eagles Still Have Work to Do With Rookie TE
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – It was a step in the right direction for Eli Stowers. The next few steps will be no less important as the rookie tight end tries to prove he can play at this level, regardless of what some thought after watching him in training camp and the preseason.
Stowers caught the first three passes of his NFL career in Sunday night’s loss to the Commanders. You could argue two were in garbage time, and they were, but they still mattered to him.
“It's always good to get the first one out of the way,” he said. “I think it was a good first step for me.”
Stowers was put on injured reserve just 48 hours before the season opener on Sept. 13. He was battling a quad injury, but his hamstring wasn’t 100%, either. It took him five games before he was able to make his debut, doing so against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football.
He only got one target. Against the Commanders a week later, he caught all three of his targets for 53 yards, including the Eagles’ most explosive play of the game, a 34-yard reception that was the final play of the 27-10 loss.
Stowers was further encouraged by the way he was able to move without feeling any pain or hesitation.
“He's been working his tail off to get healthy,” said offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. “He's mentally really, really sharp, especially at that position where there are a lot of different things that we're going to ask of you. His mental preparation's been outstanding. I think getting a chance for him to get into the games a little bit and kind of generate some more confidence while he's out there, I think will ultimately serve him well moving forward.”
It’s easy to forget that this is just the third year Stowers has played tight end, after a lifetime spent playing quarterback, and he is doing it at the highest level of the game.
“I think that there's a lot of carryover mentally from the quarterback standpoint,” he said, “but physically, there's a lot of nuances in technique at the tight end position that I've never done before, like fine-tuning the techniques and the blocking and route running, hand placement, catching the ball, all that kind of stuff.”
It’s also easy to forget just how long the year is for a rookie training for the combine, preparing for a pro day, then the draft, followed by rookie camp, OTAs, minicamp and training camp. There is very little downtime. Even the six-week gap between minicamp and training camp requires constant working out and studying the playbook.
That kind of relentless schedule can wear a player down, cause injury, and require a reset. Perhaps the six-week stint on IR will be Stowers’ reset.
“I'd say anytime you go up a level, it's gonna be more detailed, so I think here it's just the skills that I learned in college, fine-tune them even more so that at this level you can be competitive," he said. “My goal every single day is the same—put my best foot forward, work as hard as I can, and whatever my job is week-to-week, to attack that with the best of my ability.”

title: Landon Dickerson, Moro Ojomo Among Eagles Speaking Up About Trade Deadline Rumors
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Breaking news: The Eagles are trading the last two remaining players on their offensive line from the Super Bowl days of just two years ago, their alleged generational defensive tackle, and their best pass rusher, who still has a year left on his rookie contract at a relative discount.
It’s beyond silly. Sure, trade Jordan Mailata and Landon Dickerson. That opens two positions of major need in the draft. Go ahead and deal Jalen Carter; save some money, but then you need another defensive tackle. Nolan Smith? He’s a bargain next year at $13.7 million.
Landon Dickerson called it propaganda when asked where his head is, with the NFL trade deadline creeping closer. It's Tuesday at 4 p.m.
“It's really not up to me,” said the Eagles’ left guard. “I've said it a lot of times; I love this team. I love this city. This is my home right now. Really, all I care about is winning a championship.”
That’s not to say Eagles general manager Howie Roseman won’t be wheeling and dealing, and if the value is great, maybe he does part ways with one—and only one—of the aforementioned players. Nobody saw him dealing Cam Jurgens in early October, but a second-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-rounder next year was one of those Godfather deals—an offer he couldn’t refuse.
So, Jurgens is gone. To deal Mailata and Dickerson would be a clear white flag of surrender on 2026. Maybe 2027, too, depending on how and where they would find a new left tackle, a new left guard (okay, Willie Lampkin is okay, but is he really starter material?), and possibly a new right guard if Tyler Steen moves on in free agency.
Roseman doesn’t do surrender.
Maybe it will be Steen who goes. He is in the final year of his contract. That is the sweet spot, which puts players like Dallas Goedert, Riq Woolen, and Moro Ojomo in the crosshairs of a potential trade.
“I'm here right now, trying to go through practice, go through meetings, and prepare for this game,” said Goedert, referencing Sunday’s Week 9 home game against the New York Giants.
Then there’s Ojomo, who could possibly deliver the greatest return.
“Howie and [owner Jeffrey] Lurie mean so much to me for giving me this opportunity to play for this team,” said the seventh-round defensive tackle. “I think I was the 23rd DT picked up, so if we can make [a new contract] work,  I love playing for the city. I love working hard for the city. I wanna produce results for the city. I hate letting them down.”
It’s an unusual situation the Eagles are in—being potential sellers at the trade deadline, after making the playoffs in eight of the last nine seasons. But at 2-6, it doesn’t make sense to stand pat. Not since 2021, when Roseman dealt Zach Ertz, who was still in his prime, has he traded away a talent like Ertz.
The rumors of who could be going can be distracting for a player whose name is being bandied about in trade rumors. Nick Sirianni addressed it earlier in the week when asked if he talks to the team about them or the individuals involved.
“You're always in constant communication with your guys,” he said. “I think we have a good beat on what guys are going through, any situation that they're going through, what guys need to be talked to. Of course, you talk to all the guys about that. I'm not saying that necessarily is in front of the room, but maybe more one-on-one situations there.”
Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio was asked how he approaches the trade deadline with his players, and whether he talks to them about the rumors.
“No,” he said. “I mean, I would if I thought there was a rumor out there gaining steam that had no truth to it, but I don't see that at this point in time.”

title: Sean Mannion's Complicated Offense Is Becoming Another Eagles Concern
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles’ offense is too complicated for the current personnel, and the fourth-and-four sequence at Washington in Week 8 provided all the proof needed.
Trailing 16-10 with just over nine minutes left, the Eagles had driven into the red zone and faced a make-or-break situation from the Commanders’ 13-yard line.
Aggression was the correct decision by head coach Nick Sirianni . Everything unraveled, however. Rookie right tackle Markel Bell jumped offsides, and Jake Elliott’s subsequent field goal was wiped out by an illegal formation penalty on Jordan Mailata. Elliott then missed the longer kick.
From that point, the Commanders finished strongly and won going away, 27-10.
The cascade of self-inflicted damage turned a legitimate chance to cut into the deficit—or even take the lead—into another empty trip for the league’s worst offense.
It was a microcosm of the season for a unit that ranks among the worst in franchise history through eight games: dead last or near the bottom in yards, points, efficiency, and nearly every meaningful metric.
This week, embattled offensive coordinator Sean Mannion was asked by Eagles on SI about the failed fourth-down attempt and the visibly late snap. His answer was revealing:
“I think any quarterback’s going to want to gather some degree of information at the line of scrimmage,” the first-year play-caller said. “Sometimes it’s because you may have a kill on the play; sometimes it’s not.”
The Eagles rarely discuss scheme specifics, but Mannion revealed just how many moving parts exist in his Shanahan/McVay-inspired offense .
“I’m not going to get into specifics of that call necessarily, but with anything, I try to get all these calls in as quickly as possible,” he said. “Some of them have motions; some of them demand a little bit more diagnosis at the line of scrimmage than others. So sometimes when you see the clock winding down, it can be a multitude of factors there.
“But we want to give [quarterback] Tanner [McKee] the opportunity to use his cadence, to use a motion to undress things that he may or may not need to see. Sometimes it might be a call-it-run-it play, but he just wants a little bit extra intel in terms of how to execute it.
“Obviously, that was unfortunate with us jumping offsides there. It was a critical moment in the game. We work that mechanic where, hey, if we’re up against the clock and we are on a silent count—so it’s something we work on—we just didn’t execute it at the level that we need to.”
Read that again. Motions. Diagnosis. Cadence. Silent counts. Kills. Extra intel.
Those are multiple variables that must be processed, communicated, and executed under pressure by a backup quarterback in his fifth career start, working without his top two receivers and with a patchwork offensive line featuring a rookie right tackle.
That is not a criticism of the desire for information. Every good quarterback wants it. The problem is that the system appears to require too much of it, too often, from a group that is not executing at a high level and that has been rebuilt on the fly around injuries and departures.
When the play clock is winding down on fourth down in a one-score game, the margin for “a multitude of factors” does not exist.
Bell’s jump is the visible failure; the late or overloaded processing that contributed to it is the structural one.
The Eagles installed the more complex, Shanahan/McVay-influenced offense built around under-center looks, wide zone, layered play-action, and pre-snap movement.
It was supposed to create an identity and force defenses to adjust. Instead, the under-center concepts have largely been inefficient; the run game has little push; protection has been porous, and the offense has somehow looked both predictable and overcomplicated at the same time.
Different quarterbacks have produced the same problems.
That said, Mannion is right that execution failed on that snap. However, he is also describing a system in which execution has become harder than it needs to be, especially for an inexperienced quarterback.
The Eagles are 2-6. The offense is historically bad. Sirianni has said he is not changing the play-caller. Fine.
Then the play-caller and the staff need to strip the offense down to what this personnel can actually execute cleanly and repeatedly—especially on the snaps that matter most.
McVay once described his scheme as “the illusion of complexity.” Right now, the Eagles’ version is a liability because it is too complex for the group currently on the field.
Perhaps Sirianni’s about-face and decision to start Joe Milton—who arrived only on Oct. 16—at quarterback for Sunday’s game against the NFC East-leading Giants is an effort to push his offensive coordinator to scale back his ambitions and better fit the players he has.

title: Joe Milton Is Already Winning Eagles Over Amid Surprise Quarterback Change
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — In the back of the Eagles locker room on Wednesday, offensive linemen Jordan Mailata and Landon Dickerson were selling their coach’s competitive advantage talking point, telling reporters that Joe Milton and Tanner McKee were splitting reps at practice.
In another area of the locker room, Dallas Goedert, Eli Stowers, and Darius Cooper were addressing what was reported by the national media : McKee will take a seat on Sunday against the Giants, and Milton will make the first start of his career in Week 9 .
Perhaps the two QBs are splitting reps, but when you are trying to give a crash course to a player like Milton, who was signed on Oct. 16, you would think he needs every first-team rep he can get to be ready to go.
“Definitely excited for his opportunity,” Cooper said, who was then asked about how McKee took the news that he was headed to the bench after going winless in three starts.
“I feel like Tanner actually handled it pretty well. Offense has been … we've been trying to get there. Tanner, I feel like he came in and did his best at the end of the day.”
Neither quarterback was made available to give their side of the story on Wednesday, but they are expected to talk after Thursday’s practice. Players in charge of catching the ball, like Cooper, Goedert and Eli Stowers, each talked about the zip Milton has on the ball.
“He can spin it, that's for sure,” Stowers said. “You feel it when he throws it to you. I mean, it hits your hands pretty quick. And then he can, when he lets it go downfield, it's pretty good.”
Added Goedert: “It's kind of perfect for a pass catcher. The balls that are in the air for a long time, when you can think, those ones are the scary ones. The ones that get on you, you just have to catch them. Those are the easy ones. He slings that thing. He throws it hard, but it’s really a catchable ball.”
Milton only arrived from the Cowboys’ practice squad on Oct. 16. He wasted little time trying to get to know his new teammates. Shortly after he arrived, he went up to Stowers and said, ‘What’s up 8-7?’ Stowers had his head down and looked up, startled. His expression said, ‘Who are you?’
Asked about that, Stowers laughed.
“No, no, he's a great guy,’ the rookie tight end said. “Since he's got here, he's made it a priority to talk to everybody, get to know everybody, so I appreciate that. He's been kind of a light in the locker room. … He's done a really good job of being relatable to everybody.”

title: 3 Pending Eagles Free Agents Who Should Be Used as Trade Deadline Bait
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is now less than a week away, which means there could be some major moves coming for the Eagles in the very near future. The Eagles could look to recoup some value for several players prior to the deadline, especially players without a long-term future in Philadelphia.
Here's a look at three pending free agents who the Eagles should use as trade deadline bait.
A plethora of teams in the contender conversation could use some added depth at the linebacker position. Meanwhile, the Eagles aren't in the contender conversation, but they're deep enough at linebacker to get by if one is traded away.
So, the Eagles should do what they can to move on from veteran A.J. Epenesa. Not necessarily because he can't play, but because he doesn't appear to have a future with the franchise.
It seems unlikely that the Birds would bring him back in free agency over the offseason, so they should try to recoup some value while they can. Granted, they probably wouldn't get much more than a late-round pick in a potential deal, but something is better than nothing.
The Browns were interested in Epenesa over the offseason, and even signed him initially before opting out of the deal following concerns about his physical. Perhaps they'll revisit that interest now that he has shown that he's healthy enough to play. On the season, Epenesa has appeared in six games and tallied seven combined tackles and one pass defended.
This one is obvious. Brown has no future in Philly beyond the current campaign , but there are plenty of teams out there who would be interested in adding an extra weapon for a potential playoff push.
Just last season, Brown caught 49 passes for 587 yards and five touchdowns with the Kansas City Chiefs. Perhaps a reunion with the Chiefs is in the cards? Star quarterback Patrick Mahomes certainly wouldn't be upset about the addition of another viable option to throw to.
If not the Chiefs, other contenders, including the Rams, Bills and 49ers, could possibly be interested in a veteran receiver like Brown. Given his lack of action with the Eagles (4 total receptions), Brown would likely welcome a change of scenery.
As a young defensive lineman with plenty of promise, there is ample interest around the NFL in Moro Ojomo, including from the Jaguars , according to a report from ESPN . As opposed to the first two players listed above, Ojomo would likely fetch a nice return for the Eagles in a potential trade if they use him as bait prior to the deadline , which they should.
The Eagles already have a ton of money tied up in the defensive line moving forward thanks to the massive contracts of Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis, so there's a real chance that they won't be able to pay Ojomo market value over the offseason. It's also fair to wonder whether they'd want to pay him a ton, as opposed to allocating that money to a different position.
If the Eagles were contending this season, there would be a real argument for holding onto Ojomo, even without the uncertainty about his long-term future with the franchise. But since that isn't the case, they should try to recoup as much value as possible.

title: Steelers Are Going to Do It Again, Aren't They?
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers need a wide receiver. They're one of three teams that appear to be really looking at the NFL trade deadline . But once again, they're being linked to the least exciting option available.
Josh Downs and Brian Thomas Jr. were the big names to watch over the last several days, as the trade deadline approached. The Indianapolis Colts and Jacksonville Jaguars, respectively, aren't sold on dealing either of them, but teams like the Kansas City Chiefs, San Francisco 49ers and the Steelers are trying to make a push for one of the top options available.
Then, as the weekend approached and the deadline continued to near, Tennessee Titans' Calvin Ridley's name entered the mix. Ridley became the third-biggest name to watch, but a much different option than Downs or Thomas.
And, of course, everyone is going to guess that'll be who the Steelers land.
I’d rather the Steelers make no move than trade anything for Ridley. They tried the end of career receiver trade last year. https://t.co/vThkETr12U
CALVIN RIDLEY THE PITTSBURGH STEELERS LOVE YOU 😭 pic.twitter.com/l6EB0fYsij
Unlike 25-year-old Downs and 24-year-old Thomas, Ridley is 32 years old. Downs is on an expiring contract and Thomas has another year left on a rookie deal. Ridley is in the second-to-last year of a four-year, $92 million contract. Next season, he'd make $29.75 million unless he's moved. His dead cap if released is $7.5 million.
Ridley also has less receiving yards than Downs and Thomas on the season.
For Steelers fans, this may feel like deja vu. Pittsburgh is chasing a wide receiver at the deadline, clearly in need of help to make a push in the second half of the season and improve their offense, and instead of competing with other teams adding help, they'd be choosing the least favorable of those available.
Now, Ridley is a much better option than names like Adam Thielen, Mike Williams and Marquez Valdes-Scantling have been in years past, but in this year's field of options, he's very clearly No. 3.
The Steelers have a chance to chase a player in Downs who may step onto the field as their WR2 before the end of the season. The speedy inside receiver has reliable hands, great separation ability and upside he still has yet to reach.
Thomas may have fallen off with Jacksonville, but this is a 1,200-yard, 10-touchdown rookie just two years ago. With another year left on his rookie contract and first-round potential, any team that wants to take a swing should be willing to take one on the Jaguars' wideout.
Both are more expensive, though.
Ridley will likely be a late-round NFL Draft pick, while Downs could go as high as a third-rounder , and Thomas is expected to be worth even more.
So, here we go again. The Steelers know exactly what they need at the NFL trade deadline. Will they finally break the streak of disappointing additions, or is this year different?
It feels like, while it may still be better than years past, the excitement about the next addition in Pittsburgh is starting to die down, and the worry of repeating history is starting to creep in.

title: Steelers’ Jaquan Brisker Fined for Deshaun Watson Hit
full_text:
Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker has been disciplined by the NFL for a hit on Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson in Week 8.
As noted by The Ringer's Tom Pelissero, the league has handed down a fine of $17,911 to Brisker for the blow he delivered to Watson on the Browns' first drive of the game.
The NFL fined Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker $17,911 for this hit on Deshaun Watson last week. Watson entered the concussion protocol a day later and has since cleared. Shedeur Sanders is expected to start Sunday vs. New Orleans. pic.twitter.com/4EFpoA2gNj
Brisker was tagged with a roughing the passer penalty as a result, which temporarily extended the series for Cleveland on what otherwise would have been a three-and-out.
Pittsburgh ultimately forced a fumble several plays later, however, and went on to blow out the Browns by a score of 27-6 to move to 6-2 heading into its Week 9 bye.
Watson finished out the remainder of the contest after briefly being pulled for three plays immediately following Brisker's hit.
Shedeur Sanders entered in Watson's place for that span of time while the latter was evaluated.
Watson was then cleared to return, and he was sacked a total of eight times by the Steelers while completing 27 of his 39 passing attempts for 324 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions.
The 31-year-old was later evaluated after the game as well as early in the week before self-reporting concussion symptoms to Cleveland on November 3.
Watson landed in the concussion protocol from there and has been cleared ahead of the Browns' Week 9 bout vs. the New Orleans Saints.
Regardless, Watson is questionable to play while Sanders will get the start for Cleveland in a contest that has significant ramifications for Pittsburgh considering the Browns sit just a game behind it for first place in the AFC North at 5-3.
A Pittsburgh native who played his college ball at Penn State, Brisker joined his hometown team as a free agent this past offseason on what was viewed as a surprising cheap one-year, $5.5 million deal at the time.
Brisker had been a staple of the Chicago Bears' secondary for the first four seasons of his career, starting all 52 games he appeared in while recording 342 tackles, seven sacks and four interceptions.
Part of the reason why he didn't command a larger deal and thus came at an extreme discount for Pittsburgh were his concussion concerns, as he suffered three with the Bears and missed all but five contests in 2024 as a result.
Though Brisker suffered an injury during training camp that kept him off the field for several weeks, he returned in time for the start of the regular season and has played in all eight of the Steelers' games up to this point.
The 27-year-old has been on the field for 99.8 percent of the team's defensive snaps (per Pro Football Reference ), which comes out to a total of 507 and is tied with both Jalen Ramsey and Patrick Queen for the team lead.
Brisker's had an up-and-down season, as he's missed eight tackles and allowed 156 yards in coverage over 15 catches on 20 targets (per Pro Football Focus ).
He does have an interception to his name, though, and is third on the team in total tackles with 51.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Legend Jack Ham Experiences Medical Emergency at Penn State Game
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Pittsburgh Steelers legend and Pro Football Hall of Famer, Jack Ham, experienced a "medical emergency" before the Penn State Nittany Lions game against the Washington Huskies, Penn State announced.
"Penn State Sports Network analyst Jack Ham experienced a medical emergency earlier today and was transported to the University of Washington Medical Center, where he is being treated. We do not have further information at this time," the school released in a statement.
Ham is a broadcaster for Penn State, where he played from 1968 to 1970 before being drafted by the Steelers in the second round of the 1971 NFL Draft. He's the first Penn State player to be inducted into both the College Football Hall of Fame and the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
Ham was at the University of Washington versus Penn State game when the medical emergency happened.
Ham is in his 27th year as a broadcaster for the Nittany Lions. A Johnstown, Pennsylvania, native, Ham became a consensus All-American in 1970 when he recorded 91 tackles and four interceptions in a season. He finished his college career as a two-time First-Team All-East.
Ham once said graduating from Penn State was his greatest accomplishment.
"Probably graduating from Penn State with a business degree. I know my parents felt that way! Also, Joe Paterno taught me not to think I was somebody special just because I was a professional football player. It helps keep players from turning into egotistical maniacs." Ham said. "I prefer to play consistent, error-free football. If you're doing your job well and defending your area, you might not get tested that often, or get a chance to make big plays."
In the NFL, Ham spent his entire career with the Steelers. He left the National Football League with six First-Team All-Pro and two Second-Team All-Pro selections, eight Pro Bowl appearances and was part of all four Steelers Super Bowl victories in the '70s.
He was also named to the NFL's 1970's All-Decade Team, the NFL's 75th Anniversary All-Time Team, the NFL's 100th Anniversary All-Time Team, Pittsburgh Steelers All-Time Team and was inducted into the Steelers Hall of Honor.
He finished his NFL career with 32 interceptions and 25.5 sacks (sacks were not an official statistic at the time).
He was elected into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1988.
This is a developing story. Pittsburgh Steelers On SI will continue to provide updates on Ham's condition as more information becomes available.
Update: Penn State head coach Matt Campbell has confirmed that Ham is in "stable condition."
"Everybody knows that, man, this was a gut-wrenching day for Penn State football with Jack Ham," Campbell said after the game. "Obviously, a really tough situation as we get off the buses here. First of all, I think we should all know Steve Jones and the heroic effort that he did for one of his, man, somebody he loves dearly. And if it’s not for Steve, you know, what he did, I don’t know if we would have as good of news as we do right now. And then I want to also thank the University of Washington, their athletic director, their emergency team. They were incredible. They were outstanding.
"I think, hopefully, as all of you know, Jack is in stable condition right now. And then, obviously, the emotion of that. What I was really proud of our football team. We talked about a little bit before we went out for the game. The courage of our kids to play with what Jack Ham means to Penn State football. How that guy played the game. How that guy still, to this day, serves our football program. It was awesome to be able to go win the football game for him and his family."

title: Injury Rundown: When Steelers Players Can Return From IR
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are awaiting the return of several key contributors from the reserve/injured list as they enter the second half of their schedule .
Currently sitting at 6-2 while holding sole possession of first place in the AFC North during their Week 9 bye, the Steelers are in an overall good position. They could upgrade their roster even further by making an addition or two via trade ahead of the November 10 trade deadline , though getting back some of their injured players in the near future should help out a ton as well.
With that, here is every player on IR as well as the reserve/PUP list for Pittsburgh and when they may make their way back onto the field.
Harmon was placed on IR with a foot injury he suffered during the first half of Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns on Thursday Night Football.
Since he's missed the minimum of four games while residing on IR, the 2025 first-round pick is eligible to be activated next week ahead of the Steelers' Week 10 matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football.
Harmon hadn't been working with Pittsburgh's rehab group before its Week 8 rematch with Cleveland. Whether or not his 21-day practice window is opened and/or he returns to the 53-man roster by next week remains to be seen.
Pittman Jr. was first ruled out for the Steelers' Week 2 game against the New England Patriots with a foot injury before later being placed on IR, before having a chance to face his old team, the Indianapolis Colts, in Week 5.
The veteran wide receiver spoke with reporters at the start of the bye week on November 2 and stated that he's been doing "a slow progression," which has been "going well."
Pittman Jr. stated that his injury, which started out as plantar fasciitis, has "morphed into something else," which is a bit worrying.
He did state that it would "be great to be back after the bye week," and he can be activated next week since he's already missed four games, but it seems possible that he'll remain on IR beyond that timeframe.
Wilson suffered a finger injury at the end of the first half vs. Indianapolis in Week 5, resulting in a trip to IR before Pittsburgh's Week 6 bout with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
The third-year receiver has been seen working with the rehab group off to the side during recent practices. Wilson's 21-day practice window has yet to be opened, though that could potentially occur in the near future, and he will be eligible for activation in Week 11.
Joseph-Day was placed on IR before the Steelers' Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints in Paris with a triceps injury.
In an appearance on 102.5 WDVE earlier this week, Jack Sawyer stated that, "It sucks we're not gonna be able to get Sebastian back for- maybe at all," which painted a worrying picture about the odds of Joseph-Day returning in 2026.
The 31-year-old also isn't eligible to be activated until Week 12 at the earliest if he does progress quicker than expected.
A third-round pick out of Iowa in the 2026 NFL Draft, Dunker was placed on IR ahead of Pittsburgh's Week 3 contest vs. the Cincinnati Bengals with an MCL sprain.
The initial timeline for his recovery sat around the four-to-six-week mark, and he's now near the end of that interval.
Dunker became eligible to be activated in Week 7, meaning he can rejoin the 53-man roster at any time once he's cleared.
The Steelers put Driscoll on IR with a return designation at final roster cuts in late August due to an undisclosed injury.
The 29-year-old has been eligible to return since Week 5, though there's been just about zero updates on his status throughout the season up to this point.
Lee, who missed his entire rookie season in 2024 due to a calf injury, landed on IR back in August during training camp.
The former sixth-round pick will miss the remainder of the campaign as a result and will look to make his return in 2027 as he enters the final year of his rookie contract.
Kent did not play as a rookie last season after first suffering an ankle injury in training camp and landing on IR before tearing his ACL after his 21-day practice window was opened in early December.
The former seventh-round pick was placed on the active/PUP list at the beginning of training camp this year and was then moved to the reserve/PUP list at the roster cutdown deadline.
Kent has been eligible for activation since Week 5, but his timeline for a possible return in 2026 is unknown at the moment.
