title: Commanders News: Myles Garrett Could Join Aaron Donald as Washington Fights Costly False Starts | Burgundy Roundup
full_text:
Treylon Burks gave Washington its longest reception of the season against Philadelphia. Now he has missed both practices ahead of the Rams game . Burks sat out again Thursday with a foot injury, and Dyami Brown was added to the report as limited with a calf issue. Stefon Diggs returned after a Wednesday rest day. With Terry McLaurin on injured reserve, the Commanders have one more practice before they must make a call on their receivers for Sunday. Washington has a different kind of decision at defensive tackle. Jer’Zhan Newton practiced fully for the second straight day, but the Commanders still have to activate him from injured reserve before he can play. Shy Tuttle remained limited with a shoulder injury. The team moved Ricky Barber from the practice squad to the active roster Wednesday and signed Daniel Ekuale to the practice squad. Daronte Jones said replacing Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw will take the entire front seven, not just whoever lines up in their spots. Robert Henry Jr. is back on Washington’s active roster with a chance to play his first regular-season NFL game. He told the team he is preparing for that opportunity, though he does not know what his role will be against Los Angeles. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler remain the established backs. David Blough described the third running back’s job as a supplemental one, leaving Henry’s workload to be determined. The Rams have their own questions in the secondary. Jaylen Watson needs shoulder surgery and will miss the rest of the season . Trent McDuffie, dealing with a back injury, and Kam Curl, who has a foot issue, missed practice again Thursday. Los Angeles signed former Ram David Long Jr. to its practice squad, while Sean McVay said Josh Wallace and former Commanders cornerback Emmanuel Forbes will be asked to do more without Watson. How much Washington can test that group may depend on what happens with Burks and Brown on Friday. Matthew Stafford practiced fully for a second straight day despite the right elbow issue that surfaced after the Chargers game. Myles Garrett and tight end Terrance Ferguson were limited again as they work back from injured reserve; both would need to be activated to play Sunday. Guard Steve Avila improved to full participation, but linebacker Grant Stuard did not practice. Tight end Colby Parkinson and long snapper Joe Cardona also remained out.
Blough didn’t dress up Washington’s start against Philadelphia. He said the offense is still working through the mistakes that wrecked its opening 15 minutes, including pre-snap penalties that have been “killing us.” The Rams’ front gives the Commanders plenty to account for before the ball is snapped. Blough said Washington cannot simply double Aaron Donald on every play with Byron Young rushing off the edge and Garrett potentially joining him. Jones saw the rushers working together against the Eagles, whether Washington sent four or five. Stafford presents a different problem: he recognizes pressure quickly and gets the ball out. Jones also said having Steve Wilks on the sideline against Philadelphia helped him focus on the next defensive call. Sunday will show whether that arrangement and the improved rush coordination hold up against the Rams. Los Angeles made another roster move Thursday, promoting kicker Joshua Karty from its practice squad. Brandon McManus remains on the active roster; Karty handled kickoffs last week while McManus took the field goals and extra points. Washington long snapper Tyler Ott was named the team’s 2026 Salute to Service Award nominee. Ott has supported the Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors, which helps families who have lost a service member. Fan voting is open through November 30 and will help determine the award’s three finalists.
Quinn emphasized Cross’ communication against Philadelphia. “But most importantly, I really felt his communication in this game, the urgency of what we're looking for from that," Quinn said. "So I thought that was a good step forward as well.”
The Pro Football Hall of Fame announced its five remaining Contributor nominees for the Class of 2027 on Wednesday, including former Washington Redskins quarterback Doug Williams, who currently serves as a senior advisor to Commanders GM Adam Peters. The field started with 42 nominees and has been reduced to this group, which includes Robert Kraft, Ralph Hay, Virginia McCaskey, and John Wooten. The Contributor Subcommittee must still choose a single candidate who advances to the full committee.
When George Costanza pitched the show about nothing to NBC president Russell Dalrymple, Dalrymple asked, “Well, why am I watching it?" “Because it’s on TV,” Costanza said. More than 30 years later, that sentiment still applies. As evidenced by the fact that, per Nielsen, 19.015 million (on average) watched Sunday night’s snoozefest between the Eagles and Commanders on the network that Dalrymple once ran. It’s an amazing number, given that it was the 2-5 Eagles against the 1-4-1 Commanders. The game itself wasn’t particularly compelling, and it followed afternoon windows that culminated in a down-to-the-wire showdown between the Chiefs and the Broncos.
Good to have you back out there, @Flash_Garrett ! pic.twitter.com/09lBpF9I5b
Newton returned to practice last week as the team opened his 21-day practice window while he recovers from a torn pectoral muscle. He was downgraded to OUT before the Eagles game, but Commanders head coach Dan Quinn likes how his return is progressing. "The arrow is going up for sure, and I'm very optimistic for it. But it's important to stack another good week of him in practice and movements." Newton must still be activated from injured reserve before he can play against Los Angeles.

title: Commanders Mailbag: Is Luke McCaffrey Being Overlooked? Did Dan Quinn Win Back Trust?
full_text:
We want to hear from you! Each week, we invite you, the Burgundy and Gold faithful, to send in your Washington Commanders questions about everything going on in Ashburn/Landover. We want to make sure everyone gets a chance to have their take heard in the HTTR4LIFE Mailbag, so we'll answer questions on either Monday or Friday, depending on the volume of responses each week. You can send your Washington Commanders questions for the HTTR4LIFE Mailbag to hailbng+si@gmail.com . Washington’s top receiver is out for the year, yet Luke McCaffrey remains outside the main receiver rotation. This week’s mailbag examines what’s blocking his opportunity and how much confidence Dan Quinn’s Eagles win should restore.
Question from Nigel F. via email That's a great question that I've written about here before . From what I can tell, the staff likes McCaffrey, or he wouldn't be on the roster, but he somehow keeps falling outside of the group that gets the main share of the offensive snaps at receiver. Against Philadelphia, McCaffrey played just three offensive snaps. Antonio Williams played 50, Treylon Burks 40, and Stefon Diggs 39. The team loaded up at receiver this offseason, giving the staff options even after McLaurin went down.
#Commanders WR Luke McCaffrey’s two great returns set the team up in great field position On the kickoff return for 44 yds, that was his longest of the season. #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/BPqPWQGC3b
The receiver room may not be big on names outside of McLaurin and Stefon Diggs, but rookie Antonio Williams is emerging fast , and whenever Treylon Burks can stay healthy, he routinely produces. Add in the attention tight end Chig Okonkwo gets, and there's not much left for McCaffrey, Dyami Brown, or Van Jefferson. On film, McCaffrey gets open, so offensive coordinator David Blough has to make the scheme work with the talent they have. With injuries playing a factor, McCaffrey will likely get his shot to show what he brings to the field before the end of the season.
Question from Reggie D. on Facebook Last Sunday night was fun to watch, but we should keep things in perspective when it comes to changing our opinion of the third-year coach after his second win of the season against a team on a big losing streak. That said, do all winning streaks start somewhere? Certainly, but yes, I'll have to see it over multiple weeks before opinions start to shift. Washington still committed nine penalties coming out of the bye. Quinn really set himself up for a slow start filled with questions when he hired two first-time NFL coordinators in a season he needed to show improvement. What I'm really interested in this week is how well they can stand up to the Rams' two-headed monster at running back , with both starting defensive tackles now on injured reserve and one of their replacements, Shy Tuttle, banged up.
